title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
萬曆丙子秋浙江復當貢士
於是御史吳從憲行郡縣歲
徧報成事矣
上遣代者御史鮑希顏未至而從
憲不敢離境土庀事益毖八
月六日遂以伯誠與教諭林
===
守萬爲考試官教諭徐道明
梁尚忠畢大魁黃嵓陳懋昭
田舜耕爲同考試官入鎖院
而左布政使王應顯左叅政
朱炳如司提調按察使蒙詔
副使王續之司監試曁百執
事罔或不虔乃合提學僉事
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

萬曆丙子秋，浙江復當貢士。於是御史吳從憲行郡縣歲徧，報成事矣。上遣代者御史鮑希顏未至，而從憲不敢離境土，庀事益毖。八月六日，遂以伯誠與教諭林守萬爲考試官，教諭徐道明、梁尚忠、畢大魁、黃嵓、陳懋昭、田舜耕爲同考試官，入鎖院。而左布政使王應顯、左叅政朱炳如司提調，按察使蒙詔、副使王續之司監試，曁百執事，罔或不虔。乃合提學僉事
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the bingzi year of the Wanli era [1576], it was once again time for Zhejiang to present scholars for the examination. At this time, Investigating Censor Wu Congxian 吳從憲 had completed his annual circuit of prefectures and counties and reported the completion of his duties. Investigating Censor Bao Xiyan 鮑希顏, whom the Emperor had dispatched to replace him, had not yet arrived; yet Congxian did not dare leave the territory of his jurisdiction and attended to the preparations with even greater diligence. On the sixth day of the eighth month, he accordingly appointed me, [Dai] Bocheng 伯誠, together with County Director of Studies Lin Shouwan 林守萬, as Examiners, and County Directors of Studies Xu Daoming 徐道明, Liang Shangzhong 梁尚忠, Bi Dakui 畢大魁, Huang Yan 黃嵓, Chen Maozhao 陳懋昭, and Tian Shungeng 田舜耕 as Associate Examiners, to enter the locked examination compound. Left Administration Commissioner Wang Yingxian 王應顯 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhu Bingru 朱炳如 were in charge of proctoring, while Surveillance Commissioner Meng Zhao 蒙詔 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang Xuzhi 王續之 were in charge of monitoring the examination; together with all the various functionaries, there was none who was not reverent and diligent. Thereupon, they gathered the … [selected by] Assistant Surveillance Commissioner for Education…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
喬因阜所遴士二千七百人
而三試之拔其儁九十人與
其文錄焉以
獻伯誠以職事當序諸簡端竊惟
今天下兩浙實稱首藩豈惟
其山川之佳麗物產之豐盈
人文之宣朗雄海內哉乃其
===
霑濡
帝澤鬯被
皇風自
二京而下無若茲方之捷而神
也先是
皇上憫士習之日澆知功令之漸
弛乃
punctuated: 喬因阜所遴士二千七百人而三試之，拔其儁九十人，與其文錄焉以獻。伯誠以職事當序諸簡端。竊惟今天下兩浙實稱首藩，豈惟其山川之佳麗、物產之豐盈、人文之宣朗雄海內哉？乃其霑濡帝澤，鬯被皇風，自二京而下，無若茲方之捷而神也。先是，皇上憫士習之日澆，知功令之漸弛，乃
translation_en: … the 2,700 scholars selected by Qiao Yinfu 喬因阜, and tested them across three sessions, selecting ninety outstanding men among them and recording their names along with their essays for presentation to the throne. By virtue of my official duties, I, Bocheng 伯誠, ought to write a preface at the head of these pages. I humbly reflect that in the empire today, the Two Zhe 兩浙 region is truly acclaimed as the foremost province. Is this merely because the beauty of its mountains and rivers, the abundance of its products, and the brilliance of its literary culture surpass all within the seas? Rather, it is because in being steeped in imperial grace and pervasively touched by the august influence, second only to the Two Capitals, no region is as swift and marvellous in its response as this place. Earlier, His Majesty, pitying that the habits of scholars were growing daily more superficial and recognizing that the examination regulations were gradually slackening, thereupon …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
俞輔臣之請更督學憲臣之
璽書而浙之憲臣適在
輦轂下面承
德音視他省爲獨先焉士之聞風
逖聽者固已灑然變志易慮
思覲
耿光二年於此矣邇者
===
皇上德隆道積見聖
羹牆乃以八月之吉
幸臨太學釋奠
先師縟儀曠典茲惟肇舉蓋未
浹辰也而聲敎所暨霆迅飈
馳凡我多士則又動色感奮
喁喁焉冀附雲龍風虎之會
punctuated: 俞輔臣之請，更督學憲臣之璽書，而浙之憲臣適在輦轂下，面承德音，視他省爲獨先焉。士之聞風逖聽者，固已灑然變志易慮，思覲耿光，二年於此矣。邇者，皇上德隆道積，見聖羹牆，乃以八月之吉，幸臨太學，釋奠先師。縟儀曠典，茲惟肇舉，蓋未浹辰也，而聲敎所暨，霆迅飈馳。凡我多士，則又動色感奮，喁喁焉冀附雲龍風虎之會，
translation_en: …approved the request of the Grand Secretaries to renew the imperial credentials issued to the Education Intendant Censors. As it happened, the Censor appointed to Zhejiang was then at the capital beneath the imperial carriage and received the benevolent pronouncement in person, ahead of all other provinces. It has now been two years since the scholars who heard the news from afar were refreshed in spirit, transformed their ambitions and thoughts, and longed to behold the resplendent glory of the throne. Recently, as His Majesty's virtue has grown ever more exalted and his attainment of the Way ever deeper—seeing the ancient sages even in his broth and on his walls—on an auspicious day in the eighth month he graced the Directorate of Education with his imperial presence and performed the libation ritual to the Former Teacher. Though scarcely twelve days have elapsed since the inauguration of this elaborate ceremony and rare state observance, the reach of his moral prestige and teaching has spread with the swiftness of thunder and the speed of a whirlwind. All our many scholars, visibly moved and stirred to exertion, look up expectantly in the hope of joining the opportune meeting of clouds with the dragon and wind with the tiger,…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以快
聖作物覩之期志慮日以精明藻
績益以彪炳抱藝而來操觚
而書摛辭吐蘊大異疇昔其
感動之捷而神有如此者故
今觀多士所爲文雖其言人
人殊類能抉微衍奧標粹掞
===
奇有莊嚴峻潔若高山大川
莫窺其際者曰此其聞
皇上恭默思道不顯惟德之風者
耶胡深以厚也有溫純爾雅
若襲珍韞玉其光不可掩者
曰此其聞
皇上勤學好問勵精圖政之風者
punctuated: 以快聖作物覩之期。志慮日以精明，藻績益以彪炳，抱藝而來，操觚而書，摛辭吐蘊，大異疇昔，其感動之捷而神有如此者。故今觀多士所爲文，雖其言人人殊，類能抉微衍奧、標粹掞奇。有莊嚴峻潔，若高山大川莫窺其際者，曰：「此其聞皇上恭默思道、不顯惟德之風者耶？胡深以厚也！」有溫純爾雅，若襲珍韞玉其光不可掩者，曰：「此其聞皇上勤學好問、勵精圖政之風者
translation_en: … so as to rejoice in this era when a sage arises and all creatures behold him. Their aims and thoughts grow daily more refined and clear, and their literary accomplishments become ever more resplendent. Embracing their skills, they have come forward; grasping their writing tablets, they compose; unfolding their rhetoric and pouring forth their accumulated learning, they differ greatly from days past—such is the swift and marvelous power of this inspiration! Thus, when we now examine the essays composed by the many scholars, although their words differ from person to person, as a rule they are able to uncover subtleties and elaborate profundities, displaying pure essence and radiating originality. There are those whose style is solemn, lofty, and pure, like high mountains and great rivers whose bounds cannot be fathomed; of these one says: "Are these not men who have heard the inspiring example of His Majesty pondering the Way in reverent silence, his virtue all the more illustrious for being unostentatious? How deep and substantial they are!" There are those whose style is gentle, pure, and refined, like treasured gems and concealed jade whose luster cannot be hidden; of these one says: "Are these not men who have heard the inspiring example of His Majesty studying diligently, delighting in inquiry, and rousing his spirit to plan for governance? …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
耶胡瑩以徹也有縝密典則
從容於矩度若具瞻在望可
親不可狎者曰此其聞
皇上臨雍講藝尊師重傅者之風
耶胡充以達也深以厚必端
士也端斯誠誠以任事弗僨
瑩以徹必敏士也敏斯裕裕
===
以服官弗曠充以達必弘毅
士也弘毅斯勇勇以肩重致
遠弗懼得若人焉以貢春官
揚
皇廷庶幾哉以人事
君之責亦少副矣雖然有司之取
士也據其言斯登之賢書上
punctuated: 耶？胡瑩以徹也！」有縝密典則、從容於矩度，若具瞻在望，可親不可狎者，曰：「此其聞皇上臨雍講藝、尊師重傅者之風耶？胡充以達也！」深以厚，必端士也；端斯誠，誠以任事弗僨。瑩以徹，必敏士也；敏斯裕，裕以服官弗曠。充以達，必弘毅士也；弘毅斯勇，勇以肩重致遠弗懼。得若人焉，以貢春官，揚皇廷，庶幾哉以人事君之責亦少副矣！雖然，有司之取士也，據其言斯登之賢書，上
translation_en:
… Why else would they be so lustrous and pellucid?" And where there were papers that were meticulous and canonical in their norms, composed and measured in their adherence to rules, like a figure commanding universal respect in full view—approachable yet never to be treated with familiarity—I said: "Is this not someone who has heard the inspiring example of His Majesty visiting the Imperial Academy to lecture on the classic arts, honoring his teachers and esteeming his tutors? Why else would they be so abundant and far-reaching?"

One who is profound and substantial must be an upright scholar; being upright, he is sincere, and with sincerity he can take on responsibilities without faltering. One who is lustrous and pellucid must be a keen-witted scholar; being keen-witted, he has ample capability, and with ample capability he can perform official duties without neglect. One who is abundant and far-reaching must be a broad-minded and resolute scholar; being broad-minded and resolute, he is courageous, and with courage he can shoulder heavy burdens and go far without fear. To obtain such men as these, to present them to the Ministry of Rites and raise them up to the Imperial Court—perhaps in this way our responsibility of serving the Sovereign by recommending worthy men will have been fulfilled in some small measure!

Even so, when the authorities select scholars, it is on the basis of their words that they enter them into the roster of worthies and present…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之
天府矣
皇上神聖度越百王公卿大夫之
立朝者奉職兢兢若在
日月之下多士盍自思卽進對
大廷備員百執事果能稱
皇上任使乎今夫爲圭爲璋以薦
===
郊廟匪玉弗堪追而琢之礱
而磨之凡以用之也若雕文
刻鏤以供翫好則玉何貴焉
合抱之木出深山而登廣廈
以爲棟梁材斯美矣若輪囷
屈曲反不如拱把之適於用
何者物不貴異貴適也今多
punctuated: 之天府矣。皇上神聖，度越百王，公卿大夫之立朝者，奉職兢兢，若在日月之下。多士盍自思，卽進對大廷，備員百執事，果能稱皇上任使乎？今夫爲圭爲璋，以薦郊廟，匪玉弗堪。追而琢之，礱而磨之，凡以用之也；若雕文刻鏤，以供翫好，則玉何貴焉？合抱之木，出深山而登廣廈，以爲棟梁，材斯美矣；若輪囷屈曲，反不如拱把之適於用。何者？物不貴異，貴適也。今多
translation_en: … them to the Imperial Archives. His Majesty is divinely sage, surpassing the hundred kings of old, and the Dukes, Ministers, and Grand Masters who stand at court perform their duties with cautious reverence, as though standing beneath the very sun and moon. Why do you many scholars not reflect upon yourselves: if you advance to reply at the Great Court and fill posts among the various officials, will you truly be able to prove worthy of His Majesty's employment? Now then, to fashion tablets and half-tablets for presentation at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, nothing but jade will suffice. One carves and chisels it, grinds and polishes it, all so as to put it to use; if it is merely engraved with ornate patterns to serve as a plaything, what value is there in jade? When a tree of an arm's-span girth comes out of the deep mountains and is raised into a spacious hall to serve as ridgepole and beam, its timber is fine indeed; yet if it is gnarled, knotted, and crooked, it is actually inferior to a sapling a hand's span thick that is suited to practical use. Why is this? Because in things, what is valued is not rarity, but suitability for use. Now, as for the many…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
士之文誠深以厚矣瑩以徹
矣充以達矣乃其人或浮以
淺焉以任事則僨庸以闇焉
以服官則曠萎以繭焉以肩
重致遠則弗勝巵辭而靡當
空言而無實則曩所云端也
敏也弘毅也皮相爾矣何足
===
以言得士〔伯誠〕爲此懼矣伏
讀
璽書曰端軌儀崇經術使學術還
淳士有實用大哉
王言夫非洞文勝之弊敦尚行之
風與章逢之士更始者耶夫
孔子之道昭如日星書而傳
punctuated: 士之文誠深以厚矣，瑩以徹矣，充以達矣。乃其人或浮以淺焉，以任事則僨；庸以闇焉，以服官則曠；萎以繭焉，以肩重致遠則弗勝。巵辭而靡當，空言而無實，則曩所云端也、敏也、弘毅也，皮相爾矣，何足以言得士？〔伯誠〕爲此懼矣。伏讀璽書曰：「端軌儀，崇經術，使學術還淳，士有實用。」大哉王言！夫非洞文勝之弊，敦尚行之風，與章逢之士更始者耶？夫孔子之道，昭如日星，書而傳
translation_en: … the writings of the numerous scholars are indeed deep and substantial, lustrous and penetrating, full and expressive. Yet as men, some are superficial and shallow, so that when entrusted with affairs, they ruin them; some are mediocre and benighted, so that when holding office, they neglect their duties; some are listless and bound up like cocoons, so that when called upon to shoulder heavy burdens and go far, they prove unequal to the task. With shifting words that lack appropriateness and empty talk devoid of substance, what I previously called uprightness, diligence, and breadth of mind with resolute endurance would be mere judgment by outward appearances—how could that suffice to be called obtaining true scholars? I, [Bocheng 伯誠], am fearful on this account. Humbly reading the Imperial rescript, it says: "Rectify norms and deportment, revere classical learning, cause scholarship to return to purity, and ensure that scholars possess practical utility." Great indeed are the King's words! Does this not penetrate the abuses of literary floridity exceeding substance, foster a custom of prizing conduct, and make a fresh start with the scholars in their ceremonial caps and wide-sleeved robes? Now the Way of Confucius is as bright as the sun and stars; written down and transmitted…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之爲六經誦而習之爲學術
體而行之天下國家爲實用
是故以之任事而事理矣以
之服官而官飭矣以之肩重
致遠無往而弗濟矣洋洋
聖謨斯其無負矣哉如徒以其炳
炳烺烺之文聞風而興俄頃
===
而化曰我能涵濡
帝澤鬯被
皇風矣求其實用則鉛刀木刄剸
割何施毋乃與
詔旨背乎多士於此可以深長思
矣是舉也提督軍務兵部右
侍郎兼右僉都御史徐栻節
punctuated:
之爲《六經》，誦而習之爲學術，體而行之天下國家爲實用。是故以之任事而事理矣，以之服官而官飭矣，以之肩重致遠，無往而弗濟矣。洋洋聖謨，斯其無負矣哉！如徒以其炳炳烺烺之文，聞風而興，俄頃而化，曰：「我能涵濡帝澤，鬯被皇風矣。」求其實用，則鉛刀木刄，剸割何施？毋乃與詔旨背乎？多士於此，可以深長思矣。

是舉也，提督軍務兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史徐栻，節
translation_en:
… down and transmitted, it is the Six Classics; recited and practiced, it is scholarly learning; embodied and carried out across the empire and the state, it is practical utility. Therefore, when one employs it to take charge of affairs, those affairs are put in order; when one employs it to serve in office, one's official duties are kept disciplined; when one employs it to shoulder heavy burdens and go far, there is nowhere one goes without succeeding. Vast and majestic are the Sacred Counsels—thus indeed shall one not fail to live up to them! If, however, one relies merely on resplendent and dazzling literary compositions, rising up upon hearing the trend and transforming in an instant, saying, "I have been able to steep myself in the Imperial grace and be thoroughly imbued with the August wind," yet when sought for practical utility, one is like a lead knife or a wooden blade—how can it be applied to cutting and slicing? Would this not run counter to the purport of the Imperial Edict? All you scholars may well ponder this deeply and at length.

In this undertaking, Superintendent of Military Affairs, Right Vice Minister of War, and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Xu Shi 徐栻, whose baton…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
鉞維新文武爲憲前巡撫右
副都御史今晉戶部右侍郎
謝鵬舉聲猷尚暨士習夙興
巡鹽監察御史王藻問俗貞
敎雅意作人若巡鹽監察御
史房如式被
命恪趨風聲先達以使事莅玆土
===
者則刑部郎中金應徵工部
主事馬鳴鑾南京戶部主事
鄧宗臣忽鳴皆樂觀
盛典者也其綜理於外則右布
政使張任右參政滕伯輪劉
翽左參議余一龍右參議王
嘉言副使徐雲程龔大器僉
punctuated: 鉞維新，文武爲憲；前巡撫、右副都御史今晉戶部右侍郎謝鵬舉，聲猷尚暨，士習夙興；巡鹽監察御史王藻，問俗貞敎，雅意作人。若巡鹽監察御史房如式，被命恪趨，風聲先達。以使事莅玆土者，則刑部郎中金應徵、工部主事馬鳴鑾、南京戶部主事鄧宗臣、忽鳴，皆樂觀盛典者也。其綜理於外，則右布政使張任，右參政滕伯輪、劉翽，左參議余一龍，右參議王嘉言，副使徐雲程、龔大器，僉
translation_en: …with his emblems of command newly assumed, stands as a model in both civil and military affairs. The former Grand Coordinator (Xunfu) and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, Xie Pengju 謝鵬舉, has a reputation and statesmanship that still reach here, having long inspired the ethos of the scholars. The Salt-Control Investigating Censor Wang Zao 王藻 inquires into local customs, rectifies instruction, and has earnestly set his mind on cultivating men of talent. As for the Salt-Control Investigating Censor Fang Rushi 房如式, having received his commission, he is hastening here with reverence, his inspiring reputation already preceding him. As for those visiting this region on official missions—Director of a Bureau in the Ministry of Justice Jin Yingzheng 金應徵, Secretary in the Ministry of Works Ma Mingluan 馬鳴鑾, and Secretaries in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue Deng Zongchen 鄧宗臣 and Hu Ming 忽鳴—all took pleasure in witnessing this grand ceremony. As for those managing affairs on the outside, there were Right Administration Commissioner Zhang Ren 張任, Right Administration Vice Commissioners Teng Bolun 滕伯輪 and Liu Hui 劉翽, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Yu Yilong 余一龍, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Wang Jiayan 王嘉言, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Xu Yuncheng 徐雲程 and Gong Daqi 龔大器, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事王君賞張子仁而署都指
揮僉事葉歡亦與有防範之
勞焉若右叅政張國彦僉事
黃家棟署都指揮僉事韓沛
則以入
賀行署都指揮楊照則以遷秩
行皆始事有勞法當備書者
===
也
山東濟南府歷城縣儒學敎
諭吳伯誠謹序
punctuated:
事王君賞、張子仁，而署都指揮僉事葉歡亦與有防範之勞焉。若右叅政張國彦、僉事黃家棟、署都指揮僉事韓沛，則以入賀行；署都指揮楊照，則以遷秩行，皆始事有勞，法當備書者也。
山東濟南府歷城縣儒學敎諭吳伯誠謹序。
translation_en:
… Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Wang Junshang 王君賞 and Zhang Ziren 張子仁; and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Ye Huan 葉歡 also shared in the labor of taking security precautions. As for Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Guoyan 張國彦, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Huang Jiadong 黃家棟, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Han Pei 韓沛, they departed to go to court to offer congratulations; and Acting Regional Military Commissioner Yang Zhao 楊照 departed upon being promoted to a new post. All of them contributed their labor at the outset of the affair and by rule ought to be recorded in full.
Respectfully prefaced by Wu Bocheng 吳伯誠, Instructor in the Confucian School of Licheng County 歷城縣, Jinan Prefecture 濟南府, Shandong 山東.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
此謂脩身在正其心
子曰吾十有五而志于學
尊賢使能俊傑在位則天下之士皆悅而
願立於其朝矣市廛而不征法而不廛
則天下之商皆悅而願藏於其市矣關
譏而不征則天下之旅皆悅而願出於
其路矣耕者助而不稅則天下之農皆
===
悅而願耕於其野矣廛無夫里之布則
天下之民皆悅而願爲之氓矣
易
彖曰大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天雲行雨
施品物流形大明終始六位時成時乘
六龍以御天乾道變化各正性命保合
大和乃利貞首出庶物萬國咸寧象曰
天行健君子以自彊不息
君子之光其暉吉也
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

此謂脩身在正其心。
子曰：「吾十有五而志于學。」
尊賢使能，俊傑在位，則天下之士皆悅而願立於其朝矣；市，廛而不征，法而不廛，則天下之商皆悅而願藏於其市矣；關，譏而不征，則天下之旅皆悅而願出於其路矣；耕者，助而不稅，則天下之農皆悅而願耕於其野矣；廛，無夫里之布，則天下之民皆悅而願爲之氓矣。

易

彖曰：大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。雲行雨施，品物流形。大明終始，六位時成，時乘六龍以御天。乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。首出庶物，萬國咸寧。象曰：天行健，君子以自彊不息。
君子之光，其暉吉也。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"This is what is meant by: 'The cultivation of the person depends on rectifying the mind.'" [Great Learning]

"The Master said: 'At fifteen, I set my heart on learning.'" [Analects]

"If a ruler honors the worthy and employs the capable, so that men of outstanding talent are in office, then all the scholars of the world will be pleased and wish to stand in his court. In the marketplaces, if he charges a stall-rent without taxing the goods, or enforces the regulations without charging a stall-rent, then all the merchants of the world will be pleased and wish to store their goods in his marketplaces. At the border passes, if there is inspection without levying customs duties, then all the travelers of the world will be pleased and wish to travel on his roads. As for the tillers of the soil, if they are required to give mutual aid on the public fields without paying a land tax on their private fields, then all the farmers of the world will be pleased and wish to till his fields. As for the dwellings, if there is neither the fine on the unindustrious nor the levy of residential cloth, then all the people of the world will be pleased and wish to become his subjects." [Mencius]

Book of Changes (Yi)

"The Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) says: Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! All things owe their beginning to it, and thus it governs heaven. The clouds move and the rain falls, and the various things flow into their forms. Greatly luminous from end to beginning, the six positions are completed in their due time, and in due time one mounts the six dragons to drive across heaven. The way of Qian works through change and transformation, so that each thing obtains its proper nature and destiny, preserving and uniting the great harmony: thus it is advantageous and firm. It rises first above the multitude of things, and the myriad states all enjoy peace. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: The movement of heaven is full of power; thus the superior man makes himself strong and untiring."

"The light of the superior man—its radiance brings good fortune."

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
形而上者謂之道
復德之本也恒德之固也
書
帝曰咨四岳有能典朕三禮僉曰伯夷帝
曰俞咨伯汝作秩宗夙夜惟寅直哉惟
清伯拜稽首讓于夔龍帝曰俞往欽哉
帝曰夔命汝典樂教胄子直而温寛而
栗剛而無虐簡而無傲詩言志歌永言
聲依永律和聲八音克諧無相奪倫神
===
人以和
沿于江海達于淮泗
無偏無黨王道蕩蕩無黨無偏王道平平
君子所其無逸先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則
知小人之依
詩
六月食鬱及薁七月亨葵及菽八月剝棗
十月穫稻爲此春酒以介眉壽七月食
瓜八月斷壺九月叔苴采荼薪樗食我
punctuated:
形而上者謂之道。
復，德之本也；恒，德之固也。
《書》
帝曰：「咨！四岳，有能典朕三禮？」僉曰：「伯夷。」帝曰：「俞。咨！伯，汝作秩宗。夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。」伯拜稽首，讓于夔、龍。帝曰：「俞，往，欽哉！」帝曰：「夔，命汝典樂，教胄子。直而温，寛而栗，剛而無虐，簡而無傲。詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲。八音克諧，無相奪倫，神人以和。」
沿于江、海，達于淮、泗。
無偏無黨，王道蕩蕩；無黨無偏，王道平平。
君子所其無逸。先知稼穡之艱難，乃逸，則知小人之依。
《詩》
六月食鬱及薁，七月亨葵及菽，八月剝棗，十月穫稻，爲此春酒，以介眉壽。七月食瓜，八月斷壺，九月叔苴，采荼薪樗，食我…
translation_en:
“What is above form is called the Way.”

“Return is the root of virtue; Constancy is the firmness of virtue.”

Book of Documents (Shu)

“The Emperor said, ‘Ah! Chief of the Four Mountains, is there anyone who can direct my three categories of rites?’ All said, ‘Boyi.’ The Emperor said, ‘Yes. Ah! Bo, you shall be Director of Sacrificial Worship. Morning and night be reverent; be upright and be pure.’ Bo bowed and touched his head to the ground, yielding in favor of Kui and Long. The Emperor said, ‘Yes, go and be reverent!’ The Emperor said, ‘Kui, I command you to be Director of Music, to teach the heirs of the nobility: to be upright yet mild, magnanimous yet firm, strong yet not tyrannical, simple yet not arrogant. Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs the words; notes depend on the prolongation; pitch-pipes harmonize the notes. When the eight timbres can be brought into harmony and do not encroach upon one another’s order, spirits and men will thereby be brought into harmony.’”

“Following along the Yangtze and the sea, it reached the Huai and Si rivers.”

“Without deflection, without partiality, the Kingly Way is broad and wide; without partiality, without deflection, the Kingly Way is level and easy.”

“The noble man makes taking no ease his dwelling place. When one first knows the hardships of sowing and reaping, and only then takes ease, one will know that on which the common people depend.”

Book of Odes (Shi)

“In the sixth month they eat wild plums and wild grapes; in the seventh month they boil mallows and beans; in the eighth month they knock down dates; in the tenth month they harvest rice, to make this spring wine, to pray for longevity with bushy eyebrows. In the seventh month they eat melons; in the eighth month they cut down bottle-gourds; in the ninth month they gather hemp-seed; they pluck bitter herbs and cut ailanthus for firewood, to feed our…”

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
農夫九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重
穋禾麻菽麥嗟我農夫我稼旣同上入
執宮功晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋
其始播百穀二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日
納于凌陰四之日其蚤獻羔祭韭九月
肅霜十月滌場朋酒斯饗曰殺羔羊躋
彼公堂稱彼兕觥萬壽無疆
文王初載天作之合
百辟卿士媚于天子不解于位民之攸墍
===
帝命式于九圍
春秋
夏六月公會齊侯宋公陳侯鄭伯同盟于
幽〔莊公二十有七年〕齊人救邢〔閔公元〕
〔年〕遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕秋七月公會齊侯
宋公陳世子款鄭世子華盟于甯母〔僖〕
〔公七年〕
公會齊侯于城濮〔莊公二十有七年〕春王
三月甲寅齊人伐衞〔莊公二十有八年〕
punctuated:
農夫。九月築場圃，十月納禾稼，黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫，我稼旣同，上入執宮功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯，亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。二之日鑿冰冲冲，三之日納于凌陰，四之日其蚤，獻羔祭韭。九月肅霜，十月滌場，朋酒斯饗，曰殺羔羊，躋彼公堂，稱彼兕觥，萬壽無疆。
文王初載，天作之合。
百辟卿士，媚于天子，不解于位，民之攸墍。
帝命式于九圍。
《春秋》
夏六月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、鄭伯同盟于幽〔莊公二十有七年〕；齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕；遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕；秋七月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳世子款、鄭世子華盟于甯母〔僖公七年〕。
公會齊侯于城濮〔莊公二十有七年〕；春王三月甲寅，齊人伐衞〔莊公二十有八年〕；
translation_en:
… the husbandmen. In the ninth month, they prepare the vegetable gardens for their stacks; in the tenth month, they convey the sheaves to them: the millets, both the early-sown and the late, along with other grain, hemp, pulse, and wheat. "O my husbandmen, our harvest is all collected; let us go up to the town and attend to the work of our houses. In the day-time collect the grass, and at night twist it into ropes; then get up quickly on the roofs—for we shall soon have to begin sowing the hundred grains again." In the days of the second month, they hew out the ice with harmonious blows; in the days of the third month, they convey it to the ice-houses; in the days of the fourth month, early in the morning, they offer a lamb in sacrifice with scallions. In the ninth month, it is cold, with frost; in the tenth month, they sweep clean their stack-grounds. With two bottles of wine they hold the feast, and say, "Let us kill our lambs and sheep, and go up to the hall of our prince; let us raise the cup of rhinoceros horn, and wish him myriad years of life without end!"

In the early years of King Wen, Heaven made for him a mate.

The hundred lords and high ministers bear love to the Son of Heaven; never remiss in their offices, through them the people find rest.

God on High ordained him to be a model to the nine regions.

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

In summer, in the sixth month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, and together made a covenant at You [twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhuang]; the men of Qi relieved Xing [first year of Duke Min]; and thereupon they invaded Chu [fourth year of Duke Xi]; in autumn, in the seventh month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, Heir Apparent Kuan of Chen, and Heir Apparent Hua of Zheng, and made a covenant at Ningmu [seventh year of Duke Xi].

The Duke met with the Marquis of Qi at Chengpu [twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhuang]; in spring, in the King's third month, on the day jiayin, the men of Qi invaded Wei [twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang]; …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
楚屈完來盟于師僖公四年秋七月齊侯
使國佐如師成公二年
晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞昭公十有五年
禮記
是故昔先王尚有德尊有道任有能舉賢
而置之聚衆而誓之是故因天事天因
地事地因名山升中于天因吉土以饗
帝于郊升中于天而鳳皇降龜龍假饗
帝于郊而風雨節寒暑時是故聖人南
===
面而立而天下大治
縮酌用茅明酌也醆酒涗于清汁獻涗于
醆酒
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣
其在朝廷則道仁聖禮義之序燕處則聽
雅頌之音行步則有環佩之聲升車則
有鸞和之音居處有禮進退有度百官
得其宜萬事得其序
第貳場
punctuated:
楚屈完來盟于師，僖公四年；秋，七月，齊侯使國佐如師，成公二年。
晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞，昭公十有五年。

禮記
是故昔先王尚有德，尊有道，任有能，舉賢而置之，聚衆而誓之。是故因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中于天，因吉土以饗帝于郊。升中于天而鳳皇降，龜龍假；饗帝于郊而風雨節，寒暑時。是故聖人南面而立，而天下大治。
縮酌用茅，明酌也；醆酒涗于清，汁獻涗于醆酒。
朝覲，然後諸侯知所以臣。
其在朝廷，則道仁聖禮義之序；燕處，則聽雅頌之音；行步，則有環佩之聲；升車，則有鸞和之音。居處有禮，進退有度，百官得其宜，萬事得其序。

第貳場
translation_en:
…"Qu Wan 屈完 of Chu 楚 came and made a covenant with the army" (4th year of Duke Xi 僖公); "In autumn, in the seventh month, the Marquis of Qi 齊侯 sent Guo Zuo 國佐 to the army" (2nd year of Duke Cheng 成公).
"Xun Wu 荀吳 of Jin 晉 led a force and attacked Xianyu 鮮虞" (15th year of Duke Zhao 昭公).

Book of Rites (Liji 禮記)
"Therefore, in antiquity the former kings esteemed those who had virtue, honored those who possessed the Way, employed those who had ability, promoted the worthy and placed them in office, and gathered the multitude and bound them with solemn oaths. Therefore, taking advantage of the nature of Heaven, they served Heaven; taking advantage of the nature of Earth, they served Earth; by means of famous mountains, they caused the record of peaceful achievement to ascend to Heaven; by means of auspicious ground, they offered sacrificial feasts to the Supreme Ancestor in the suburban sacrifice. When the record of peaceful achievement ascended to Heaven, phoenixes descended and tortoises and dragons arrived; when sacrificial feasts were offered to the Supreme Ancestor in the suburban sacrifice, wind and rain were seasonable, and cold and heat came at their proper times. Therefore, the sage stood facing south, and all under Heaven was in great order."
"Straining the wine for libation through cogon grass is with the clear water; the unstrained wine (zhanjiu 醆酒) is strained by adding clear wine, and the spiced juice offering (zhixian 汁獻) is strained by adding unstrained wine."
"Through the spring and autumn audiences at court, the feudal lords knew how to act as subjects."
"When he is at court, the proper order of benevolence, sageliness, ritual propriety, and righteousness is spoken of; when he is at leisure in retirement, he listens to the music of the Odes (Ya 雅) and Hymns (Song 頌); when he walks, there is the sound of his girdle pendants; when he mounts his carriage, there is the music of the luan 鸞 and he 和 bells. In his daily life there is ritual propriety; in his advancing and retiring there is due measure; the hundred officials obtain their proper places, and the myriad affairs obtain their proper order."

Second Session (第貳場)

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
論
人主當防未萌之欲
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢申明車服制度詔〔永平十三年〕
擬唐以張說兼集賢院學士誥〔開元十六年〕
擬宋御製爲君難爲臣不易論示輔臣謝
表〔祥符五年〕
判語〔五條〕
===
照刷文卷
欺隱田糧
服舍違式
驛使稽程
私鑄銅錢
第叄場
第五道
問夫自黃虞姬炎而下賢聖之君代作罔
弗欽禋蒼昊崇表素王肆類柴望之典
punctuated:
論：
「人主當防未萌之欲。」

詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕：
擬漢申明車服制度詔〔永平十三年〕；
擬唐以張說兼集賢院學士誥〔開元十六年〕；
擬宋御製《爲君難爲臣不易論》示輔臣謝表〔祥符五年〕。

照刷文卷；
欺隱田糧；
服舍違式；
驛使稽程；
私鑄銅錢。

第叄場

第五道：
問：夫自黃、虞、姬、炎而下，賢聖之君代作，罔弗欽禋蒼昊，崇表素王。肆類柴望之典，
translation_en:
Discourse:
"A ruler must guard against desires before they sprout."

Edict, Mandate, and Memorial (candidates answer one):
Imitation of a Han edict reiterating the regulations on carriages and vestments (13th year of Yongping [70 CE]).
Imitation of a Tang mandate appointing Zhang Yue 張說 concurrently as Academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies (16th year of Kaiyuan [728 CE]).
Imitation of a Song memorial of gratitude upon the Emperor showing his ministers of state the imperial composition "Discourse on the Difficulty of Being a Ruler and the Uneasiness of Being a Subject" (5th year of Xiangfu [1012 CE]).

Legal Judgments (five items):
Auditing official documents;
Fraudulently concealing taxable land and grain;
Violating regulations on dress and dwellings;
Postal couriers delaying beyond the scheduled time;
Privately casting copper coins.

Third Session

Five Policy Questions [? 第五道, lit. "Fifth Question", error for 策五道]:
Question: From the Yellow Emperor, Yu [Shun], Ji [Zhou], and Yan [Han] onward, worthy and sage rulers have arisen in succession, and none failed to reverently sacrifice to vast Heaven and to honor and exalt the Uncrowned King [Confucius]. The canons of thelei sacrifice, burnt offerings, and sacrifices to distant mountains and rivers,…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
明堂辟雍之建詩書所稱曷以加巳其
儀度品式可傳而數歟厥所以凝帝祉
而章儒化者應效亦有聞歟若分祀合
祀配天配帝義各有指歟而三歲一郊
毋迺疏歟釋奠養老頒樂舞簡不率事
各有屬歟而帝入四學毋迺繁歟我
太祖奄有區夏首建南北
郊壇分祀
天地而繼復合祀斷自
===
宸衷抑有所本歟肇脩人紀創行太學釋奠再
舉
臨幸而
列聖初服率一
親御果為定制歟逮我
世宗神聖追媲
太祖
郊祀
視學纘𢘆紹勤而南北郊分建之議其有据周
punctuated: 明堂、辟雍之建，《詩》、《書》所稱，曷以加巳！其儀度品式可傳而數歟？厥所以凝帝祉而章儒化者，應效亦有聞歟？若分祀、合祀，配天、配帝，義各有指歟？而三歲一郊，毋迺疏歟？釋奠、養老，頒樂舞、簡不率，事各有屬歟？而帝入四學，毋迺繁歟？我太祖奄有區夏，首建南北郊壇，分祀天地，而繼復合祀，斷自宸衷，抑有所本歟？肇脩人紀，創行太學釋奠，再舉臨幸，而列聖初服，率一親御，果為定制歟？逮我世宗，神聖追媲太祖，郊祀、視學，纘𢘆紹勤，而南北郊分建之議，其有据《周…
translation_en:
…and the establishment of the Hall of Light (Mingtang) and the Circular Moat Academy (Biyong)—how could anything surpass what is praised in the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu)! Can their ceremonial regulations and institutional forms be recounted and enumerated? Have we also heard of the resulting efficacy by which they consolidated blessings from the Supreme Lord and manifested Confucian transformation? As for separate sacrifices versus combined sacrifices, and associating ancestors with Heaven versus associating them with the Lord on High, does the meaning of each have its own specific reference? And is performing the suburban sacrifice once every three years not rather infrequent? As for the libation ritual (shidian) and the nourishing of the aged, or the bestowal of music and dances and the weeding out of the disobedient, does each affair have its proper category? And is the ruler's entering the Four Schools not rather overly frequent?

When Our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) came to possess all within the Chinese realm, he first established the northern and southern suburban altars to sacrifice separately to Heaven and Earth, and subsequently combined the sacrifices again; was this decided solely from the imperial heart, or did it have a textual basis? In first rectifying human relationships, he initiated the libation ritual at the National University and twice conducted imperial visits in person; yet when the successive sacred emperors first assumed the throne, they generally attended in person once—did this indeed become the fixed institution? Coming down to Our Emperor Shizong, whose divine sageliness rivaled that of the Grand Progenitor, in the suburban sacrifices and imperial inspections of the National University he continued the constancy and inherited the diligence; as for the deliberations on separately establishing the northern and southern suburban altars, was this based on the Rites of Zhou (Zhou…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
禮歟正
先師孔子之位果度越千古歟
皇上嗣臨丕基
郊祀則積誠致潔
視學則弁服賜講暨於
二聖鴻庥駿儀有符合歟亦可揚其盛歟然而
合祀所以尊
天養老所以教孝兩者討述而著令焉尤不能
無竢於
===
===
聖天子議禮也諸士其鋪張揚搉之以賛
盛典毋讓
問自昔英辟碩輔所以昌化翊烈者孰不
以率綜吏理為首務哉虞周穆灝欽亮
董訓楙景靡尚已嗣玆敏睿端扆壹以
振核程工而御座書刺史之名縣令試
理人之論毋迺煩黷過歟孝宣之優孝
文也何繇而又謂孝文非以寛致平抑
有說歟洪惟我
punctuated:
禮歟？正先師孔子之位，果度越千古歟？皇上嗣臨丕基，郊祀則積誠致潔，視學則弁服賜講，暨於二聖鴻庥駿儀，有符合歟？亦可揚其盛歟？然而合祀所以尊天，養老所以教孝，兩者討述而著令焉，尤不能無竢於聖天子議禮也。諸士其鋪張揚搉之，以賛盛典，毋讓。

問：自昔英辟碩輔，所以昌化翊烈者，孰不以率綜吏理為首務哉？虞、周穆灝，欽亮董訓，楙景靡尚已。嗣玆敏睿端扆，壹以振核程工，而御座書刺史之名，縣令試理人之論，毋迺煩黷過歟？孝宣之優孝文也何繇？而又謂孝文非以寛致平，抑有說歟？洪惟我
translation_en:
… the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli)? Did rectifying the ritual status of the Former Teacher Confucius truly surpass all antiquity?

Now that His Majesty has succeeded to the great foundation, in the Suburban Sacrifices he accumulates sincerity and achieves purity, and in inspecting the Imperial Academy he dons the ceremonial cap and robes and bestows lectures. Does this not accord with the vast blessings and grand ceremonies of the Two Sages [Taizu and Shizong]? Can we not also extol its magnificence? Yet joint sacrifice is the means to venerate Heaven, and nourishing the aged is the means to teach filial piety; to investigate and expound upon both of these and establish them as ordinances is something for which we cannot but await the sacred Son of Heaven's deliberation on the rites. Let you gentlemen set this forth in full and discuss it thoroughly to assist in the grand canons; do not decline to speak.

Question: Since antiquity, among heroic sovereigns and great ministers, in the means by which they made governance flourish and assisted in illustrious achievements, who did not take leading and synthesizing the administration of officials as their foremost task? The eras of Yu [Shun] and Zhou were reverent and vast; with respectful亮 [trust/assistance] and supervision of instruction, their flourishing brilliance could not be surpassed. Thereafter, perspicacious and wise rulers stood before the throne screen, exclusivelyrousing and verifying to measure performance; yet writing the names of Regional Inspectors (cishi) on the imperial throne screen, or testing District Magistrates (xianling) with essays on governing the people—was this not overly troublesome and meddlesome? On what grounds was Emperor Xiaoxuan [of Han] considered superior to Emperor Xiaowen? And as for the claim that Emperor Xiaowen did not achieve peace through leniency, is there an explanation for this? Looking upon our great…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
二祖稽制
列聖繩軌有司百執事條式舉課令森且飭凡
以惠賜元元登理爾厥載
會典可槩陳歟維時吏奉職符泰階也亦可
揚其盛歟我
皇上勵精法
祖脩明典常
申敕羣工罔弗嚮卽有僚廩廩承
休德巳顧宇内治猶鮮效省方之使奏計之吏
===
所以課功實而稽殿最者猶皇皇焉未
足盡稱
主上意也毋廼吏猶競名襲奇鮮實政歟闒茸
叨憤在位未盡殄歟將采名拘文法溷
碔璧而士鮮奮歟然則漢制六條九年
之令唐人五術八計之議厥於我
祖宗法意有縣合者歟亦可於
今日彷行否歟夫吏不奉詔書有責上計簿
徒具文有責而條奏故事最稱上意在
punctuated: 二祖稽制，列聖繩軌，有司百執事條式舉課，令森且飭，凡以惠賜元元登理爾。厥載《會典》，可槩陳歟？維時吏奉職符泰階也，亦可揚其盛歟？我皇上勵精法祖，脩明典常，申敕羣工，罔弗嚮卽，有僚廩廩承休德巳。顧宇内治猶鮮效，省方之使、奏計之吏，所以課功實而稽殿最者，猶皇皇焉未足盡稱主上意也。毋廼吏猶競名襲奇，鮮實政歟？闒茸叨憤在位，未盡殄歟？將采名拘文法，溷碔璧而士鮮奮歟？然則漢制六條、九年之令，唐人五術、八計之議，厥於我祖宗法意有縣合者歟？亦可於今日彷行否歟？夫吏不奉詔書有責，上計簿徒具文有責，而條奏故事最稱上意，在
translation_en:
… Two Progenitors established the institutions and the successive Sacred Emperors maintained the standards, the regulations and evaluations for the authorities and the hundred functionaries were made strict and orderly—all simply in order to bestow blessings upon the common people and achieve good governance. As these are recorded in the Collected Statutes (Huidian), can you give a general account of them? At that time, officials fulfilled their duties in harmony with an era of great peace; can you also extol that flourishing state?

Our reigning Sovereign devotes himself to emulating the Ancestors, clarifies and renews the constant statutes, and repeatedly admonishes all officials. None fail to turn toward and rally to him, and the bureaucrats reverently uphold his illustrious virtue. Yet within the empire, governance still shows little efficacy. The envoys who inspect the regions and the officials who submit accounting reports—those through whom actual achievements are evaluated and the lowest and highest ratings are verified—are still anxious and hurried, unable to fully satisfy the Sovereign's intentions. Could it be that officials still compete for reputation and copy novelties, with little substantive administration? Have the mediocre, greedy, and muddled [?] in office not been completely eradicated? Or does the selection by reputation and adherence to the letter of the law confound worthless stones with jade, so that scholars are rarely roused to effort? If so, do the Han regulations of the Six Articles and the nine-year ordinances, or the Tang discussions of the Five Methods and the Eight Criteria for Evaluation, correspond across the ages with the legislative intent of our Imperial Ancestors? And can they be imitated and put into practice today, or not? Now, there were reprimands for officials who did not uphold imperial edicts, reprimands for submitting accounting registers that were mere formalities, and itemized memorials on precedent that best matched the Emperor's intentions—in…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
今日咸起敝維風之所願聞者試颺言之以
商
太平之略
問學術逸軌則道統蝕異端說昌則正學
裂異端之害莫甚二氏當孔子時佛教
未興而老聃氏實與接轂孔子不爲非
且就而問禮焉三千之徒何不聞有惑
其說者歟楊氏出於老墨氏近於佛乃
孟軻氏則肆辯而力排之至指數爲無
===
父無君充塞仁義若將迸殛之佴罔逃
臯抑何嚴歟夫老佛楊墨畔我正道章
章較著乃吾黨又有謂似是之非者有
謂彌近理而大亂眞者旣曰似矣何以
言非旣曰近矣何以言亂此必有說矣
我
國家崇儒重道異類屏息而都人士亦率羹
墻唐虞歩趨孔孟陳仁義之弘謨談性
命之奧旨及叩其指歸尚不能窺異端
punctuated:
今日咸起敝維風之所願聞者，試颺言之，以商太平之略。

問：學術逸軌，則道統蝕；異端說昌，則正學裂。異端之害，莫甚二氏。當孔子時，佛教未興，而老聃氏實與接轂，孔子不爲非，且就而問禮焉。三千之徒，何不聞有惑其說者歟？楊氏出於老，墨氏近於佛，乃孟軻氏則肆辯而力排之，至指數爲無父無君，充塞仁義，若將迸殛之，佴罔逃臯，抑何嚴歟？夫老、佛、楊、墨，畔我正道，章章較著。乃吾黨又有謂「似是之非」者，有謂「彌近理而大亂眞」者。旣曰「似」矣，何以言「非」？旣曰「近」矣，何以言「亂」？此必有說矣。我國家崇儒重道，異類屏息，而都人士亦率羹墻唐、虞，歩趨孔、孟，陳仁義之弘謨，談性命之奧旨，及叩其指歸，尚不能窺異端…
translation_en:
…are today all matters that those wishing to remedy abuses and uphold customs desire to hear about. Try to set them forth clearly, so that we may deliberate upon the grand strategy for Great Peace.

Question: When scholarly learning strays from the proper track, the transmission of the Way is eroded; when heterodox doctrines flourish, orthodox learning is rent apart. Among the harms of heterodoxy, none are worse than the Two Teachings [Daoism and Buddhism]. In the time of Confucius, Buddhism had not yet arisen, whereas Lao Dan [Laozi] actually lived side by side with him. Confucius did not condemn him; on the contrary, he went to him to inquire about ritual. Why is it that among his three thousand disciples, none were ever heard to have been deluded by Laozi's doctrines? Yang Zhu derived from Laozi, and Mo Di was close to Buddhism; yet Meng Ke [Mencius] argued at length and vigorously refuted them, going so far as to denounce them by name as recognizing neither father nor ruler and as blocking up benevolence and righteousness—as though he were about to banish and execute them so that they could not escape their crime [?]. Why was he so severe? Now, that Laozi, the Buddha, Yang Zhu, and Mo Di rebel against our orthodox Way is crystal clear. Yet among our own ranks there are those who speak of "what seems right but is wrong," and those who speak of doctrines that "come ever closer to principle and yet greatly confound the truth." Since they are called "seeming," why are they called "wrong"? Since they are called "close," why are they called "confounding"? There must be an explanation for this. Our dynasty reveres Confucianism and honors the Way, so that heterodox sorts hold their breath in submission; meanwhile, scholars and gentlemen everywhere generally yearn constantly for the ages of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], follow in the footsteps of Confucius and Mencius, set forth the grand plans of benevolence and righteousness, and discourse upon the profound import of human nature and destiny. Yet when one probes their ultimate purport, they cannot even peer over the outer hedge of heterodoxy…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之藩籬甚者包藏詐譎厚裒朋援立標
幟設門竇以獵取聲譽爲世大蠹然則
道之不明也老佛之害歟楊墨之害歟
夫老佛之徒雖離宗貫尚能堅信其師
說而不變乃吾孔孟之徒外雖誦習其
言而中自矛盾跋疐者將誰與闢歟昔
孟子欲正人心而曰息邪說距詖行今
之所當息而距者安在諸士辨業景聖
將慨然有决鵠坊潰之思者其詳著於
===
篇以爲世教助
問記言廣谷大川異制民生其間異俗蓋
俗尚之殊自古記之矣乃曰上化下謂
之風下從上謂之俗則風習之異亦係
於所化然耶浙省扆山襟海應潮分東
西其名郡象邑星列棊布蓋文獻奧區
已迺其俗尚有迥然不侔者何耶說者
謂杭處會省籍先朝繁華又車舟輻輳
民樂商趨業然好蕩而習靡嘉湖澤洰
punctuated:
之藩籬。甚者包藏詐譎，厚裒朋援，立標幟，設門竇，以獵取聲譽，爲世大蠹。然則道之不明也，老佛之害歟？楊墨之害歟？夫老佛之徒雖離宗貫，尚能堅信其師說而不變；乃吾孔孟之徒，外雖誦習其言，而中自矛盾跋疐者，將誰與闢歟？昔孟子欲正人心，而曰：「息邪說，距詖行。」今之所當息而距者安在？諸士辨業景聖，將慨然有决鵠坊潰之思者，其詳著於篇，以爲世教助。

問：《記》言「廣谷大川異制，民生其間異俗」，蓋俗尚之殊，自古記之矣。乃曰：「上化下謂之風，下從上謂之俗。」則風習之異，亦係於所化然耶？浙省扆山襟海，應潮分東西，其名郡象邑星列棊布，蓋文獻奧區已。迺其俗尚有迥然不侔者，何耶？說者謂杭處會省，籍先朝繁華，又車舟輻輳，民樂商趨業，然好蕩而習靡；嘉湖澤洰
translation_en:
… boundaries [of heterodox teachings]. Worse still, some harbor deceit and cunning, amass wide cliques of partisans, set up banners, and establish factional gateways in order to hunt for fame and reputation, becoming great parasites upon the world. If that is so, when the Way is not made clear, is it the harm caused by Laozi and the Buddha? Or is it the harm caused by Yang Zhu and Mo Di? Now, although the followers of Laozi and the Buddha have departed from the fundamental thread of truth, they are still able to firmly believe in their masters' doctrines without wavering; yet when our own followers of Confucius and Mencius outwardly recite and study their words while inwardly contradicting and stumbling over themselves, with whom shall we refute [heterodoxy]? In the past, Mencius wished to rectify men's hearts and said, "Put an end to perverse doctrines and oppose one-sided actions." Where do the things that ought to be ended and opposed today lie? You gentlemen, who discern your studies and revere the sages, and who are filled with the resolute aspiration to hit the bullseye and dike the breached torrent, set forth your views in detail in your essays as an aid to the moral instruction of the age.

Question: The Record of Rites (Liji) states: "Broad valleys and great rivers have different formations, and the people born between them have different customs." Indeed, differences in customs and preferences have been recorded since antiquity. Yet it is also said: "When superiors transform inferiors, it is called 'wind' [moral influence]; when inferiors follow superiors, it is called 'custom.'" Does the difference in customs and habits, then, also depend upon how they are transformed? Zhejiang province backs against the mountains and embraces the sea, divided into East and West according to the tides. Its famed prefectures and prominent districts are arrayed like stars and spread out like pieces on a chessboard; it is truly a profound heartland of culture and learning. Why is it, then, that their customs and preferences are so vastly dissimilar from one another? Commentators say that Hangzhou (Hang) is situated at the provincial capital, inheriting the splendor of former dynasties, and is moreover a hub where carriages and boats converge; its people delight in commerce and flock to trade as their livelihood, yet they are fond of dissipation and accustomed to extravagance. Jiaxing (Jia) and Huzhou (Hu) are vast marshy …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之國殖餉所資民饒而喜事越以東民
嗇業尚虛江左之餘風在焉齒繁多慧
每射利四出而輕去其鄉婺衢上流諸
郡衣冠淳龐尚有先進之遺然往往訐
而好鬭勇而尚氣甌栝之俗亦號近古
雖兩地奢儉異齊而玩法逋賦則均其
俗尚之殊若此無亦自昔所遺耶夫習
俗移人流弊日趨議者謂獻疇靡費婚
娶傾貲服用太僭樗蒲競肆然歟否歟
===
===
又謂緇黃雜沓倡優駢聚豪强逞威遊
俠踰檢然歟否歟又謂南北選募人樂
從兵山海阻遙民多獷習抑何繇而致
是歟今欲刬削舊習與民維新一道德
以同風俗使奢者約薄者敦賈勇者知
輕生之戒逐利者更力本之圖其政令
當何為先其禁革當何最急轉移默奪
之機又果安在此諸生扼腕以談時事
所當急陳也願與商之
punctuated: 之國，殖餉所資，民饒而喜事；越以東，民嗇業，尚虛，江左之餘風在焉，齒繁多慧，每射利四出而輕去其鄉；婺、衢上流諸郡，衣冠淳龐，尚有先進之遺，然往往訐而好鬭，勇而尚氣；甌、栝之俗，亦號近古，雖兩地奢儉異齊，而玩法逋賦則均。其俗尚之殊若此，無亦自昔所遺耶？夫習俗移人，流弊日趨。議者謂獻疇靡費，婚娶傾貲，服用太僭，樗蒲競肆，然歟否歟？又謂緇黃雜沓，倡優駢聚，豪强逞威，遊俠踰檢，然歟否歟？又謂南北選募，人樂從兵，山海阻遙，民多獷習，抑何繇而致是歟？今欲刬削舊習，與民維新，一道德以同風俗，使奢者約，薄者敦，賈勇者知輕生之戒，逐利者更力本之圖，其政令當何為先？其禁革當何最急？轉移默奪之機又果安在？此諸生扼腕以談時事，所當急陳也，願與商之。
translation_en: …is a land of [waterways], upon which grain production and state revenue rely; its people are affluent and fond of meddling in affairs. East of Yue [Shaoxing], the people are frugal in their livelihoods and value empty show, where the lingering customs of Jiangzuo remain; the population is dense and full of cleverness, so they constantly go out in all directions in pursuit of profit and lightly leave their native places. In the upstream prefectures of Wu [Jinhua] and Qu [Quzhou], the gentry are simple and honest, still retaining the legacy of Earlier Ages, yet the people often expose others' secrets and love to brawl, being fierce and prizing bravado. The customs of Ou [Wenzhou] and Gua [Chuzhou] are also said to be close to antiquity; although the two regions differ in their degree of extravagance and frugality, they are alike in flouting the law and evading taxes. That their customs and preferences differ like this—is it not also what has been handed down from the past? Now, habits and customs transform people, and ongoing abuses worsen day by day. Critics say that banquets and social exchanges are wasteful, marriages exhaust family fortunes, clothing and utensils are overly sumptuous and presumptuous, and gambling runs rampant—is this so or not? They also say that Buddhist monks and Daoist priests mingle in crowds, actors and entertainers gather in droves, local bullies flex their power, and wandering knights-errant transgress the bounds of propriety—is this so or not? They also say that in the selection and recruitment of troops for the north and south, people gladly join the military, and that because the mountains and seas are obstructed and remote, the people have many fierce and unruly habits—by what cause has it come to this? Today, if we wish to pare away old habits and renew ourselves along with the people, unifying morality so as to harmonize customs, making the extravagant frugal, the frivolous sincere, those who peddle their bravery aware of the warning against taking life lightly, and those who chase after profit turn instead to plans for working at the fundamental occupation [agriculture]—what should come first in our administrative orders? What is most urgent in our prohibitions and reforms? And where indeed lies the pivot for subtly shifting and imperceptibly transforming them? These are matters that you students, clasping your wrists in earnest discussion of current affairs, ought urgently to set forth; I wish to deliberate on them with you.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
問東南海內財貨之所總土沃物饒民衆
煩夥加以波濤之險舟楫之便故姦宄
萌生其間即吾浙省會之地防範捕詰
亦云人具而法申迺郊關暮夜則有剽
吏而奪之金者至厪
嚴旨督獲雖旋即逮繫然亦肆矣夫曩者醜夷
不靖師旅叢興憂在四境耳今稱乂安
矣而猶有此盜殆非盛世所宜見也豈
凋瘵未復而衣食闕歟抑導民之路失
===
===
歟古者太宰以九職任萬民大司馬以
九伐正邦國法至詳密後世無聞獨操
一切勝之故有以鉤鉅者有以投缿者
有以致羣偷者有以知主名者有以解
繩喻者有以設三科者有單車而下之
者非無聲施抑亦末矣昔人有言平盜
非難絕之爲難吾觀賈子瑰瑋之論亦
爲太息所以消姦萌而保大業者宜在
今日豈無其術歟幸商榷之以佐元元毋謂
punctuated: 問：東南海內財貨之所總，土沃物饒，民衆煩夥，加以波濤之險，舟楫之便，故姦宄萌生其間。即吾浙省會之地，防範捕詰，亦云人具而法申；迺郊關暮夜，則有剽吏而奪之金者，至厪嚴旨督獲，雖旋即逮繫，然亦肆矣。夫曩者醜夷不靖，師旅叢興，憂在四境耳；今稱乂安矣，而猶有此盜，殆非盛世所宜見也。豈凋瘵未復而衣食闕歟？抑導民之路失歟？古者太宰以九職任萬民，大司馬以九伐正邦國，法至詳密。後世無聞，獨操一切勝之：故有以鉤鉅者，有以投缿者，有以致羣偷者，有以知主名者，有以解繩喻者，有以設三科者，有單車而下之者，非無聲施，抑亦末矣。昔人有言：「平盜非難，絕之爲難。」吾觀賈子瑰瑋之論，亦爲太息。所以消姦萌而保大業者，宜在今日，豈無其術歟？幸商榷之，以佐元元，毋謂
translation_en:
Question: The Southeast is where the wealth and goods within the seas converge. Its soil is fertile, its products abundant, and its population dense and numerous. Added to this are the hazards of waves and billows and the convenience of boats and oars; hence evil-doers and traitors sprout up in its midst. Even here in our Zhejiang provincial capital, as for preventive measures, arrests, and interrogations, it may well be said that the personnel are complete and the laws clearly set forth; yet at dusk and night in the suburban passes, there were those who robbed officials and seized their gold, going so far as to cause anxiety in a stern imperial decree supervising their capture. Although they were soon arrested and bound, this is nonetheless brazen indeed! Now, in the past, when vile barbarians were unpacified and military forces repeatedly rose up, the worry lay only at the four borders. Today is acclaimed as a time of peace and order, and yet there are still such bandits; this is perilous close to something that ought not to be seen in a flourishing age. Could it be that exhaustion and distress have not yet been recovered from, so that clothing and food are lacking? Or has the path of guiding the people been lost?

In antiquity, the Grand Counselor (Taizai) employed the myriad people through the Nine Occupations, and the Minister of War (Da sima) rectified the states through the Nine Punitive Expeditions; the laws were detailed and thorough to the utmost. In later ages nothing of this was heard, and men merely wielded expedient measures to prevail over them. Thus there were those who used "hooks and barbs" (clever cross-examination), those who used "secret-ballot jars" (for anonymous denunciations), those who summoned the leaders of bands of thieves, those who knew the names of the ringleaders, those who used the analogy of untying a knotted rope, those who established three categories of amnesty, and those who brought bandits to submission from a single carriage. It is not that these lacked renown and achievement, yet they were merely dealing with the branches rather than the root! A man of the past had a saying: "Pacifying bandits is not difficult; eradicating them is what is difficult." When I examine the extraordinary discourses of Master Jia (Jia Yi 賈誼), I too heave a deep sigh over this. The means by which to eliminate the sprouts of wickedness and preserve the great enterprise ought to lie in the present day—how could there be no art for it? I hope you will deliberate upon this to assist the common people; do not say that…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
此謂脩身在正其心
朱用光
同考試官教諭田批脩身正心乃大學一篇要
領此作發明殆盡
同考試官教諭畢批講脩正多拘局上文惟此
獨得題㫖錄之
考試官教諭林批說理頗明
===
考試官教諭吳批順暢
傳者結言脩身之要善事其心而已蓋身統於
心者也心有所累而身因之謂脩身不在于正
心也哉今夫天下國家之本在身則身之不可
以不脩也固矣然經文必先之以正心也果何
謂哉蓋心所以主宰乎此身者也今觀喜怒憂
懼一累於私而視聽飲食遂失其則此之謂吾
身非外也而制外必始於養中此心非內也而
直內斯可以方外欲身之善其應事之則也而
punctuated:
第壹場。
四書。
「此謂脩身在正其心。」
朱用光。
同考試官教諭田批：脩身正心，乃《大學》一篇要領，此作發明殆盡。
同考試官教諭畢批：講脩正多拘局上文，惟此獨得題㫖，錄之。
考試官教諭林批：說理頗明。
考試官教諭吳批：順暢。
傳者結言脩身之要，善事其心而已。蓋身統於心者也。心有所累而身因之，謂脩身不在于正心也哉？今夫天下國家之本在身，則身之不可以不脩也固矣。然經文必先之以正心也，果何謂哉？蓋心所以主宰乎此身者也。今觀喜怒憂懼一累於私，而視聽飲食遂失其則。此之謂吾身非外也，而制外必始於養中；此心非內也，而直內斯可以方外。欲身之善其應事之則也，而
translation_en:
First Session.
Four Books.
"This is whyit is said that the cultivation of the person depends on rectifying the mind."
Zhu Yongguang 朱用光.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Tian 田: Cultivating the person and rectifying the mind are the essential points of the entire Great Learning (Daxue); this composition elucidates them almost completely.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Bi 畢: Discussions of cultivating and rectifying are mostly constrained by the preceding passage; only this piece grasps the true purport of the theme. Record it for publication.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Lin 林: The explanation of principle is quite clear.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Wu 吳: Smooth and fluent.
The commentator concludes by stating the essential point of cultivating the person: it is simply a matter of tending well to one's mind. For the body is governed by the mind. When the mind is encumbered by something, the body follows suit; could one then say that cultivating the person does not lie in rectifying the mind? Now, the root of the empire, the state, and the family lies in the person; that the person cannot go uncultivated is certain indeed. Yet why does the Classic text necessarily precede this with rectifying the mind? What does this truly mean? It is because the mind is that which acts as the master of this body. Now we observe that once fondness, anger, worry, or fear are encumbered by selfishness, looking, listening, eating, and drinking consequently lose their proper norms. What this means is not that our body is external, yet regulating the external must begin with nourishing the center; nor is it that this mind is internal, yet straightening the internal is how one can square the external. If one wishes the body to perfect the norms by which it responds to affairs, yet…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
心固事之綱維也于未事之先而懋夫操存之
力誠其所必有事焉者矣欲身之善其應物之
則也而心固物之權度也于無物之始而致夫
時保之功誠其所不容緩焉者矣存養夫至虛
之體俾將迎之私不得以擾之是非專事于心
也不如是吾懼心一馳焉而身將無所管攝也
然則經文語脩身而必在正心也非此之謂哉
省察夫至靈之用俾情欲之感不得以累之是
非徒存其心也不如是吾恐心一放焉而身將
===
無所檢束也然則經文以脩身而本之正心也
非此之謂哉誠能正心以脩身則齊治均平一
以貫之而大學之道無餘蘊矣雖然正心之功
密矣誠意之後非幾盡黜所未正者先事後事
之際耳正之云者豈有加於誠之之功哉操而
存之順天機自然之妙而不容以人力參焉未
應不先已應不後感而遂通可以言正亦可以
言脩矣噫此聖學也善學者思之
子曰吾十有五而志于學
punctuated:
心固事之綱維也，于未事之先，而懋夫操存之力，誠其所必有事焉者矣。欲身之善其應物之則也，而心固物之權度也，于無物之始，而致夫時保之功，誠其所不容緩焉者矣。存養夫至虛之體，俾將迎之私不得以擾之，是非專事于心也；不如是，吾懼心一馳焉，而身將無所管攝也。然則經文語脩身而必在正心也，非此之謂哉？省察夫至靈之用，俾情欲之感不得以累之，是非徒存其心也；不如是，吾恐心一放焉，而身將無所檢束也。然則經文以脩身而本之正心也，非此之謂哉？誠能正心以脩身，則齊、治、均、平一以貫之，而大學之道無餘蘊矣。雖然，正心之功密矣。誠意之後，非幾盡黜，所未正者，先事後事之際耳。正之云者，豈有加於誠之之功哉？操而存之，順天機自然之妙，而不容以人力參焉；未應不先，已應不後，感而遂通，可以言正，亦可以言脩矣。噫！此聖學也，善學者思之。

子曰：「吾十有五而志于學。」
translation_en:
… the mind is inherently the guiding thread of affairs; before any affair arises, to exert the strength of grasping and preserving it is truly what one must engage in. If one wishes the person to perfect its standard in responding to things, the mind is inherently the balance and measure of things; at the beginning before any thing is present, to carry out the effort of constant preservation is truly what admits of no delay. To preserve and nourish its supremely empty substance so that the selfishness of anticipation and lingering cannot disturb it—this is not merely attending exclusively to the mind; were it not so, I fear that once the mind gallops away, the person would have nothing to govern and hold it together. If so, when the Classic speaks of cultivating the person as necessarily lying in rectifying the mind, is this not what it means? To examine and reflect upon its supremely numinous function so that the stirrings of passions and desires cannot encumber it—this is not merely preserving the mind in vain; were it not so, I fear that once the mind is let loose, the person would have nothing to restrain and bind it. If so, when the Classic takes cultivating the person and roots it in rectifying the mind, is this not what it means? If one can truly rectify the mind in order to cultivate the person, then regulating the family, ordering the state, and bringing peace and equilibrium to the world are all penetrated by a single thread, and the Way of the Great Learning (Daxue) has no remaining secrets. Even so, the effort of rectifying the mind is subtle indeed. After making the intentions sincere, wrong incipient tendencies are completely dismissed; what remains unrectified is only the interval before and after affairs. Can what is called "rectifying it" add anything beyond the effort of "making it sincere"? To grasp and preserve it, following the natural wonder of the heavenly mechanism without allowing human artifice to interfere therein—neither anticipating before responding, nor lingering after responding, but when stimulated, immediately penetrating—this may be called rectified, and it may also be called cultivated. Alas! This is the learning of the sages; let those who are good at learning ponder it.

The Master said: "At fifteen, I set my heart upon learning."

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王建中
同考試官教諭陳批聖學成始成終不外此志
是作得之宜式
同考試官教諭黃批發志學在於及時尤得聖
人語意
考試官教諭林批親切有味
考試官教諭吳批平正
聖人自叙其始之所志作聖之功在是矣蓋學
以求至乎聖也始學而志于是焉謂非夫子聖
===
功之所在乎宜其自叙以勉人也若曰君子之
學有所以詣其極必有所以立其基我非生而
知之者也而其始之所從事何如哉蓋年至十
五成人之德雖未敢以自居聖脩之功則于是
乎託始意念之精專不眩於他岐必以大道爲
嚮往之歸精神之凝聚不安於小成務以至善
爲進脩之準方幸其時之旣至而又慮其或至
于易失也汲汲焉乗時以自勵而一心典學之
勤固有好古敏求而日與此學相爲周旋者矣
punctuated:
王建中
同考試官教諭陳批：聖學成始成終，不外此志。是作得之，宜式。
同考試官教諭黃批：發志學在於及時，尤得聖人語意。
考試官教諭林批：親切有味。
考試官教諭吳批：平正。
聖人自叙其始之所志，作聖之功在是矣。蓋學以求至乎聖也，始學而志于是焉，謂非夫子聖功之所在乎？宜其自叙以勉人也。若曰：君子之學，有所以詣其極，必有所以立其基。我非生而知之者也，而其始之所從事何如哉？蓋年至十五，成人之德雖未敢以自居，聖脩之功則于是乎託始。意念之精專，不眩於他岐，必以大道爲嚮往之歸；精神之凝聚，不安於小成，務以至善爲進脩之準。方幸其時之旣至，而又慮其或至于易失也，汲汲焉乗時以自勵，而一心典學之勤，固有好古敏求而日與此學相爲周旋者矣。
translation_en:
Wang Jianzhong 王建中

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Chen 陳 comments: "The learning of the sages, from beginning to end, is nothing other than this determination. This essay grasps it and is worthy to serve as a model."
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Huang 黃 comments: "By bringing out that setting one's heart on learning lies in seizing the proper time, he especially captures the meaning of the Sage's words."
Examiner and County Director of Studies Lin 林 comments: "Intimate, apt, and rich in flavor."
Examiner and County Director of Studies Wu 吳 comments: "Balanced and sound."

When the Sage recounted what he first set his heart upon, the effort of becoming a sage resided therein. For learning is the quest to reach sagehood; when at the beginning of one's learning one sets one's heart upon it, how could this not be wherein the Master's sagely effort lay? Fitting it is that he recounted it of himself in order to encourage others. It is as if he said: In the learning of a gentleman, if there is that by which he reaches its ultimate pinnacle, there must first be that by which he establishes its foundation. I am not one who was born with knowledge; what, then, was it that I devoted myself to at the very beginning? When my years reached fifteen, although I did not yet dare claim for myself the virtue of a fully grown man, the work of sagely self-cultivation found its starting point right here. With pure and focused thoughts, unbewildered by diverging paths, I resolutely took the Great Way as the destination toward which I aspired; with concentrated spirit, refusing to rest content with minor achievements, I made it my task to take the highest good as the standard for my advancement and cultivation. Just as I rejoiced that the proper time had arrived, I was also anxious lest it be easily lost; eagerly seizing the moment to spur myself on, with wholehearted diligence in constant study, I was indeed one who loved antiquity, earnestly sought after it, and day by day revolved together with this learning. …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
此志立而大人之學不有以心而會其精乎方
喜其年之可爲而尤懼其或至于不及焉也孜
孜焉及時以自勉而一念發憤之誠固有忘食
忘憂而時與此學相爲循環者矣此志定而大
學之道不有以心而體其全乎功難驟進而志
有所先道難徑造而趨則已定此固吾之在始
學者然也過此以往雖造漸以純不能有加于
此志而道漸以妙亦不能有加于此學信乎志
一辨而聖功無餘事也已抑聖人生知安行宜
===
若無所事志者然觀其自敘始學以至從心不
踰矩皆於志焉基之何哉蓋從容中道者夫子
天縱之聖而純亦不已者聖不自聖之心故堯
之兢舜之勅湯之盤武之銘皆是道也聖人之
心類如此
尊賢使能俊傑在位則天下之士皆悅而
願立於其朝矣市廛而不征法而不廛
則天下之商皆悅而願藏於其市矣關
譏而不征則天下之旅皆悅而願出於
punctuated:
此志立，而大人之學不有以心而會其精乎？方喜其年之可爲，而尤懼其或至于不及焉也。孜孜焉及時以自勉，而一念發憤之誠，固有忘食忘憂，而時與此學相爲循環者矣。此志定，而大學之道不有以心而體其全乎？功難驟進，而志有所先；道難徑造，而趨則已定。此固吾之在始學者然也。過此以往，雖造漸以純，不能有加于此志；而道漸以妙，亦不能有加于此學。信乎志一辨，而聖功無餘事也已。抑聖人生知安行，宜若無所事志者。然觀其自敘始學以至從心不踰矩，皆於志焉基之，何哉？蓋從容中道者，夫子天縱之聖；而純亦不已者，聖不自聖之心。故堯之兢、舜之勅、湯之盤、武之銘，皆是道也。聖人之心類如此。

尊賢使能，俊傑在位，則天下之士皆悅，而願立於其朝矣；市，廛而不征，法而不廛，則天下之商皆悅，而願藏於其市矣；關，譏而不征，則天下之旅皆悅，而願出於
translation_en:
Once this resolve is established, does one not comprehend the essence of the learning of the great man with one's mind? Just when rejoicing that I am at an age to accomplish something, I especially fear that I might fail to reach the mark. Diligently I seize the time to exert myself, and with the sincerity of a single thought of roused determination, I indeed forget to eat and forget my worries, constantly revolving around this learning. Once this resolve is settled, does one not embody the entirety of the Way of the Great Learning with one's mind? Achievement is difficult to advance suddenly, yet resolve takes precedence; the Way is difficult to reach directly, yet one's direction is already fixed. Such indeed was my state when I first began to learn. Going forward from this, although my attainment gradually became pure, nothing could be added to this resolve; and although the Way gradually became subtle, nothing could be added to this learning. Truly, once one's resolve is clearly discerned, there is nothing further required in the work of sagehood! Yet a sage knows from birth and acts with ease, so it would seem he has no need to bother with setting his resolve. However, looking at his own account, from the beginning of his learning right up to following what his heart desired without overstepping the square, all of it was founded upon this resolve—why is that? Because hitting the mean with effortless ease is the Master's heaven-endowed sagehood, whereas unceasing purity is the mind of a sage who does not regard himself as a sage. Therefore, the cautiousness of Yao, the diligence of Shun, the basin inscription of Tang, and the inscriptions of Wu all followed this Way. The minds of the sages are all like this.

"If a ruler honors the worthy and employs the able so that men of outstanding talent are in office, then all the scholars of the world will be pleased and wish to stand in his court. In the marketplaces, if he provides stalls without taxing goods, or enforces regulations without taxing the stalls, then all the merchants of the world will be pleased and wish to store their goods in his marketplaces. At the passes, if there is inspection without levying duties, then all the travelers of the world will be pleased and wish to travel on …"

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其路矣耕者助而不稅則天下之農皆
悅而願耕於其野矣廛無夫里之布則
天下之民皆悅而願為之氓矣
楊道南
同考試官教諭黃批此題說王政所及則盡乎
天下之人矣作亦稱是
同考試官教諭徐批講四民而所重在士最得
題意
考試官教諭林批文有波瀾
===
考試官教諭吳批詞婉而達
大賢詳舉王政之行盡天下而歸心焉夫人心
未易感也王者之政盡天下而仁之則咸歸之
也固宜孟子之意蓋謂王天下以得人心為本
得人心以行王政為先王政惟何蓋天下之人
其環向于一人之治至弗齊也王者之政其聯
屬于億兆之心至無外也誠知得人為王政之
首務而賢者尊之能者使之則列之朝廷固已
慶一時之選而風之天下莫不起效用之思天
punctuated:
其路矣；耕者助而不稅，則天下之農皆悅而願耕於其野矣；廛無夫里之布，則天下之民皆悅而願為之氓矣。」

楊道南

大賢詳舉王政之行，盡天下而歸心焉。夫人心未易感也，王者之政盡天下而仁之，則咸歸之也固宜。孟子之意，蓋謂王天下以得人心為本，得人心以行王政為先。王政惟何？蓋天下之人，其環向于一人之治，至弗齊也；王者之政，其聯屬于億兆之心，至無外也。誠知得人為王政之首務，而賢者尊之，能者使之，則列之朝廷，固已慶一時之選，而風之天下，莫不起效用之思。天

… its roads; if regarding tillers of the soil, the state relies on mutual aid and does not levy a tax, then all the farmers of the world will be pleased and wish to till in its fields; if regarding dwellings, there are no imposts for uncultivated land or extra cloth taxes, then all the people of the world will be pleased and wish to become its subjects."

Yang Daonan 楊道南

The Great Worthy details the practice of kingly government, whereby the entire world turns its hearts in allegiance. Now, human hearts are not easily moved; yet when the government of a true king extends benevolence to the entire world, it is only fitting that all turn to him in allegiance. The intent of Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) is roughly to say that in reigning as a true king over the world, winning the hearts of the people is fundamental, and in winning the hearts of the people, practicing kingly government comes first. What, then, is kingly government? For the people of the world, as they turn from all sides toward the rule of the One Man, are utmost in their diversity; yet the government of a true king, as it binds together the hearts of the millions, leaves nothing outside its embrace. If one truly knows that obtaining men of talent is the foremost task of kingly government—honoring the worthy and employing the able—then placing them in the court will assuredly bring celebration over the finest selection of the age, and as their influence spreads throughout the world, none will fail to be stirred by the thought of rendering service. title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
下之士歸而天下之人心舉係於斯矣以言其
仁乎商雖市地之廛市官之法固未嘗廢而貨
非其所征焉由是商有餘蓄有不願藏於市者
否矣以言其仁乎旅雖譏察之禁禦暴之令固
弗敢弛而稅非其所取焉由是旅有餘資有不
願出於塗者否矣至於國有常賦使民輸之制
也然特藉其力耳而私田之稅蠲之則天下之
農皆動耕野之思非悅其野也悅吾政之足以
厚其生也民有常業以廛賦之制也然特賦其
===
廛耳而夫里之罰緩之則天下之氓皆懷受廛
之願非悅其廛也悅吾政之足以恤其私也至
是仁心仁政之兼著萬邦士庶之共臣其感而
悅也皆至德之孚也其悅而歸也亦誠心之應
也蓋奉天之道而天下所當聽命焉者矣雖然
王政固足以孚天下而謂其有所要於天下非
也蓋王者自盡其道而天下自獻其誠如天道
運而萬物化生均之無心焉耳若有所爲而爲
之是則霸者之假仁而民亦將以僞應之矣又
punctuated: 下之士歸，而天下之人心舉係於斯矣。以言其仁乎商，雖市地之廛、市官之法固未嘗廢，而貨非其所征焉，由是商有餘蓄，有不願藏於市者否矣。以言其仁乎旅，雖譏察之禁、禦暴之令固弗敢弛，而稅非其所取焉，由是旅有餘資，有不願出於塗者否矣。至於國有常賦，使民輸之，制也；然特藉其力耳，而私田之稅蠲之，則天下之農皆動耕野之思，非悅其野也，悅吾政之足以厚其生也。民有常業，以廛賦之，制也；然特賦其廛耳，而夫里之罰緩之，則天下之氓皆懷受廛之願，非悅其廛也，悅吾政之足以恤其私也。至是，仁心仁政之兼著，萬邦士庶之共臣，其感而悅也，皆至德之孚也；其悅而歸也，亦誠心之應也。蓋奉天之道，而天下所當聽命焉者矣。雖然，王政固足以孚天下，而謂其有所要於天下，非也。蓋王者自盡其道，而天下自獻其誠，如天道運而萬物化生，均之無心焉耳。若有所爲而爲之，是則霸者之假仁，而民亦將以僞應之矣，又
translation_en: …scholars of the world give their allegiance, and the hearts of all under heaven are bound to this. To speak of benevolence toward merchants: although the stall-rent for market plots and the regulations of market officials are certainly never abolished, no tax is levied on their goods; consequently, merchants have surplus savings, and there are none who do not wish to store their goods in his marketplaces. To speak of benevolence toward travelers: although the prohibitions of inspection at the borders and the ordinances for preventing violence are certainly never relaxed, no duty is exacted from them; consequently, travelers have surplus funds, and there are none who do not wish to travel upon his roads. As for the state having regular revenues that it requires the people to contribute, that is the established system; yet if one merely relies upon their labor to cultivate the public fields while remitting the tax on their private fields, then the farmers of the world will all be stirred with the desire to plough in his fields—not because they delight in the fields themselves, but because they delight in our governance being sufficient to enrich their livelihood. As for the people having regular occupations and being taxed according to their dwelling plots, that is the established system; yet if one merely taxes their dwelling plots while remitting the fines for uncultivated land and idle hands—the head-tax and neighborhood-cloth levies—then the commoners of the world will all cherish the wish to receive dwelling plots—not because they delight in the plots themselves, but because they delight in our governance being sufficient to show compassion for their private needs. At this point, with benevolent heart and benevolent governance both made manifest, and the scholars and commoners of the myriad states all submitting as subjects, their being moved to delight is entirely through the trust inspired by supreme virtue; their delighting and giving allegiance is likewise the response of sincere hearts. For he upholds the Way of Heaven, and all under heaven ought rightly to obey his mandate. Even so, while kingly governance is indeed sufficient to inspire trust throughout the world, to say that the king does this in order to seek something from the world would be wrong. Rather, the true king simply fulfills his own Way to the utmost, and the world naturally offers up its sincerity—just as the Way of Heaven revolves and the myriad things are transformed and generated, both alike being without deliberate calculation. If one acts with an ulterior motive, that is the feigned benevolence of a hegemon, and the people will likewise respond to him with deceit; how then…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
何以心悅而誠服耶吁知王霸之辨可與行王
政矣
易
彖曰大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天雲行雨
施品物流形大明終始六位時成時乗
六龍以御天乾道變化各正性命保合
大和乃利貞首出庶物萬國咸寧象曰
天行健君子以自彊不息
孫如游
===
同考試官教諭田批天道聖人之四德皆健之
所爲也是作能發明之深於易者
同考試官教諭畢批天人合一之理言之詳明
而意更貫串可錄
考試官教諭林批深得題旨
考試官教諭吳批雅健
彖象交發乾義而天人合一之妙見矣盖天以
四德運于上而所以本之者健也然則聖人憲
天之化謂非同天之健以致之哉宜彖象交發
punctuated:
何以心悅而誠服耶？吁！知王霸之辨，可與行王政矣。

《易》
「《彖》曰：大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。雲行雨施，品物流形。大明終始，六位時成，時乗六龍以御天。乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。首出庶物，萬國咸寧。《象》曰：天行健，君子以自彊不息。」

孫如游

同考試官教諭田批：天道、聖人之四德，皆健之所爲也。是作能發明之，深於《易》者。
同考試官教諭畢批：天人合一之理，言之詳明，而意更貫串，可錄。
考試官教諭林批：深得題旨。
考試官教諭吳批：雅健。

《彖》、《象》交發乾義，而天人合一之妙見矣。盖天以四德運于上，而所以本之者，健也。然則聖人憲天之化，謂非同天之健以致之哉？宜《彖》、《象》交發
translation_en:
… how could they be pleased in heart and sincerely submit? Alas! Once one understands the distinction between the true king and the hegemon, one is ready to practice kingly governance.

Classic of Changes (Yijing)

"The Commentary on the Judgments (Tuan) says: Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! All things owe their beginning to it, and thus it governs Heaven. The clouds move and the rain falls, and the various things flow into their forms. Greatly luminous from end to beginning, the six positions are completed in their proper times; at the proper times he mounts the six dragons to drive across Heaven. The Way of Qian changes and transforms, so that each thing rectifies its nature and destiny; preserving and uniting the great harmony, thus it is advantageous and貞 [correct and firm]. Rising first above the multitude of things, the myriad states all enjoy peace. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: Heaven's movement is vigorous; the noble man thus makes himself strong and untiring."

By Sun Ruyou 孫如游

Associate Examiner Instructor Tian comments: The four virtues of the Way of Heaven and of the sage are all brought about by vigor. This composition is able to elucidate this; its author is deeply versed in the Classic of Changes.
Associate Examiner Instructor Bi comments: The principle of the unity of Heaven and humanity is stated with detailed clarity, and the ideas are even more coherently threaded together. Worthy of recording.
Examiner Instructor Lin comments: Deeply grasps the purport of the topic.
Examiner Instructor Wu comments: Elegant and vigorous.

The Commentary on the Judgments (Tuan) and the Commentary on the Images (Xiang) mutually bring forth the meaning of Qian, and the subtlety of the unity of Heaven and humanity is thereby revealed. For Heaven revolves on high through the four virtues, and that which serves as their foundation is vigor. Such being the case, when the sage models himself on Heaven's transformations, how could one say he does not achieve this through a vigor identical to Heaven's? Rightly do the Commentary on the Judgments and the Commentary on the Images mutually bring forth…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其義也且夫聖人者法天者也天有至教聖人
有至德均於乾義盡之矣是故天道有元亨自
其開物之始著物之形者見之也聖人者以吾
之心契天之心則乾道終始之運既大明于中
而六龍卷舒之妙自以時措之焉一天之元亨
而已矣天道有利貞自其足物之理凝物之氣
者見之也聖人者體天之化爲吾之化則首出
庶物之上雖不見其爲而萬國咸寧之治自垂
拱而致焉一天之利貞而已矣若是者豈無所
===
本哉蓋乾之象天也四德循環迭運不已非至
健乎君子觀乾之象法天之行而亦如其健焉
以吾精一之學養其天德之剛而毅然者常在
我蓋自一念之微以達於萬感之著而道心不
爲之少懈矣以吾有主之天勝其易動之欲而
浩然者常不屈蓋自無斁之保以極於不已之
純而已私不爲之少間矣至是則君子之彊卽
天之健存之于心是謂純天之德達之于治是
謂憲天之化而所以乘龍御天萬國咸寧者皆
punctuated: 其義也。且夫聖人者，法天者也。天有至教，聖人有至德，均於《乾》義盡之矣。是故天道有元、亨，自其開物之始、著物之形者見之也。聖人者，以吾之心契天之心，則乾道終始之運既大明于中，而六龍卷舒之妙自以時措之焉，一天之元、亨而已矣。天道有利、貞，自其足物之理、凝物之氣者見之也。聖人者，體天之化爲吾之化，則首出庶物之上，雖不見其爲，而萬國咸寧之治自垂拱而致焉，一天之利、貞而已矣。若是者，豈無所本哉？蓋《乾》之象，天也。四德循環，迭運不已，非至健乎？君子觀《乾》之象，法天之行，而亦如其健焉。以吾精一之學，養其天德之剛，而毅然者常在我，蓋自一念之微以達於萬感之著，而道心不爲之少懈矣。以吾有主之天，勝其易動之欲，而浩然者常不屈，蓋自無斁之保以極於不已之純，而已私不爲之少間矣。至是，則君子之彊卽天之健。存之于心，是謂純天之德；達之于治，是謂憲天之化。而所以乘龍御天、萬國咸寧者，皆
translation_en:
… its meaning.

Moreover, the sage is one who models himself upon Heaven. Heaven possesses supreme instruction, and the sage possesses supreme virtue; both are fully exhausted in the meaning of the Qian hexagram. Therefore, the Way of Heaven has origination (yuan) and flourishing (heng), which are seen from its initiating the beginning of things and manifesting the forms of things. When the sage aligns his own mind with the mind of Heaven, the cycle of the ending and beginning of the Way of Qian becomes grandly illuminated within him, and the wondrous subtlety of the six dragons furling and unfurling is naturally put into practice according to the time—this is simply identical with Heaven's origination and flourishing, and nothing more. The Way of Heaven has advantage (li) and贞 firmness (zhen), which are seen from its completing the principles of things and consolidating the vital forces of things. When the sage embodies the transformations of Heaven as his own transformations, he rises preeminent above the multitude of things; even though his actions are not seen, the governance whereby the myriad states all enjoy peace is naturally achieved with robes hanging down and hands folded—this is simply identical with Heaven's advantage and firmness, and nothing more.

Being such as this, how could it be without a foundation? For the image of Qian is Heaven. Its four virtues revolve in a cycle, alternating in their operation without ceasing—is this not supreme vigor? The noble man observes the image of Qian, models himself on the movement of Heaven, and likewise matches its vigor. Through one's learning of refinement and unity, one nourishes the firmness of one's heavenly virtue, so that resolute fortitude always abides within oneself; thus, from the subtlety of a single thought all the way to the manifestation of ten thousand responses, the mind of the Way does not slacken in the slightest on their account. Through one's heaven-endowed nature that has a master within, one overcomes desires that are easily stirred, so that the vast and flowing vital energy never yields; thus, from preserving it without weariness to reaching the utmost of unceasing purity, one's selfish desires [reading 己私 for 已私] do not intrude in the slightest to interrupt it.

When it reaches this point, the strength of the noble man is none other than the vigor of Heaven. Preserved in the mind, this is called making pure the virtue of Heaven; extended to governance, this is called taking as one's model the transformations of Heaven. And that whereby he mounts the dragons to drive across Heaven and brings peace to all the myriad states all…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
自此出也是故合彖與象觀之而乾之義寧有
餘蘊哉蓋甞觀之堯之放勳舜之重華其治隆
矣然而無怠無荒之念欽若昊天之誠堯舜且
惓惓焉何也聖人自彊不息之心固如是也故
曰帝王之治本於道帝王之道本於心明乎乾
之義者可以識帝王之心矣
形而上者謂之道
屠隆
同考試官教諭田批卦爻陰陽無非至理聖人
===
所以立象盡意也是作能言之宜錄以式
同考試官教諭畢批發揮道妙於形之意簡明
可觀
考試官教諭林批理明詞整
考試官教諭吳批切實不浮
大傳卽易之超乎形者而著道之名焉夫道妙
於無形者也自易之形而上者觀之而道在是
矣孰謂意之不盡於象乎且夫聖人之作易也
意固盡於象之中而象實涵乎道之蘊何以言
punctuated:
自此出也。是故合《彖》與《象》觀之，而乾之義寧有餘蘊哉！蓋甞觀之，堯之放勳、舜之重華，其治隆矣。然而無怠無荒之念、欽若昊天之誠，堯、舜且惓惓焉，何也？聖人自彊不息之心，固如是也。故曰：帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於心。明乎乾之義者，可以識帝王之心矣。
「形而上者謂之道。」
屠隆
同考試官教諭田批：卦爻陰陽，無非至理，聖人所以立象盡意也。是作能言之，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭畢批：發揮道妙於形之意，簡明可觀。
考試官教諭林批：理明詞整。
考試官教諭吳批：切實不浮。
《大傳》卽《易》之超乎形者，而著道之名焉。夫道妙於無形者也，自《易》之形而上者觀之，而道在是矣，孰謂意之不盡於象乎？且夫聖人之作《易》也，意固盡於象之中，而象實涵乎道之蘊。何以言…
translation_en:
…issue forth from this. Therefore, when one examines the Judgment (Tuan) and the Image (Xiang) together, how could there be any remaining profundities in the meaning of the Qian hexagram left unexpressed! Indeed, if we observe the far-reaching merit of Yao and thesplendid brilliance of Shun, their governance was lofty indeed. Yet even Yao and Shun were earnestly devoted to the thought of being neither remiss nor negligent, and to the sincerity of reverently conforming to August Heaven—why was this? Because the sage's mind of unceasing self-strengthening is inherently like this. Thus it is said: the governance of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and the Way of emperors and kings is rooted in the mind. One who understands the meaning of Qian can recognize the mind of emperors and kings.

"What is above form is called the Way."
Tu Long 屠隆

Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Tian comments: The hexagrams, lines, yin, and yang are nothing other than the ultimate principle; this is how the sages established images to fully express their ideas. This composition is able to articulate this and should be recorded as a model.
Associate Examiner Instructor Bi comments: It elaborates the idea that the subtlety of the Way transcends form; concise, clear, and worth reading.
Examiner Instructor Lin comments: The reasoning is clear and the diction is well-ordered.
Examiner Instructor Wu comments: Concrete and substantial, without superficiality.

The Great Commentary (Dazhuan) looks directly at that in the Changes (Yi) which transcends form, and thereby makes manifest the name of the Way. Now, the Way finds its subtlety in formlessness. Viewed from what in the Changes is above form, the Way is right there—who then could say that the sages' ideas are not fully expressed in the images? Moreover, when the sages created the Changes, their ideas were assuredly exhausted within the images, while the images in fact encompass the profound essence of the Way. How can we say…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之卦爻陰陽皆形也若不足以為道也然陰之
形不徒陰也必有超乎陰之上者存焉陽之形
不徒陽也亦必有超乎陽之上者寓焉斂之無
端而主宰於二體之中不滯於剛柔之畫藏之
無朕而貫徹於六虛之内不泥於奇偶之文若
此者將不謂之道乎吾知陰而曰上陰不足盡
之也意象俱泯一於穆不已之眞陽而曰上陽
不足名之也方體俱無實太極本然之懿統觀
於卦而其不囿於卦者乃道之渾然者焉二體
===
之成列皆兩間之至理而所謂通神明之德者
通此而已踰法象而獨運孰非乾坤之精也哉
析觀於爻而其不囿於爻者乃道之燦然者焉
六位之時成皆三才之妙用而所謂順性命之
理者順此而已超形器而獨存孰非乾坤之祕
也哉要之爻象未立而理已具道固不倚於形
也爻象旣立而理斯顯道亦不離於形也自理
之可見者若為形自形之不可見者實為道矣
知道不外乎形此象之能盡乎意也歟雖然易
punctuated: 之？卦爻陰陽皆形也，若不足以為道也。然陰之形不徒陰也，必有超乎陰之上者存焉；陽之形不徒陽也，亦必有超乎陽之上者寓焉。斂之無端，而主宰於二體之中，不滯於剛柔之畫；藏之無朕，而貫徹於六虛之内，不泥於奇偶之文。若此者，將不謂之道乎？吾知陰而曰上，陰不足盡之也，意象俱泯，一於穆不已之眞；陽而曰上，陽不足名之也，方體俱無，實太極本然之懿。統觀於卦，而其不囿於卦者，乃道之渾然者焉。二體之成列，皆兩間之至理，而所謂通神明之德者，通此而已。踰法象而獨運，孰非乾坤之精也哉！析觀於爻，而其不囿於爻者，乃道之燦然者焉。六位之時成，皆三才之妙用，而所謂順性命之理者，順此而已。超形器而獨存，孰非乾坤之祕也哉！要之，爻象未立而理已具，道固不倚於形也；爻象旣立而理斯顯，道亦不離於形也。自理之可見者，若為形；自形之不可見者，實為道矣。知道不外乎形，此象之能盡乎意也歟！雖然，易
translation_en:
… [How can we say] this? The hexagrams, lines, yin, and yang are all physical forms; they would seem insufficient to constitute the Way. Yet the form of yin is not merely yin; there must be something existing that transcends yin. The form of yang is not merely yang; there must also be something residing within that transcends yang. Gathered in without beginning or end, it presides within the two constituent trigrams without being confined to the strokes of the firm and the yielding; hidden away without trace or sign, it penetrates throughout the six fluctuating line-positions without being bogged down in the patterns of odd and even. Such being the case, shall we not call it the Way?

I know that when speaking of yin we say "above form," yin is insufficient to exhaust it; conceptualizing and emblematic imagery both vanish, and it is purely the truth of profound and unceasing solemnity. When speaking of yang we say "above form," yang is insufficient to name it; spatial direction and physical body are both absent, and it is truly the original perfection of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji).

Viewing the hexagrams as a whole, that which is not confined by the hexagrams is the Way in its undifferentiated completeness. The arrangement of the two constituent trigrams represents the ultimate principles between heaven and earth, and what is called "communicating the virtues of spiritual intelligence" is simply communicating this. Transcending models and emblems to operate independently, what part of it is not the essence of Qian and Kun! Viewing the lines analytically, that which is not confined by the lines is the Way in its resplendent clarity. The timely completion of the six positions represents the wondrous functioning of the Three Powers (heaven, earth, and man), and what is called "according with the principles of nature and destiny" is simply according with this. Transcending physical forms and vessels to exist independently, what part of it is not the mystery of Qian and Kun!

In sum, before the lines and emblems were established, the principle was already complete; the Way indeed does not depend upon form. Once the lines and emblems were established, the principle thus became manifest; the Way also does not separate from form. Viewed from the aspect of principle that can be seen, it appears as form; viewed from the aspect of form that cannot be seen, it is in reality the Way. Knowing that the Way is not external to form—is this not how the emblems are able to fully express the meaning! Even so, the [principles of the] Changes (Yi)…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之理固不外於陰陽而實吾心之動靜也聖人
作易不過以心之精而形之易以濟民行耳學
易者靜虛動直存吾心以契聖人之心則由象
識意易之形而上者在我矣噫此聖人洗心之
訓昭如也學易者其知之
書
帝曰咨四岳有能典朕三禮僉曰伯夷帝
曰俞咨伯汝作秩宗夙夜惟寅直哉惟
清伯拜稽首讓于夔龍帝曰俞往欽哉
===
帝曰夔命汝典樂敎胄子直而溫寬而
栗剛而無虐簡而無傲詩言志歌永言
聲依永律和聲八音克諧無相奪倫神
人以和
胡士奇
同考試官敎諭陳批 題以禮樂作對類難整齊
此作鋪敘得體而發明虞廷命官之旨殆盡可錄
考試官敎諭林批 整飭
考試官敎諭吳批 莊重
punctuated:
之理固不外於陰陽，而實吾心之動靜也。聖人作《易》，不過以心之精而形之《易》，以濟民行耳。學《易》者，靜虛動直，存吾心以契聖人之心，則由象識意，《易》之形而上者在我矣。噫！此聖人洗心之訓昭如也，學《易》者其知之。

《書》：
「帝曰：『咨四岳，有能典朕三禮？』僉曰：『伯夷。』帝曰：『俞。咨伯，汝作秩宗。夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。』伯拜稽首，讓于夔、龍。帝曰：『俞，往欽哉！』帝曰：『夔，命汝典樂，敎胄子。直而溫，寬而栗，剛而無虐，簡而無傲。詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲，八音克諧，無相奪倫，神人以和。』」

胡士奇。
同考試官敎諭陳批：題以禮樂作對，類難整齊。此作鋪敘得體，而發明虞廷命官之旨殆盡，可錄。
考試官敎諭林批：整飭。
考試官敎諭吳批：莊重。
translation_en:
… principle of the Changes (Yi) certainly does not lie outside of yin and yang, yet in reality it is the activity and stillness of our own mind. When the sages created the Changes, they did no more than take the essence of their minds and give it form in the Changes in order to aid the conduct of the people. If those who study the Changes maintain emptiness in stillness and uprightness in activity, preserving our own mind so as to tally with the mind of the sages, then by proceeding from the images to recognize the meaning, that which is above form in the Changes will reside within us. Alas! How luminous is this teaching of the sages on cleansing the mind; let those who study the Changes take note of it.

Book of Documents (Shu):
"The Sovereign said, 'Oh, Four Mountains! Is there anyone who can direct my three rites?' All said, 'Boyi.' The Sovereign said, 'Yes. Oh, Bo, you shall be Director of Sacrifices. Morning and night be reverent; be upright, be pure.' Bo bowed and touched his head to the ground, yielding in favor of Kui and Long. The Sovereign said, 'Yes, go and be reverent!' The Sovereign said, 'Kui, I appoint you to direct music and to teach the heirs of the nobility: to be straightforward yet mild,寬 [broad-minded/tolerant] yet栗 [firm/careful], strong yet not tyrannical, simple yet not arrogant. Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs the words; the notes depend on the prolonged words; the pitch-pipes harmonize the notes. When the eight timbres can be brought into harmony and do not encroach upon one another's order, spirits and men will thereby be brought into harmony.'"

Hu Shiqi 胡士奇.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen: A topic pairing rites and music is typically difficult to arrange with balanced symmetry. This composition lays out the narrative fittingly and elucidates almost completely the purport of appointing officials at the court of Yu; it is worthy of inclusion.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Lin: Well-ordered.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wu: Dignified and weighty.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖君命官以典禮樂惟敬與和而已夫禮主於
敬而樂主於和也聖君命官以是禮樂其有興
乎且夫天子建中和之極人臣職明聽之司吾
於虞廷之命官而知其得人矣彼幽以事神存
乎禮而知禮者伯夷其選也故帝因四岳之舉
而命之曰秩宗之官所以交神明而命汝作之
則凡祀天地而享人鬼者固有在於禮矣而禮
豈外于心之敬乎必嚴諸夙夜之際而惕然其
常寅者克純夫直內之功斯反諸本原之天而
===
湛然其無欲者適得乎澄清之體一敬之所以
常存固三禮之所以無愧矣伯夷宜承命以莅
其職而顧有夔龍之讓帝能已于往欽之勅乎
是命一伯夷而典禮者有專責也已明以育材
存乎樂而知樂者夔其選也故帝因夷之讓而
命之曰典樂之官所以敎胄子而命汝爲之則
凡翼其偏而防其過者固在于樂矣而樂豈外
于心之和乎始則詩以言志而歌聲因之旣肇
夫聲氣之原旣則律以和聲而損益成之適得
