punctuated: 聖君命官以典禮樂，惟敬與和而已。夫禮主於敬，而樂主於和也。聖君命官以是，禮樂其有興乎！且夫天子建中和之極，人臣職明聽之司，吾於虞廷之命官，而知其得人矣。彼幽以事神，存乎禮，而知禮者，伯夷其選也。故帝因四岳之舉而命之曰：秩宗之官，所以交神明，而命汝作之，則凡祀天地而享人鬼者，固有在於禮矣，而禮豈外于心之敬乎？必嚴諸夙夜之際，而惕然其常寅者，克純夫直內之功；斯反諸本原之天，而湛然其無欲者，適得乎澄清之體。一敬之所以常存，固三禮之所以無愧矣。伯夷宜承命以莅其職，而顧有夔、龍之讓，帝能已于「往欽」之勅乎？是命一伯夷，而典禮者有專責也已。明以育材，存乎樂，而知樂者，夔其選也。故帝因夷之讓而命之曰：典樂之官，所以敎胄子，而命汝爲之，則凡翼其偏而防其過者，固在于樂矣，而樂豈外于心之和乎？始則詩以言志，而歌聲因之，旣肇夫聲氣之原；旣則律以和聲，而損益成之，適得
translation_en:
When a sage ruler appoints officials to take charge of rites and music, it is solely a matter of reverence and harmony. Now, rites are governed by reverence, and music is governed by harmony. When a sage ruler appoints officials on this basis, surely rites and music will flourish! Moreover, the Son of Heaven establishes the supreme standard of centrality and harmony, while his ministers hold the offices of clear-sightedness and acute hearing; looking at the appointment of officials in the court of Yu [Shun], I know that he found the right men.

To serve the spirits in the unseen realm depends on rites, and among those who understood the rites, Boyi was the choice. Therefore the Sovereign [Shun], following the recommendation of the Four Peaks, charged him, saying: "The office of Director of Rites is that by which one communicates with the bright spirits, and since I charge you to fill it, everything involved in sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and making offerings to human ghosts truly rests upon the rites. Yet how could the rites be external to the reverence of the mind? One must be strict from early morning to late at night, so that in vigilant and constant respect one perfects the effort of straightening the inner self; thus returning to the original nature of Heaven, crystal-clear and free of selfish desires, one attains the pure and limpid substance." That single reverence being constantly preserved is indeed the reason why he could be without shame in the Three Rites. Boyi ought to have accepted the charge and entered upon his post, yet instead he yielded in favor of Kui and Long—how then could the Sovereign refrain from the admonition to "go and be reverent"? Thus, by appointing a single Boyi, the person in charge of the rites was given dedicated responsibility.

To nurture talent in the visible realm depends on music, and among those who understood music, Kui was the choice. Therefore the Sovereign, following Boyi's yielding in his favor, charged him, saying: "The office of Director of Music is that by which one instructs the eldest sons, and since I charge you to perform it, everything involved in rectifying their one-sidedness and guarding against their excesses truly rests upon music. Yet how could music be external to the harmony of the mind? At the outset, poetry expresses intent, and singing and vocal notes follow upon it, thereby initiating the source of sound and breath; next, the pitch-pipes harmonize the notes, and adding and subtracting bring them to completion, thereby attaining…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夫節宣之妙八音克諧而不亂斯神人協和而
不違矣后夔能率是以盡其職而為冑子之敎
尚何感化之難乎是命一后夔而典樂者有攸
賴也已要之和敬一心禮樂一道而惟夷夔之
深於禮樂者當之此虞廷禮明樂備其盛矣乎
雖然帝舜不自有其盛也方且亮功之戒咨命
惟勤黜陟之法大明罔私而交儆之謨勅天之
歌相與都俞于一堂者秩秩乎渢渢乎揖讓希
音可觀而聆也故曰見禮知政聞樂知德吾于
===
帝舜有深感焉
君子所其無逸先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則
知小人之依
陳性學
同考試官敎諭陳批 講所其與知稼穡處皆有
分曉且清逸俊雅迥異他作
考試官敎諭林批 涵蓄有味深得周公忠愛
之意
考試官敎諭吳批 調格古雅
punctuated:
夫節宣之妙。八音克諧而不亂，斯神人協和而不違矣。后夔能率是以盡其職，而為冑子之敎，尚何感化之難乎？是命一后夔，而典樂者有攸賴也已。要之，和敬一心，禮樂一道，而惟夷、夔之深於禮樂者當之，此虞廷禮明樂備，其盛矣乎！雖然，帝舜不自有其盛也，方且亮功之戒，咨命惟勤；黜陟之法，大明罔私。而交儆之謨，勅天之歌，相與都俞于一堂者，秩秩乎，渢渢乎，揖讓希音，可觀而聆也。故曰：「見禮知政，聞樂知德。」吾于帝舜有深感焉。

君子所其無逸，先知稼穡之艱難乃逸，則知小人之依。
陳性學
同考試官敎諭陳批：講「所其」與「知稼穡」處，皆有分曉，且清逸俊雅，迥異他作。
考試官敎諭林批：涵蓄有味，深得周公忠愛之意。
考試官敎諭吳批：調格古雅。
translation_en:
… the subtlety of regulation and expression. When the eight timbres can be harmonized without disorder, then spirits and men will be brought into concord without discrepancy. If Lord Kui (后夔) can follow this to fulfill his duties and instruct the noble youths, what difficulty could there still be in moving and transforming them? Thus, by appointing one Lord Kui, the office of directing music had someone upon whom to rely.

In sum, harmony and reverence stem from a single mind, and ritual and music share a single Way; only Boyi (夷) and Kui, who were profound in ritual and music, were fit to undertake these charges. How flourishing indeed it was that in the court of Yu, ritual was illustrious and music was complete! Even so, Emperor Shun (帝舜) did not claim this flourishing state as his own doing. Just then, in his admonition to assist in achievements, he was diligent in consulting and giving charges; in the laws of demotion and promotion, he was grandly fair and without partiality. Moreover, the counsels of mutual caution and the songs of revering Heaven’s mandate, with which ruler and ministers voiced their agreement and approval together in a single hall—how orderly in ceremony, how resonant in melody! Their yielding courtesy and rare tones could be witnessed and heard. Therefore it is said: "By viewing the rituals one knows the governance; by hearing the music one knows the virtue." Toward Emperor Shun I feel a profound admiration.

"The noble man makes having no leisure his dwelling place. When he first knows the hardships of sowing and reaping and only then takes his ease, he will know that upon which the lesser people depend."
By Chen Xingxue (陳性學).
Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: The explanations of the passages "makes ... his dwelling place" and "knows the hardships of sowing and reaping" are both clear and distinct; moreover, the style is pure,unconstrained, refined, and elegant—vastly different from other compositions.
Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: Reserved and rich in flavor, it deeply grasps the loyal and affectionate intent of the Duke of Zhou (周公).
Examiner and Instructor Wu comments: Its tone and structure are ancient and elegant.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大臣述君子之居勤而因原其所由勤焉蓋君
之逸者凡以其忽民事也君子先知其艱而克
勤也固其所哉周公戒成王若曰王業始于憂
勤而君道戒乎逸豫吾王纘艱難之業而居小
民之上也亦知君子之無逸乎蓋其仰觀天命
靈長之機而兢兢焉怠荒之是戒俯察民心怨
樂之故而業業乎勤勵之是圖內無逸志而所
以致謹于淵默之中者無一念不居于勤也外
無逸樂而所以矜持于臨御之際者無一事不
===
任其勞也君子之無逸如此果何由而然哉蓋
君之位至逸也民之稼穡至艱也惟不知其艱
而遽享其逸此逸心所由起也君子方其未居
位之先而慮周天下已洞徹其艱難之狀乃其
旣居位之後而心存畎畝自莫巳其憂勤之思
知民之有稼民之所依以爲命也吾欲立民之
命則凡可以開其麗者雖勤力圖之而猶恐其
不給矣况敢乘以逸哉知民之有穡民之所依
以爲生也吾欲全民之生則凡可以導其利者
punctuated: 大臣述君子之居勤，而因原其所由勤焉。蓋君之逸者，凡以其忽民事也。君子先知其艱而克勤也，固其所哉！周公戒成王若曰：王業始于憂勤，而君道戒乎逸豫。吾王纘艱難之業，而居小民之上也，亦知君子之無逸乎？蓋其仰觀天命靈長之機，而兢兢焉怠荒之是戒；俯察民心怨樂之故，而業業乎勤勵之是圖。內無逸志，而所以致謹于淵默之中者，無一念不居于勤也；外無逸樂，而所以矜持于臨御之際者，無一事不任其勞也。君子之無逸如此，果何由而然哉？蓋君之位至逸也，民之稼穡至艱也，惟不知其艱而遽享其逸，此逸心所由起也。君子方其未居位之先，而慮周天下，已洞徹其艱難之狀；乃其旣居位之後，而心存畎畝，自莫巳其憂勤之思。知民之有稼，民之所依以爲命也。吾欲立民之命，則凡可以開其麗者，雖勤力圖之，而猶恐其不給矣，况敢乘以逸哉？知民之有穡，民之所依以爲生也。吾欲全民之生，則凡可以導其利者，
translation_en:
The great minister recounts how the noble ruler abides in diligence, and thereby traces the source of his diligence. Indeed, when a ruler indulges in ease, it is always because he neglects the affairs of the people. That the noble ruler first understands their hardships and is therefore able to be diligent—is this not naturally his proper place?

The Duke of Zhou admonished King Cheng as if to say: Royal enterprise begins in anxious diligence, and the way of the sovereign warns against comfort and indulgence. Our King has inherited an enterprise won through hardship and sits above the common people; does he also understand how the noble ruler allows himself no luxurious ease? Looking up, he contemplates the subtle mechanisms by which the Mandate of Heaven is prolonged, and cautiously guards against idleness and neglect; looking down, he examines the causes of resentment and joy in the hearts of the people, and fearfully plans for diligence and exertion. Within, he harbors no thoughts of ease, so that in exercising caution amidst deep silence, there is not a single thought that does not abide in diligence; without, he indulges in no pleasures of ease, so that in maintaining self-restraint when presiding over his subjects, there is not a single affair in which he does not shoulder the toil himself.

That the noble ruler allows himself no ease in this manner—from what, indeed, does it arise? Now, the position of the ruler is one of supreme ease, whereas the sowing and reaping of the people are of supreme hardship. Only when one does not understand their hardship and precipitously enjoys one's ease does a mind of indulgence arise. Before the noble ruler has even assumed the throne, his thoughts encompass the whole world, and he already thoroughly perceives the conditions of their hardships; then, after he has assumed the throne and enjoys its ease, his heart remains among the furrowed fields, and he naturally cannot cease [reading 巳 as 已] his thoughts of anxious diligence.

He knows that the people's sowing is what the people depend upon for their very lives. "If I wish to establish the lives of the people, then in everything that can open up their resources [? 麗], even though I plan for it with diligent effort, I still fear it may not suffice—how much less would I dare to take advantage of my position to indulge in ease?" He knows that the people's reaping is what the people depend upon for their livelihood. "If I wish to preserve the livelihood of the people, then in everything that can guide their benefit, …"

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
雖勵精謀之而猶恐其弗迨矣况敢淫于逸哉
是可見惟知依而後能足民依惟無逸而後能
享其逸古君子之存心於民蓋如此王其知所
法矣抑周以后稷開基稼穡尤其所首務者成
王幼冲席已成之業而未見祖宗之勞周公所
爲懼也至於豳風之歌視無逸尤加咏嘆深長
思焉成王之所以享盛治而延卜歷也是故稱
周公之德不衰
詩
===
百辟卿士媚于天子不解于位民之攸墍
邵倬
同考試官教諭黃批發揮不解民墍得詩人忠
愛之旨宜錄以傳
同考試官教諭徐批規戒之意溢於言表也佳
士佳士
考試官教諭林批旨遠詞文
考試官教諭吳批醇正
羣臣愛君惟切保治之願焉蓋安民所以致治
punctuated:
雖勵精謀之，而猶恐其弗迨矣，况敢淫于逸哉？是可見惟知依而後能足民依，惟無逸而後能享其逸。古君子之存心於民蓋如此，王其知所法矣。抑周以后稷開基，稼穡尤其所首務者。成王幼冲，席已成之業，而未見祖宗之勞，周公所爲懼也。至於《豳風》之歌，視《無逸》尤加咏嘆，深長思焉。成王之所以享盛治而延卜歷也，是故稱周公之德不衰。

詩

百辟卿士，媚于天子，不解于位，民之攸墍。

邵倬

同考試官教諭黃批：發揮「不解」、「民墍」，得詩人忠愛之旨，宜錄以傳。
同考試官教諭徐批：規戒之意，溢於言表也。佳士，佳士。
考試官教諭林批：旨遠詞文。
考試官教諭吳批：醇正。

羣臣愛君，惟切保治之願焉。蓋安民所以致治，
translation_en:
…even if one strives with utmost vigor to plan for it, one still fears falling short—how much less would one dare to indulge in ease! From this it can be seen that only by knowing what the people depend upon can one suffice for their dependence, and only by not indulging in ease can one enjoy ease. Such was the way the noble men of antiquity kept the people in their hearts; may the King know to take them as his model! Moreover, the Zhou dynasty founded its enterprise through Houji (Lord Millet), so sowing and reaping were especially its foremost concern. That King Cheng, being young and tender, inherited an already accomplished enterprise without having witnessed the toil of his ancestors was what made the Duke of Zhou fearful. As for the songs of the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng), compared to the "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi), they added even more chanting and sighing, inspiring deep and lasting reflection. This was whereby King Cheng enjoyed flourishing governance and prolonged the divined reign-years of the dynasty; therefore, the praise of the Duke of Zhou's virtue has never waned.

Classic of Poetry (Shi)

"The hundred lords and ministers show their love for the Son of Heaven; not slackening in his position, he is the one in whom the people find rest."

By Shao Zhuo 邵倬.

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Huang: It elaborates on "not slackening" and "the people finding rest," grasping the poet's intent of loyal affection. It ought to be recorded and transmitted.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Xu: The admonition and caution overflow beyond the words. A fine scholar, a fine scholar!
Comment by Examiner Instructor Lin: Far-reaching in purport and refined in diction.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Wu: Pure and upright.

When all the ministers love their ruler, they are solely earnest in their wish to preserve good governance. Indeed, bringing peace to the people is the means to achieve good governance,…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而不解者乆安長治之道也羣臣以此願君忠
愛寧有既乎想其願嗣王之意以為明君不以
世治而忽遠圖善保治者也良臣不以主聖而
忘進規善用愛者也嗣王之綱之紀固貽臣下
以莫大之安矣為諸臣者將何以自效哉彼外
而百辟佐天子以分治者也其心同則其媚同
油然忠愛之無巳者蓋不以今日之綏和為可
樂而欲引之為道乆化成之休內而卿士輔天
子以出治者也同此心則同此媚翕然仰戴之
===
惟殷者蓋不以目前之寧謐為可喜而欲衍之
為悠乆無疆之慶運精神于五位而綱焉常張
效法於無斁焉則民之安者益以安而咸和之
化歷萬年如一日也凡在燕及之下者不以是
而輸忠藎耶廑念慮於萬幾而紀焉常理媲美
於執競焉則民之寧者益以寧而永清之治歷
萬禩如一時也凡興媚兹之懷者不以是而申
報稱耶夫臣之媚君不忘乎防微杜漸之思君
能諒臣不替其持盈保泰之慮君臣相與以有
punctuated: 而不解者，乆安長治之道也。羣臣以此願君，忠愛寧有既乎？想其願嗣王之意，以為明君不以世治而忽遠圖，善保治者也；良臣不以主聖而忘進規，善用愛者也。嗣王之綱之紀，固貽臣下以莫大之安矣，為諸臣者將何以自效哉？彼外而百辟，佐天子以分治者也，其心同則其媚同，油然忠愛之無巳者，蓋不以今日之綏和為可樂，而欲引之為道乆化成之休；內而卿士，輔天子以出治者也，同此心則同此媚，翕然仰戴之惟殷者，蓋不以目前之寧謐為可喜，而欲衍之為悠乆無疆之慶。運精神于五位，而綱焉常張，效法於無斁焉，則民之安者益以安，而咸和之化歷萬年如一日也。凡在燕及之下者，不以是而輸忠藎耶？廑念慮於萬幾，而紀焉常理，媲美於執競焉，則民之寧者益以寧，而永清之治歷萬禩如一時也。凡興媚兹之懷者，不以是而申報稱耶？夫臣之媚君，不忘乎防微杜漸之思；君能諒臣，不替其持盈保泰之慮。君臣相與以有
translation_en:
… whereas never slackening is the way to achieve lasting peace and enduring order. Since the assembled ministers wish this for their ruler, how could their loyalty and affection ever have an end?

Imagining the intent of their wishes for the succeeding king, they held that an enlightened ruler does not neglect far-sighted plans because the world is well-governed—he is one who knows well how to preserve good governance; and good ministers do not forget to offer admonition because their sovereign is sage—they are ones who know well how to put their affection into practice. By directing the overarching guidelines and lesser threads of government, the succeeding king has surely bequeathed immense peace upon his subjects below; how, then, shall the various ministers exert themselves in return?

Out in the provinces, the hundred lords assist the Son of Heaven in sharing the administration. Because their minds are the same, their loving devotion is the same. Their irrepressibly endless loyalty and affection stem from not taking today's peace and harmony as mere cause for pleasure, but wishing to extend it into the blessing of a Way long-enduring and transformation brought to completion. Within the court, the ministers and officers aid the Son of Heaven in issuing governance. Sharing this mind, they share this loving devotion. Their harmonious and deeply earnest reverence and support stem from not taking the present tranquility as mere cause for delight, but wishing to prolong it into a felicity enduring and boundless.

If he exerts his vital spirit upon the supreme sovereign position so that the overarching guidelines are ever taut, modeling himself on untiring diligence, then the people who are at peace will become ever more peaceful, and the transformation of universal harmony will pass through ten thousand years as if a single day. Among all who enjoy the ruler's gracious reach, who would not thereby pour forth their loyal devotion? If he applies his anxious thoughts to the myriad affairs of state so that the lesser threads of governance are ever ordered, rivaling the excellence of steadfast vigor, then the people who are tranquil will become ever more tranquil, and the rule of eternal clarity will pass through ten thousand generations as if a single moment. Among all who harbor feelings of loving devotion toward him, who would not thereby express their reciprocation?

Now, when ministers show loving devotion to their ruler, they do not forget the thought of guarding against the minute and checking the incipient; if the ruler can understand his ministers, he will not relax his concern for maintaining fullness and preserving great prosperity. Ruler and ministers working together to…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
成王嗣之福孰有大於是哉噫此虞庭賡歌意
也舜之時稱極治矣而禹益諸臣惟惓惓以時
幾之勅逸樂之防告其君豈過計哉蓋有初鮮
終者人之恒情而憂盛危明藎臣之用心固如
此嘉樂詩人得之矣昔人謂太和之氣常在虞
周宇宙間有以夫
帝命式于九圍
查允元
同考試官教諭黃批帝命二字少能發揮惟此
===
作運意敷詞精雅宜錄以式
同考試官教諭徐批文以成命世德並起以建
中執中入講末用順治威嚴含蓄下意此何等心思
考試官教諭林批文思雋永
考試官教諭吳批精確
聖君受命而為法於天下一敬之所感也甚矣
天之所親惟敬也然則命湯以式天下也固其
所哉此商人袷祭而歌之也若曰天有成命商
有世德而所以靈承之有常光紹之弗替者匪
punctuated:
成，王嗣之福，孰有大於是哉？噫！此虞庭賡歌意也。舜之時稱極治矣，而禹、益諸臣，惟惓惓以時幾之勅、逸樂之防告其君，豈過計哉？蓋有初鮮終者，人之恒情；而憂盛危明，藎臣之用心固如此，《嘉樂》詩人得之矣。昔人謂太和之氣，常在虞、周宇宙間，有以夫！

帝命式于九圍。
查允元。
同考試官教諭黃批：帝命二字少能發揮，惟此作運意敷詞精雅，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭徐批：文以成命、世德並起，以建中、執中入講，末用順治、威嚴含蓄下意，此何等心思！
考試官教諭林批：文思雋永。
考試官教諭吳批：精確。

聖君受命而為法於天下，一敬之所感也。甚矣，天之所親惟敬也！然則命湯以式天下也，固其所哉！此商人袷祭而歌之也，若曰：天有成命，商有世德，而所以靈承之有常、光紹之弗替者，匪…
translation_en:
…achievement; what blessing for the royal successors could be greater than this? Ah! This is the spirit of the responsive songs in the court of Yu [Shun]. The time of Shun was acclaimed as the pinnacle of good governance, yet ministers such as Yu and Yi earnestly admonished their sovereign only with cautioning about timely attention to the subtle springs of action and guarding against idleness and pleasure. Was this excessive calculation? Indeed, having a beginning but rarely an end is the constant nature of man, whereas worrying in times of prosperity and feeling trepidation in times of enlightenment is inherently the mindset of a loyal minister; the poet of "Jia le" (Admirable and Amiable) grasped this. When people of the past said that thevital breath of supreme harmony always abided within the universe of Yu and Zhou, there was truly a reason for it!

"God on High ordained him to be a model to the nine regions" [Ode "Chang fa" in the Book of Odes].
By Zha Yunyuan 查允元.
Associate Examiner Instructor Huang comments: Few were able to elaborate on the two words "God ordained" (Di ming), and only this composition deploys its ideas and sets forth its phrasing with refined elegance; it should be recorded as a model.
Associate Examiner Instructor Xu comments: The essay opens by pairing the settled mandate and generational virtue, enters the exposition through establishing the Mean and holding fast to the Mean, and at the end uses compliant governance and august severity to implicitly anticipate the meaning of the following lines—what extraordinary thought!
Examiner Instructor Lin comments: The literary thought is rich and enduring.
Examiner Instructor Wu comments: Precise and exact.

That the sage ruler received the Mandate and became a model for all under heaven was brought about by a singlereverence. Extreme indeed is the way Heaven holds dear only reverence! This being so, that it ordained Tang to be a model for all under heaven was truly fitting! This was sung by the people of Shang at the collective ancestral sacrifice (xia), as if to say: Heaven has its settled Mandate, and Shang has its generational virtue, yet the means by which to felicitously receive it with constancy and gloriously continue it without fail, without…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
敬弗克也我湯純敬以祗帝德斯其至矣而天
之命之也何如哉彼監觀求莫帝之心也惟日
躋則一敬之精純有以孚其簡在之實降衷綏
猷帝之命也惟昭假則一敬之專一足以承其
申錫之休故九圍異制無所於統紀則弗率乃
作之君若曰凡厥弗率爾其正域之而天與之
意昭然於行事之示也九圍異俗無所於節約
則罔中乃作之師若曰凡厥罔中爾其表正之
而帝眷之隆顯然於咨命之間也中天地而爲
===
綱常之主紀綱法度於此乎受成焉建中之矩
其治統之所歸乎纘有夏而膺曆數之傳禮樂
敎化於此乎立極焉執中之要其道統之所傳
乎至是則命之始受於玄王而今會其成列辟
侯服於順治而輯瑞者盡天下也旣發之丕基
此其維新矣孰非一德之所致哉命之益大於
相土而今統其盛庶邦震疊於威嚴而貢琛者
盡天下也有截之弘烈此其重光矣又孰非一
敬之所感哉吁此湯之所以大造我商也嗣天
punctuated: 敬弗克也。我湯純敬以祗帝，德斯其至矣，而天之命之也何如哉？彼監觀求莫，帝之心也，惟日躋，則一敬之精純，有以孚其簡在之實；降衷綏猷，帝之命也，惟昭假，則一敬之專一，足以承其申錫之休。故九圍異制，無所於統紀，則弗率，乃作之君，若曰：「凡厥弗率，爾其正域之。」而天與之意，昭然於行事之示也。九圍異俗，無所於節約，則罔中，乃作之師，若曰：「凡厥罔中，爾其表正之。」而帝眷之隆，顯然於咨命之間也。中天地而爲綱常之主，紀綱法度於此乎受成焉，建中之矩，其治統之所歸乎！纘有夏而膺曆數之傳，禮樂敎化於此乎立極焉，執中之要，其道統之所傳乎！至是，則命之始受於玄王，而今會其成，列辟侯服於順治，而輯瑞者盡天下也。旣發之丕基，此其維新矣，孰非一德之所致哉！命之益大於相土，而今統其盛，庶邦震疊於威嚴，而貢琛者盡天下也。有截之弘烈，此其重光矣，又孰非一敬之所感哉！吁！此湯之所以大造我商也，嗣天
translation_en: … reverence, one cannot succeed. Our Tang, with pure reverence, honored the Lord on High; his virtue thus reached the utmost. And how did Heaven charge him? Looking down and seeking peace for the people is the mind of the Lord on High; because Tang's reverence ascended daily, the pure essence of his single-minded reverence matched the reality of his being chosen by Heaven. Sending down the moral sense to the people and tranquilly guiding their way is the mandate of the Lord on High; because Tang's reverence shone forth and reached Heaven, the undivided focus of his single-minded reverence sufficed to receive the blessing of Heaven's renewed gifts. Therefore, when the nine regions had different institutions and lacked unifying order, they were disobedient; Heaven then made him their ruler, as if to say: "All who are disobedient, you shall bring order to their lands." Thus Heaven's intent to grant him the realm was clearly manifested in the demonstration of actual deeds. When the nine regions had different customs and lacked restraining norms, they missed the mean; Heaven then made him their teacher, as if to say: "All who miss the mean, you shall set an example to rectify them." Thus the abundance of the Lord on High's favor was unmistakably evident in the conferring of the mandate. Standing at the center of Heaven and Earth as the master of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues, the principles of governance and laws took their completed form from him—was not the standard of establishing the mean that in which the lineage of governance converged! Continuing the line of the Xia dynasty and receiving the transmission of the heavenly succession, rites, music, and moral transformation established their supreme standard in him—was not the essence of holding fast to the mean that by which the lineage of the Way was transmitted! At this point, the mandate that was first received by the Dark King (Xuanwang, i.e., Xie) now reached its fulfillment; the various princes and feudal lords submitted to his benign rule, and those who gathered to present theirjade tallies encompassed the entire world. The great foundation that had already been opened was hereby renewed—how could any of this not be brought about by his pure, single virtue! The mandate that had grown even greater under Xiangtu now united its full flourishing in him; the numerous states trembled in awe of his majesty, and those who offered precious tribute encompassed the entire world. The vast achievements that brought整齐 uniform order to the realm hereby shone with renewed splendor—and how could any of this not be inspired by his single-minded reverence! Alas, this was how Tang grandly founded our Shang dynasty. Those who succeed to the realm…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
下者顧不當永念之乎抑斯敬也卽堯舜禹相
傳之心法也心之敬卽道之中也湯以此得統
亦以此造商而後賢又能世守其德故享年六
百最爲有道之長也然則敬之一言其萬世帝
王祈天永命之本乎吁君天下者可以惕然思
矣
春秋
夏六月公會齊侯宋公陳侯鄭伯同盟于
幽〔莊公二十有七年〕齊人救邢〔閔公元〕
===
〔年〕遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕秋七月公會齊侯
宋公陳世子欵鄭世子華盟于甯母〔僖公七年〕
沈雲楫
同考試官敎諭梁批此篇發齊桓始霸以見魯
怨當釋且不脫易世意乃長於經者
考試官敎諭林批發魯當從義意明盡
考試官敎諭吳批詞簡意明
觀嗣世者迭爲霸圖見怨之所當釋矣蓋魯怨
punctuated:
下者，顧不當永念之乎？抑斯敬也，卽堯、舜、禹相傳之心法也。心之敬，卽道之中也。湯以此得統，亦以此造商，而後賢又能世守其德，故享年六百，最爲有道之長也。然則敬之一言，其萬世帝王祈天永命之本乎！吁，君天下者，可以惕然思矣。

春秋

夏六月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、鄭伯同盟于幽〔莊公二十有七年〕；齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕；遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕；秋七月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳世子欵、鄭世子華盟于甯母〔僖公七年〕。

沈雲楫
同考試官敎諭梁批：此篇發齊桓始霸，以見魯怨當釋，且不脫易世意，乃長於經者。
考試官敎諭林批：發魯當從義，意明盡。
考試官敎諭吳批：詞簡意明。

觀嗣世者迭爲霸圖，見怨之所當釋矣。蓋魯怨
translation_en:
…[one who succeeds to the] realm—ought he not bear this forever in mind? Moreover, this reverence is precisely the method of the mind transmitted one to another by Yao, Shun, and Yu. The reverence of the mind is none other than the centrality of the Way. Through this, Tang gained the legitimate succession, and through this he also founded the Shang; because worthy successors were further able to preserve his virtue generation after generation, the dynasty enjoyed six hundred years of rule, the longest among those possessing the Way. This being so, is not this single word “reverence” the foundation by which emperors and kings for ten thousand generations pray to Heaven for a perpetual mandate! Ah, he who rules the realm may well reflect on this with vigilant awe.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

“In summer, in the sixth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, and together made a covenant at You” [27th year of Duke Zhuang]; “The men of Qi rescued Xing” [1st year of Duke Min]; “They thereupon attacked Chu” [4th year of Duke Xi]; “In autumn, in the seventh month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, Heir Apparent Kuan of Chen, and Heir Apparent Hua of Zheng, and made a covenant at Ningmu” [7th year of Duke Xi].

Shen Yunji 沈雲楫
Associate Examiner and Instructor Liang comments: This essay brings out how Duke Huan of Qi first established his hegemony in order to show that Lu’s enmity ought to be laid aside, and moreover does not lose sight of the significance of the change of generation; it is the work of one well-versed in the Classic.
Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: It brings out how Lu ought to follow righteousness; the meaning is clear and thorough.
Examiner and Instructor Wu comments: The phrasing is concise and the meaning clear.

When one observes that the ruler of a succeeding generation repeatedly pursued the undertakings of a hegemon, one sees that the enmity ought to be laid aside. For the enmity of Lu…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之所當報者非桓也而况肇於圖霸乎春秋所
以不貶于柯之盟也且桓何人也非襄之子乎
爲襄之子者是爲齊也仇乃莊之釋怨而與盟
安得遽從無貶耶蓋君子不責於易世之怨孝
子必圖夫宗社之安襄魯仇也而今則非其人
矣况桓之創霸又義之所當從焉今觀其于幽
一盟懷鄭貳也則眾志孚而諸侯合矣又慮諸
夏不可棄也畏簡書以恤患而于邢安焉于楚
一伐聲外暴也則大義著而夷狄攘矣又慮周
===
室所當尊也定方物以作貢而甯毋盟焉卽今
日之成匡合之功雖未著而所以樹厥功者從
玆始也從之卽所以從霸而魯安矣若之何其
以一盟而不惠徼於魯之社稷也卽今日之舉
尊攘之績雖未成而所以建厥績者由玆肇也
悖之卽所以悖霸而魯危矣若之何愛於一盟
而不以綏夫魯之宗社耶故春秋不貶于柯之
盟蓋與其脩怨怒鄰之爲孝不若順義安邦之
爲孝亦度其怨之可釋而非與之也明乎此者
punctuated: 之所當報者，非桓也，而况肇於圖霸乎？《春秋》所以不貶于柯之盟也。且桓何人也？非襄之子乎？爲襄之子者，是爲齊也仇。乃莊之釋怨而與盟，安得遽從無貶耶？蓋君子不責於易世之怨，孝子必圖夫宗社之安。襄，魯仇也，而今則非其人矣；况桓之創霸，又義之所當從焉。今觀其于幽一盟，懷鄭貳也，則眾志孚而諸侯合矣；又慮諸夏不可棄也，畏簡書以恤患，而于邢安焉。于楚一伐，聲外暴也，則大義著而夷狄攘矣；又慮周室所當尊也，定方物以作貢，而甯毋盟焉。卽今日之成，匡合之功雖未著，而所以樹厥功者從玆始也。從之卽所以從霸，而魯安矣，若之何其以一盟而不惠徼於魯之社稷也？卽今日之舉，尊攘之績雖未成，而所以建厥績者由玆肇也。悖之卽所以悖霸，而魯危矣，若之何愛於一盟而不以綏夫魯之宗社耶？故《春秋》不貶于柯之盟，蓋與其脩怨怒鄰之爲孝，不若順義安邦之爲孝；亦度其怨之可釋，而非與之也。明乎此者，
translation_en:
… ought to seek vengeance against was not Duke Huan; and how much the more so when he was initiating his enterprise as hegemon? That is why the Spring and Autumn Annals does not censure the covenant at Ke.

Moreover, who was Duke Huan? Was he not the successor of Duke Xiang [literally "son of Xiang"]? As the successor of Xiang, he was Qi, the enemy. When Duke Zhuang let go of his enmity and entered into a covenant with him, how could this immediately be exempted from censure? It is because the gentleman does not demand vengeance for enmity after a change of generation, and a filial son must plan for the security of his ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain. Duke Xiang was Lu's enemy, but now the ruler was no longer that same man; furthermore, Duke Huan's founding of the hegemony was something that in righteousness ought to be followed.

Look now at his single covenant at You: it was to win over the wavering state of Zheng, whereby the minds of the multitude were won to trust and the feudal lords were united. Considering also that the central states could not be abandoned, he revered the bamboo dispatches to succor those in distress, and thus at Xing brought security. Look at his single campaign against Chu: it was to denounce external aggression, whereby great righteousness was made manifest and the barbarians were repelled. Considering also that the Royal House of Zhou ought to be honored, he regulated local tribute goods to establish proper offerings, and thus made the covenant at Ningmu.

Even at the conclusion of today's affair, although the merit of rectifying the realm and uniting the lords was not yet fully manifest, the foundation for establishing that merit began right here. To follow him was to follow the hegemon, and thereby Lu would be secure; how could one withhold a single covenant and fail to seek blessings for the altars of Lu? Even in today's undertaking, although the achievement of honoring the king and repelling the barbarians was not yet completed, the basis for erecting that achievement originated from this. To defy him was to defy the hegemon, and thereby Lu would be imperiled; how could one begrudge a single covenant and fail to bring peace to the ancestral temple and altars of Lu?

Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not censure the covenant at Ke. For rather than considering it filial to nurse a grudge and provoke a neighbor's wrath, it is better to consider it filial to comply with righteousness and secure the state; it also judged that the enmity could properly be laid aside, rather than merely granting unconditional approval. One who understands this…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
可以知權可以擇義而霸業其有興矣抑是盟
也莊公謂生不如死曹子欲請當其臣似憤然
有激於衷者而竟以汶陽之田請則彭生之刃
魯且忘之矣而能以許地之信孚於諸侯而霸
業成焉故桓之伯仲教之也
晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞昭公十有五年
蔣承勛
同考試官教諭梁批此篇作者多褒荀吳語予
獨發免於貶意最得經旨
===
考試官教諭林批鎔鑄傳語而題旨自明
考試官教諭吳批得春秋用兵禦狄之旨
春秋於霸兵之近正而特平詞以紀之焉蓋兵
以却叛爲正荀吳之伐鮮虞近於是矣春秋所
以平其詞乎且鮮虞之伐以略遠也而荀吳實
董是役焉殆於潞甲之滅昔陽之入等耳何以
獨稱名氏與其稱人稱國者殊耶蓋兵一耳而
期於殄滅者失之暴行以狄道者失之詐均之
非用兵之正也乃若荀吳則異於是方圍鼓而
punctuated:
可以知權，可以擇義，而霸業其有興矣。抑是盟也，莊公謂「生不如死」，曹子欲「請當其臣」，似憤然有激於衷者；而竟以汶陽之田請，則彭生之刃，魯且忘之矣。而能以許地之信孚於諸侯，而霸業成焉。故桓之伯，仲教之也。

晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞（昭公十有五年）
蔣承勛
同考試官教諭梁批：此篇作者多褒荀吳語，予獨發免於貶意，最得經旨。
考試官教諭林批：鎔鑄傳語，而題旨自明。
考試官教諭吳批：得《春秋》用兵禦狄之旨。

《春秋》於霸兵之近正，而特平詞以紀之焉。蓋兵以却叛爲正，荀吳之伐鮮虞，近於是矣，《春秋》所以平其詞乎！且鮮虞之伐，以略遠也，而荀吳實董是役焉，殆於潞甲之滅、昔陽之入等耳。何以獨稱名氏，與其稱人、稱國者殊耶？蓋兵一耳，而期於殄滅者失之暴，行以狄道者失之詐，均之非用兵之正也。乃若荀吳則異於是。方圍鼓而
translation_en:
…can understand how to weigh circumstances, can choose what is righteous, and the hegemonic enterprise will flourish. Yet in this covenant, Duke Zhuang said that "living is worse than dying," and Caozi wished to "ask to confront his ministers," seeming indignantly stirred in their hearts; yet in the end they merely requested the fields of Wenyang, so that Lu had all but forgotten the blade of Pengsheng. Meanwhile, [Qi] was able to win the trust of the feudal lords through the good faith of returning the promised land, and thus the hegemonic enterprise was accomplished. Therefore, Duke Huan's hegemony was taught to him by Guan Zhong.

"Xun Wu of Jin led a force to attack Xianyu" (fifteenth year of Duke Zhao)
Jiang Chengxun 蔣承勛
Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Liang: Most authors on this topic use words that praise Xun Wu, whereas I alone bring out the meaning that he was merely spared from censure, which best captures the intent of the Classic.
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Lin: It melts down and casts the words of the commentary so that the purport of the topic becomes self-evident.
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Wu: It captures the Spring and Autumn Annals' principle of using military force to defend against the Di.

Toward a hegemon's military expedition that approximates righteousness, the Spring and Autumn Annals specially records it in neutral language. This is because in warfare, rejecting traitors is what is upright; Xun Wu's campaign against Xianyu came close to this, which is why the Spring and Autumn Annals used neutral language for it! Moreover, the campaign against Xianyu was launched to seize distant territory, and Xun Wu actually directed this expedition—it was nearly on a par with the destruction of the Ji clan of Lu [Lujia] and the entry into Xiyang. Why then is he alone recorded by his personal and lineage names, differing from those instances where the text refers merely to "men" or to the state? Now, military action is one and the same, yet those who aim at total annihilation err in brutality, and those who act by the ways of the Di err in deceit; both alike fail to represent the proper use of military force. As for Xun Wu, however, he differed from this. Just when he was besieging Gu and…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
請以城叛力屈而請以城降也在彼巳無效死
之心然請叛而俾之繕守力屈而俾之修城也
在我則堅却叛之信非故獲城而不取也以好
惡不愆而後民知所適惡吾叛而受其叛何以
示民信耶是故雖可以得城而弗受也非故勤
民而頓兵也以率義不爽而後民知事君邑可
獲而賈民怠其何以事君耶是故雖可以獲邑
而弗爲也以是用兵則不欲城而邇姦是謂守
正而行其得城且不戮也暴云乎哉不失信以
===
庇民是謂師貞之吉其力盡而後取也詐云乎
哉經故於荀吳而獨舉名氏非褒之也纔免於
貶耳而窮兵略遠者可知矣春秋此義不可以
見用兵禦狄之略哉抑鮮虞之伐却叛正也嗣
是陸渾之滅以靖王室君子以爲義而猶有所
不滿者蓋晉昭之世荆楚暴橫不是之慮而攘
却無聞焉獨於鮮虞陸渾是亟自是吳楚爭衡
而晉霸之業衰荀吳諸臣不得不任其咎
禮記
punctuated:
請以城叛，力屈而請以城降也，在彼巳無效死之心；然請叛而俾之繕守，力屈而俾之修城也，在我則堅却叛之信。非故獲城而不取也，以好惡不愆，而後民知所適；惡吾叛而受其叛，何以示民信耶？是故雖可以得城而弗受也。非故勤民而頓兵也，以率義不爽，而後民知事君；邑可獲而賈民怠，其何以事君耶？是故雖可以獲邑而弗爲也。以是用兵，則不欲城而邇姦，是謂守正而行，其得城且不戮也，暴云乎哉？不失信以庇民，是謂師貞之吉，其力盡而後取也，詐云乎哉？經故於荀吳而獨舉名氏，非褒之也，纔免於貶耳，而窮兵略遠者可知矣。春秋此義，不可以見用兵禦狄之略哉？抑鮮虞之伐，却叛正也；嗣是陸渾之滅，以靖王室，君子以爲義，而猶有所不滿者。蓋晉昭之世，荆楚暴橫，不是之慮，而攘却無聞焉，獨於鮮虞、陸渾是亟。自是吳、楚爭衡，而晉霸之業衰，荀吳諸臣不得不任其咎。

禮記
translation_en:
…offered to defect with the city, and when their strength was exhausted they offered to surrender with the city—on their part, they already lacked the resolve to fight to the death. Yet when they offered to defect, he made them strengthen their defenses; and when their strength was exhausted, he made them repair their walls—on his own part, he held fast to the good faith of rejecting defectors. It was not that he deliberately refused to take a city within his grasp; rather, it is only when one's likes and dislikes do not err that the people know which course to follow. If we hate rebellion among our own people yet accept rebellion among theirs, how can we demonstrate good faith to the people? Therefore, although he could have gained the city, he would not accept it. Nor was it that he deliberately wore out his people and blunted his troops; rather, it is only when one leads by righteousness without deviation that the people know how to serve their ruler. If a town can be gained at the cost of encouraging slackness among the people, how then will they serve their ruler? Therefore, although he could have captured the town, he would not do so. Using military force in this manner—not coveting a city at the expense of drawing near to treachery—may be called acting in adherence to rectitude; and when he did take the city, he did not even put anyone to death—how could that be called brutal? Not breaking faith in order to shelter the people may be called the auspiciousness of a righteous army (as in the "Army" hexagram of the Changes); and since he took it only after their strength was utterly spent, how could that be called deceitful? Thus the Classic singles out Xun Wu (荀吳) by recording his personal name and clan name—not to praise him, but merely to spare him from censure; and from this one may judge those who exhaust their armies in seizing distant territories! Does not this principle in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) allow us to see the proper strategy for employing military force to ward off the northern tribes (Di 狄)? Yet while the campaign against Xianyu (鮮虞) was righteous in its rejection of defectors, and the subsequent destruction of the Luhun (陸渾) Rong was undertaken to pacify the royal house—which the gentleman considered righteous—there remained something unsatisfactory. For during the reign of Duke Zhao of Jin (晉昭公), Chu (荊楚) was violent and overbearing; yet Jin gave no thought to this, and nothing was heard of any effort to repel them, while it was urgent only toward Xianyu and Luhun. From this time on, Wu (吳) and Chu contended for supremacy while the hegemonic enterprise of Jin declined—for which Xun Wu and the other ministers cannot escape responsibility.

Record of Rites (Liji 禮記)

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
是故昔先王尚有德尊有道任有能舉賢
而置之聚衆而誓之是故因天事天因
地事地因名山升中于天因吉土以饗
帝于郊升中于天而鳳皇降龜龍假饗
帝于郊而風雨節寒暑時是故聖人南
面而立而天下大治
王豫
考試官敎諭林批先王祭則受福而至治成
得人故耳子能詳言之且簡潔可誦取之
===
考試官敎諭吳批詞約而意已盡
觀聖王用賢舉祀之效而其享至治也有由矣
夫治至無爲治之極也先王得賢以舉大祭而
瑞應臻焉此所以享無爲之治歟記禮器者蓋
謂人君一身敬天勤民之責萃焉所以迓神休
而登治理者要在於用賢也已吾觀先王以天
地肇乎大祭而助祭貴於得人也于是尚德尊
道而使能之不遺焉舉賢誓衆而莅事之有恪
焉其慎擇乎左右者無弗豫已由是因天因地
punctuated:
是故昔先王尚有德，尊有道，任有能，舉賢而置之，聚衆而誓之。是故因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中于天，因吉土以饗帝于郊。升中于天而鳳皇降，龜龍假；饗帝于郊而風雨節，寒暑時。是故聖人南面而立，而天下大治。
王豫
考試官敎諭林批：先王祭則受福而至治成，得人故耳。子能詳言之，且簡潔可誦，取之。
考試官敎諭吳批：詞約而意已盡。
觀聖王用賢舉祀之效，而其享至治也有由矣。夫治至無爲，治之極也。先王得賢以舉大祭，而瑞應臻焉，此所以享無爲之治歟！記《禮器》者蓋謂：人君一身，敬天勤民之責萃焉，所以迓神休而登治理者，要在於用賢也已。吾觀先王以天地肇乎大祭，而助祭貴於得人也。于是尚德尊道，而使能之不遺焉；舉賢誓衆，而莅事之有恪焉。其慎擇乎左右者，無弗豫已。由是因天因地，
translation_en:
"Therefore, in ancient times the former kings esteemed those who had virtue, honored those who possessed the Way, and employed those who had ability; they elevated the worthy and placed them in office, and gathered the multitude and bound them with a solemn charge. Therefore, taking their cue from Heaven, they served Heaven; taking their cue from Earth, they served Earth; by means of the famous mountains, they ascended and reported the completion of peace to Heaven; by means of the auspicious ground, they presented offerings to the Supreme Lord in the suburban sacrifice. When they reported the completion of peace to Heaven, phoenixes descended and tortoises and dragons arrived; when they presented offerings to the Supreme Lord in the suburban sacrifice, the winds and rains were regulated, and the cold and heat came in their proper seasons. Therefore, the sage stood facing south, and All Under Heaven was in a state of great order."

Wang Yu 王豫

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Lin 林: When the former kings sacrificed, they received blessings and perfect governance was achieved; this was simply because they obtained the right men. You are able to expound upon this in detail, and your writing is concise and well worth reciting. Accepted.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wu 吳: The phrasing is economical, yet the meaning is fully expressed.

When we observe the efficacy of the sage kings in employing the worthy to perform the sacrifices, we see that their enjoyment of perfect governance had its cause. Now, when governance reaches the state of non-action (wuwei 無爲), it is the ultimate pinnacle of governance. The former kings obtained the worthy to perform the great sacrifices, and auspicious responses arrived; is this not why they enjoyed the governance of non-action? The writer of the "Ritual Vessels" (Liqi 禮器) chapter [of the Record of Rites] meant to say that in the single person of the ruler are gathered the responsibilities of revering Heaven and laboring for the people, and the means by which to welcome divine blessings and ascend to orderly governance lies essentially in employing the worthy, and nothing more. I observe that as the former kings initiated the great sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, they valued obtaining the right men to assist in the sacrifices. Thereupon, they esteemed virtue and honored the Way, so that in employing the able none were overlooked; they elevated the worthy and bound the multitude with a solemn charge, so that in attending to the rites there was reverent care. In carefully selecting their attendants, there was nothing not prepared in advance. From this, taking their cue from Heaven and taking their cue from Earth, …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而天地之禮制焉升中享帝而內外之祭行焉
其秩舉乎祀典者無弗周巳惟其禮行於天則
天心鑒之而鳳皇龜龍之咸臻所以昭其貺于
神物也惟其禮行於郊則天神享之而寒暑風
雨之以時所以效其靈于歲功也夫眾職樂于
官備而神道速於感通如此聖王於此又何為
哉但見其撫運於穆清惟克端其嚮明之度而
弘化于熈皞自聿臻夫極治之休王心無為而
有道之化以成百姓則太和也萬物則咸若也
===
各順治於無方矣帝位允陟而無虞之盛以隆
中國則乂安焉外夷則輯服焉咸蕩平於無外
矣向非先王擇人於未祭之先舉祭於得人之
後胡為而有是休徵瑞物也又胡為而能致天
下之盛治也圖治者信必有道矣抑考虞書夷
典禮夔典樂而禋望肆類之禮無不徧舉以故
七政順於上鳳皇儀於庭非天下大治之驗歟
所以然者以聖人之心與天為一而感格之本
端是以天不愛道地不愛寶而至治成耳若本
punctuated: 而天地之禮制焉，升中享帝而內外之祭行焉，其秩舉乎祀典者無弗周巳。惟其禮行於天，則天心鑒之，而鳳皇龜龍之咸臻，所以昭其貺于神物也；惟其禮行於郊，則天神享之，而寒暑風雨之以時，所以效其靈于歲功也。夫眾職樂于官備，而神道速於感通如此，聖王於此又何為哉？但見其撫運於穆清，惟克端其嚮明之度；而弘化于熈皞，自聿臻夫極治之休。王心無為，而有道之化以成，百姓則太和也，萬物則咸若也，各順治於無方矣；帝位允陟，而無虞之盛以隆，中國則乂安焉，外夷則輯服焉，咸蕩平於無外矣。向非先王擇人於未祭之先，舉祭於得人之後，胡為而有是休徵瑞物也？又胡為而能致天下之盛治也？圖治者信必有道矣。抑考《虞書》，夷典禮，夔典樂，而禋望肆類之禮無不徧舉，以故七政順於上，鳳皇儀於庭，非天下大治之驗歟？所以然者，以聖人之心與天為一，而感格之本端，是以天不愛道，地不愛寶，而至治成耳。若本
translation_en: … and the rites for Heaven and Earth were thereby established; ascending to present the burnt offering at the center and sacrificing to the Supreme Lord, the inner and outer sacrifices were thereby performed—thus in the orderly observance of the sacrificial canons, nothing was left incomplete. Because these rites were performed before Heaven, the mind of Heaven examined and approved them, and phoenixes, spirit-turtles, and dragons all arrived, thereby manifesting its favor through numinous creatures. Because these rites were performed at the suburban altar, the spirits of Heaven enjoyed them, and cold and heat, wind and rain came in their proper seasons, thereby proving their efficacy in the yearly agricultural achievements. Now, when the many offices rejoice in having a full complement of officials and the way of the spirits is so swift in responding and communicating, what more need the sage-king do in this? One simply sees him presiding over the cycle of rule in solemn serenity, able solely to rectify his bearing as he faces the light; and as he broadens transformation in harmonious peace, he naturally attains the blessings of ultimate order. The king's mind acts through non-action, and the transformation of the Way is accomplished: the hundred surnames enjoy supreme harmony, the myriad things all flourish according to their natures, and each is smoothly governed without bounds. The imperial throne is truly ascended, and the flourishing age free of anxiety reaches its height: the Central States are well-ordered and tranquil, the outer tribes are pacified and submissive, and all is level and at peace with nothing left outside. Had the former kings not selected men before performing the sacrifices, and had they not performed the sacrifices only after obtaining the right men, how could there have been these auspicious signs and felicitous creatures? And how could they have brought about such flourishing order across the realm? Those who plan for governance truly must have a proper Way! Moreover, if we examine the Book of Yu (Yushu), Boyi was in charge of rites and Kui was in charge of music, and the rites of the pure sacrifice, the distant sacrifice to mountains and rivers, and the special sacrifice to the Supreme Lord were all comprehensively performed; therefore, the seven celestial governors moved in harmony above, and phoenixes came to dance in the courtyard—was this not the proof of great order throughout the realm? The reason it was so is that the mind of the sage was one with Heaven, and the foundation for moving and reaching the spirits was upright; therefore, Heaven did not withhold its Way, Earth did not withhold its treasures, and supreme governance was achieved. If the foundation…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之不端而徒欲徼福於神明可乎故曰惟聖人
爲能饗帝信夫
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣
吳一貫
考試官敎諭林批說武王偃武修文而天下
知臣禮明鬯可觀
考試官敎諭吳批得諸侯知所以臣意
聖王制禮而天下喻于忠焉夫以臣尊君忠道
也武王制朝覲之禮而諸侯知尊君焉其文敎
===
之隆何如哉夫子舉之以告賓牟賈也蓋謂上
之所以率下與下之所以奉上者惟禮以爲之
防也觀我周文敎之修而知臣禮之明矣蓋周
自受命以來武王已爲天下君而天下旣幸其
有君亦欲知其所以臣也但禮未制耳武王於
是撫萬邦之廣以昭一統之尊因典禮之常以
示服從之化時其春也而制爲之朝以聯其情
藹乎喜起之休也時乎秋也而制爲之覲以明
其分秩乎等威之辨也斯禮也所以明君臣之
punctuated:
之不端，而徒欲徼福於神明，可乎？故曰：「惟聖人爲能饗帝。」信夫！

朝覲，然後諸侯知所以臣。
吳一貫
考試官敎諭林批：說武王偃武修文，而天下知臣禮，明鬯可觀。
考試官敎諭吳批：得「諸侯知所以臣」意。

聖王制禮，而天下喻于忠焉。夫以臣尊君，忠道也。武王制朝覲之禮，而諸侯知尊君焉，其文敎之隆何如哉！夫子舉之以告賓牟賈也，蓋謂上之所以率下，與下之所以奉上者，惟禮以爲之防也。觀我周文敎之修，而知臣禮之明矣。蓋周自受命以來，武王已爲天下君，而天下旣幸其有君，亦欲知其所以臣也，但禮未制耳。武王於是撫萬邦之廣，以昭一統之尊；因典禮之常，以示服從之化。時其春也，而制爲之朝，以聯其情，藹乎喜起之休也；時乎秋也，而制爲之覲，以明其分，秩乎等威之辨也。斯禮也，所以明君臣之
translation_en:
… is not upright, and yet one merely wishes to seek blessings from the spirits, how could that be permissible? Therefore it is said: "Only the sage is able to sacrifice to the Supreme Ancestor." Truly it is so!

"Through the spring and autumn court audiences, the feudal lords thereupon knew how to act as subjects."
By Wu Yiguan 吳一貫.
Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: It explains how King Wu desisted from military affairs and cultivated civil culture so that the world came to know the rites of a subject; clear, fluent, and worth reading.
Examiner and Instructor Wu 吳 comments: It grasps the meaning of "the feudal lords knew how to act as subjects."

When the sage-king established the rites, the world came to understand loyalty. Now, for a subject to honor his ruler is the way of loyalty. When King Wu established the rites of the spring and autumn court audiences, the feudal lords knew how to honor their ruler—how grand was the flourishing of his civil teachings! When the Master cited this to instruct Bin Moujia 賓牟賈, he meant that whereby superiors lead inferiors and whereby inferiors serve superiors is solely by taking the rites as a regulating dyke. Observing the cultivation of civil teachings in our Zhou dynasty, one knows the clarity of the rites for subjects. Ever since the Zhou received the Mandate, King Wu had already become ruler of the world; and as the world was already fortunate to have its ruler, it also wished to know how to act as subjects—only the rites had not yet been established. Thereupon, King Wu pacified the vastness of the myriad states to manifest the dignity of unified rule, and relied on the constancy of canonical rites to display the transformative influence of obedience. When the season was spring, he instituted the spring court audience (chao 朝) for them so as to bind their affections—how harmonious was the felicity of joyful exhortation! When the season was autumn, he instituted the autumn audience (jin 覲) for them so as to clarify their lot—how orderly was the distinction of hierarchical majesty! These rites were the means to clarify the…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
義而教天下之忠也夫然後為諸侯者覩王制
之聿新大明乎靖恭之節思王章之有恪共輸
其精白之忱禮行於朝而愛心生焉所以媚茲
一人者真知其情之有不可解而莫不來享莫
不來王合同姓異姓而皆然矣何侯度之不明
也哉禮行於覲而敬心生焉所以欽若從王者
真見於分之有不可逃而以考制度以明黜陟
合大邦小邦而同然矣何臣紀之或昧也哉謂
之曰知所以臣信乎天王彰紀法之宗而百辟
===
遵紀法之守以行於一時則一時知所以臣也
以行於萬世則萬世知所以臣也武王復古禮
而教臣忠如此周道其極隆矣乎抑天下勢而
已矣勢之所在禮由出焉聖王壹戎衣有天下
勢已定矣而不以禮維之亂未巳也故禮射脫
劒明堂朝覲之教不憚其煩正以消其悖戾而
使之常定也然論勢則朝廷為重正體統尊朝
廷吾於朝覲有厚望焉
第貳場
punctuated:
義，而教天下之忠也。夫然後為諸侯者，覩王制之聿新，大明乎靖恭之節；思王章之有恪，共輸其精白之忱。禮行於朝，而愛心生焉；所以媚茲一人者，真知其情之有不可解，而莫不來享，莫不來王，合同姓異姓而皆然矣，何侯度之不明也哉！禮行於覲，而敬心生焉；所以欽若從王者，真見於分之有不可逃，而以考制度，以明黜陟，合大邦小邦而同然矣，何臣紀之或昧也哉！謂之曰「知所以臣」，信乎天王彰紀法之宗，而百辟遵紀法之守。以行於一時，則一時知所以臣也；以行於萬世，則萬世知所以臣也。武王復古禮而教臣忠如此，周道其極隆矣乎！

抑天下勢而已矣，勢之所在，禮由出焉。聖王壹戎衣有天下，勢已定矣，而不以禮維之，亂未巳也。故禮射、脫劒、明堂、朝覲之教，不憚其煩，正以消其悖戾而使之常定也。然論勢則朝廷為重，正體統、尊朝廷，吾於朝覲有厚望焉。

第貳場
translation_en:
… righteousness between ruler and minister, and to teach loyalty to the world. Only then did the feudal lords, beholding the renewal of the royal institutions, greatly understand the integrity of quiet reverence; and reflecting upon the solemnity of the royal statutes, together offer up their pure and unblemished sincerity. When ritual was practiced at the spring court audience (chao), feelings of affection were born therein. Those who thus devoted themselves to the One Man truly knew that their bond of affection could not be dissolved; none failed to come with offerings, and none failed to come to pay homage to the king. Uniting those of the same surname and those of different surnames, all were alike in this—how could the standards of the feudal lords not be clear! When ritual was practiced at the autumn audience (jin), feelings of reverence were born therein. Those who thus reverently complied in following the king truly saw that their allotted duty could not be evaded; and thereby institutions were examined and demotions and promotions were made clear. Uniting great states and small states, all were the same in this—how could the discipline of ministers ever be obscured! When the text calls this "knowing how to act as ministers," truly the Heavenly King manifested the foundation of rules and laws, and the hundred lords abided by the observance of those rules and laws. Practiced in one era, that era knew how to act as ministers; practiced for ten thousand generations, ten thousand generations knew how to act as ministers. King Wu restored the ancient rituals and taught ministers loyalty in such a manner—how supremely flourishing was the Way of Zhou!

And yet, the empire is a matter of the configuration of power (shi) and nothing more; where power resides, ritual emerges therefrom. Once the sage king donned armor to take possession of the empire, the configuration of power was already settled; yet if he did not maintain it with ritual, disorder would not have ceased. Therefore, in the teachings of ritual archery, unbuckling swords, the Hall of Distinction (Mingtang), and the spring and autumn court audiences, he did not shrink from their complexity, precisely so as to dissolve perversity and rebelliousness and cause the empire to remain permanently settled. Nevertheless, in discussing the configuration of power, the royal court is paramount. For rectifying the system of authority and honoring the royal court, I place deep hopes in the spring and autumn court audiences.

Second Session

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
論
人主當防未萌之欲
朱用光
同考試官教諭田批作此題者只是說防欲不
曾發得未萌之欲此作窮徹本原矣
同考試官教諭畢批作論者多喜馳騁浮語惟
此全在心上作工夫深得題旨
考試官教諭林批說理之文
考試官教諭吳批理邃詞逸
===
無欲者其心之初乎人君察其幾而防之豫則
心之天常如初而欲不能爲之累矣夫人主一
心萬事萬化取則焉一旦而或動于欲常患其
不知防知防矣則其端雖萌終必隱伏而不得
肆夫有欲而使其不得肆是亦足矣而不知此
心之天其初未始有欲也凡欲者皆人也非天
也後來之所交引而非其初之本有也夫欲非
此心之初而必待其既有而後求其無其時亦
已晚而其力亦已難矣人主思端運化之本而
punctuated:
論
人主當防未萌之欲
朱用光
同考試官教諭田批：作此題者，只是說防欲，不曾發得「未萌之欲」，此作窮徹本原矣。
同考試官教諭畢批：作論者多喜馳騁浮語，惟此全在心上作工夫，深得題旨。
考試官教諭林批：說理之文。
考試官教諭吳批：理邃詞逸。
無欲者，其心之初乎！人君察其幾而防之豫，則心之天常如初，而欲不能爲之累矣。夫人主一心，萬事萬化取則焉。一旦而或動于欲，常患其不知防；知防矣，則其端雖萌，終必隱伏而不得肆。夫有欲而使其不得肆，是亦足矣，而不知此心之天，其初未始有欲也。凡欲者，皆人也，非天也；後來之所交引，而非其初之本有也。夫欲非此心之初，而必待其既有而後求其無，其時亦已晚，而其力亦已難矣。人主思端運化之本，而
translation_en:
Discourse

"The Ruler Ought to Guard Against Desires Before They Sprout"

Zhu Yongguang 朱用光

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Tian 田: Those who write on this topic merely speak of guarding against desires, failing to bring out the meaning of "desires before they sprout." This piece thoroughly penetrates to the fundamental source.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Bi 畢: Writers of discourses mostly like to indulge in superficial rhetoric; only this piece directs all its effort toward the mind, deeply grasping the purport of the topic.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Lin 林: An essay that expounds principle.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wu 吳: Profound in principle and transcendent in diction.

To be without desire—is this not the original state of the mind? If the sovereign discerns its subtle incipient stirrings and guards against them beforehand, then the heavenly nature of his mind will forever remain as it was in the beginning, and desires will not be able to encumber it. Now, from the single mind of the ruler, the myriad affairs and myriad transformations all take their model. Once it happens to be moved by desire, the constant worry is that he does not know to guard against it; if he knows to guard against it, then even though its beginnings may sprout, in the end they must remain hidden and unable to run rampant. Now, to have desires and yet prevent them from running rampant would seem to be sufficient; yet this is failing to understand that in the heavenly nature of this mind, originally there were never any desires at all. All desires are of human artifice, not of Heaven; they are drawn forth by subsequent interactions with external things, and are not inherent in the mind's original state. Since desire is not part of the original state of this mind, if one must wait until it already exists before seeking to eliminate it, the timing is already late and the effort required is already difficult. When the ruler ponders how to rectify the foundation of revolving transformation, yet…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
顧任其晚且難無論不識不力雖識與力無救
於害也是故人主欲保其本然之天其必及其
初而豫防其人乎初者欲未萌之時也豫之云
者防於未萌之謂也而因以是申程氏之說夫
以天下之大萬幾之煩惟人主所裁制而以有
欲之心主宰於其間則天下始有不得其理者
故人主不可有欲也而欲實為人主所恒有夫
惟其欲之恒有也禁之則止縱之則熾止則階
福熾則速戾其辨甚著也故欲不可不防也而
===
昔人之言防者大端有二有防於已萌者太甲
之圖厥終秦誓之憂逾邁是也有防於未萌者
禮之禁未發詩之保無射是也其防則一而遲
疾難易之效判然殊焉何以明其然也蓋齊民
之欲難遂而人主之欲易窮眾庶之欲易節而
人主之欲難制玉帛萬國奔走遐方任土作貢
畢獻方物其欲之萌罔弗得也巧嬖諧媚伺便
頤指齒馬投鼠莫敢先事其欲之萌罔以禁也
以易窮之資挾難制之勢而恣其已萌之欲即
punctuated: 顧任其晚且難，無論不識不力，雖識與力，無救於害也。是故人主欲保其本然之天，其必及其初而豫防其人乎！初者，欲未萌之時也；豫之云者，防於未萌之謂也。而因以是申程氏之說。夫以天下之大、萬幾之煩，惟人主所裁制，而以有欲之心主宰於其間，則天下始有不得其理者。故人主不可有欲也，而欲實為人主所恒有。夫惟其欲之恒有也，禁之則止，縱之則熾；止則階福，熾則速戾，其辨甚著也。故欲不可不防也。而昔人之言防者，大端有二：有防於已萌者，《太甲》之「圖厥終」、《秦誓》之「憂逾邁」是也；有防於未萌者，《禮》之「禁未發」、《詩》之「保無射」是也。其防則一，而遲疾難易之效判然殊焉。何以明其然也？蓋齊民之欲難遂，而人主之欲易窮；眾庶之欲易節，而人主之欲難制。玉帛萬國，奔走遐方，任土作貢，畢獻方物，其欲之萌，罔弗得也；巧嬖諧媚，伺便頤指，齒馬投鼠，莫敢先事，其欲之萌，罔以禁也。以易窮之資，挾難制之勢，而恣其已萌之欲，即
translation_en:
…yet allows it to become late and difficult, then regardless of whether he lacks awareness or effort, even if he possesses both awareness and effort, it will do nothing to rescue him from harm. Therefore, if a ruler wishes to preserve his original Heavenly nature, must he not attend to it at its beginning and take precautions against human artifice beforehand? "The beginning" refers to the time when desires have not yet sprouted; "taking precautions beforehand" means guarding against them before they have sprouted. And on this basis I shall elaborate the doctrine of Master Cheng.

Now, given the vastness of the empire and the multitude of its myriad affairs, all are decided and regulated solely by the ruler; if a mind harbouring desires presides over them, then things in the empire will begin to fail to attain their proper principle. Therefore, a ruler must not have desires—and yet desires are in fact something that rulers constantly have. Now, precisely because desires are constantly present, if one prohibits them they cease, and if one indulges them they blaze up; ceasing leads to blessings, while blazing up invites disaster—the distinction between them is most evident. Therefore, desires must be guarded against.

Yet when men of the past spoke of guarding against desires, there were broadly two approaches. There is guarding against them after they have already sprouted, such as "planning for the end" in the "Tai Jia" (太甲) chapter of the Book of Documents and "worrying over the passing of time" in the "Oath of Qin" (秦誓). And there is guarding against them before they have sprouted, such as "prohibiting before it arises" in the Record of Rites (禮) and "preserving without weariness" in the Book of Odes (詩). The act of guarding is the same, yet the effects—whether slow or swift, difficult or easy—are starkly different. How can we explain why this is so?

Indeed, the desires of commoners are hard to satisfy, whereas the desires of a ruler are easily indulged to the utmost; the desires of the multitude are easy to moderate, whereas the desires of a ruler are hard to restrain. With jade and silk from ten thousand states and distant regions hastening to serve him, offering tribute according to the products of their lands and presenting all manner of local goods, whenever his desires sprout, there is nothing he cannot obtain. With artful favourites flattering and fawning, watching for the slightest nod of his chin, while others dread counting the ruler's horse's teeth or pelting a rat near a precious vessel and none dare to act beforehand, whenever his desires sprout, there is nothing to prohibit them. Relying on resources that easily indulge him to the utmost, backed by a position of power that is hard to restrain, and giving free rein to desires that have already sprouted—even if…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
幸而明諸心矣未必遽防也卽防矣未必能遽
復也卽復矣而未復之前其害弗可極亦弗可
追也蓋防於已萌者其效如此則初之不豫之
過也復其本然之天而非保其本然之天也是
故善防欲者不當防於已萌之後而當防於未
萌之先夫未萌之先本然之天也心之初也其
猶鑑之明而水之清乎鑑欲其常明時其未蔽
而拂拭之則塵垢不止而妍媸常定矣水欲其
常清時其未淆而正錯之則湛濁不動足以燭
===
鬚眉而察理矣君心之天其初而欲之未萌也
虛然明耳湛然清耳當是之時有理無欲有天
無人完其理守其天而不以人欲參焉其爲防
甚易也然而理與欲迭爲貞勝天與人迭爲消
長故出乎理則入乎欲人爲主則天必漓自此
則牽引蔓延潰裂四出而始難防矣非防之難
其防於已萌者之難也若夫未萌之防則人主
之所以易其防也是衆人以爲不必防而君子
深以爲當防者也知其當防及其初而豫爲之
punctuated: 幸而明諸心矣，未必遽防也；卽防矣，未必能遽復也；卽復矣，而未復之前，其害弗可極，亦弗可追也。蓋防於已萌者，其效如此，則初之不豫之過也，復其本然之天，而非保其本然之天也。是故善防欲者，不當防於已萌之後，而當防於未萌之先。夫未萌之先，本然之天也，心之初也，其猶鑑之明而水之清乎！鑑欲其常明，時其未蔽而拂拭之，則塵垢不止，而妍媸常定矣；水欲其常清，時其未淆而正錯之，則湛濁不動，足以燭鬚眉而察理矣。君心之天，其初而欲之未萌也，虛然明耳，湛然清耳。當是之時，有理無欲，有天無人；完其理，守其天，而不以人欲參焉，其爲防甚易也。然而理與欲迭爲貞勝，天與人迭爲消長，故出乎理則入乎欲，人爲主則天必漓。自此則牽引蔓延，潰裂四出，而始難防矣。非防之難，其防於已萌者之難也。若夫未萌之防，則人主之所以易其防也。是衆人以爲不必防，而君子深以爲當防者也。知其當防，及其初而豫爲之
translation_en: …even if one is fortunate enough to perceive them clearly in the mind, one will not necessarily guard against them at once; even if one guards against them, one will not necessarily be able to recover at once; and even if one recovers, prior to that recovery the harm done can neither be fully measured nor undone. For when one guards against desires only after they have sprouted, such is the result—this is the fault of not taking precautions at the beginning, and it is a matter of restoring one's original Heaven-endowed nature rather than preserving one's original Heaven-endowed nature. Therefore, he who is skilled at guarding against desires ought not to guard against them after they have already sprouted, but ought to guard against them before they have sprouted. Now, the state before they have sprouted is the original Heaven-endowed nature and the initial state of the mind—is it not like the brightness of a mirror and the clarity of water? If one wishes a mirror to remain ever bright, one wipes it at the time when it is not yet obscured; then dust and grime will not settle upon it, and beauty and ugliness will always be distinguishably fixed. If one wishes water to remain ever clear, one sets it upright and still at the time when it is not yet muddied; then the settled dregs will not be stirred up, and it will suffice to reflect beard and eyebrows and to discern fine patterns. The Heaven-endowed nature of the ruler's mind, in its initial state before desires have sprouted, is simply vacuous and bright, simply limpid and clear. At such a time, there is principle and no desire, there is Heaven and no human artifice; to keep its principle whole, to guard its Heaven-endowed nature, and not to let human desires intrude therein—such prevention is very easy. Yet principle and desire alternate in prevailing over one another, and the Heavenly and the human alternate in waxing and waning; thus, to depart from principle is to enter into desire, and when the human becomes master, the Heavenly necessarily grows thin. From this point on, desires draw one another along and spread, bursting forth in every direction, and only then do they become difficult to guard against. It is not that prevention itself is difficult, but that guarding against what has already sprouted is difficult. As for guarding against what has not yet sprouted, that is whereby the ruler makes his prevention easy. This is what the multitude consider unnecessary to guard against, yet what the noble man deeply considers imperative to guard against. Knowing that it must be guarded against, and taking precautions at its very inception…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
防視無若有視未形以爲已形故用力省而取
效博也是故守眞保素謹於冲夷恬淡之時却
照返觀嚴於凝寂定靜之際戒謹恐懼凜於尸
居淵默之境憂勤祗惕勵於蚤夜平旦之候聲
色未邇也而燕處雅頌居寢瞽御慎防其淫玩
好未開也而異物不貴遠物不寳慎防其侈未
懷宴安而日出聽政日昃不遑防佚豫也未思
馳騁而遊田有箴蒐狩有禮防荒樂也土木未
興而有勞民費財之防是故瓊瑶示戒雕峻示
===
警焉邊功未啓而有起釁召禍之防是故却贄
不享閉關謝使焉虞賔在位三恪助祭夏士在
庭殷士在廟雝民在甸夷隸在門防吾之萌于
欲也疑丞後先卜筮左右太史奉諱工師誦詩
御瞽幾聲士庶傳謗防人之萌吾欲也夫是謂
禁於未發夫是謂保於無射若是者豈故用其
心於無所用之地而爲是私憂過計哉其防於
未萌者正所以絕其已萌者也蓋至是則理常
爲主欲常爲客人泯而本然之天常如其初矣
punctuated: 防，視無若有，視未形以爲已形，故用力省而取效博也。是故守眞保素，謹於冲夷恬淡之時；却照返觀，嚴於凝寂定靜之際；戒謹恐懼，凜於尸居淵默之境；憂勤祗惕，勵於蚤夜平旦之候。聲色未邇也，而燕處雅頌，居寢瞽御，慎防其淫；玩好未開也，而異物不貴，遠物不寳，慎防其侈；未懷宴安，而日出聽政，日昃不遑，防佚豫也；未思馳騁，而遊田有箴，蒐狩有禮，防荒樂也。土木未興，而有勞民費財之防，是故瓊瑶示戒，雕峻示警焉；邊功未啓，而有起釁召禍之防，是故却贄不享，閉關謝使焉。虞賔在位，三恪助祭，夏士在庭，殷士在廟，雝民在甸，夷隸在門，防吾之萌于欲也；疑丞後先，卜筮左右，太史奉諱，工師誦詩，御瞽幾聲，士庶傳謗，防人之萌吾欲也。夫是謂禁於未發，夫是謂保於無射。若是者，豈故用其心於無所用之地，而爲是私憂過計哉？其防於未萌者，正所以絕其已萌者也。蓋至是，則理常爲主，欲常爲客，人泯而本然之天常如其初矣。
translation_en: …precautions against them, treating the nonexistent as if it existed and what has not yet taken shape as if it had already taken shape, then the effort expended will be slight while the results achieved will be extensive. Therefore, he preserves his genuineness and maintains his unadorned simplicity, being cautious in moments of serene and tranquil detachment; he turns his gaze inward in self-reflection, being strict at times of composed stillness and calm; he maintains wary caution and fearful reverence, standing in awe in states of motionless and deep silence; and he cultivates anxious diligence and respectful vigilance, exerting himself during the hours of early morning, late night, and dawn. Sensual pleasures of sound and sight have not yet come near, yet in his private leisure he listens to the Odes and Hymns, and in his bedchamber blind musicians attend him, carefully guarding against licentiousness. A taste for curiosities and trinkets has not yet been indulged, yet he does not value strange objects or treasure things from afar, carefully guarding against extravagance. Before harbouring thoughts of ease and comfort, he holds court at sunrise and allows himself no leisure even as the sun declines, guarding against idleness and indulgence. Before thinking of galloping afield, he heeds admonitions on excursions and hunting and observes ritual in the spring and winter hunts, guarding against wild pleasures. Before construction projects are launched, he takes precautions against exhausting the people and wasting wealth; thus he takes warning from jade palaces and remains alert against carved rafters and lofty roofs. Before frontier exploits are initiated, he takes precautions against provoking hostilities and inviting disaster; thus he rejects tribute gifts and refuses offerings, closing the passes and turning away envoys. The guests of Yu occupy their places, the descendants of the Three Revered Dynasties assist in the sacrifices, the officers of Xia stand in the courtyard, the officers of Yin attend in the ancestral temple, the harmonious populace dwells in the royal domain, and the barbarian retainers stand at the gates—all this is to guard against desires sprouting from within himself. The Resolver of Doubts and the Assistant stand before and behind him, diviners by tortoise-shell and milfoil attend at his left and right, the Grand Scribe presents warnings of tabooed faults, the Master of Artisans recites cautionary odes, the Attending Blind Musicians scrutinize the musical tones, and officers and commoners pass along criticisms—all this is to guard against others causing desires to sprout within him. This is what is meant by prohibiting evil before it arises; this is what is meant by preserving virtue without weariness. In acting thus, how could he be deliberately applying his mind where it has no use, indulging in private worries and excessive calculations? Guarding against desires before they have sprouted is precisely the means to cut them off once they have sprouted. When this point is reached, principle is always the master and desire is always the transient guest; human artifice vanishes, and his original heavenly nature remains ever as it was at the beginning.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
是故虛然常明湛然常清性靜情恬神凝氣定
而妄思雜慮無所留也即其慆心適志之事日
交於前而隨過隨滅弗能擾也巧言勿聽諛說
勿容而震撼搖動弗能傾也尚何欲之能萌而
亦奚難於防哉何也彼其初固防之豫也豫故
不難也而成效所臻能使庶績凝百度貞德化
薰蒸蒼生康豫普天率土無呻吟咨籲之聲而
常有忻懽鼓舞之志相愉以樂相恬以熙相安
於太平無事之天而莫知誰氏之賜此防於未
===
萌之明驗也蓋古之善防者莫若周成王其詩
曰日就月將學有緝熙于光明曰光明者欲未
萌之初此心本然之天也曰就曰將曰緝熙無
時而不豫為之防也故成王之學至于基命宥
密克單厥心而四方日靖與二后比隆此善保
其初者也後世若漢武帝之悔輪臺唐太宗之
悔遼左感悼懲創惕然思幡然悟毅然而隨以
止非不稱知防也然而君子不滿焉以其能防
已萌而不知防未萌也是失之初而救於終汩
punctuated:
是故虛然常明，湛然常清，性靜情恬，神凝氣定，而妄思雜慮無所留也。即其慆心適志之事日交於前，而隨過隨滅，弗能擾也；巧言勿聽，諛說勿容，而震撼搖動，弗能傾也。尚何欲之能萌，而亦奚難於防哉？何也？彼其初固防之豫也，豫故不難也。而成效所臻，能使庶績凝、百度貞，德化薰蒸，蒼生康豫，普天率土無呻吟咨籲之聲，而常有忻懽鼓舞之志，相愉以樂，相恬以熙，相安於太平無事之天，而莫知誰氏之賜。此防於未萌之明驗也。
蓋古之善防者，莫若周成王。其《詩》曰：「日就月將，學有緝熙于光明。」曰「光明」者，欲未萌之初，此心本然之天也；曰「就」、曰「將」、曰「緝熙」，無時而不豫為之防也。故成王之學，至于「基命宥密，克單厥心」，而四方日靖，與二后比隆，此善保其初者也。後世若漢武帝之悔輪臺、唐太宗之悔遼左，感悼懲創，惕然思、幡然悟、毅然而隨以止，非不稱知防也，然而君子不滿焉，以其能防已萌，而不知防未萌也。是失之初而救於終，汩
translation_en:
Therefore, when the mind is vacuous and ever luminous, limpid and ever pure, the nature tranquil and the emotions serene, the spirit concentrated and the vital energy settled, then deluded thoughts and miscellaneous anxieties have nowhere to linger. Even if things that flatter the mind and please the will daily cross before one's eyes, they vanish as soon as they pass and cannot disturb one; artful words are not heeded, flattering speeches are not tolerated, and neither shock nor agitation can overturn one. What desires could still sprout, and what difficulty would there be in guarding against them? Why is this? Because at the very beginning one guarded against them beforehand; being prepared beforehand, it is not difficult. And the results achieved can cause the myriad accomplishments to be consolidated and all standards to be rectified; moral transformation permeates like rising vapor, and the common people enjoy health and comfort. Throughout the whole world, to the very borders of the land, there are no sounds of groaning or lamenting appeals, and instead there is always a spirit of joy and encouragement. People delight in one another with happiness, rest contentedly with one another in harmony, and live together in peace under a heaven of great tranquility free of incidents, without knowing whose gift it is. This is the clear proof of guarding against desires before they sprout.

Indeed, among those in antiquity who were skilled at guarding against desires, none surpassed King Cheng of Zhou 周成王. His Ode in the Book of Odes (Shijing) says: "With daily progress and monthly advance, I learn so as to have continuous brightness unto illumination." What is called "illumination" is the original heavenly nature of this mind at the beginning before desires have sprouted; what are called "progress," "advance," and "continuous brightness" mean that there is no moment when one is not taking precautions beforehand. Thus the learning of King Cheng reached the point where he "established the Mandate in deep and quiet breadth, able to exhaust his heart," so that the four quarters grew daily more tranquil and his rule rivaled the glory of the Two Former Kings. This was someone skilled at preserving his initial state. In later ages, cases such as Emperor Wu of Han 漢武帝 regretting his campaigns at Luntai 輪臺, or Emperor Taizong of Tang 唐太宗 regretting his campaigns in Liaozuo 遼左—being moved to grief and chastened by suffering, reflecting with alarm, awakening suddenly, and resolutely desisting forthwith—cannot be denied the name of knowing how to guard against desires. Yet the gentleman is dissatisfied with them, because they were able to guard against what had already sprouted, yet did not know how to guard against what had not yet sprouted. This is to lose it at the beginning and rescue it at the end, to be submerged…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於人而後復其天者也故其力弗豫而其功難
圖也故海內未耗輪臺之詔未肯下也遼俘果
獻班師之詔未可期也蓋萌成也一成而不肯
變故難防也然則人主奚防哉防於未萌而已
矣抑防又有要焉烏喙之毒也神農氏辨之掲
書以詔後世自古及今未有中其毒者之燕者
南行向于郢或告之曰此非適燕之路也遂反
焉故往哲遺言今世之明鑑也逆耳忠告岐路
之指南也今夫嗜欲之戕人不啻烏喙矣而古
===
訓備之理欲之殊塗不啻燕郢矣而明者能别
之然則人主欲防未萌之欲者其惟學古乎其
惟親賢乎善乎真德秀有言曰惟學可以養此
心惟賢人君子可以維持此心此防未萌之要
法也此又程氏未盡之旨也
表
擬宋御製爲君難爲臣不易論示輔臣謝
表〔祥符五年〕
陳堯言
punctuated:
於人而後復其天者也。故其力弗豫，而其功難圖也。故海內未耗，輪臺之詔未肯下也；遼俘果獻，班師之詔未可期也。蓋萌成也，一成而不肯變，故難防也。然則人主奚防哉？防於未萌而已矣。抑防又有要焉。烏喙之毒也，神農氏辨之，掲書以詔後世，自古及今，未有中其毒者。之燕者南行向于郢，或告之曰：「此非適燕之路也。」遂反焉。故往哲遺言，今世之明鑑也；逆耳忠告，岐路之指南也。今夫嗜欲之戕人，不啻烏喙矣，而古訓備之；理欲之殊塗，不啻燕郢矣，而明者能别之。然則人主欲防未萌之欲者，其惟學古乎！其惟親賢乎！善乎真德秀有言曰：「惟學可以養此心，惟賢人君子可以維持此心。」此防未萌之要法也，此又程氏未盡之旨也。
表
擬宋御製《爲君難爲臣不易論》示輔臣謝表〔祥符五年〕
陳堯言
translation_en:
…in human desires and only afterward recovering their heavenly nature. Therefore, their efforts were not made in advance, and their success was hard to achieve. Thus, had the realm within the seas not been exhausted, the edict of Luntai would not yet have been willingly issued; had captives from Liaodong actually been presented, the edict to withdraw the army could not have been expected. This is because the sprout had already grown; once formed, it refuses to change, and thus is difficult to guard against. How, then, should a ruler guard against desires? Simply by guarding against them before they sprout.

Moreover, there is an essential principle to such prevention. As for the poison of aconite (wuhui), the Divine Farmer (Shennong) identified it and posted writings to warn later generations, so that from antiquity to the present no one has been poisoned by it. When someone bound for Yan traveled south toward Ying, someone told him, "This is not the road to Yan," and he thereupon turned back. Therefore, the words left behind by past sages are a clear mirror for the present age, and loyal advice that grates on the ear is a south-pointing guide at the crossroads. Now, the way indulgent desires harm a person is even worse than aconite, yet ancient teachings have fully prepared us against them; the divergence between principle and desire is even greater than that between Yan and Ying, yet the clear-sighted are able to distinguish them. If so, when a ruler wishes to guard against desires before they sprout, lies it not solely in studying antiquity? Lies it not solely in drawing close to the worthy? Well did Zhen Dexiu 真德秀 say: "Only through learning can one nourish this mind; only worthy men and gentlemen can sustain this mind." This is the essential method for guarding against desires before they sprout, and this is also the meaning that Master Cheng had not fully exhausted.

Memorial (Biao)
Draft of a Song-dynasty Memorial of Thanks by Assisting Officials upon Being Shown the Imperially Composed Discourse "To Be a Ruler Is Difficult, to Be a Minister Is Not Easy" [Fifth year of the Xiangfu 祥符 era (1012)]
By Chen Yaoyan 陳堯言

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Tian: The conception of ideas and crafting of phrases mostly accord with refined style; this is not something an ordinary hand could achieve.

On a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of the Xiangfu reign [1012], having humbly received Sacred Grace in showing to your servants and others the Imperial Discourse on the Difficulty of Being a Ruler and the Uneasiness of Being a Minister, we respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude. Humbly we consider: When the Way harmonizes with the Two Primal Forces, the hexagram images of Fuxi reveal the mysteries of earth and heaven; when sageliness exalts Unified Virtue, the literary accomplishments of Yao radiate the splendor of the sun and moon. Bestowing favor like the hexagram Jin upon the chief ministers, and uniting ruler and subject like the hexagram Tai between the hall and the steps, we receive the imperial composition with bowed hands, and bear the admonitions of Shun engraved upon our hearts. Your servants So-and-so and others, in utmost awe and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground and respectfully state: We humbly reflect that though the Emperor is divinely sage, martial, and civil, in the subtle springs of action he is still strict about being cautious in his position; as ministers serve as…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
股肱耳目義必重於欽鄰故垂衣聽朝誥
興若采錫圭祗奏謨矢克艱歌勅明良虞
后絲綸駿發命休乂食商宗黼藻鴻宣湯
陟丕釐瞻九主而嚴三宅成基宥密鑒四
墉以翼十夫惟作聖述明用軫無虞之戒
故君仁臣直咸綿有道之長肆喜起之聲
希越諂驕之響應端居寳曆情罔繫乎苞
桑望重金鉉慮弗廑於覆餗箴規日隔駕

王心允眷於
天心
punctuated: 股肱耳目，義必重於欽鄰。故垂衣聽朝，誥興若采；錫圭祗奏，謨矢克艱。歌勅明良，虞后絲綸駿發；命休乂食，商宗黼藻鴻宣。湯陟丕釐，瞻九主而嚴三宅；成基宥密，鑒四墉以翼十夫。惟作聖述明，用軫無虞之戒；故君仁臣直，咸綿有道之長。肆喜起之聲希，越諂驕之響應。端居寳曆，情罔繫乎苞桑；望重金鉉，慮弗廑於覆餗。箴規日隔，駕言魚水之懽；倡和雷同，寧作鸑堂之處。集栢梁而歌詠，徒矜一豫一遊；宴凌煙以品題，孰誠同心同德？聖明天啓，輔弼雲從。玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，德合乾坤，文行風水。芝封玉檢，王心允眷於天心；
translation_en:
… [the sovereign's] limbs, ears, and eyes, their duty necessarily places great weight on revering the ruler's close associates. Therefore, when [Shun] let his robes hang down and held court, his announcements arose from seeking out those who would match their actions to their words; when [Yu], having been bestowed the jade tablet, respectfully presented his report, his counsels vowed to realize the difficulty [of being ruler and minister]. Singing the admonition of the enlightened ruler and worthy ministers, the sovereign of Yu [Shun] swiftly issued his silken words; commanding the fine seasoning of the soup, the high ancestor of Shang [Wu Ding] grandly proclaimed his ornate compositions. When Tang ascended to bring great order, Yi Zhi looked back upon the nine types of rulers and strictly upheld the three appointments; when King Cheng established his foundation in serene profundity, [the Duke of Zhou] took warning from the four walls [of the states] to assist the ten worthy men. Only because the sage creates and the enlightened transmits do they take to heart the warning against unforeseen perils; thus, when the ruler is benevolent and the ministers are upright, together they prolong the endurance of a state that possesses the Way.

When the sounds of "rejoicing and rising up" grew rare, the echoes of flattery and arrogance responded in turn. Sitting upright upon the precious throne, [rulers'] sentiments were no longer bound to the "bushy mulberry" [of dynastic stability]; enjoying prestige as heavy as the golden rings of the tripod, [ministers'] anxieties no longer dwelt upon "overturning the tripod's contents." As remonstrance and regulation grew daily more distant, they falsely spoke of the joy of fish and water; as their lead and response became mere blind echoing, how could they heed the dwelling like a swallow in a hall [about to burn]? Gathering at the Cypress Beam Terrace (Boliang tai) to chant and sing, they merely boasted of a single excursion or a single diversion; feasting at the Lingyan Pavilion to evaluate and inscribed rankings, who among them was truly of one heart and one virtue?

Sacred enlightenment is opened by Heaven, and auxiliar ministers follow like clouds. This is indeed because we humbly encounter Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇]: your virtue matches Heaven and Earth, and your cultural patterns move like wind over water. With ganoderma-sealed letters and jade-clasped slips, the King's mind truly accords with Heaven's mind; …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
藻思瑶編
君道率先乎臣道欹器有
賛仰
龍德之正中崇術敷言識
鴻猷之廣大邇於
萬幾之暇永念一言之艱謂
九重繫四海之安危豈容逸豫而百僚共
一人之休戚寧事逢迎誕啓
玄精親揮
===
宸翰紬繹乎無怠無荒之旨反覆乎多譽多懼
之占敘感遇而興思冰淵咸惕勉正直以
行事蓍蔡永懷
先后謨謀廣著
席前之問累朝得失釐繙
座右之藏
帝典
皇猷禹皐服之無斁
金聲玉振游夏賛而莫能
punctuated: 藻思瑶編，君道率先乎臣道。欹器有賛，仰龍德之正中；崇術敷言，識鴻猷之廣大。邇於萬幾之暇，永念一言之艱。謂九重繫四海之安危，豈容逸豫；而百僚共一人之休戚，寧事逢迎。誕啓玄精，親揮宸翰。紬繹乎「無怠無荒」之旨，反覆乎「多譽多懼」之占。敘感遇而興思，冰淵咸惕；勉正直以行事，蓍蔡永懷。先后謨謀，廣著席前之問；累朝得失，釐繙座右之藏。帝典皇猷，禹、皐服之無斁；金聲玉振，游、夏賛而莫能。
translation_en: …with ornate thoughts and jade-like compilations, the Way of the Ruler leads the Way of the Minister. With a eulogy on the tilting vessel, we look up to the Centered Correctness of Your Dragon Virtue; exalting arts and setting forth words, we recognize the vastness of Your Great Plan. Recently, in the leisure from Your myriad affairs of state, You have perpetually reflected on the difficulty of a single word. You declare that the Ninefold Palace is bound to the security and peril of the Four Seas—how could ease and indulgence be permitted?—and that the hundred officials share the joys and sorrows of the One Man—how could they engage in flattery and compliance? Grandly opening Your profound spirit, You personally wield the Imperial brush. You draw out and ponder the meaning of "without idleness, without荒 [neglect]," and repeatedly examine the divination of "much praise and much fear." Recounting how auspicious encounters inspire reflection, all are as cautious as if on thin ice or by a deep abyss; urging uprightness in the conduct of affairs, You forever cherish the milfoil and tortoise shell of divination. The counsels and plans of former rulers are broadly set forth in the inquiries before Your mat; the successes and failures of successive reigns are carefully unrolled from the repository beside Your seat. Such Imperial canons and august plans, Yu and Gao Yao would submit to without ever growing weary; such golden sound and jade vibration, Ziyou and Zixia could not add a word of praise to…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詔發西崑製恢唐體
文躔東壁雅邁漢風展
寶卷於
黼扆首頒芸閣橫牙籤於
御禁副載蘭臺眷茲
上下之交奚啻腹心之感臣等俯慙石畫仰荷
珍符誦
帝德之罔愆莫裨高厚代天工之無曠未效涓
埃拜
===
錫百朋色動青藜之影捧聯什襲光生
紫泥之封敢不刻以丹衷期遠垂乎竹帛佩
茲素志謝近取於韋弦致
君深戒面從論事何妨骨鯁蹇王臣而附鳳舉
矢竭微忠歌天保以報鹿鳴益祈
戩穀遵
德音於補衮悟
雅意於忘筌伏願
君君臣臣兢兢業業
punctuated: 詔發西崑，製恢唐體；文躔東壁，雅邁漢風。展寶卷於黼扆，首頒芸閣；橫牙籤於御禁，副載蘭臺。眷茲上下之交，奚啻腹心之感！臣等俯慙石畫，仰荷珍符。誦帝德之罔愆，莫裨高厚；代天工之無曠，未效涓埃。拜錫百朋，色動青藜之影；捧聯什襲，光生紫泥之封。敢不刻以丹衷，期遠垂乎竹帛；佩茲素志，謝近取於韋弦。致君深戒面從，論事何妨骨鯁。蹇王臣而附鳳舉，矢竭微忠；歌《天保》以報《鹿鳴》，益祈戩穀。遵德音於補衮，悟雅意於忘筌。伏願君君臣臣，兢兢業業；
translation_en: When edicts issue from the Western Kunlun—the imperial library—their composition expands upon the style of the Tang; when literary brilliance traverses the Eastern Wall constellation, its elegance surpasses the manner of the Han. Unrolling the precious scrolls before theaxe-embroidered imperial screen, they are first bestowed upon the Rue Pavilion; arraying the ivory book-tags within the imperial precincts, duplicate copies are stored in the Orchid Terrace. Contemplating this communion between ruler above and ministers below, how could it be merely the gratitude of heart and core! Your servants, looking down, are ashamed of the inadequacy of our rock-solid plans, while looking up, we bear the grace of this precious talisman. Reciting the flawlessness of the Imperial Virtue, we have added nothing to its height and depth; acting on behalf of Heaven's work so that nothing is neglected, we have yet to contribute a single drop or grain of dust. Bowing to receive a hundred sets of cowries, our countenances are stirred by the glow of the green goosefoot staff; holding up the bound volumes wrapped tenfold, radiance springs from their purple-clay seals. How dare we not engrave them upon our loyal hearts, hoping to hand them down far into the future on bamboo and silk; wearing these pure intentions at our sashes, we have no further need of the leather strap and bowstring for immediate self-correction. In serving our Sovereign, we deeply guard against mere surface compliance; in discussing affairs of state, what harm is there in outspoken candor? Toiling as the King's ministers and clinging to the phoenix's flight, we swear to exhaust our humble loyalty; singing "Heaven Protects" (Tianbao) in answer to "The Deer Cry" (Luming), we pray all the more for every blessing and felicity. Following Your virtuous words to mend the imperial robes, we comprehend Your refined intent even to the forgetting of the fish-trap once the fish is caught. We humbly wish that ruler be ruler and minister be minister, cautious and conscientious, …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
臨民若馭朽敬懷可願之脩
從諫如轉圜懋延交儆之益禹湯文武媲千
古而凝
配帝之圖稷契伊周聚一堂而建
格天之治臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
===
聞
第叄場
策
第一問
王建中
同考試官教諭陳批仁孝立說足以仰誦
聖天子格天錫極之蘊而援據明實可錄
同考試官教諭黃批敷陳合祀養老之議甚爲
明悉宜錄以式
punctuated:
臨民若馭朽，敬懷可願之脩；從諫如轉圜，懋延交儆之益。禹、湯、文、武媲千古而凝配帝之圖，稷、契、伊、周聚一堂而建格天之治。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叄場
策
第一問
王建中
同考試官教諭陳批：仁孝立說，足以仰誦聖天子格天錫極之蘊，而援據明實，可錄。
同考試官教諭黃批：敷陳合祀、養老之議，甚爲明悉，宜錄以式。
translation_en:
…in governing the people, be as cautious as if driving a team of horses with rotten reins, reverently cherishing the cultivation of desirable virtues; in following remonstrance, be as swift as turning a wheel, diligently extending the benefits of mutual admonition. Thus you will rival Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu across a thousand ages in consolidating the grand plan of matching Heaven, while ministers like Hou Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou gather in a single hall to establish a governance that reaches to Heaven. Your servants, overcome with the utmost awe and earnest devotion as we gaze up at Heaven and look toward Your Sacred Majesty, respectfully present this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Wang Jianzhong 
Associate Examiner Instructor Chen comments: Grounding the argument in benevolence and filial piety suffices to reverently extol the profound essence of the Sacred Son of Heaven reaching Heaven and bestowing the highest standard of perfection, while the citations are clear and substantive; it is worthy of selection.
Associate Examiner Instructor Huang comments: The exposition of the discussions on joint sacrifices and nourishing the elderly is exceedingly clear and thorough; it should be selected to serve as a model.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭林批敷答詳明引據切當
考試官教諭吳批援禮議制卓然有見
帝王之會作述而垂典禮也有格天之至
仁而昭事於不匱有法聖之達孝而錫極
於無方夫禮有本也有文也而考禮者貴
繹其義行禮者貴返諸古是故王者爲天
元子於是有升中饗帝之禮焉無非所以
達類禋之馨德迓眷顧之顯休也抑豈徒
以肅雝陟降焉哉是必有精通天地者相
===
凝會焉而合祀之議則凝之之大端也作
民君師於是有釋奠臨雍之禮焉無非所
以示尊聖之謙光廣崇儒之弘德也抑豈
徒以屈體侈觀已哉是必有孝治天下者
相風勸焉而養老之議則風之之大要也
然禮有屢更於制作而習於因者憚變易
之難禮有常行於曠古而廢於久者詘脩
復之迂方今
聖天子格天之德懋敬於
punctuated:
考試官教諭林批：敷答詳明，引據切當。
考試官教諭吳批：援禮議制，卓然有見。

帝王之會作述而垂典禮也，有格天之至仁而昭事於不匱，有法聖之達孝而錫極於無方。夫禮有本也，有文也；而考禮者貴繹其義，行禮者貴返諸古。是故王者爲天元子，於是有升中饗帝之禮焉，無非所以達類禋之馨德，迓眷顧之顯休也。抑豈徒以肅雝陟降焉哉？是必有精通天地者相凝會焉，而合祀之議則凝之之大端也。作民君師，於是有釋奠臨雍之禮焉，無非所以示尊聖之謙光，廣崇儒之弘德也。抑豈徒以屈體侈觀已哉？是必有孝治天下者相風勸焉，而養老之議則風之之大要也。然禮有屢更於制作，而習於因者憚變易之難；禮有常行於曠古，而廢於久者詘脩復之迂。方今聖天子格天之德懋敬於
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: The exposition and answers are detailed and clear, and the citations are apt and fitting.
Examiner and Instructor Wu comments: Citing ritual principles to discuss institutional regulations, it displays outstanding insight.

When emperors and kings bring together creation and transmission to hand down canonical rituals, they possess the utmost benevolence that reaches Heaven and manifest their service unceasingly; they possess the far-reaching filial piety that models itself on the sages and bestows the highest standard without bounds. Now, ritual has its root and its outward form; those who investigate ritual value unfolding its meaning, while those who practice ritual value returning to antiquity. Therefore, the true king is the eldest son of Heaven, and thus there is the ritual of ascending to offer the central sacrifice and feasting the Supreme Ancestor. This is nothing other than the means to convey the fragrant virtue of the special and pure sacrifices, and to welcome the manifest blessings of Heaven's favor. Yet how could it merely be a matter of solemn harmony in ascending and descending? There must be a spiritual communion with Heaven and Earth that coalesces therein, and the deliberation on joint sacrifice is the great key to coalescing it. Acting as ruler and teacher of the people, there is thus the ritual of offering libations to the former sages and visiting the Imperial University.
