title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
公而風之潰也不可返巳他日猶諄切于
野史之辨不遜寧固之譏而寤寐憲章則
惟先進是從焉孔子非不知頹波之横流
而力爲之障其情則誠亟也嗟乎知孔子
維周之意則今日誠不容以不汲汲矣洪
惟我
太祖定鼎開基首崇風教以浙服爲文獻峩冕
靈秀鬱鍾金華一莅啓萬年文治之精華
于時懸禮樂而置軌範家稷契而人皐陶
===
卽山陬海澨咸翕然相逐淳謹官府斂董
治之威閭閻聞頌聲之作鄉之老成猶能
談浙之舊事乃今之浙固昔之浙而今之
習則殊非昔之習矣故杭承先朝繁華又
舟車所輳湖山所環其四方之游士賈客
肩摩踵躡風會趨靡遂日流於好蕩而無
節其西郡澤菹田疇殖餉攸資民俗多饒
而繁文競侈不免喜事之嫌又其甚則私
艇出沒群猾所淵藪也其東郡聲名文物
punctuated: 公，而風之潰也不可返巳。他日猶諄切于「野」、「史」之辨，「不遜」、「寧固」之譏，而寤寐憲章，則惟「先進」是從焉。孔子非不知頹波之横流，而力爲之障，其情則誠亟也。嗟乎！知孔子維周之意，則今日誠不容以不汲汲矣。洪惟我太祖定鼎開基，首崇風教，以浙服爲文獻峩冕，靈秀鬱鍾，金華一莅，啓萬年文治之精華。于時懸禮樂而置軌範，家稷、契而人皐陶，卽山陬海澨，咸翕然相逐淳謹。官府斂董治之威，閭閻聞頌聲之作，鄉之老成猶能談浙之舊事。乃今之浙固昔之浙，而今之習則殊非昔之習矣。故杭承先朝繁華，又舟車所輳，湖山所環，其四方之游士賈客，肩摩踵躡，風會趨靡，遂日流於好蕩而無節。其西郡澤菹田疇，殖餉攸資，民俗多饒，而繁文競侈，不免喜事之嫌；又其甚則私艇出沒，群猾所淵藪也。其東郡聲名文物，
translation_en:
… Duke of Zhou, the collapse of customs could never have been reversed. On other occasions, he still earnestly emphasized the distinction between being "rustic" and being "pedantic," and expressed his disapproval in the remark that "rather than being presumptuous, it is better to be stubborn," while in his waking and sleeping thoughts of modeling himself on the ancient institutions, he declared that he would follow the "men of former times." It was not that Confucius failed to realize how the decadent tide was overflowing everywhere, yet he strove with all his might to dam it up; his concern was truly urgent. Alas! If one understands Confucius's intention in upholding the Zhou, then today we truly cannot afford not to be just as urgently devoted to the task.

Reflecting upon how our Grand Progenitor established the dynasty and laid the foundations of the empire, he first of all revered moral instruction and customs. Taking the Zhejiang region to be a towering crown of scholarly heritage and refined culture, where spiritual excellence was richly concentrated, his single visit to Jinhua的金華 opened up the quintessential brilliance of ten thousand years of civil governance. At that time, rites and music were held aloft and standards and models were instituted; every family aspired to be like Hou Ji and Xie, and every person like Gao Yao. Even in remote mountain corners and along distant sea shores, all harmoniously pursued pure and conscientious ways together. Government offices reined in the severity of their supervision and punishments, while among the village lanes could be heard the rising sounds of praise; the venerable elders of the countryside can still recount the old affairs of Zhejiang.

Yet the Zhejiang of today is certainly the same Zhejiang as of old, whereas the customs of today are altogether different from the customs of the past! Thus, Hangzhou has inherited the flourishing splendor of former dynasties; moreover, it is a hub where boats and carriages converge, surrounded by lakes and mountains. Traveling scholars and merchants from all four directions rub shoulders and follow close on one another's heels there. The prevailing ethos tends toward extravagance, and so day by day it slides into a fondness for dissipation without restraint. In the western prefectures, with their marshes and cultivated fields upon which production and provisions depend, the popular customs are mostly marked by affluence; yet people compete in elaborate formalities and luxury, not escaping the suspicion of being overly fond of meddlesome display. Where it is even worse, illicit boats appear and disappear, making the area a haven for bands of cunning miscreants. In the eastern prefectures, renowned for cultural prestige and refinement, …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詩書比屋民俗多慧而嗇業尚虚稍沿江
左之習又其甚則齒繁射利游食所四出
也上游諸郡睦之俗簡訟而奉公較爲寡
尤然業貧而惰事亦縁以積困至婺衢之
墟衣冠淳龐猶有先民之遺然訐而好鬭
勇而尚氣乃家藏戈矛視殺人僅若草菅
則其居使之然矣甌栝之俗奢儉異習亦
有近古之稱然負山阻海均爲遠屬乃法
令多玩積逋賦且至千萬則其流之弊乆
===
矣習俗之異若此是豈振古如兹而竟莫
可挽耶愚聞之上化下謂之風下從上謂
之俗言應也又曰上行下效謂之風衆心
安定謂之俗言機也故風之所在不兵革
而威不燎揚而焰不迅雷而厲不戴星而
馳有移風之責者亦愼其所以風之而已
矣夫三家之市十金之貲乃中人所恃以
卒歲而不至展轉流離於中路者也然能
儉約以居之則用享延年使奢靡以繼之
punctuated: 詩書比屋，民俗多慧而嗇業，尚虚，稍沿江左之習；又其甚，則齒繁射利，游食所四出也。上游諸郡，睦之俗簡訟而奉公，較爲寡尤，然業貧而惰事，亦縁以積困。至婺、衢之墟，衣冠淳龐，猶有先民之遺，然訐而好鬭，勇而尚氣，乃家藏戈矛，視殺人僅若草菅，則其居使之然矣。甌、栝之俗，奢儉異習，亦有近古之稱，然負山阻海，均爲遠屬，乃法令多玩，積逋賦且至千萬，則其流之弊乆矣。習俗之異若此，是豈振古如兹，而竟莫可挽耶？愚聞之：「上化下謂之風，下從上謂之俗」，言應也；又曰：「上行下效謂之風，衆心安定謂之俗」，言機也。故風之所在，不兵革而威，不燎揚而焰，不迅雷而厲，不戴星而馳。有移風之責者，亦愼其所以風之而已矣。夫三家之市、十金之貲，乃中人所恃以卒歲，而不至展轉流離於中路者也。然能儉約以居之，則用享延年；使奢靡以繼之，
translation_en:
…with classical learning in every house; the customs of the people are mostly clever, yet they are sparing in productive livelihoods and value empty show, somewhat following the habits of Jiangzuo (the lower Yangtze region). At its worst, the population is dense and pursues profit, so that itinerant idlers go out in all directions to make a living.

Among the prefectures further upstream, the customs of Mu (Yanzhou) are sparing in litigation and law-abiding, having relatively few faults; yet their livelihoods are poor and they are lax in their affairs, and because of this they accumulate hardship. As for the territories of Wu (Jinhua) and Qu (Quzhou), their gentry are simple and substantial, still retaining the legacy of the people of antiquity; yet they are contentious and fond of fighting, bold and given to temper, so that families hide away halberds and spears and regard killing a person merely as cutting grass—it is their environment that makes them so. In the customs of Ou (Wenzhou) and Gua (Chuzhou), extravagance and frugality differ in practice, and they also have a reputation for being close to antiquity; yet backed by mountains and blocked by the sea, both are remote dependencies, where laws and ordinances are often trifled with and accumulated tax arrears reach into the tens of millions—the abuses of this trend have lasted a long time indeed.

That the differences in customs are like this—could it really have been so since antiquity, and in the end be impossible to reverse? I have heard it said: "When superiors transform inferiors, it is called wind (moral influence); when inferiors follow superiors, it is called custom"—this speaks of responsiveness. And it is also said: "When superiors act and inferiors imitate, it is called wind; when the hearts of the multitude are settled, it is called custom"—this speaks of the motivating mechanism. Therefore, where moral influence resides, without weapons and armor it is awe-inspiring, without a fanned blaze it flames up, without swift thunder it is fierce, and without traveling under the stars it speeds forth. Those who bear the responsibility of transforming customs need only be careful about that by which they influence them!

Now, a market of three households and property worth ten pieces of gold are what persons of middling means rely upon to get through the year without coming to toss about as refugees along the road. Yet if one can dwell in them with frugality and restraint, one will enjoy sufficiency and prolong one's years; whereas if one continues them with extravagance and waste…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則立見傾覆此其明效大驗者况進三家
十金而上之者乎今環淅之境有獻酬而
動費數金竭其身力以奉者有作嬪而傾
貲無量不足則稱貸以益者奔走之僕紈
綺相炫輿臺之輩絢縟爭侈不知在上之
章德何物也專業樗蒲延招朋類轉瞬一
擲蓋藏靡遺不知注孤而盜起相繼也披
緇髠髮寔繁有徒寶觀崇菴侈隆鼎建是
不可以不急汰也振履連翩競標姱麗結
===
駟絡繹馳騖冶容是不可以不急逐也里
閈富强偃仰瞪盻浚貧民之錐刀以冒道
家之忌所謂陸梁其性也是不可以不重
懲也少年遊俠黨附逍遙飛終日之崇觴
以起遊觀之艷所謂蜉蝣其習也是不可
以不亟屏也見隸戎籍用之本省所謂練
土著者誠以是矣而各省徵募復且歲至
安可不蚤杜以塞其流乎歲輸課額朘剥
艱阻所繇免漕輓者誠以是矣而本郡餉
punctuated: 則立見傾覆，此其明效大驗者，况進三家十金而上之者乎？今環淅之境，有獻酬而動費數金，竭其身力以奉者；有作嬪而傾貲無量，不足則稱貸以益者；奔走之僕，紈綺相炫，輿臺之輩，絢縟爭侈，不知在上之章德何物也。專業樗蒲，延招朋類，轉瞬一擲，蓋藏靡遺，不知注孤而盜起相繼也。披緇髠髮，寔繁有徒，寶觀崇菴，侈隆鼎建，是不可以不急汰也。振履連翩，競標姱麗，結駟絡繹，馳騖冶容，是不可以不急逐也。里閈富强，偃仰瞪盻，浚貧民之錐刀，以冒道家之忌，所謂陸梁其性也，是不可以不重懲也。少年遊俠，黨附逍遙，飛終日之崇觴，以起遊觀之艷，所謂蜉蝣其習也，是不可以不亟屏也。見隸戎籍，用之本省，所謂練土著者誠以是矣；而各省徵募，復且歲至，安可不蚤杜以塞其流乎？歲輸課額，朘剥艱阻，所繇免漕輓者誠以是矣；而本郡餉…
translation_en: …then its ruin will be seen immediately. This is a clear and great proof; how much more so for what goes beyond a market of three households or a fortune of ten pieces of gold? Nowadays, throughout the territory of Zhejiang, there are those who in hosting banquets readily spend several pieces of gold, exhausting their own strength to provide for them; there are those who in marrying off daughters pour out limitless wealth, and when it is insufficient, take out loans to add to it. Errand-running servants show off their fine white silks to one another, and menial attendants compete in gorgeous extravagance, not knowing what the emblems of virtue of those above even are. Those who make a profession of gambling invite and gather their associates, and with a single throw in the blink of an eye, their stored savings are completely gone—not realizing that when their stakes are exhausted, banditry arises in succession. Those who don black robes and shave their heads truly have numerous followers, and precious Daoist temples and lofty Buddhist retreats are built with extravagant grandeur; these cannot but be urgently culled. Those who trail their shoes in a continuous stream, competing to display their alluring finery, or hitch up teams of four horses in an unbroken line, galloping after seductive appearances; these cannot but be urgently expelled. The rich and powerful of the neighborhood villages act haughtily and glare about, draining the petty profits of poor commoners and thereby defying the taboos of the Daoists—this is what is called having an unruly nature, and it cannot but be severely punished. Young wandering gallants form cliques and roam at ease, sending tall goblets flying all day long to stir up envy in sightseeing—this is what is called having the habits of mayflies, and they cannot but be promptly banished. Those currently registered on the military rolls are employed within this province; what is called training local troops is truly for this reason. Yet conscription and recruitment from various provinces still arrive year after year—how can we not block this early on so as to stop the flow? The annual tax quotas delivered are subject to exploitation and difficult obstructions; the reason they are exempted from canal transport is truly for this reason. Yet this prefecture's military provisioning…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
額復且歲逋安可不嚴覈以懲其玩乎凡
若是者均於習俗爲累非細故也顧風會
之趨今之各郡俱互有之靡靡風塵悠悠
歲月其所由來有漸矣玆欲捄之其道何
繇董子曰質樸之謂性性非敎化不成人
欲之謂情情非制度不節今之敝也無它
敎化不章而制度未壹也夫蓬之蔓生匪
麻弗直水之就下匪堤弗止誠使崇奬恬
澹抑黜澆漓遵漢詔之孝弟力田禁吳客
===
之短纓曼胡寧用萬石之恂恂謹厚勿取
嗇夫之喋喋利口而又彷夫里之罰酌農
桑之條申車服宮室之等約冠昏喪祭之
儀諸凡名器攸存者雖繁纓無所假借講
飮射讀法之禮聯比閭族黨之衆俾父老
相慰於農畮少年相戒於出疆而游食有
禁俠邪有禁作奇技淫巧者有禁操戈矛
而相目從軍者有禁如是而時察其化訓
之民表宅里而樹之風聲簡其弗率之民
punctuated: 額復且歲逋，安可不嚴覈以懲其玩乎？凡若是者，均於習俗爲累，非細故也。顧風會之趨，今之各郡俱互有之，靡靡風塵，悠悠歲月，其所由來有漸矣。玆欲捄之，其道何繇？董子曰：「質樸之謂性，性非敎化不成；人欲之謂情，情非制度不節。」今之敝也無它，敎化不章而制度未壹也。夫蓬之蔓生，匪麻弗直；水之就下，匪堤弗止。誠使崇奬恬澹，抑黜澆漓，遵漢詔之孝弟力田，禁吳客之短纓曼胡，寧用萬石之恂恂謹厚，勿取嗇夫之喋喋利口；而又彷夫里之罰，酌農桑之條，申車服宮室之等，約冠昏喪祭之儀，諸凡名器攸存者，雖繁纓無所假借；講飮射讀法之禮，聯比閭族黨之衆，俾父老相慰於農畮，少年相戒於出疆，而游食有禁，俠邪有禁，作奇技淫巧者有禁，操戈矛而相目從軍者有禁；如是，而時察其化訓之民，表宅里而樹之風聲，簡其弗率之民，
translation_en:
…supply quotas are furthermore in arrears year after year—how can we not strictly audit them to punish their negligence? All such matters alike burden our customs and are no trivial affairs. Yet looking at the trend of prevailing mores, the various prefectures today all share in these traits to one degree or another; amid decadent worldly currents and the long passage of years and months, they have come about gradually. If we now wish to remedy them, what way should we follow?

Master Dong [Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒] said: "Unadorned simplicity is called human nature, and human nature is not perfected without moral transformation and instruction; human desires are called the emotions, and the emotions are not regulated without institutional rules." The abuses of today stem from nothing else than that moral instruction is not made manifest and institutional rules are not unified. Indeed, when fleabane grows wild and sprawling, without hemp to support it, it will not stand straight; when water flows downward, without dikes, it will not be stopped. If we truly honor and encourage quiet modesty while suppressing and dismissing thin and decadent mores; follow the Han imperial edicts promoting filial piety, fraternal submission, and diligent farming, and prohibit the short cap-strings and coarse robes of the swordsmen of Wu; prefer to employ the deferential and cautious honesty of Lord Wanshi [Shi奮] rather than choose the glib and sharp-tongued chatter of the petty bailiff [at Shanglin]; and furthermore imitate the penalties of the labor-levy and neighborhood taxes [of the Rites of Zhou], deliberate upon regulations for agriculture and sericulture, reiterate the gradations of carriages, vestments, and dwellings, and restrain the ceremonies of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice, so that in all matters where titles and insignia of rank are concerned, not even a decorative horse-girth is improperly conceded; expound the rites of the community wine-drinking, archery, and reading of the laws, and bind together the multitudes of five-family, twenty-five-family, hundred-family, and five-hundred-family neighborhoods, causing the elders to comfort one another in the farmed fields and the youths to warn one another against leaving their home boundaries; while placing prohibitions on idle consumers, prohibitions on wandering knights-errant and wicked ways, prohibitions on those who craft strange contrivances and extravagant curiosities, and prohibitions on those who grasp halberds and spears and eye one another to join the army; if we act thus, and from time to time inspect the people who have been transformed and instructed, erecting emblems at their homes and neighborhoods to establish a moral example, while singling out the people who do not comply…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
殊井疆而俾之畏慕庶幾乎制度以壹然
後教化以章教化章然後人心以古人心
古然後風俗以淳起敝維風之道意者不
出乎此也然此特論其政令當先禁革當
急而其本猶不在是申公曰爲治不在多
言顧力行何如耳故有一朱子而男女不
敢入僧廬有一楊綰而宴座音樂減十之
七今之司世教者其果端諸意嚮運諸精
神由躬行而表帥之又鄉之宦達相與羽
===
翼而倡導於邑里民之俊秀相與講明而
率先於黌校刋爲定則著爲章程鄉約以
此而示旌别保甲以此而犁苗莠無上下
賢愚無遠近大小咸使變聽改觀回心而
嚮道間猶有言不顧行實不中聲是薄惡
之尤孔子相魯所以首正于兩觀而不可
使一日梗化于明盛者也夫表帥既端則
鄉黨知慕禁令既肅則黎庶懷刑省會先
舉則僻壤嚮風持之以有恒積之以歲月
punctuated: 殊井疆而俾之畏慕。庶幾乎制度以壹，然後教化以章；教化章，然後人心以古；人心古，然後風俗以淳。起敝維風之道，意者不出乎此也。然此特論其政令當先、禁革當急，而其本猶不在是。申公曰：「爲治不在多言，顧力行何如耳。」故有一朱子，而男女不敢入僧廬；有一楊綰，而宴座音樂減十之七。今之司世教者，其果端諸意嚮、運諸精神，由躬行而表帥之；又鄉之宦達相與羽翼而倡導於邑里，民之俊秀相與講明而率先於黌校。刋爲定則，著爲章程；鄉約以此而示旌别，保甲以此而犁苗莠。無上下賢愚，無遠近大小，咸使變聽改觀，回心而嚮道。間猶有言不顧行、實不中聲，是薄惡之尤，孔子相魯所以首正于兩觀，而不可使一日梗化于明盛者也。夫表帥既端，則鄉黨知慕；禁令既肅，則黎庶懷刑；省會先舉，則僻壤嚮風。持之以有恒，積之以歲月，
translation_en: … segregate their neighborhood boundaries so as to make them feel both awe and admiration. Perhaps through this, institutions will be unified, and only then will moral transformation become manifest; when moral transformation is manifest, human minds will return to the ways of antiquity; and when human minds return to the ways of antiquity, customs will become pure and honest. The way to remedy decay and uphold good customs presumably does not go beyond this. Yet this merely discusses what administrative orders ought to be prioritized and what prohibitions and reforms are urgent—the fundamental root still does not lie herein. Master Shen (Shen Gong) said: "Governance does not lie in many words; it depends only on how earnestly one puts it into practice." Thus, when there was a single Master Zhu (Zhu Xi), men and women dared not enter Buddhist monasteries; when there was a single Yang Wan, music at banquets was reduced by seven-tenths. If those in charge of the moral instruction of the world today truly rectify their intentions and direct their spiritual energy, leading the way by personal example; and if, moreover, the prominent officials of the local communities join in assisting and taking the initiative in the towns and villages, while the talented scholars among the people join in elucidating these principles and setting the precedent in the schools; and if these are carved into fixed rules and set forth as formal regulations, whereby the community compacts (xiangyue) use them to display distinctions of honor and disgrace, and the mutual security system (baojia) uses them to weed out the tares from the good grain—then, regardless of whether high or low, worthy or foolish, far or near, great or small, all will be made to change what they hear and alter what they see, turning their hearts toward the Way. Should there still be among them those whose words do not match their deeds and whose reality does not correspond to their reputation, these are the worst of the shallow and wicked—the very sort whom Confucius, when serving as prime minister of Lu, first executed beneath the Two Watchtowers, and who must not be allowed for a single day to obstruct moral transformation in an enlightened and flourishing age. Indeed, once leadership by example is upright, the local communities will know what to admire; once prohibitions and orders are strict, the common people will be mindful of punishments; and once the provincial capital takes the lead, remote regions will turn toward the wind of reform. Holding to this with constancy and accumulating results over the months and years, …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
將見侈者可使約薄者可使敦輕生者變
賈勇之習逐末者返力本之圖而謂全浙
之民有不迪德承休遵行古道者否也由
是上追成周忠厚太平之盛仰符
國初樸素醇謹之遺而孔子從先進之意其
在玆乎語不云乎日中必彗操刀必割又
曰日中則昃月盈則食隨其盈虛與時消
息識其弊而亟反之誠今日所當轉移而
斡旋者若行一事曰煩苛也布一令曰操
===
切也相安上下和同之爲功而不知挽回
風俗之爲急是失明彗剸割之方昧盈虛
消息之道俗之衰奚有已也而況四方之
偷靡尤有逾倍於浙者其杞人之憂又當
何如也睹時感事烏得而不廩廩惟執事
重圖之
第五問
秦應鵬
同考試官教諭畢 批 此策以移風易俗爲弭盜
punctuated:
將見侈者可使約，薄者可使敦，輕生者變賈勇之習，逐末者返力本之圖，而謂全浙之民有不迪德承休、遵行古道者？否也。由是上追成周忠厚太平之盛，仰符國初樸素醇謹之遺，而孔子從先進之意，其在玆乎！語不云乎：「日中必彗，操刀必割。」又曰：「日中則昃，月盈則食。」隨其盈虛，與時消息。識其弊而亟反之，誠今日所當轉移而斡旋者。若行一事，曰「煩苛也」；布一令，曰「操切也」。相安上下和同之爲功，而不知挽回風俗之爲急，是失明彗剸割之方，昧盈虛消息之道，俗之衰奚有已也？而況四方之偷靡，尤有逾倍於浙者，其杞人之憂，又當何如也！睹時感事，烏得而不廩廩？惟執事重圖之。

第五問
秦應鵬
同考試官教諭畢批：此策以移風易俗爲弭盜
translation_en:
…Then we shall see that the extravagant can be made frugal, the mean-spirited can be made generous, those who take life lightly will abandon their habit of showing off bravado, and those who pursue secondary occupations will return to the endeavor of working at the fundamental [agriculture]. Under such circumstances, could it be said that the people of the entire Zhejiang region would fail to walk in virtue, receive blessings, and follow the ancient Way? Certainly not. Thus we may trace back above to the flourishing loyalty, generosity, and grand peace of the Accomplished Zhou, and conform reverently to the legacy of simplicity, purity, and prudence from the founding of our dynasty. Does not Confucius's intention in "following the men of former times" lie right here! Does the saying not go: "When the sun is at midday, one must dry things in it; when holding a knife, one must cut with it"? And it is also said: "When the sun reaches midday, it declines; when the moon is full, it wanes." Following their waxing and waning, one adapts to the cycle of growth and decline over time. Recognizing these abuses and urgently reversing them is truly what must be transformed and turned around today. If, whenever a single measure is carried out, people say, "It is overly petty and harsh!"; and whenever a single order is promulgated, they say, "It is overly hasty and severe!"—being content to regard superficial harmony between superiors and inferiors as a merit, while not knowing that reversing the decline of customs is an urgent priority—this is to lose the method of drying in the bright sun and decisive cutting, and to be blind to the principle of waxing, waning, growth, and decline. How then would the decay of customs ever come to an end? Moreover, when the frivolity and extravagance of the four quarters are even doubly worse than in Zhejiang, how much greater still must be one's anxiety, like the man of Qi [who worried the sky might fall]! Observing the times and being moved by events, how can one not tremble with trepidation? I pray only that Your Excellency give this weighty consideration.

Question Five
Qin Yingpeng 秦應鵬
Associate Examiner Instructor Bi 畢 comments: This policy essay takes transforming customs and habits as the…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之原誠非謾語
考試官教諭林批策末尤究極於爲政得人
足徵經濟之略
考試官教諭吳批學博才優
聖王疆畫天下犁若土田然民譬則穀也
官司者所以耘耔非種而佐之植者也寒
暑失節雨暘愆期如是而病天可也若其
嘉種而化爲稂莠上田而化爲瘠丘是天
之所以爲鹵莽滅裂報也田者責也而奚
責焉故樹穀者務索草樹民者務索盜束
以法禁程以政教先民而使民有不敢爲
盜之意日訢訢鋤其莠心而不自知是道
民之上務而弭盜之首策已自昔之論盜
者曰衣食不足也守令無良也政賦不均
也三者之外無他異故也然有不盡爾者
往者鯨鯢失路海波播颺而我民之無良
者出入島嶼之間以爲之嚮而熾其兇於
是乎有瀕海之盜師旅繁興征發繹騷墨
punctuated:
之原，誠非謾語。
考試官教諭林批：策末尤究極於爲政得人，足徵經濟之略。
考試官教諭吳批：學博才優。
聖王疆畫天下，犁若土田然。民譬則穀也，官司者，所以耘耔非種而佐之植者也。寒暑失節，雨暘愆期，如是而病天，可也。若其嘉種而化爲稂莠，上田而化爲瘠丘，是天之所以爲鹵莽滅裂報也，田者責也，而奚責焉？故樹穀者務索草，樹民者務索盜。束以法禁，程以政教，先民而使民有不敢爲盜之意，日訢訢鋤其莠心而不自知，是道民之上務，而弭盜之首策已。自昔之論盜者曰：衣食不足也，守令無良也，政賦不均也，三者之外，無他異故也。然有不盡爾者。往者鯨鯢失路，海波播颺，而我民之無良者，出入島嶼之間，以爲之嚮而熾其兇，於是乎有瀕海之盜；師旅繁興，征發繹騷，墨
translation_en:
… [of suppressing banditry] is truly no empty talk.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Lin: The end of the policy essay thoroughly probes into how governance depends on obtaining the right men, which is sufficient to demonstrate his talent for statecraft.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wu: Broadly learned and superior in talent.

The sage kings demarcated the realm just like plowing fields. The people may be compared to grain, and the officials are those who weed and mound the earth around the roots to remove alien species and assist the grain's growth. When cold and heat lose their seasonal regularity, and rain and sunshine miss their proper times, to blame Heaven in such cases is permissible. But if fine seed turns into weeds and tares, and superior fields turn into barren mounds, this is Heaven's recompense for careless and slipshod cultivation; it is the responsibility of the cultivator, so whom else could one blame? Therefore, he who cultivates grain devotes himself to seeking out weeds, and he who cultivates the people devotes himself to seeking out bandits. Restraining them with legal prohibitions and regulating them with governance and moral instruction, guiding the people beforehand so that they harbor the intention of not daring to become bandits, and day by day joyfully weeding out their weedy hearts without even realizing it—this is the paramount task in guiding the people and the foremost strategy for suppressing banditry.

Those who have discussed banditry since antiquity say: food and clothing are insufficient; Prefectural and County Magistrates are unscrupulous; governance and taxation are unequal; and beyond these three, there are no other unusual causes. Yet this does not entirely account for it. In the past, when piratical leviathans lost their way and ocean waves tossed and surged, unscrupulous elements among our people went in and out among the islands to act as their guides and fan their ferocity; thus there were bandits along the coast. As military campaigns frequently arose, requisitions and conscriptions caused continuous disruption, and corrupt…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
吏乘機而剝膚庶頑樂亂而弄兵於是乎
有內地之盜探丸借客避仇亡命之徒以
武犯禁於是乎有鄉里之盜今則異是
天子憂勞萬民曠然與天下更始而氛霾清明
暴豪善良有司斤斤守法五穀時登海淮
之間帖席而宴起焉不可謂非樂時寧歲
也然而洪波曲沚之間尚有馳舠鼓楫隱
約於暮夜而椎剽以為利者即如兩浙都
會名區豈乏譏關詰慝之素迺羣飲之徒
===
邂逅將輸之命吏乘其弗戒倏起而奪之
金至廑
嚴旨督責長吏雖其時縶之不旋踵而黨與以
次就縛然豈盛世事哉夫不有饑寒困苦
之迫與怨家墨吏之敺而甘棄其身於盜
賊非人之所宜有也而今有之愚故曰導
民之無策而教化之不先也蓋後世所以
考鏡于先王者莫備于周禮周禮太宰以
九職任萬民大司徒辨十有二土之名物
punctuated: 吏乘機而剝膚，庶頑樂亂而弄兵，於是乎有內地之盜；探丸借客，避仇亡命之徒，以武犯禁，於是乎有鄉里之盜。今則異是。天子憂勞萬民，曠然與天下更始，而氛霾清明，暴豪善良，有司斤斤守法，五穀時登，海淮之間，帖席而宴起焉，不可謂非樂時寧歲也。然而洪波曲沚之間，尚有馳舠鼓楫，隱約於暮夜，而椎剽以為利者。即如兩浙都會名區，豈乏譏關詰慝之素？迺羣飲之徒，邂逅將輸之命吏，乘其弗戒，倏起而奪之金，至廑嚴旨督責長吏。雖其時縶之不旋踵，而黨與以次就縛，然豈盛世事哉！夫不有饑寒困苦之迫，與怨家墨吏之敺，而甘棄其身於盜賊，非人之所宜有也，而今有之。愚故曰：導民之無策，而教化之不先也。蓋後世所以考鏡于先王者，莫備于《周禮》。《周禮》太宰以九職任萬民，大司徒辨十有二土之名物，
translation_en:
…officials took advantage of the opportunity to fleece the people to the bone, and the recalcitrant populace delighted in disorder and took up arms; thus there were bandits in the interior. Those who drew lots to murder for hire, or fugitives fleeing vendettas, violated the prohibitions by force; thus there were bandits in the local villages.

Today, however, things are different from this. The Son of Heaven is anxious and toils for the myriad people, magnanimously making a fresh start with the empire. The miasmas and haze have cleared, the violent and overbearing have become good and law-abiding, the authorities fastidiously observe the laws, and the five grains ripen in season. Between the coast and the Huai River, people sleep soundly on their mats and rise late in peace; it cannot be said that these are not happy times and peaceful years. And yet, amid the vast waves and winding inlets, there are still those who speed in skiffs and ply their oars, lurking in the dusk and night, bludgeoning and plundering for profit. Take for instance a celebrated metropolis like that of the Two Zhe [Zhejiang]: how could it lack established routines for inspecting at barriers and interrogating evildoers? Yet a gang of carousers chanced upon a commissioned official transporting tax silver, took advantage of his lack of vigilance, and suddenly rose up to seize the silver from him—going so far as to trouble His Majesty to issue a stern decree reprimanding the senior officials. Although at the time they were apprehended before one could turn on one's heel, and their accomplices were bound one after another, how could this be an affair fitting for a flourishing age!

Now, without being driven by the pressure of hunger, cold, and hardship, or by personal enemies and corrupt officials, to willingly abandon oneself to banditry is not something that is in human nature to do—and yet today it happens. Therefore I say: it is because there is no strategy for guiding the people, and moral transformation through instruction has not been put first. Indeed, among the means by which later ages examine and mirror the former kings, none is more complete than the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). In the Rites of Zhou, the Grand Councilor (Taizai) employs the myriad people through the nine occupations, and the Grand Minister of Education (Da situ) distinguishes the names and products of the twelve types of land…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而施十有二敎鄉大夫考德行察道藝州
長讀法黨正掌敎治族師掌政事司諫糾
民德司救誅邪惡日夜整齊其民而納之
於善惟恐不及然而有不勝也於是乎大
司馬以九伐正邦國士師掌八成聨什伍
比追胥司厲辨盜物野廬攄賓客達道路
司寤詔夜禁脩閭禁徑踰所以捍禦不虞
而遏民狂謀者如此故雖有奇心袤行無
以爲也夫先王非恃其有圉姦之法而恃
===
其有擯姦之法非恃其民之必相戒不扦
吾網而恃其民無恣睢之心蓋禁於未發
則逸而有成禁於已發則勞而罔功此先
王深憂天下而豫爲之隄防者也愚獨悲
夫後世不講于先王防微之意而詳于先
王救敗之法故建議畫制日易月更聨之
以官司布之以邏諜專之以信地課之以
賞罰自謂是足以弭盜而不知和恒輯寧
之方未講於上徒恃法度禁令之繁遏止
punctuated: 而施十有二敎。鄉大夫考德行，察道藝；州長讀法；黨正掌敎治；族師掌政事；司諫糾民德；司救誅邪惡。日夜整齊其民而納之於善，惟恐不及。然而有不勝也，於是乎大司馬以九伐正邦國，士師掌八成，聨什伍，比追胥；司厲辨盜物；野廬攄賓客，達道路；司寤詔夜禁；脩閭禁徑踰。所以捍禦不虞，而遏民狂謀者如此。故雖有奇心袤行，無以爲也。夫先王非恃其有圉姦之法，而恃其有擯姦之法；非恃其民之必相戒不扦吾網，而恃其民無恣睢之心。蓋禁於未發，則逸而有成；禁於已發，則勞而罔功。此先王深憂天下，而豫爲之隄防者也。愚獨悲夫後世不講于先王防微之意，而詳于先王救敗之法。故建議畫制，日易月更，聨之以官司，布之以邏諜，專之以信地，課之以賞罰，自謂是足以弭盜，而不知和恒輯寧之方未講於上，徒恃法度禁令之繁，遏止
translation_en:
… and apply the twelve teachings. The Grand Masters of the Districts (Xiang dafu) examine moral conduct and inspect proficiency in the Way and the arts; the Heads of the Regions (Zhouzhang) read out the laws; the Heads of the Cantons (Dangzheng) oversee instruction and governance; the Preceptors of the Clans (Zushi) manage administrative affairs; the Directors of Remonstrance (Sijian) rectify the people's virtue; and the Directors of Relief (Sijiu) reprove wickedness and evil. Day and night they regulate their people and guide them toward goodness, fearing only that they might fall short. Yet there are still those who cannot be overcome. Thereupon, the Minister of War (Da sima) uses the nine punitive expeditions to rectify the states; the Master of Playas/Judges (Shishi) oversees the eight categories of judicial precedents, links the five- and ten-family groups, and organizes the pursuit and capture of thieves; the Director of Miscreants (Sili) identifies stolen goods; the Lodge-keepers of the Open Country (Yelu) attend to guests and keep the roads clear [?]; the Director of Night-watches (Siwu) proclaims the night curfews; and the Maintainers of the Hamlet Gates (Xiulü) forbid taking shortcuts or climbing over walls. Such were the means by which they guarded against the unexpected and curbed the reckless plots of the people. Therefore, even if someone harbored deviant thoughts or crooked conduct, there was no way to act upon them.

Now, the former kings did not rely on having laws to imprison the wicked, but relied on having laws to shun wickedness; they did not rely on their people necessarily warning one another not to violate our nets of the law, but relied on their people having no unbridled or defiant inclinations. Indeed, to prohibit wrongdoing before it breaks out is effortless and effective; to prohibit it after it has already broken out is toilsome and fruitless. This is why the former kings worried deeply about the realm and erected dikes of prevention in advance.

I alone grieve that later ages do not study the former kings' intent in preventing nascent evils, yet are meticulous about the former kings' methods for remedying failure. Thus, in proposing policies and devising regulations, changing them daily and altering them monthly, they link responsibilities through official bureaus, deploy patrols and spies, assign specific jurisdictions of responsibility, and evaluate performance with rewards and punishments. They tell themselves that this is sufficient to suppress banditry, not realizing that when the methods for harmonizing, sustaining, and pacifying the populace are not cultivated at the top, and one merely relies on the proliferation of laws, regulations, and prohibitions to check and stop them…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於下末矣故趙廣漢之治京兆也以鉤鉅
王溫舒之治關中也以投筩張敞之治長
安也以致羣偷尹翁歸之治扶風也以知
主名龔遂之治渤海也以解亂繩虞詡之
治朝歌也以設三科張綱之治廣陵也以
驟單車非不足以博稜名于一時而快雄
心于小割然而車不旋軫坐不敝席而鳴
鏑已交於境內矣則何也恃其勝之之術
以為已之之術故也善乎秦觀之言曰盜
===
賊者平之非難絕之為難今欲絕盜其惟
抑遊惰定經制乎夫今之四民非古之四
民也古之為士者羣萃而州處閒燕則服
仁義稱先王父與父言慈子與子言孝今
士作無用之文以媒祿利鶩寵而炫華矣
古之為工者無斲削之技磨礱之功相材
審時成構而已今工刻畫五色金罍玉尊
雕文彤漆銀口黃耳箕子之譏始在主上
今在匹夫矣古之商者察其四時而監貨
punctuated: 於下，末矣。故趙廣漢之治京兆也，以鉤鉅；王溫舒之治關中也，以投筩；張敞之治長安也，以致羣偷；尹翁歸之治扶風也，以知主名；龔遂之治渤海也，以解亂繩；虞詡之治朝歌也，以設三科；張綱之治廣陵也，以驟單車。非不足以博稜名于一時，而快雄心于小割；然而車不旋軫，坐不敝席，而鳴鏑已交於境內矣。則何也？恃其勝之之術，以為已之之術故也。善乎秦觀之言曰：「盜賊者，平之非難，絕之為難。」今欲絕盜，其惟抑遊惰、定經制乎？夫今之四民，非古之四民也。古之為士者，羣萃而州處，閒燕則服仁義、稱先王，父與父言慈，子與子言孝；今士作無用之文，以媒祿利，鶩寵而炫華矣。古之為工者，無斲削之技、磨礱之功，相材審時，成構而已；今工刻畫五色，金罍玉尊，雕文彤漆，銀口黃耳，箕子之譏，始在主上，今在匹夫矣。古之商者，察其四時而監貨
translation_en:
…them from below—this is merely attending to the branches! Thus, when Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢 governed the Capital Prefecture (Jingzhao 京兆), he relied on cunning interrogation by comparison (gouju 鉤鉅); when Wang Wenshu 王溫舒 governed the Region Within the Passes (Guanzhong 關中), he relied on anonymous accusation boxes (toutong 投筩); when Zhang Chang 張敞 governed Chang'an 長安, he relied on recruiting ringleaders of thieves to catch others; when Yin Wonggui 尹翁歸 governed Fufeng 扶風, he relied on knowing the names of key offenders; when Gong Sui 龔遂 governed Bohai 渤海, he treated it like untangling a knotted cord; when Yu Xu 虞詡 governed Zhaoge 朝歌, he relied on establishing three categories of recruits; and when Zhang Gang 張綱 governed Guangling 廣陵, he relied on riding straight into the bandits' camp in a single carriage. None of these measures failed to win them a reputation for stern capability in their own time, or to gratify their ambitious spirits with minor successes. And yet, before their carriages had even turned around or their sitting mats had worn thin, whistling arrows were already flying across the borders again. Why was this? Because they mistook techniques for defeating bandits for techniques for putting an end to them altogether.

Well spoken were the words of Qin Guan 秦觀: "With bandits and rebels, suppressing them is not what is difficult; eradicating them is what is difficult." If today we wish to eradicate banditry, does it not lie solely in curbing idleness and establishing regular sumptuary institutions?

Indeed, the four classes of people today are not the four classes of antiquity. In antiquity, scholars (shi 士) gathered together and dwelt in communities; in their leisure they practiced benevolence and righteousness and praised the Former Kings, fathers speaking with fathers of parental kindness, and sons speaking with sons of filial piety. Today's scholars compose useless writings as a means to procure emoluments and profit, chasing after favor and showing off flowery ornamentation. In antiquity, artisans (gong 工) did not indulge in intricate carving or elaborate polishing; they simply examined the materials, observed the proper seasons, and completed the needed structures. Today's artisans carve and paint in the five colors, crafting gold wine-jars and jade goblets, with engraved patterns and vermilion lacquer, silver rims and golden handles; the extravagance that Jizi 箕子 once censured in his sovereign is now found among commoners. In antiquity, merchants (shang 商) observed the four seasons, inspected their goods, …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
知賈服牛輅馬以遊四方今商粥難得之
貨剷山沒淵以市異物矣古者常民衣服
溫暖而不靡器質牢樸而致用車足以自
載馬足以代步酒取合懽而不湛樂取理
心而不淫行卽負擔止卽耡耘養生適而
不奢送死哀而不華今民間有層梁雕檻
飛榱步欄被服纖麗翫好玄黃塗屏錯跗
文杯畫案燔胾之食靡曼之聲葬死殫家
遣女滿車富者欲過貧者欲及富者空藏
===
貧者稱息矣古者君子孳孳思其德小人
孜孜思其力故其心安焉不見異物而遷
焉今豪家惡少商販庸兒黏竿掩罝逐狗
呼雞擁脂曲房探赤通衢宵宴朝歌博塞
嘯壺不富家而富身不耻盜而耻貧矣易
曰負且乘致寇至夫是數者則謂之盜夸
何也彼其所以靡麗衍溢者皆足以生民
心而荒淫佚樂之後又未有不胥而爲盜
者故今之爲盜者率是類也欲令盜賊不
punctuated: 知賈，服牛輅馬以遊四方；今商粥難得之貨，剷山沒淵以市異物矣。古者常民衣服溫暖而不靡，器質牢樸而致用，車足以自載，馬足以代步，酒取合懽而不湛，樂取理心而不淫，行卽負擔，止卽耡耘，養生適而不奢，送死哀而不華；今民間有層梁雕檻、飛榱步欄，被服纖麗，翫好玄黃，塗屏錯跗、文杯畫案，燔胾之食、靡曼之聲，葬死殫家，遣女滿車，富者欲過，貧者欲及，富者空藏，貧者稱息矣。古者君子孳孳思其德，小人孜孜思其力，故其心安焉，不見異物而遷焉；今豪家惡少、商販庸兒，黏竿掩罝，逐狗呼雞，擁脂曲房，探赤通衢，宵宴朝歌，博塞嘯壺，不富家而富身，不耻盜而耻貧矣。《易》曰：「負且乘，致寇至。」夫是數者，則謂之盜夸，何也？彼其所以靡麗衍溢者，皆足以生民心，而荒淫佚樂之後，又未有不胥而爲盜者，故今之爲盜者率是類也。欲令盜賊不
translation_en: …and knew their prices, driving oxen and hitching horses to travel in all directions; today's merchants peddle rare goods, leveling mountains and diving into the depths to trade in exotic things. In antiquity, the clothing of ordinary folk was warm without being extravagant, and the substance of their vessels was sturdy and plain so as to be practical; their carts sufficed to carry themselves, and their horses sufficed to spare them walking; wine was taken to join in conviviality without overindulgence, and music was taken to order the mind without licentiousness; when traveling they carried their own loads, and when staying at home they hoed and weeded; in nourishing the living they sought comfort without luxury, and in sending off the dead they showed grief without ostentation. Today, among the people there are tiered beams and carved balustrades, flying rafters and galleried corridors; their garments are fine and ornate, their playthings are of dark and yellow silks; they have painted screens and inlaid pedestals, patterned cups and decorated tables, meals of roasted meats and seductive, languid music; burying the dead exhausts the family fortune, and marrying off a daughter fills whole carriages; the rich wish to surpass others and the poor wish to catch up, until the rich empty their treasuries and the poor borrow at interest. In antiquity, gentlemen tirelessly reflected upon their virtue, while petty men diligently reflected upon their labor; thus their minds were at peace, and they did not shift their desires upon seeing exotic things. Today, wicked youths from powerful families and base fellows among merchants and peddlers use limed poles and set nets, chase dogs and call cocks, embrace heavily made-up women in secluded chambers, draw red lots to rob on the thoroughfares, feast by night and sing by morning, play board games and shout over pitch-pot; they enrich their own persons rather than their households, and are ashamed not of robbery, but of poverty. The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Bearing a burden on the back yet riding in a carriage brings on the arrival of robbers." Now, why is it that these several types are called "flaunting to invite robbery"? Because all their extravagance and excess suffice to stir covetousness in the people's hearts, and after indulging in dissipation and pleasure, there are none who do not end up becoming robbers themselves; therefore, those who act as robbers today are generally of this sort. If one wishes to see to it that robbers and bandits do not…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
與莫若脩其本如以爲周人之敎有難卒
幾者非也曷不引已事觀之
高皇帝體國經野設法明禁制度昭於日星典
則貽于
子孫與周官之意皆相表裏至詳密也及夫
理道陵夷網亦疏濶民如蜚鳥曾無寧心
故遊食多於丁夫漏口什於見戶一人務
奢而弗禁衆皆馳騖以爲奢曰此所以爲
廣大也彼戔戔胡爲者也一人務佚而不
===
禁衆皆遊遨以爲佚曰此所以爲通適也
彼踽踽胡爲者也笑勤恪爲俗吏詆約嗇
爲守虜俗尚旣成恬不爲怪夫天之所覆
者雖難窮而地之所容者則有限以氣數
之不齊而重以人事之多變於是乎生民
有盛衰生物有多寡以益盛之生民而用
益寡之生物然且不操夫撙節之政而猥
恣其無已之心此立盡之術也愚請取天
下之民不緣南畝者一切繩之以法非已
punctuated: 與，莫若脩其本。如以爲周人之敎有難卒幾者，非也。曷不引已事觀之？高皇帝體國經野，設法明禁，制度昭於日星，典則貽于子孫，與《周官》之意皆相表裏，至詳密也。及夫理道陵夷，網亦疏濶，民如蜚鳥，曾無寧心。故遊食多於丁夫，漏口什於見戶。一人務奢而弗禁，衆皆馳騖以爲奢，曰：「此所以爲廣大也，彼戔戔胡爲者也？」一人務佚而不禁，衆皆遊遨以爲佚，曰：「此所以爲通適也，彼踽踽胡爲者也？」笑勤恪爲俗吏，詆約嗇爲守虜。俗尚旣成，恬不爲怪。夫天之所覆者雖難窮，而地之所容者則有限。以氣數之不齊，而重以人事之多變，於是乎生民有盛衰，生物有多寡。以益盛之生民，而用益寡之生物，然且不操夫撙節之政，而猥恣其無已之心，此立盡之術也。愚請取天下之民不緣南畝者，一切繩之以法：非已
translation_en: …arise [reading 與 as 興], there is nothing better than cultivating the fundamental root. If one considers the teachings of the people of Zhou too difficult to quickly approach, that is wrong. Why not examine the matter by citing precedents from our own past? When the Exalted Emperor [Gao Huangdi, i.e., Emperor Taizu] organized the state and laid out the land, he established laws and clarified prohibitions; his institutions shone as brightly as the sun and stars, and his canons and rules were bequeathed to his descendants, all corresponding internally and externally with the spirit of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), and were most detailed and thorough. Yet when the way of governance declined, the net of the law also grew loose and wide; the people became like flying birds, never having a settled mind. Thus, idle consumers outnumber able-bodied laborers, and unregistered persons are ten times as many as registered households. When one person pursues extravagance and is not prohibited, the multitude all rush after him to practice extravagance, saying, "This is how one shows magnanimity; what use is that petty stinginess?" When one person pursues idleness and is not prohibited, the multitude all roam about in pursuit of idleness, saying, "This is how one attains free ease; what use is that solitary plodding?" They laugh at the diligent and conscientious as vulgar clerks, and disparage the frugal and thrifty as mere money-guarding slaves. Once such customs and fashions have formed, people take them for granted and do not consider them strange. Now, although what Heaven covers is hard to exhaust, what Earth can hold is finite. Because of the unevenness of natural cycles, compounded by the many vicissitudes of human affairs, the population has its flourishing and decline, and the production of goods has its abundance and scarcity. To take an ever-growing population and have them consume ever-scarcer goods, and yet not exercise a policy of restraint and moderation, instead rashly indulging their insatiable desires—this is a recipe for immediate exhaustion. I humbly request that all people in the empire who do not engage in farming the southern acres be strictly bound by the law: unless one has already…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嘗仕者不得服華美非戍卒不得帶劍非
大享燕不得舉樂非飲射讀法不得羣留
於城市宮室器用輿馬之物婚娶喪葬之
儀一稟裁於
國典不得有所踰越有司時察其奇袤者而
法之必無赦若是則雖未逮夫先王化民
成俗之意而猶庶幾乎禁姦銷慝之心此
所謂朝令而夕至上不勞而下易從之術
又何憚而不爲此也賈子有言天下有瑰
===
政於此予民而民愈貧衣民而民愈寒使
民樂而民愈苦使民智而民愈罹於懸網
有瑋術於此奪民而民益富不衣民而民
益煖苦民而民益樂使民愈愚而益不罹
於懸網夫雕文刻鏤之物繁多而纖微苦
窳之器日變民棄完堅而競巧脆宜一日
而作者今十日不能成可用一歲者今半
歲而敝不耕而食農人之食是天下之所
以困貧而不足也故以末予民民大貧以
punctuated: 嘗仕者，不得服華美；非戍卒，不得帶劍；非大享燕，不得舉樂；非飲射讀法，不得羣留於城市。宮室、器用、輿馬之物，婚娶、喪葬之儀，一稟裁於國典，不得有所踰越。有司時察其奇袤者而法之，必無赦。若是，則雖未逮夫先王化民成俗之意，而猶庶幾乎禁姦銷慝之心。此所謂朝令而夕至，上不勞而下易從之術，又何憚而不爲此也？賈子有言：「天下有瑰政於此，予民而民愈貧，衣民而民愈寒，使民樂而民愈苦，使民智而民愈罹於懸網。有瑋術於此，奪民而民益富，不衣民而民益煖，苦民而民益樂，使民愈愚而益不罹於懸網。夫雕文刻鏤之物繁多，而纖微苦窳之器日變，民棄完堅而競巧脆，宜一日而作者，今十日不能成；可用一歲者，今半歲而敝。不耕而食農人之食，是天下之所以困貧而不足也。故以末予民，民大貧；以
translation_en: … who have already held official rank, they shall not be permitted to wear华美 (splendid and sumptuous) clothing; unless they are garrison soldiers, they shall not be permitted to carry swords; unless it is a grand sacrificial banquet, they shall not be permitted to perform music; and unless it is for the community drinking ceremony, archery ritual, or the reading of the laws, they shall not be permitted to gather and linger in the cities. Dwellings, utensils, carriages, and horses, as well as the rituals of marriage, mourning, and burial, must all be regulated strictly according to the statutes of the state, with no transgression allowed. The authorities should regularly investigate those who are deviant and perverse and punish them according to the law without pardon. If this is done, then although it may not yet reach the former kings' ideal of transforming the people and perfecting customs, it will still come close to the aim of prohibiting wickedness and eradicating evil. This is what is called a method whereby an order given in the morning takes effect by evening, where superiors are not burdened and inferiors easily comply—why then shrink from doing it? Master Jia (Jia Yi 賈誼) had a saying: "Suppose there is an extraordinary policy in the world: you give to the people, yet the people become poorer; you clothe the people, yet the people become colder; you seek to make the people happy, yet the people suffer more; you make the people clever, yet the people fall ever more into the suspended net of the law. And suppose there is an admirable art here: you take from the people, yet the people grow richer; you do not clothe the people, yet the people grow warmer; you impose hardship on the people, yet the people grow happier; you make the people simpler, and they fall ever less into the suspended net of the law. Now, when carved and engraved objects proliferate, and delicate, shoddy wares change day by day, the people abandon what is whole and sturdy to compete for what is ingenious and fragile. What ought to be made in a single day cannot now be completed in ten; what could be used for a full year now wears out in half a year. Without plowing, the artisans eat the food of farmers—this is why the world is distressed, impoverished, and lacking in sufficiency. Therefore, if you give the people secondary pursuits, the people will become大変 (greatly) poor; if with …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
本予民民大富其數不可不知也故語曰
豐世無盜者足也治世無盜者均也化世
無盜者順也然而陶唐之世比屋可封舜
總百揆咎繇作士而宼賊姦宄之命諄諄
不忘聖人豈以平世忘戒備哉天下之患
不在於有形而在於無形於不足畏之中
而藏深可畏之端常人以其無畏成其可
畏聖人以其有畏成其無畏彼其椎牛掘
冢鑄山煮海行氣勢於鄉里而使一方爲
===
之下者皆畏人也雖堯舜之世何甞無之
而堯舜能使其帖然以終其身故晉用隨
會而盜奔秦子太叔用子產之言而萑苻
之澤不乂驚夫盜何足憂哉君子憂其大
者而已矣
punctuated: 本予民，民大富。其數不可不知也。故語曰：「豐世無盜者，足也；治世無盜者，均也；化世無盜者，順也。」然而陶唐之世，比屋可封，舜總百揆，咎繇作士，而宼賊姦宄之命，諄諄不忘。聖人豈以平世忘戒備哉？天下之患，不在於有形，而在於無形。於不足畏之中，而藏深可畏之端。常人以其無畏，成其可畏；聖人以其有畏，成其無畏。彼其椎牛掘冢，鑄山煮海，行氣勢於鄉里，而使一方爲之下者，皆畏人也。雖堯、舜之世，何甞無之？而堯、舜能使其帖然以終其身。故晉用隨會而盜奔秦，子太叔用子產之言而萑苻之澤不乂驚。夫盜何足憂哉？君子憂其大者而已矣。
translation_en: … fundamental occupation [agriculture], the people become greatly enriched. This principle cannot go unknown. Thus the saying goes: "That an age of abundance has no bandits is due to sufficiency; that a well-governed age has no bandits is due to equitable distribution; that a morally transformed age has no bandits is due to harmony." Yet in the age of Tao Tang [Yao], when every household was worthy of enfeoffment, Shun supervised all the affairs of state and Gao Yao served as Chief Justice, and still the charge regarding "robbers, bandits, villains, and traitors" was earnestly and unceasingly remembered. How could the sages forget vigilance and preparedness just because the world was at peace? The perils of the empire lie not in the visible, but in the invisible; within what seems nothing to fear lurks the deeply fearful beginning. Ordinary men, taking there to be nothing to fear, allow it to grow into something to be feared; sages, maintaining their sense of fear, bring about a state where there is nothing to fear. Those who slaughter cattle and rob graves, smelt copper from the mountains and boil salt from the sea, lording it over their乡里 [local communities] and forcing an entire region to submit to them—these are all men to be feared [or: men who nonetheless fear others]. Even in the age of Yao and Shun, how could such men never have existed? Yet Yao and Shun were able to keep them submissive to the end of their lives. Thus, when the state of Jin employed Sui Hui, bandits fled to Qin; when Zitaishu acted upon the words of Zichan, the marshes of Huanfu were no longer [乂 -> 又] alarmed by unrest. Why, then, should bandits be worth worrying about? The gentleman worries only about the greater matters.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
萬曆丙子浙江遵例舉士於
鄉錄旣告成守萬乃颺言曰
昔在先王之世衆建萬國以
親諸侯諸侯各收其士而用
之所求者狹所用者小然猶
鏗鉤炳燿以樹勳于當時光
===
載史冊後世讓弗及焉今天
下一家
皇化汪濊士風蔚起有司盡羅而
貢之南宮以爲
一人用故學宮之士百而一鄕書
之士千而一南宮之士萬而
一至於協化翊世爛焉不朽
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

萬曆丙子，浙江遵例舉士於鄉。錄旣告成，守萬乃颺言曰：昔在先王之世，衆建萬國以親諸侯，諸侯各收其士而用之。所求者狹，所用者小，然猶鏗鉤炳燿，以樹勳于當時，光載史冊，後世讓弗及焉。今天下一家，皇化汪濊，士風蔚起，有司盡羅而貢之南宮，以爲一人用。故學宮之士百而一，鄕書之士千而一，南宮之士萬而一，至於協化翊世、爛焉不朽
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the bingzi year of the Wanli era (1576), Zhejiang, in accordance with precedent, recommended scholars from the province. Once the examination record was completed, Shouwan spoke forth, saying: "In antiquity, during the age of the Former Kings, myriad states were widely established in order to keep the feudal lords close, and the feudal lords each gathered their own scholars and employed them. What they sought was narrow in scope, and how they employed them was on a small scale; yet even so, those men were resounding and illustrious, establishing meritorious achievements in their own time and having their glory recorded in the historical annals, such that later ages yield to them as unattainable. Today, all under Heaven is a single family; the imperial transformative influence is vast and deep, and the morale of the literati flourishes. The authorities gather them all in their net and present them as tribute to the Southern Palace [the Ministry of Rites] for the use of the One Man [the Emperor]. Therefore, among the scholars of the state schools, one in a hundred is chosen; among the scholars inscribed in the provincial register, one in a thousand; among the scholars of the Southern Palace, one in ten thousand; and when it comes to those who harmonize with the imperial transformation and assist the age, shining with immortal…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者不過億兆而一故古者諸
侯求士得國士焉用之足矣
今有司爲
天子求士非得天下士不足以塞
厚望稱隆寄也乃諸士之貢
直發軔耳無爲豪於鄕必也
銘太常勒彝鼎睥睨百世上
===
下而爲豪諸士往矣且
明興二百餘年以來史氏大書
之事凡幾見其賛
元命迪
靈符榦軸
乾坤濯磨
日月至于今望其人如龍如虎不
punctuated: 者，不過億兆而一。故古者諸侯求士，得國士焉，用之足矣；今有司爲天子求士，非得天下士，不足以塞厚望、稱隆寄也。乃諸士之貢，直發軔耳，無爲豪於鄕，必也銘太常、勒彝鼎，睥睨百世上下而爲豪。諸士往矣！且明興二百餘年以來，史氏大書之事凡幾見，其賛元命、迪靈符、榦軸乾坤、濯磨日月，至于今望其人如龍如虎，不
translation_en: …are no more than one in a hundred million or a trillion. Therefore, in antiquity, when the feudal lords sought scholars, if they obtained a scholar of the state, it was sufficient for their use; today, when the authorities seek scholars for the Son of Heaven, unless they obtain scholars of the empire, it is not enough to fulfill the high expectations and match the weighty trust placed in them. Thus, the presentation of these scholars for tribute is merely the removal of the wheel-chock at the start of their journey. Do not merely act as heroes in your home communities; rather, you must have your achievements inscribed on the banners of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and engraved on sacrificial vessels and tripods, looking proudly across a hundred generations past and future as true heroes. Go forth, scholars! Moreover, in the more than two hundred years since the rise of the Ming, how many times have great deeds been recorded at length by the historians? And among those who assisted the Primal Mandate, guided the Numinous Tally, served as the pivot of Heaven and Earth, and polished the Sun and Moon—men whom we look up to even today as dragons and tigers, not…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
可狎視者凡幾人守萬不暇
更僕請論其大者
高皇帝草艾羣雄雲從衆傑其時
居中持議論尊禮不名則青
田金華與閎夭散宜生爭烈
矣名世嗣興若肅愍
社稷之勛屹然厎定不啻虞淵
夾日也新建奮烏合之旅經
營江右甫旬日而氛曀廓清
分瑞析圭傳世罔極繇斯以
談凡我
國家殊尤之績多浙人士功也
故海內之望而浙若神龍之
重淵黝然深矣寶劔出匣萬
punctuated: 可狎視者，凡幾人？守萬不暇更僕，請論其大者。高皇帝草艾羣雄，雲從衆傑，其時居中持議論，尊禮不名，則青田、金華與閎夭、散宜生爭烈矣。名世嗣興，若肅愍社稷之勛，屹然厎定，不啻虞淵夾日也。新建奮烏合之旅，經營江右，甫旬日而氛曀廓清，分瑞析圭，傳世罔極。繇斯以談，凡我國家殊尤之績，多浙人士功也。故海內之望而浙，若神龍之重淵，黝然深矣；寶劔出匣，萬
translation_en: … cannot be viewed with casual familiarity—how many have there been in all? I, Shouwan, have no time to count them all out one after another, so let me discuss the greatest among them. When the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝, i.e. Emperor Taizu 太祖) mowed down the rival warlords like grass and the multitude of heroes followed him like clouds, those who at that time remained at the center directing deliberations and counsels, honored with rites and not addressed by personal name—they were the men of Qingtian 青田 (i.e. Liu Ji 劉基) and Jinhua 金華 (i.e. Song Lian 宋濂), who vied in brilliance with Hong Yao 閎夭 and San Yisheng 散宜生 of antiquity! Renowned worthies of their age arose in succession: such was the merit toward the altars of soil and grain of Duke Sumin 肅愍 (i.e. Yu Qian 于謙), standing firm like a mountain to bring about stability, which was nothing less than holding up the sun over the Abyss of Yu (Yuyuan 虞淵). The Earl of Xinjian 新建 (i.e. Wang Shouren 王守仁) roused an unseasoned, hastily gathered force to campaign in Jiangxi (Jiangyou 江右); in barely ten days the miasmic gloom was swept clear, and he was granted a tally of investiture and ajade tablet of enfeoffment to be handed down to his descendants without end. Speaking from this perspective, of all the extraordinary achievements of our Dynasty, most have been the work of scholars and gentlemen from Zhejiang. Therefore, the way all within the seas look upon your Zhejiang is as though looking upon thelayered abyss of a divine dragon—dark and unfathomably deep! When a treasured sword comes forth from its scabbard, ten thousand…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夫搖精諸士之往天下目隨
焉其何以無媿於先達而名
天下士哉始守萬應聘未至
常患以爲空言質人若空券
質貝故曰雖有健筆不如缺
斧或謂不然金錫不和不成
器事詞不會不成文文何容
===
易彼四君子之始遭猶之乎
諸士也彼主司之得四君子
猶之乎今也士脩之於家而
慷慨論事則任者多効官擔
爵持之太重則讓者多夫人
而讓豪傑不幾見矣守萬固
願諸生之毋讓務趨前茅斯
punctuated: 夫搖精。諸士之往，天下目隨焉。其何以無媿於先達，而名天下士哉？始守萬應聘未至，常患以爲空言質人，若空券質貝。故曰：「雖有健筆，不如缺斧。」或謂不然，金錫不和不成器，事詞不會不成文，文何容易？彼四君子之始遭，猶之乎諸士也；彼主司之得四君子，猶之乎今也。士脩之於家，而慷慨論事，則任者多；効官擔爵，持之太重，則讓者多。夫人而讓，豪傑不幾見矣。守萬固願諸生之毋讓，務趨前茅，斯
translation_en:
… the spirits of ten thousand men are shaken. As you gentlemen go forth, the eyes of the empire follow you. How will you avoid bringing shame upon those eminent predecessors and truly earn the name of scholars of the empire?

At first, when I, [Lin] Shouwan, had accepted the invitation to serve as examiner but had not yet arrived, I often worried that judging men by empty words is like pawning valuables with an empty promissory note. Thus it is said: "Even a vigorous brush is not as good as a chipped axe." Yet someone said this is not so: if bronze and tin do not blend, they do not form a vessel; if deeds and words do not meet, they do not form true writing. How could writing be taken lightly? When those four noble men first met with their opportunity, they were just like you gentlemen today; and when those examiners found the four noble men, it was just like today. When scholars cultivate themselves at home and discourse passionately upon affairs, many are ready to take up the burden; but when they serve in office and bear noble rank, holding on too cautiously to their positions, many yield and shrink back. If everyone yields, heroic men will scarcely be seen! I, Shouwan, truly wish that you students will not yield, but strive to advance in the vanguard, so that…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
主司之質不爽矣如以爲四
君子猶其小者也則主司謝
不敏大喜過望其懋勉行哉
河南開封府鄭州滎澤縣儒
學敎諭林守萬謹序
punctuated:
主司之質不爽矣。如以爲四君子猶其小者也，則主司謝不敏，大喜過望。其懋勉行哉！
河南開封府鄭州滎澤縣儒學敎諭林守萬謹序。
translation_en:
…the pledge of the examiners will not fail. If you consider those four gentlemen to be still of comparatively small attainment, then the examiners will apologize for their own inadequacy and rejoice beyond all expectations. Strive earnestly and go forth!

Respectfully prefaced by Lin Shouwan 林守萬, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xingze County, Zhengzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
萬曆丙子秋浙江復當貢士
於是御史吳從憲行郡縣歲
徧報成事矣
上遣代者御史鮑希顏未至而從
憲不敢離境土庀事益毖八
月六日遂以伯誠與教諭林
===
守萬爲考試官教諭徐道明
梁尚忠畢大魁黃嶫陳懋昭
田舜耕爲同考試官入鎖院
而左布政使王應顯左參政
朱炳如司提調按察使蒙詔
副使王續之司監試暨百執
事罔或不虔乃合提學僉事
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序
萬曆丙子秋，浙江復當貢士。於是御史吳從憲行郡縣，歲徧報成事矣。上遣代者御史鮑希顏未至，而從憲不敢離境土，庀事益毖。八月六日，遂以伯誠與教諭林守萬爲考試官，教諭徐道明、梁尚忠、畢大魁、黃嶫、陳懋昭、田舜耕爲同考試官，入鎖院。而左布政使王應顯、左參政朱炳如司提調，按察使蒙詔、副使王續之司監試，暨百執事罔或不虔。乃合提學僉事
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the bingzi year of the Wanli era [1576], it was once again time for Zhejiang to present tribute scholars through the provincial examination. At that time, Investigating Censor Wu Congxian 吳從憲 had completed his year-long tour of inspection through the prefectures and counties and had reported the completion of his mission. His Majesty had dispatched Investigating Censor Bao Xiyan 鮑希顏 to replace him, but before he arrived, Congxian did not dare leave the territory of the province and attended to the preparations for the examination with even greater care and caution.

On the sixth day of the eighth month, he accordingly appointed me, [Sun] Bocheng 伯誠, together with County Director of Studies Lin Shouwan 林守萬 as Examiners, and County Directors of Studies Xu Daoming 徐道明, Liang Shangzhong 梁尚忠, Bi Dakui 畢大魁, Huang Ye 黃嶫, Chen Maozhao 陳懋昭, and Tian Shungeng 田舜耕 as Associate Examiners, to enter the locked examination compound. Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Yingxian 王應顯 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhu Bingru 朱炳如 served as Proctors, while Surveillance Commissioner Meng Zhao 蒙詔 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang Xuzhi 王續之 served as Monitoring Officials, and among the hundred functionaries there were none who were not reverent and diligent. Thereupon, they gathered the [2,700 scholars selected by] Assistant Surveillance Commissioner for Education…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
喬因阜所遴士二千七百人
而三試之拔其儁九十人與
其文錄焉以
獻伯誠以職事當序諸簡端竊惟
今天下兩浙實稱首藩豈惟
其山川之佳麗物產之豐盈
人文之宣朗雄海內哉乃其
===
霑濡
帝澤鬯被
皇風自
二京而下無若茲方之捷而神
也先是
皇上憫士習之日澆知功令之漸
弛乃
punctuated: 喬因阜所遴士二千七百人，而三試之，拔其儁九十人，與其文錄焉以獻。伯誠以職事當序諸簡端。竊惟今天下，兩浙實稱首藩，豈惟其山川之佳麗、物產之豐盈、人文之宣朗雄海內哉？乃其霑濡帝澤，鬯被皇風，自二京而下，無若茲方之捷而神也。先是，皇上憫士習之日澆，知功令之漸弛，乃
translation_en: … the two thousand seven hundred scholars selected by [Education Intendant Assistant Surveillance Commissioner] Qiao Yinfu 喬因阜, and examined them in three sessions, selecting ninety outstanding men among them and recording their names together with their essays to present to the throne. By virtue of my official duties, I, Bocheng 伯誠, ought to write a preface at the head of these pages. I humbly reflect that in the empire today, the Two Zhe [Zhejiang] truly is acclaimed as the foremost province. Is this merely because the beauty of its mountains and rivers, the abundance of its products, and the brilliance of its cultural refinement preeminently surpass all within the seas? Rather, it is because in being steeped in the imperial grace and pervasively reached by the august moral influence, below the Two Capitals there is no region as swift and wondrous in its response as this place. Prior to this, His Majesty, pitying that the habits of scholars were growing daily more superficial and knowing that the regulations governing examinations and schools were gradually slackening, thereupon …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
俞輔臣之請更督學憲臣之
璽書而浙之憲臣適在
輦轂下面承
德音視他省爲獨先焉士之聞風
逖聽者固已灑然變志易慮
思覲
耿光二年於此矣邇者
===
皇上德隆道積見聖
羹墻乃以八月之吉
幸臨太學釋奠
先師縟儀曠典玆惟肇舉蓋未
浹辰也而聲敎所曁霆迅飈
馳凡我多士則又動色感奮
喁喁焉冀附雲龍風虎之會
punctuated: 俞輔臣之請，更督學憲臣之璽書，而浙之憲臣適在輦轂下，面承德音，視他省爲獨先焉。士之聞風逖聽者，固已灑然變志易慮，思覲耿光，二年於此矣。邇者，皇上德隆道積，見聖羹墻，乃以八月之吉，幸臨太學，釋奠先師。縟儀曠典，玆惟肇舉，蓋未浹辰也，而聲敎所曁，霆迅飈馳。凡我多士，則又動色感奮，喁喁焉冀附雲龍風虎之會，
translation_en: …approved the request of the Grand Secretaries to revise the imperial commission for the Education Intendant Censors, and the Censor assigned to Zhejiang happened to be right at the capital beneath the imperial carriage, where he received the benevolent pronouncement in person, ahead of all the other provinces. The scholars who heard the news from afar had already been refreshed in spirit, transforming their ambitions and renewing their thoughts, longing to behold the radiant glory of the throne—and it has now been two years since then. Recently, as His Majesty’s virtue has grown ever more exalted and his Way ever more accumulated, seeing the sages as if in his very broth and on his walls, on an auspicious day in the eighth month he graced the National University with his presence and performed the libation sacrifice to the Former Teacher. It has not yet been twelve days since these elaborate rites and rare ceremonies were first carried out, yet the reach of his moral prestige and teachings has spread as swiftly as thunder and whirlwind. All our many scholars have been visibly moved and inspired, eagerly hoping to attach themselves to this auspicious encounter of clouds following the dragon and winds following the tiger…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以快
聖作物覩之期志慮日以精明藻
績益以彪炳抱藝而來操觚
而書縭辭吐蘊大異疇昔其
感動之捷而神有如此者故
今觀多士所為文雖其言人
人殊類能抉微衍奧標粹掞
===
奇有莊嚴峻潔若高山大川
莫窺其際者曰此其聞
皇上恭默思道不顯惟德之風者
耶胡深以厚也有溫純爾雅
若襲珍韞玉其光不可掩者
曰此其聞
皇上勤學好問勵精圖政之風者
punctuated: 以快聖作物覩之期。志慮日以精明，藻績益以彪炳；抱藝而來，操觚而書，縭辭吐蘊，大異疇昔。其感動之捷而神有如此者！故今觀多士所為文，雖其言人人殊，類能抉微衍奧、標粹掞奇。有莊嚴峻潔，若高山大川莫窺其際者，曰：「此其聞皇上恭默思道、不顯惟德之風者耶？胡深以厚也！」有溫純爾雅，若襲珍韞玉其光不可掩者，曰：「此其聞皇上勤學好問、勵精圖政之風者
translation_en: … so as to rejoice in this moment when a sage arises and all creatures behold him. Their minds and thoughts grow daily more refined and clear, their literary accomplishments ever more brilliant and resplendent; coming forth with their mastery of the arts, taking up writing tablets to compose, they weave their phrases and pour forth their inner store in a manner vastly different from days past. Such is the swiftness and marvelous power of this inspiration! Thus, when we now examine the essays composed by the many scholars, although each man's words are distinct, as a rule they are able to uncover subtleties and expound profundities, displaying pure essence and unfurling rare brilliance. Where there are writings that are solemn, lofty, and pure, like high mountains and great rivers whose bounds cannot be fathomed, one says: "Could these be from those who have heard the transformative influence of His Majesty's reverent silence in pondering the Way and his unostentatious virtue? How deep and substantial they are!" Where there are writings that are gentle, pure, and refined, like treasured gems and concealed jade whose luster cannot be hidden, one says: "Could these be from those who have heard the transformative influence of His Majesty's diligent study, fondness for inquiry, and vigorous dedication to governance? …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
耶胡瑩以徹也有縝密典則
從容於矩度若具瞻在望可
親不可狎者曰此其聞
皇上臨雍講藝尊師重傅者之風
耶胡充以達也深以厚必端
士也端斯誠誠以任事弗僨
瑩以徹必敏士也敏斯裕裕
===
以服官弗曠充以達必弘毅
士也弘毅斯勇勇以肩重致
遠弗懼得若人焉以貢春官
揚
皇廷庶幾哉以人事
君之責亦少副矣雖然有司之取
士也據其言斯登之賢書上
punctuated: 耶？胡瑩以徹也！有縝密典則、從容於矩度，若具瞻在望、可親不可狎者，曰：此其聞皇上臨雍講藝、尊師重傅者之風耶？胡充以達也！深以厚，必端士也；端斯誠，誠以任事弗僨。瑩以徹，必敏士也；敏斯裕，裕以服官弗曠。充以達，必弘毅士也；弘毅斯勇，勇以肩重致遠弗懼。得若人焉，以貢春官、揚皇廷，庶幾哉以人事君之責亦少副矣。雖然，有司之取士也，據其言，斯登之賢書、上
translation_en:
… How lustrous and lucid they are! For those whose essays are meticulous and canonical, moving with ease within the rules and standards, like a figure of universal reverence in plain sight who can be approached with affection yet never treated with familiarity—I said: Are these not inspired by hearing of the Emperor’s example in visiting the Imperial University to lecture on the arts and honoring his teachers and tutors? How full and far-reaching they are!

Those who are profound and substantial must be upright scholars; being upright, they are sincere, and with sincerity they can take on responsibilities without faltering. Those who are lustrous and lucid must be acute scholars; being acute, they are resourceful, and with resourcefulness they can perform official duties without neglect. Those who are full and far-reaching must be broad-minded and resolute scholars; being broad-minded and resolute, they are courageous, and with courage they can shoulder heavy burdens and go far without fear. In obtaining such men to present to the Ministry of Rites and advance to the imperial court, perhaps the responsibility of serving the sovereign by recommending worthy men has been fulfilled to some small degree.

Even so, when the authorities select scholars, they judge them by their words, and on that basis enroll them in the roster of worthies and present…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之
天府矣
皇上神聖度越百王公卿大夫之
立朝者奉職兢兢若在
日月之下多士盍自思卽進對
大廷備員百執事果能稱
皇上任使乎今夫爲圭爲璋以薦
===
郊廟匪玉弗堪追而琢之礱
而磨之凡以用之也若雕文
刻鏤以供翫好則玉何貴焉
合抱之木出深山而登廣厦
以爲棟梁材斯美矣若輪囷
屈曲反不如拱把之適於用
何者物不貴異貴適也今多
punctuated: 之天府矣。皇上神聖，度越百王，公卿大夫之立朝者，奉職兢兢，若在日月之下。多士盍自思，卽進對大廷，備員百執事，果能稱皇上任使乎？今夫爲圭爲璋，以薦郊廟，匪玉弗堪。追而琢之，礱而磨之，凡以用之也；若雕文刻鏤，以供翫好，則玉何貴焉？合抱之木，出深山而登廣厦，以爲棟梁，材斯美矣；若輪囷屈曲，反不如拱把之適於用。何者？物不貴異，貴適也。今多
translation_en: …presented to the Imperial Storehouse. His Majesty is divinely sage, surpassing the hundred kings of old, and the Dukes, Ministers, and Grand Masters who stand at court perform their duties with cautious reverence, as though beneath the light of the sun and moon. Why do you many scholars not ask yourselves: if you advance to reply in the Great Court and fill posts among the hundred offices, will you truly prove worthy of His Majesty's employment? Now, when it comes to fashioning gui and zhang tablets to present at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, nothing but jade will suffice. One chisels and carves it, grinds and polishes it, all so that it may be put to use; if it is merely engraved with ornate patterns to serve as a plaything, what value is there in jade? When a tree a full arm's span around comes out of the deep mountains and ascends into a grand hall to serve as ridgepole and beam, its timber is fine indeed; yet if it is gnarled, knotted, and crooked, it is actually less suited for use than a sapling one can grasp with two hands. Why is this? Things are not valued for being extraordinary; they are valued for being suited to use. Now the many…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
士之文誠深以厚矣瑩以徹
矣充以達矣乃其人或浮以
淺焉以任事則僨庸以闇焉
以服官則曠萎以繭焉以肩
重致遠則弗勝巵辭而靡當
空言而無實則曩所云端也
敏也弘毅也皮相爾矣何足
===
以言得士伯誠爲此懼矣伏
讀
璽書曰端軌儀崇經術使學術還
淳士有實用大哉
王言夫非洞文勝之弊敦尚行之
風與章逢之士更始者耶夫
孔子之道昭如日星書而傳
punctuated: 士之文，誠深以厚矣，瑩以徹矣，充以達矣。乃其人或浮以淺焉，以任事則僨；庸以闇焉，以服官則曠；萎以繭焉，以肩重致遠則弗勝。巵辭而靡當，空言而無實，則曩所云端也、敏也、弘毅也，皮相爾矣，何足以言得士？伯誠爲此懼矣。伏讀璽書曰：「端軌儀，崇經術，使學術還淳，士有實用。」大哉王言！夫非洞文勝之弊，敦尚行之風，與章逢之士更始者耶？夫孔子之道，昭如日星，書而傳
translation_en: …the writings of the scholars are indeed deep and substantial, lustrous and penetrating, full and well-articulated! Yet if as men they should prove frivolous and shallow, then when entrusted with affairs they will ruin them; if mediocre and benighted, then when holding office they will neglect their duties; if limp and constricted, then when called upon to shoulder heavy burdens and go far they will be unequal to the task. If they offer shifting words without appropriateness and empty talk without substance, then what I previously termed uprightness, acuity, and breadth of mind with resolute endurance would be mere superficial appearances—how could that suffice to be called obtaining true scholars? I, Bo, am truly fearful of this. Humbly reading the Imperial Patent, it states: "Rectify demeanor and standards, esteem Classical learning, cause scholarship to return to purity, and ensure that scholars possess practical utility." Great indeed are the King's words! Does this not penetrate the abuses of literary floridity exceeding substance, foster a custom of prizing conduct, and make a fresh start with the scholars in their ceremonial caps and ample robes? Now, the Way of Confucius is as bright as the sun and stars. Written down and transmitted…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之為六經誦而習之為學術
體而行之天下國家為實用
是故以之任事而事理矣以
之服官而官飭矣以之肩重
致遠無往而弗濟矣洋洋
聖謨斯其無負矣哉如徒以其炳
炳烺烺之文聞風而興俄頃
===
而化曰我能涵濡
帝澤鬯被
皇風矣求其實用則鉛刀木刃剸
割何施毋乃與
詔旨背乎多士於此可以深長思
矣是舉也提督軍務兵部右
侍郎兼右僉都御史徐栻節
punctuated:
之為六經，誦而習之為學術，體而行之天下國家為實用。是故以之任事而事理矣，以之服官而官飭矣，以之肩重致遠無往而弗濟矣。洋洋聖謨，斯其無負矣哉！如徒以其炳炳烺烺之文，聞風而興，俄頃而化，曰：「我能涵濡帝澤，鬯被皇風矣。」求其實用，則鉛刀木刃，剸割何施？毋乃與詔旨背乎？多士於此可以深長思矣。
是舉也，提督軍務、兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史徐栻，節
translation_en:
… down and transmitted, it is the Six Classics; recited and practiced, it is scholarly learning; embodied and put into practice throughout the empire and the state, it is practical utility. Therefore, when one uses it to undertake affairs, affairs are well ordered; when one uses it to serve in office, official duties are properly regulated; when one uses it to shoulder heavy responsibilities and go far, there is nowhere one goes without succeeding. Vast and grand are the Sacred Counsels—in this way, surely one will not fail them! If instead one merely relies on resplendent and dazzling literary compositions, rising at the first wind of fashion and transforming in an instant, saying, "I have been steeped in the Sovereign's grace and fully bathed in the August wind," yet when sought for practical utility, one is like a lead knife or a wooden blade—how can it be used to cut and cleave? Would this not run counter to the imperial edict? On this point, the many scholars would do well to reflect deeply and at length.

In this undertaking, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, Right Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Xu Shi 徐栻, whose insignia of command …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
鉞維新文武爲憲前巡撫右
副都御史今晉戶部右侍郎
謝鵬舉聲猷尚暨士習夙興
巡鹽監察御史王藻問俗貞
敎雅意作人若巡鹽監察御
史房如式祗
命恪趨風聲先達以使事莅茲土
===
者則刑部郎中金應徵工部
主事馬鳴鑾南京戶部主事
鄧宗臣忽鳴皆樂觀
盛典者也其綜理於外則右布
政使張任右叅政滕伯輪劉
翽左叅議余一龍右叅議王
嘉言副使徐雲程龔大器僉
punctuated: 鉞維新，文武爲憲；前巡撫、右副都御史、今晉戶部右侍郎謝鵬舉，聲猷尚暨，士習夙興；巡鹽監察御史王藻，問俗貞敎，雅意作人；若巡鹽監察御史房如式，祗命恪趨，風聲先達。以使事莅茲土者，則刑部郎中金應徵、工部主事馬鳴鑾、南京戶部主事鄧宗臣、忽鳴，皆樂觀盛典者也。其綜理於外，則右布政使張任，右叅政滕伯輪、劉翽，左叅議余一龍，右叅議王嘉言，副使徐雲程、龔大器，僉
translation_en: … emblem of authority is newly assumed, serving as a model in both civil and military affairs. The former Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, Xie Pengju 謝鵬舉, whose reputation and plans still extend here, has long inspired the customs of the scholars. The Salt-Control Investigating Censor Wang Zao 王藻 inquires into local customs and upholds sound instruction, with a refined commitment to cultivating men of talent. As for the Salt-Control Investigating Censor Fang Rushi 房如式, he reverently received his mandate and hastens to his post, his moral reputation arriving before him. Those who have come to this land on official missions—the Director in the Ministry of Justice Jin Yingzheng 金應徵, the Secretary in the Ministry of Works Ma Mingluan 馬鳴鑾, and the Secretaries in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue Deng Zongchen 鄧宗臣 and Hu Ming 忽鳴—were all delighted to witness this grand occasion. As for those who managed affairs on the outside, there were the Right Administration Commissioner Zhang Ren 張任, the Right Administration Vice Commissioners Teng Bolun 滕伯輪 and Liu Hui 劉翽, the Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Yu Yilong 余一龍, the Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Wang Jiayan 王嘉言, the Surveillance Vice Commissioners Xu Yuncheng 徐雲程 and Gong Daqi 龔大器, the Assistant Surveillance Commissioners…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事王君賞張子仁而署都指
揮僉事葉歡亦與有防範之
勞焉若右叅政張國彦僉事
黃家棟署都指揮僉事韓沛
則以入
賀行署都指揮楊照則以遷秩
行皆始事有勞法當備書者
===
也
山東濟南府歷城縣儒學敎
諭吳伯誠謹序
punctuated:
事王君賞、張子仁，而署都指揮僉事葉歡亦與有防範之勞焉。若右叅政張國彦、僉事黃家棟、署都指揮僉事韓沛，則以入賀行；署都指揮楊照，則以遷秩行，皆始事有勞，法當備書者也。
山東濟南府歷城縣儒學敎諭吳伯誠謹序。
translation_en:
… Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Wang Junshang 王君賞 and Zhang Ziren 張子仁; and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Ye Huan 葉歡 also shared in the labor of security and supervision. As for Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Guoyan 張國彦, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Huang Jiadong 黃家棟, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Han Pei 韓沛, who departed to offer congratulations at Court; and Acting Regional Military Commissioner Yang Zhao 楊照, who departed upon promotion in rank—all contributed their efforts at the beginning of the affair, and by rule ought to be recorded in full.
Respectfully prefaced by Wu Bocheng 吳伯誠, Instructor of the Confucian School of Licheng County 歷城縣, Jinan Prefecture 濟南府, Shandong 山東.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
萬曆肆年浙江鄉試
監臨官
巡按浙江監察御史吳從憲〔惟時福建晉江縣人壬戌進士〕
提調官
浙江等處承宣布政使司左布政使王應顯〔惟謨福建漳浦縣人庚戌進士〕
浙江等處承宣布政使司左參政朱炳如〔仲南湖廣衡州衛籍桂陽縣人己未進士〕
監試官
浙江等處提刑按察司按察使蒙詔〔廷綸廣東番禺縣人壬戌進士〕
浙江等處提刑按察司副使王續之〔大卿四川南充縣人壬戌進士〕
===
考試官
山東濟南府歷城縣儒學教諭吳伯誠〔實甫直隸江寧縣人庚午貢士〕
河南開封府鄭州榮澤縣儒學教諭林守萬〔可一廣東番禺縣人辛酉貢士〕
同考試官
福建漳州府龍溪縣儒學教諭徐道明〔行之江西臨川縣人乙卯貢士〕
山東兗州府滕縣儒學教諭梁尚忠〔藎卿福建晉江縣人辛酉貢士〕
福建福州府侯官縣儒學教諭畢大魁〔元卿湖廣江陵縣人丁卯貢士〕
河南歸德府寧陵縣儒學教諭黃𡽪〔原靜湖廣麻城縣人甲子貢士〕
福建漳州府漳浦縣儒學教諭陳懋昭〔建中江西泰和縣人辛酉貢士〕
punctuated:
萬曆肆年浙江鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按浙江監察御史吳從憲〔惟時，福建晉江縣人，壬戌進士〕。

提調官：
浙江等處承宣布政使司左布政使王應顯〔惟謨，福建漳浦縣人，庚戌進士〕；
浙江等處承宣布政使司左參政朱炳如〔仲南，湖廣衡州衛籍，桂陽縣人，己未進士〕。

監試官：
浙江等處提刑按察司按察使蒙詔〔廷綸，廣東番禺縣人，壬戌進士〕；
浙江等處提刑按察司副使王續之〔大卿，四川南充縣人，壬戌進士〕。

考試官：
山東濟南府歷城縣儒學教諭吳伯誠〔實甫，直隸江寧縣人，庚午貢士〕；
河南開封府鄭州榮澤縣儒學教諭林守萬〔可一，廣東番禺縣人，辛酉貢士〕。

同考試官：
福建漳州府龍溪縣儒學教諭徐道明〔行之，江西臨川縣人，乙卯貢士〕；
山東兗州府滕縣儒學教諭梁尚忠〔藎卿，福建晉江縣人，辛酉貢士〕；
福建福州府侯官縣儒學教諭畢大魁〔元卿，湖廣江陵縣人，丁卯貢士〕；
河南歸德府寧陵縣儒學教諭黃𡽪〔原靜，湖廣麻城縣人，甲子貢士〕；
福建漳州府漳浦縣儒學教諭陳懋昭〔建中，江西泰和縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Examination of the Fourth Year of the Wanli Era (1576)

Supervising Official (監臨官):
Wu Congxian 吳從憲, Regional Inspector of Zhejiang and Investigating Censor (courtesy name Weishi 惟時, a native of Jinjiang County, Fujian; metropolitan graduate of the renxu year [1562]).

Proctors (提調官):
Wang Yingxian 王應顯, Left Administration Commissioner of the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission (courtesy name Weimo 惟謨, a native of Zhangpu County, Fujian; metropolitan graduate of the gengxu year [1550]).
Zhu Bingru 朱炳如, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission (courtesy name Zhongnan 仲南, a native of Guiyang County registered in Hengzhou Guard, Huguang; metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year [1559]).

Monitoring Officials (監試官):
Meng Zhao 蒙詔, Surveillance Commissioner of the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Commission (courtesy name Tinglun 廷綸, a native of Panyu County, Guangdong; metropolitan graduate of the renxu year [1562]).
Wang Xuzhi 王續之, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Commission (courtesy name Daqing 大卿, a native of Nanchong County, Sichuan; metropolitan graduate of the renxu year [1562]).

Examiners (考試官):
Wu Bocheng 吳伯誠, Instructor in the Confucian School of Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong (courtesy name Shifu 實甫, a native of Jiangning County, Southern Metropolitan Area [Zhili]; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the gengwu year [1570]).
Lin Shouwan 林守萬, Instructor in the Confucian School of Rongze County, Zhengzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan (courtesy name Keyi 可一, a native of Panyu County, Guangdong; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the xinyou year [1561]).

Associate Examiners (同考試官):
Xu Daoming 徐道明, Instructor in the Confucian School of Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian (courtesy name Xingzhi 行之, a native of Linchuan County, Jiangxi; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the yimao year [1555]).
Liang Shangzhong 梁尚忠, Instructor in the Confucian School of Teng County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong (courtesy name Jinqing 藎卿, a native of Jinjiang County, Fujian; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the xinyou year [1561]).
Bi Dakui 畢大魁, Instructor in the Confucian School of Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian (courtesy name Yuanqing 元卿, a native of Jiangling County, Huguang; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the dingmao year [1567]).
Huang Jie 黃𡽪, Instructor in the Confucian School of Ningling County, Guide Prefecture, Henan (courtesy name Yuanjing 原靜, a native of Macheng County, Huguang; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the jiazi year [1564]).
Chen Maozhao 陳懋昭, Instructor in the Confucian School of Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian (courtesy name Jianzhong 建中, a native of Taihe County, Jiangxi; tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the xinyou year [1561]).

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
直隸順德府唐山縣儒學教諭田舜耕〔宗孝廣西臨桂縣籍湖廣江夏縣人丁卯貢士〕
印卷官
浙江等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷周鳴鎬〔象文湖廣蘄水縣人監生〕
浙江等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷朱邦嘉〔逢高江西南城縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
兩浙都轉運鹽使司運使林應雷〔宗復福建閩縣人丙辰進士〕
杭州府知府吳自新〔伯恒應天府江寧縣籍直隸祁門縣人戊辰進士〕
嘉興府知府李橡〔孟栗江西豐城縣人壬戌進士〕
湖州府知府李頤〔惟貞江西餘干縣人戊辰進士〕
===
寧波府知府周良賓〔以尚福建晉江縣人乙丑進士〕
紹興府知府彭富〔仲理雲南大理衛人壬戌進士〕
受卷官
台州府知府李時漸〔伯鴻山東壽光縣人丙辰進士〕
嚴州府知府陳文煥〔汝昭江西臨川縣人乙丑進士〕
處州府知府熊子臣〔國良江西新昌縣人乙丑進士〕
杭州府推官胡桂芳〔時榮江西金谿縣人甲戌進士〕
寧波府推官葉時新〔惟懷直隸休寧縣人辛未進士〕
紹興府推官張孫振〔公緒廣西臨桂縣人辛未進士〕
punctuated:
直隸順德府唐山縣儒學教諭田舜耕〔宗孝，廣西臨桂縣籍，湖廣江夏縣人，丁卯貢士〕。
印卷官：
浙江等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷周鳴鎬〔象文，湖廣蘄水縣人，監生〕、浙江等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷朱邦嘉〔逢高，江西南城縣人，監生〕。
收掌試卷官：
兩浙都轉運鹽使司運使林應雷〔宗復，福建閩縣人，丙辰進士〕、杭州府知府吳自新〔伯恒，應天府江寧縣籍，直隸祁門縣人，戊辰進士〕、嘉興府知府李橡〔孟栗，江西豐城縣人，壬戌進士〕、湖州府知府李頤〔惟貞，江西餘干縣人，戊辰進士〕、寧波府知府周良賓〔以尚，福建晉江縣人，乙丑進士〕、紹興府知府彭富〔仲理，雲南大理衛人，壬戌進士〕。
受卷官：
台州府知府李時漸〔伯鴻，山東壽光縣人，丙辰進士〕、嚴州府知府陳文煥〔汝昭，江西臨川縣人，乙丑進士〕、處州府知府熊子臣〔國良，江西新昌縣人，乙丑進士〕、杭州府推官胡桂芳〔時榮，江西金谿縣人，甲戌進士〕、寧波府推官葉時新〔惟懷，直隸休寧縣人，辛未進士〕、紹興府推官張孫振〔公緒，廣西臨桂縣人，辛未進士〕。
translation_en:

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
