title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
此謂脩身在正其心
子曰吾十有五而志于學
尊賢使能俊傑在位則天下之士皆悅而
願立於其朝矣市廛而不征法而不廛
則天下之商皆悅而願藏於其市矣關
譏而不征則天下之旅皆悅而願出於
其路矣耕者助而不稅則天下之農皆
===
悅而願耕於其野矣廛無夫里之布則
天下之民皆悅而願爲之氓矣
易
彖曰大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天雲行雨
施品物流形大明終始六位時成時乗
六龍以御天乾道變化各正性命保合
大和乃利貞首出庶物萬國咸寧象曰
天行健君子以自彊不息
君子之光其暉吉也
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
此謂脩身在正其心。
子曰：「吾十有五而志于學。」
尊賢使能，俊傑在位，則天下之士皆悅而願立於其朝矣；市廛而不征，法而不廛，則天下之商皆悅而願藏於其市矣；關譏而不征，則天下之旅皆悅而願出於其路矣；耕者助而不稅，則天下之農皆悅而願耕於其野矣；廛無夫里之布，則天下之民皆悅而願爲之氓矣。

易
彖曰：大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。雲行雨施，品物流形。大明終始，六位時成，時乗六龍以御天。乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。首出庶物，萬國咸寧。象曰：天行健，君子以自彊不息。
君子之光，其暉吉也。
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

"This is what is meant by saying that the cultivation of the person depends on rectifying the mind." [Great Learning (Daxue)]

The Master said, "At fifteen, I set my heart upon learning." [Analects (Lunyu)]

"If a ruler honors the worthy and employs the able, so that men of outstanding talent are in office, then all the scholars of the world will be pleased and wish to stand in his court. If in the marketplace he levies a site-rent on shops without taxing the goods, or enforces the regulations without levying a site-rent, then all the merchants of the world will be pleased and wish to store their goods in his marketplace. If at the border passes there is inspection but no customs duty, then all the travelers of the world will be pleased and wish to travel on his roads. If those who till the fields assist in cultivating the public land and are not otherwise taxed, then all the farmers of the world will be pleased and wish to till in his fields. If the dwellings have no individual or neighborhood imposts of cloth, then all the people of the world will be pleased and wish to become his subjects." [Mencius (Mengzi)]

Book of Changes (Yijing)

"The Commentary on the Judgments (Tuan) says: Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! All things owe their beginning to it, and thus it governs heaven. The clouds move and the rain is distributed, and the various things flow into their forms. Greatly luminous from end to beginning, the six positions are completed according to their times, and at the proper time he mounts the six dragons to drive through heaven. The Way of Qian changes and transforms, so that each thing rectifies its nature and destiny; preserving and uniting the great harmony, it is advantageous and correct. He rises preeminent above the multitude of things, and the myriad states all enjoy peace. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: The movement of heaven is full of power; thus the superior man makes himself strong and untiring."

"The light of the superior man—its radiance brings good fortune."

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
形而上者謂之道
復德之本也恒德之固也
書
帝曰咨四岳有能典朕三禮僉曰伯夷帝
曰俞咨伯汝作秩宗夙夜惟寅直哉惟
清伯拜稽首讓于夔龍帝曰俞往欽哉
帝曰夔命汝典樂敎胄子直而溫寬而
栗剛而無虐簡而無傲詩言志歌永言
聲依永律和聲八音克諧無相奪倫神
===
人以和
沿于江海達于淮泗
無偏無黨王道蕩蕩無黨無偏王道平平
君子所其無逸先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則
知小人之依
詩
六月食鬱及薁七月亨葵及菽八月剝棗
十月穫稻為此春酒以介眉壽七月食
瓜八月斷壺九月叔苴采荼薪樗食我
punctuated:
形而上者謂之道。
復，德之本也；恒，德之固也。
書
帝曰：「咨！四岳，有能典朕三禮？」僉曰：「伯夷。」帝曰：「俞。咨！伯，汝作秩宗。夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。」伯拜稽首，讓于夔、龍。帝曰：「俞。往，欽哉！」帝曰：「夔！命汝典樂，敎胄子：直而溫，寬而栗，剛而無虐，簡而無傲。詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲。八音克諧，無相奪倫，神人以和。」
沿于江海，達于淮泗。
無偏無黨，王道蕩蕩；無黨無偏，王道平平。
君子所其無逸。先知稼穡之艱難，乃逸，則知小人之依。
詩
六月食鬱及薁，七月亨葵及菽，八月剝棗，十月穫稻，為此春酒，以介眉壽。七月食瓜，八月斷壺，九月叔苴，采荼薪樗，食我
translation_en:
"What is above form is called the Way."
"Return is the root of virtue; Constancy is the firmness of virtue."

Book of Documents (Shu)
"The Emperor said, 'Ah, Four Mountains! Is there anyone who can direct my three categories of rites?' All said, 'Boyi.' The Emperor said, 'Yes. Ah, Bo, you shall be Director of Sacrificial Rites. Morning and night be reverent; be upright, be pure.' Bo bowed and knocked his head on the ground, yielding in favor of Kui and Long. The Emperor said, 'Yes. Go, and be reverent!' The Emperor said, 'Kui! I command you to direct music and to teach the eldest sons: to be upright yet gentle, broad-minded yet firm, strong yet not tyrannical, simple yet not arrogant. Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs the words; notes depend on the prolongation; pitch-pipes harmonize the notes. When the eight timbres can be harmonized and do not encroach upon one another's order, spirits and men will thereby be brought into harmony.'"
"Following along the Yangzi and the sea, and reaching the Huai and the Si."
"Without偏 (partiality) and without faction, the Kingly Way is broad and vast; without faction and without partiality, the Kingly Way is level and easy."
"The noble man abides in taking no ease. When he first understands the hardships of sowing and reaping, and then takes his ease, he will understand what the lesser people depend upon."

Book of Odes (Shi)
"In the sixth month they eat dwarf-plums and wild grapes; in the seventh month they boil mallows and beans; in the eighth month they knock down dates; in the tenth month they harvest rice, to make this spring wine, so as to assist longevity. In the seventh month they eat melons; in the eighth month they cut down gourds; in the ninth month they gather hemp-seed; they pluck bitter herbs and cut ailanthus for firewood, to feed our…"

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
農夫九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重
穋禾麻菽麥嗟我農夫我稼旣同上入
執宮功晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋
其始播百穀二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日
納于凌陰四之日其蚤獻羔祭韭九月
肅霜十月滌場朋酒斯饗曰殺羔羊躋
彼公堂稱彼兕觥萬壽無疆
文王初載天作之合
百辟卿士媚于天子不解于位民之攸墍
===
帝命式于九圍
春秋
夏六月公會齊侯宋公陳侯鄭伯同盟于
幽〔莊公二十有七年〕齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕
遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕秋七月公會齊侯
宋公陳世子款鄭世子華盟于寗母〔僖公七年〕
公會齊侯于城濮〔莊公二十有七年〕春王
三月甲寅齊人伐衛〔莊公二十有八年〕
punctuated:
農夫。九月築場圃，十月納禾稼。黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫，我稼旣同，上入執宮功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯，亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。二之日鑿冰冲冲，三之日納于凌陰。四之日其蚤，獻羔祭韭。九月肅霜，十月滌場。朋酒斯饗，曰殺羔羊。躋彼公堂，稱彼兕觥，萬壽無疆。
文王初載，天作之合。
百辟卿士，媚于天子。不解于位，民之攸墍。
帝命式于九圍。
《春秋》
夏六月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、鄭伯同盟于幽〔莊公二十有七年〕；齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕；遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕；秋七月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳世子款、鄭世子華盟于寗母〔僖公七年〕；公會齊侯于城濮〔莊公二十有七年〕；春王三月甲寅，齊人伐衛〔莊公二十有八年〕；
translation_en:
… our farmers. In the ninth month they beat hard the vegetable garden for a threshing floor; in the tenth month they bring in the harvested grain: glutinous millet, panicled millet, late-sown and early-ripening grain, grain on the stalk, hemp, beans, and wheat. Oh, our farmers! Now that our harvests are gathered in, let us go up and enter to do the work on our houses. By day go gather thatch-grass; by night twist ropes; make haste to climb onto the roofs, for soon we shall begin again to sow the hundred grains. In the days of the second month they hew out the ice with ringing blows; in the days of the third month they convey it into the ice-house. In the days of the fourth month, early in the morning, they offer a lamb and sacrifice with wild chives. In the ninth month there is nipping frost; in the tenth month they sweep clean the threshing floor. With the two goblets of wine they hold a feast, saying, "Let us kill lambs and sheep, let us ascend that public hall, let us raise that rhinoceros-horn cup: 'Myriad years of life without bound!'"

In the early years of King Wen, Heaven made for him a match.

All the feudal lords and noble officers are devoted to the Son of Heaven; never remiss in their posts, through them the people find rest.

God on High commanded him to be a model to the nine regions.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):

In summer, in the sixth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, and together they made a covenant at You [twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhuang]; the men of Qi rescued Xing [first year of Duke Min]; thereupon they invaded Chu [fourth year of Duke Xi]; in autumn, in the seventh month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, Heir Apparent Kuan of Chen, and Heir Apparent Hua of Zheng, and made a covenant at Ningmu [seventh year of Duke Xi]; the Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Chengpu [twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhuang]; in spring, in the King's third month, on the day jiayin, the men of Qi invaded Wei [twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang]…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
楚屈完來盟于師僖公四年秋七月齊侯
使國佐如師成公二年
晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞昭公十有五年
禮記
是故昔先王尚有德尊有道任有能舉賢
而置之聚衆而誓之是故因天事天因
地事地因名山升中于天因吉土以饗
帝于郊升中于天而鳳皇降龜龍假饗
帝于郊而風雨節寒暑時是故聖人南
===
面而立而天下大治
縮酌用茅明酌也醆酒涗于清汁獻涗于
醆酒
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣
其在朝廷則道仁聖禮義之序燕處則聽
雅頌之音行步則有環佩之聲升車則
有鸞和之音居處有禮進退有度百官
得其宜萬事得其序
第貳塲
punctuated:
楚屈完來盟于師，僖公四年；秋七月，齊侯使國佐如師，成公二年。
晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞，昭公十有五年。
《禮記》
「是故昔先王尚有德，尊有道，任有能，舉賢而置之，聚衆而誓之。是故因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中于天，因吉土以饗帝于郊。升中于天而鳳皇降，龜龍假；饗帝于郊而風雨節，寒暑時。是故聖人南面而立而天下大治。」
「縮酌用茅，明酌也；醆酒涗于清，汁獻涗于醆酒。」
「朝覲，然後諸侯知所以臣。」
「其在朝廷，則道仁聖禮義之序；燕處，則聽雅頌之音；行步，則有環佩之聲；升車，則有鸞和之音。居處有禮，進退有度，百官得其宜，萬事得其序。」
第貳塲
translation_en:
"Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army" (4th year of Duke Xi); "In autumn, in the seventh month, the Marquis of Qi sent Guo Zuo to go to the army" (2nd year of Duke Cheng).
"Xun Wu of Jin led an army to attack Xianyu" (15th year of Duke Zhao).
Record of Rites (Liji)
"Therefore, in antiquity the former kings esteemed those who had virtue, honored those who possessed the Way, employed those who had ability, promoted the worthy and placed them in office, and assembled the multitude and bound them with solemn oaths. Therefore, following Heaven they served Heaven; following Earth they served Earth; making use of famous mountains they reported the achievement of great peace to Heaven; making use of auspicious ground they presented sacrificial offerings to the Supreme Ruler in the suburban sacrifice. When they reported the achievement of great peace to Heaven, the phoenixes descended and the tortoises and dragons arrived; when they presented sacrificial offerings to the Supreme Ruler in the suburban sacrifice, the winds and rains were seasonably regulated and cold and heat came at their proper times. Therefore, the sage stood facing south and all under Heaven was in great order."
"Straining the sacrificial wine through couch-grass produces the clear wine; the zhan wine is strained by mixing it with clear liquid, and the aromatic herbal juice is strained by mixing it with zhan wine."
"Through court audiences, the feudal lords know how to act as subjects."
"When he is in the court, he speaks of the order of benevolence, sageliness, ritual propriety, and righteousness; when he is at leisure in private, he listens to the music of the Odes and Hymns; when he walks, there is the sound of his girdle-pendants; when he mounts his carriage, there is the sound of the luan and he bells. His dwelling and demeanor have ritual propriety, his advancing and retiring have measure, the hundred officials obtain their proper places, and the myriad affairs obtain their proper order."
Second Session

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
明堂辟雍之建詩書所稱曷以加巳其
儀度品式可傳而數歟厥所以凝帝祉
而章儒化者應效亦有聞歟若分祀合
祀配天配帝義各有指歟而三歲一郊
毋迺疏歟釋奠養老頒樂舞簡不率事
各有屬歟而帝入四學毋迺繁歟我
太祖奄有區夏首建南北
郊壇分祀
天地而繼復合祀斷自
===
宸衷抑有所本歟肇脩人紀創行太學釋奠再
舉
臨幸而
列聖初服率一
親御果爲定制歟逮我
世宗神聖追媲
太祖
郊祀
視學纘𠼪紹勤而南北郊分建之議其有据周
punctuated: 明堂、辟雍之建，《詩》《書》所稱，曷以加巳！其儀度品式，可傳而數歟？厥所以凝帝祉而章儒化者，應效亦有聞歟？若分祀、合祀，配天、配帝，義各有指歟？而三歲一郊，毋迺疏歟？釋奠、養老，頒樂舞、簡不率，事各有屬歟？而帝入四學，毋迺繁歟？我太祖奄有區夏，首建南北郊壇，分祀天地，而繼復合祀，斷自宸衷，抑有所本歟？肇脩人紀，創行太學釋奠，再舉臨幸，而列聖初服，率一親御，果爲定制歟？逮我世宗，神聖追媲太祖，郊祀、視學，纘𠼪紹勤，而南北郊分建之議，其有据《周…
translation_en:
…and the establishment of the Hall of Light (Mingtang) and the Circular Moat Academy (Piyong)—what is praised in the Classic of Poetry (Shi) and the Classic of History (Shu) could hardly be surpassed! Can their ceremonial regulations and ritual specifications be recounted and enumerated? And has anything been heard of the efficacious responses by which they consolidated imperial blessings and made manifest the transforming influence of Confucian learning? As for separate sacrifices versus joint sacrifices, and associating ancestors with Heaven versus associating them with the Lord on High, does the meaning of each have its specific purport? And was performing the suburban sacrifice once every three years not perhaps too infrequent? As for the libation ceremony (shidian) and the nourishing of the aged, the promulgation of music and dances and the weeding out of the disobedient, did each matter have its proper sphere? And was the ruler's entering the four academies not perhaps too burdensome?

When our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) came to possess the realm of China, he first built the Northern and Southern Suburban Altars to offer separate sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, and then subsequently returned to joint sacrifices; was this decided purely from the imperial heart, or was it based on precedent? Setting in order the bonds of human society, he initiated the performance of the libation ceremony at the Directorate of Education (Taixue) and twice graced it with his imperial presence, whereas the successive sacred emperors at the beginning of their reigns generally attended in person once—did this indeed become the established institution? Coming down to our Emperor Shizong, whose divine sageliness matched that of the Grand Progenitor, in the suburban sacrifices and the inspection of the academy he continued the martial and diligent heritage; as for the deliberations on establishing separate Northern and Southern Suburban Altars, were they based on the Rites of Zhou (Zhou…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
禮歟正
先師孔子之位果度越千古歟
皇上嗣臨丕基
郊祀則積誠致潔
視學則弁服賜講暨於
二聖鴻庥駿儀有符合歟亦可揚其盛歟然而
合祀所以尊
天養老所以教孝兩者討述而著令焉尤不能
無竢於
===
聖天子議禮也諸士其鋪張揚搉之以賛
盛典毋讓
問自昔英辟碩輔所以昌化翊烈者孰不
以率綜吏理爲首務哉虞周穆灝欽亮
董訓楙景靡尚已嗣兹敏睿端扆壹以
振核程工而御座書刺史之名縣令試
理人之論毋迺煩黷過歟孝宣之優孝
文也何繇而又謂孝文非以寛致平抑
有説歟洪惟我
punctuated:
禮歟？正先師孔子之位，果度越千古歟？皇上嗣臨丕基，郊祀則積誠致潔，視學則弁服賜講，暨於二聖鴻庥駿儀，有符合歟？亦可揚其盛歟？然而合祀所以尊天，養老所以教孝，兩者討述而著令焉，尤不能無竢於聖天子議禮也。諸士其鋪張揚搉之，以賛盛典，毋讓。

問：自昔英辟碩輔，所以昌化翊烈者，孰不以率綜吏理爲首務哉？虞、周穆灝，欽亮董訓，楙景靡尚已。嗣兹敏睿端扆，壹以振核程工，而御座書刺史之名，縣令試理人之論，毋迺煩黷過歟？孝宣之優孝文也何繇？而又謂孝文非以寛致平，抑有説歟？洪惟我
translation_en:
… Rites of Zhou (Zhouli)? And did rectifying the title and status of the Former Teacher Confucius truly surpass all antiquity? Since His Majesty succeeded to the great foundation, in the suburban sacrifices he has accumulated sincerity and achieved purity, and in inspecting the Imperial University he has donned the ceremonial cap and robes and bestowed lectures. Do these accord with the vast blessings and grand ceremonies of the Two Sages [Emperors Taizu and Shizong]? Can their flourishing magnificence also be extolled? Yet joint sacrifice is the means to venerate Heaven, and nourishing the aged is the means to teach filial piety; to investigate and set forth both of these and codify them into ordinances is something for which we cannot but await the Sacred Son of Heaven's deliberation on the rites. Gentlemen, set this forth and discuss it fully to assist in the grand canons, and do not hold back.

Question: Since antiquity, among illustrious sovereigns and great chief ministers who made transformative governance flourish and assisted in meritorious achievements, who did not take leading and overseeing the administration of officials as their foremost task? The eras of Yu [Shun] and Zhou were august and vast; with reverent trustworthiness they supervised and instructed, and their flourishing brilliance cannot be surpassed. Thereafter, perspicacious and sagely rulers sat upright before the imperial screen, devoting themselves single-mindedly to rousing and verifying performance and measuring accomplishments. Yet writing the names of Regional Inspectors (cishi) on the screen beside the imperial throne, or testing District Magistrates (xianling) with discourses on governing the people—were these not overly繁瑣 (cumbersome) and meddlesome? On what grounds was Emperor Xiaoxuan of Han judged superior to Emperor Xiaowen? And is there an explanation for the claim that Emperor Xiaowen did not achieve peace through leniency? Reflecting upon our…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
二祖稽制
列聖繩軌有司百執事條式舉課令森且飭凡
以惠賜元元登理爾厥載
會典可槩陳歟維時吏奉職職符泰階也亦可
揚其盛歟我
皇上勵精法
祖脩明典常
申敕羣工罔弗嚮卽有僚稟稟承
休德巳顧宇內治猶鮮效省方之使奏計之吏
===
所以課功實而稽殿最者猶皇皇焉未
足盡稱
主上意也毋迺吏猶競名襲奇鮮實政歟闒茸
叨憤在位未盡殄歟將采名拘文法溷
碔璧而士鮮奮歟然則漢制六條九年
之令唐人五術八計之議厥於我
祖宗法意有繇合者歟亦可於
今日彷行否歟夫吏不奉詔書有責上計簿
徒具文有責而條奏故事最稱上意在
punctuated: 二祖稽制，列聖繩軌，有司百執事條式舉課，令森且飭，凡以惠賜元元登理爾。厥載《會典》，可槩陳歟？維時吏奉職，職符泰階也，亦可揚其盛歟？我皇上勵精法祖，脩明典常，申敕羣工，罔弗嚮。卽有僚稟稟承休德巳，顧宇內治猶鮮效，省方之使、奏計之吏，所以課功實而稽殿最者，猶皇皇焉未足盡稱主上意也。毋迺吏猶競名襲奇，鮮實政歟？闒茸叨憤在位，未盡殄歟？將采名拘文法，溷碔璧而士鮮奮歟？然則漢制六條、九年之令，唐人五術、八計之議，厥於我祖宗法意，有繇合者歟？亦可於今日彷行否歟？夫吏不奉詔書有責，上計簿徒具文有責，而條奏故事最稱上意，在
translation_en:
… Two Founders examined and established the institutions, and the Successive Sages followed the tracks. For the authorities and the hundred functionaries, the regulations and models for evaluation and assessment were made strict and orderly—all merely in order to bestow favor upon the common people and ascend to good governance. As these are recorded in the Collected Statutes (Huidian), can they be outlined in general? At those times, officials fulfilled their duties, and their performance matched the Grand Staircase of peace; can that flourishing state also be extolled?

Our Emperor exerts his spirit to model himself on the Ancestors, clarifying and renewing the constant statutes, and repeatedly admonishing the assembled officials, so that none fail to turn toward the right path. Even though the officials reverently and fearfully uphold his illustrious virtue, looking across the realm, governance still shows few results. The envoys who inspect the regions and the officials who submit their reports of accounts—those by whom actual achievements are evaluated and ranks of demerit and merit are verified—are still anxiously hurrying about, yet unable to fully satisfy the Sovereign's intentions. Could it be that officials still compete for fame and affect novelty, with little substantive governance? Or that base and incompetent men, greedily and recklessly [?] occupying office, have not been completely eradicated? Or is it that in selecting reputations and clinging to the letter of the law, worthless stones and fine jade are confounded, so that gentlemen rarely rouse themselves?

If so, then the Han regulations of the Six Articles and the ordinance of nine-year terms, and the Tang discussions of the Five Methods and the Eight Assessments—do they have points of convergence with the spirit of the laws of our Ancestors? And can they also be imitated and put into practice today, or not? Now, there was a reprimand for officials who did not carry out imperial decrees, and there was a reprimand when the submitted account registers were mere formalities, whereas presenting itemized memorials on precedents best suited the Sovereign's intentions. In…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
今日咸起敝維風之所願聞者試颺言之以
商
太平之略
問學術逸軌則道統蝕異端說昌則正學
裂異端之害莫甚二氏當孔子時佛教
未興而老聃氏實與接轂孔子不爲非
且就而問禮焉三千之徒何不聞有惑
其說者歟楊氏出於老墨氏近於佛乃
孟軻氏則肆辯而力排之至指數爲無
===
父無君充塞仁義若將迸殛之俾罔逃
臯抑何嚴歟夫老佛楊墨畔我正道章
章較著乃吾黨又有謂似是之非者有
謂彌近理而大亂真者旣曰似矣何以
言非旣曰近矣何以言亂此必有說矣
我
國家崇儒重道異類屏息而都人士亦率羹
牆唐虞步趨孔孟陳仁義之弘謨談性
命之奧旨及叩其指歸尚不能窺異端
punctuated:
今日咸起敝維風之所願聞者。試颺言之，以商太平之略。

問：學術逸軌，則道統蝕；異端說昌，則正學裂。異端之害，莫甚二氏。當孔子時，佛教未興，而老聃氏實與接轂，孔子不爲非，且就而問禮焉，三千之徒，何不聞有惑其說者歟？楊氏出於老，墨氏近於佛，乃孟軻氏則肆辯而力排之，至指數爲無父無君，充塞仁義，若將迸殛之，俾罔逃臯，抑何嚴歟？夫老、佛、楊、墨畔我正道，章章較著。乃吾黨又有謂「似是之非」者，有謂「彌近理而大亂真」者。旣曰似矣，何以言非？旣曰近矣，何以言亂？此必有說矣。我國家崇儒重道，異類屏息，而都人士亦率羹牆唐、虞，步趨孔、孟，陳仁義之弘謨，談性命之奧旨；及叩其指歸，尚不能窺異端
translation_en:
… at the present day are all matters we wish to hear about for reviving what has fallen into decay and upholding the moral wind. Try to set them forth clearly, so that we may deliberate upon the grand strategy for Great Peace.

Question: When scholarly learning strays from the proper track, the transmission of the Way is eroded; when heterodox doctrines flourish, orthodox learning is rent apart. Among the harms of heterodoxy, none is worse than the two sects [of Daoism and Buddhism]. In the time of Confucius, Buddhism had not yet arisen, whereas Lao Dan actually rubbed hubs with him as a contemporary. Confucius did not condemn him, and even went to inquire of him about ritual; yet among his three thousand disciples, why do we never hear of anyone being deluded by Laozi's doctrines? Yang Zhu derived from Laozi, and Mo Di was close to Buddhism; yet Meng Ke [Mencius] argued at length and forcefully rejected them, going so far as to point them out and denounce them as acknowledging neither father nor ruler and blocking up benevolence and righteousness—as though he were about to banish and execute them so that they could not escape their guilt. Why was he so severe? Now, that Laozi, the Buddha, Yang Zhu, and Mo Di rebel against our orthodox Way is crystal clear. Yet within our own Confucian school there are also those who speak of what is "seemingly right but actually wrong," and those who speak of what is "all the closer to principle and yet greatly confounds the truth." Since it is called "seemingly right," why call it wrong? Since it is called "close," why say it confounds? There must be an explanation for this. Our dynasty reveres Confucianism and honors the Way, so that heterodox sorts hold their breath in submission. Meanwhile, scholars and gentlemen everywhere generally fix their gaze upon Tang Yao and Yu Shun [as if seeing them in their soup and on their walls], and walk in the footsteps of Confucius and Mencius, setting forth grand plans of benevolence and righteousness and discussing the abstruse purport of human nature and destiny. Yet when one probes their ultimate aim, they cannot even peer past the…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之藩籬甚者包藏詐譎厚裒朋援立標
幟設門竇以獵取聲譽爲世大蠹然則
道之不明也老佛之害歟楊墨之害歟
夫老佛之徒雖離宗貫尚能堅信其師
說而不變乃吾孔孟之徒外雖誦習其
言而中自矛盾敧鑿者將誰與闢歟昔
孟子欲正人心而曰息邪說距詖行今
之所當息而距者安在諸士辨業景聖
將慨然有決鵠坊潰之思者其詳著於
===
篇以爲世教助
問記言廣谷大川異制民生其間異俗蓋
俗尚之殊自古記之矣乃曰上化下謂
之風下從上謂之俗則風習之異亦係
於所化然耶浙省扆山襟海應潮分東
西其名郡象邑星列碁布蓋文獻奧區
已廼其俗尚有迥然不侔者何耶說者
謂杭處會省籍先朝繁華又車舟輻輳
民樂商趨業然好蕩而習靡嘉湖澤沮
punctuated:
之藩籬。甚者，包藏詐譎，厚裒朋援，立標幟、設門竇，以獵取聲譽，爲世大蠹。然則道之不明也，老、佛之害歟？楊、墨之害歟？夫老、佛之徒，雖離宗貫，尚能堅信其師說而不變；乃吾孔、孟之徒，外雖誦習其言，而中自矛盾敧鑿者，將誰與闢歟？昔孟子欲正人心，而曰「息邪說，距詖行」，今之所當息而距者安在？諸士辨業景聖，將慨然有決鵠坊潰之思者，其詳著於篇，以爲世教助。
問：《記》言：「廣谷大川異制，民生其間異俗。」蓋俗尚之殊，自古記之矣。乃曰：「上化下謂之風，下從上謂之俗。」則風習之異，亦係於所化然耶？浙省扆山襟海，應潮分東、西，其名郡象邑，星列碁布，蓋文獻奧區已。廼其俗尚有迥然不侔者，何耶？說者謂杭處會省，籍先朝繁華，又車舟輻輳，民樂商趨業，然好蕩而習靡；嘉、湖澤沮
translation_en:
…the outer fence [of those heterodox teachings]. Worse still, they harbor deceit and guile, amass cliques and mutual support, set up banners, and establish factional gateways in order to hunt for fame and reputation, becoming great parasites upon the world. If that is so, when the Way is not made clear, is it the harm done by Laozi and the Buddha? Or is it the harm done by Yang Zhu and Mo Di? Now, although the followers of Laozi and the Buddha have departed from the fundamental thread of truth, they are still able to firmly believe in their masters' doctrines without wavering. Yet among the followers of our Confucius and Mencius, who outwardly recite and practice their words while inwardly contradicting and subverting them—with whom shall we join to refute them? In antiquity, Mencius wished to rectify the human mind and said, "Put an end to perverse doctrines and oppose one-sided conduct." Wherein lie the things that today ought to be ended and opposed? You gentlemen, who discern your studies and revere the sages, and who surely harbor the impassioned resolve to aim squarely at the target and dam up the bursting dike—set forth your views in detail in your essays, as an aid to the moral instruction of the age.

Question: The Record of Rites (Liji) states: "Broad valleys and great rivers have different formations, and the people born among them have different customs." Indeed, differences in popular customs and preferences have been recorded since antiquity. Yet it is also said: "When superiors transform inferiors, it is called moral influence (feng); when inferiors follow superiors, it is called custom (su)." Does the divergence in customs and habits, then, also depend upon how the people are transformed? Zhejiang province backs against the mountains and embraces the sea, divided into East and West along the tidal bore; its famed prefectures and prominent counties are arrayed like stars and spread out like pieces on a chessboard—truly a profound heartland of culture and learning. Why is it, then, that their customs and preferences are utterly dissimilar? Commentators say that Hangzhou (Hang), situated as the provincial capital, relies on the splendor inherited from the former dynasty, and with carriages and boats converging upon it like spokes to a hub, its people delight in taking up commerce as their livelihood, yet they are fond of dissipation and accustomed to extravagance; Jiaxing (Jia) and Huzhou (Hu) are marshy and low-lying…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之國殖餉所資民饒而喜事越以東民
嗇業尚虛江左之餘風在焉齒繁多慧
每射利四出而輕去其鄉婺衢上流諸
郡衣冠淳龐尚有先進之遺然往往訐
而好鬪勇而尚氣甌栝之俗亦號近古
雖兩地奢儉異齊而玩法逋賦則均其
俗尚之殊若此無亦自昔所遺耶夫習
俗移人流弊日趨議者謂獻疇靡費婚
娶傾貲服用太僭樗蒲競肆然歟否歟
===
又謂緇黃雜沓倡優駢聚豪强逞威遊
俠踰檢然歟否歟又謂南北選募人樂
從兵山海阻遙民多獷習抑何繇而致
是歟今欲剗削舊習與民維新一道德
以同風俗使奢者約薄者敦賈勇者知
輕生之戒逐利者更力本之圖其政令
當何爲先其禁革當何最急轉移默奪
之機又果安在此諸生扼腕以談時事
所當急陳也願與商之
punctuated: 之國，殖餉所資，民饒而喜事。越以東民嗇業、尚虛，江左之餘風在焉；齒繁多慧，每射利四出而輕去其鄉。婺、衢上流諸郡，衣冠淳龐，尚有先進之遺，然往往訐而好鬪，勇而尚氣。甌、栝之俗亦號近古，雖兩地奢儉異齊，而玩法逋賦則均。其俗尚之殊若此，無亦自昔所遺耶？夫習俗移人，流弊日趨。議者謂獻疇靡費、婚娶傾貲、服用太僭、樗蒲競肆，然歟否歟？又謂緇黃雜沓、倡優駢聚、豪强逞威、遊俠踰檢，然歟否歟？又謂南北選募，人樂從兵，山海阻遙，民多獷習，抑何繇而致是歟？今欲剗削舊習，與民維新，一道德以同風俗，使奢者約、薄者敦，賈勇者知輕生之戒，逐利者更力本之圖，其政令當何爲先？其禁革當何最急？轉移默奪之機，又果安在？此諸生扼腕以談時事，所當急陳也，願與商之。
translation_en: …[Jiaxing and Huzhou are marshy] lands upon which agricultural production and state revenue depend; the people there are affluent and fond of making trouble. East of Yue (Shaoxing), the people have meager livelihoods and value empty talk, retaining the lingering airs of the Jiangzuo region; their population is dense and many are clever, so they often go out in all directions in pursuit of profit and lightly leave their native places. In the upstream prefectures of Wu (Jinhua) and Qu (Quzhou), the gentry are simple and honest, still preserving the legacy of earlier generations, yet people frequently expose others' faults and love to brawl, prizing bravery and spiritedness. The customs of Ou (Wenzhou) and Gua (Chuzhou) are also said to be close to antiquity; although the two regions differ in extravagance and frugality, they are alike in trifling with the law and evading taxes. That their customs and preferences differ like this—is it not something handed down from the past? Now, habits and customs transform people, and rampant abuses worsen day by day. Critics say that banquets and social exchanges are wasteful, marriages exhaust family fortunes, clothing and articles of use are overly presumptuous, and gambling is fiercely unrestrained—is this so or not? They also say that Buddhist monks and Daoist priests mingle in crowds, entertainers and actors gather in droves, local bullies flex their might, and wandering knights-errant transgress the bounds of propriety—is this so or not? They also say that with recruitment in the north and south, people gladly join the military, and where mountains and seas are remote and obstructing, the people mostly have fierce and unruly habits—by what cause has it come to this? If today we wish to pare away old habits, make a fresh start with the people, and unify morality in order to harmonize customs—causing the extravagant to become frugal, the frivolous to become earnest, those who peddle bravery to know the warning against taking life lightly, and those who chase profit to instead plan on devoting their strength to the fundamental occupation (agriculture)—what should take precedence in our administrative orders? What is most urgent in our prohibitions and reforms? And where indeed lies the pivot for shifting and quietly transforming them? These are current affairs that you students discuss while clasping your wrists in indignation, and which you ought urgently to set forth; I wish to deliberate on them with you.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
問東南海內財貨之所總土沃物饒民衆
煩夥加以波濤之險舟楫之便故姦宄
萌生其間即吾浙省會之地防範捕詰
亦云人具而法申廼郊關暮夜則有剽
吏而奪之金者至厪
嚴旨督獲雖旋即逮繫然亦肆矣夫曩者醜夷
不靖師旅叢興憂在四境耳今稱乂安
矣而猶有此盜殆非盛世所宜見也豈
凋瘵未復而衣食闕歟抑導民之路失
===
歟古者太宰以九職任萬民大司馬以
九伐正邦國法至詳密後世無聞獨操
一切勝之故有以鉤鉅者有以投筩者
有以致羣偷者有以知主名者有以解
繩喻者有以設三科者有單車而下之
者非無聲施抑亦末矣昔人有言平盜
非難絕之爲難吾觀賈子瑰瑋之論亦
爲太息所以消姦萌而保大業者宜在
今日豈無其術歟幸商摧之以佐元元毋謂
punctuated: 問：東南海內財貨之所總，土沃物饒，民衆煩夥，加以波濤之險，舟楫之便，故姦宄萌生其間。即吾浙省會之地，防範捕詰，亦云人具而法申；廼郊關暮夜，則有剽吏而奪之金者，至厪嚴旨督獲，雖旋即逮繫，然亦肆矣！夫曩者醜夷不靖，師旅叢興，憂在四境耳；今稱乂安矣，而猶有此盜，殆非盛世所宜見也。豈凋瘵未復，而衣食闕歟？抑導民之路失歟？古者太宰以九職任萬民，大司馬以九伐正邦國，法至詳密；後世無聞，獨操一切勝之。故有以鉤鉅者，有以投筩者，有以致羣偷者，有以知主名者，有以解繩喻者，有以設三科者，有單車而下之者，非無聲施，抑亦末矣。昔人有言：「平盜非難，絕之爲難。」吾觀賈子瑰瑋之論，亦爲太息。所以消姦萌而保大業者，宜在今日，豈無其術歟？幸商摧之，以佐元元，毋謂
translation_en: Question: The southeast is where the wealth and goods of the empire converge. Its soil is fertile, its products abundant, and its population dense and numerous. Added to this are the hazards of wind and waves and the convenience of boats and oars; hence, evildoers and bandits sprout up in its midst. Even here in the provincial capital of our Zhejiang, as for precautions, defense, arrest, and interrogation, it may be said that the personnel are in place and the laws are clearly promulgated; yet at dusk and night around the suburban customs barriers, there have been those who robbed officials and seized their money, to the point of troubling His Majesty to issue a stern decree supervising their capture. Although they were soon arrested and bound, this was nonetheless brazen! In the past, when vile barbarians were restive and military expeditions repeatedly arose, the worry lay along the four borders; now the realm is said to be at peace and well-governed, yet there are still such bandits—this is hardly what ought to be seen in a flourishing age. Could it be that exhaustion and distress have not yet been alleviated, and food and clothing are lacking? Or has the way of guiding the people been lost? In antiquity, the Grand Councilor (Taizai) employed the myriad people through the Nine Occupations, and the Minister of War (Da sima) rectified the states through the Nine Punitive Expeditions; the institutions were extremely detailed and thorough. In later ages nothing of this was heard, and officials merely relied on expedient measures to prevail over them. Thus there were those who used "hooks and barbs" (clever interrogation techniques), those who used "secret举报 bamboo tubes" (touyong), those who summoned the band of thieves together, those who knew the ringleaders' names, those who used the analogy of untying a knotted cord, those who established three categories of criteria, and those who brought them to submission riding in a single carriage—not that these lacked renown and effect, yet they were merely addressing the branches rather than the root. People of the past had a saying: "Suppressing bandits is not difficult; eradicating them is what is difficult." When I read Master Jia's (Jia Yi 賈誼) extraordinary discourse, I too heave a deep sigh. The means to eliminate the buds of villainy and preserve the great enterprise ought to lie in the present day—how could there be no art for it? Please deliberate upon this to aid the common people; do not say…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
此謂脩身在正其心
朱用光
同考試官教諭田批脩身正心乃大學一篇要
領此作發明殆盡
同考試官教諭畢批講脩正多拘局上文惟此
獨得題旨錄之
考試官教諭林批說理頗明
===
考試官教諭吳批順暢
傳者結言脩身之要盖事其心而已蓋身統於
心者也心有所累而身因之謂脩身不在于正
心也哉今夫天下國家之本在身則身之不可
以不脩也固矣然經文必先之以正心也果何
謂哉蓋心所以主宰乎此身者也今觀喜怒憂
懼一累於私而視聽飲食遂失其則此之謂吾
身非外也而制外必始於養中此心非內也而
直內斯可以方外欲身之善其應事之則也而
punctuated:
第壹場。
四書。
「此謂脩身在正其心。」
朱用光。
同考試官教諭田批：「脩身正心，乃《大學》一篇要領，此作發明殆盡。」
同考試官教諭畢批：「講脩正多拘局上文，惟此獨得題旨，錄之。」
考試官教諭林批：「說理頗明。」
考試官教諭吳批：「順暢。」

傳者結言脩身之要，盖事其心而已。蓋身統於心者也，心有所累而身因之，謂脩身不在于正心也哉？今夫天下國家之本在身，則身之不可以不脩也固矣。然經文必先之以正心也，果何謂哉？蓋心所以主宰乎此身者也。今觀喜怒憂懼一累於私，而視聽飲食遂失其則，此之謂：吾身非外也，而制外必始於養中；此心非內也，而直內斯可以方外。欲身之善其應事之則也，而
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books

"This is why it is said that the cultivation of the person depends on rectifying the mind."
By Zhu Yongguang 朱用光.

Associate Examiner and Instructor Tian 田 comments: "Cultivating the person and rectifying the mind are the essential points of the entire Great Learning (Daxue). This composition elucidates them almost exhaustively."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Bi 畢 comments: "In discussing cultivation and rectification, most candidates were overly constrained by the preceding passage; this piece alone grasped the true purport of the topic, so I have selected it for inclusion."
Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: "Its exposition of moral principle is quite clear."
Examiner and Instructor Wu 吳 comments: "Smooth and fluent."

The commentator concludes by stating the essential point of cultivating the person: it is simply a matter of attending to one's mind. For the person is governed by the mind; when the mind is encumbered by something, the person follows suit. How then could one say that cultivating the person does not lie in rectifying the mind? Now, the root of the empire, the state, and the family lies in the person; that the person cannot go uncultivated is therefore certain. Yet why did the Classic text necessarily precede this with rectifying the mind? It is because the mind is that which acts as master over this person. When we observe how, once fondness, anger, worry, or fear are encumbered by selfish partiality, seeing, hearing, eating, and drinking consequently lose their proper norms—this is what is meant: Our person is not merely external, yet regulating the external must begin with nourishing the center; this mind is not merely internal, yet straightening the internal is how one can square the external. If one wishes the person to perfect its norms in responding to affairs, …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
心固事之綱維也于未事之先而懋夫操存之
力誠其所必有事焉者矣欲身之善其應物之
則也而心固物之權度也于無物之始而致夫
時保之功誠其所不容緩焉者矣存養夫至虛
之體俾將迎之私不得以擾之是非專事于心
也不如是吾懼心一馳焉而身將無所管攝也
然則經文語脩身而必在正心也非此之謂哉
省察夫至靈之用俾情欲之感不得以累之是
非徒存其心也不如是吾恐心一放焉而身將
===
無所檢束也然則經文以脩身而本之正心也
非此之謂哉誠能正心以脩身則齊治均平一
以貫之而大學之道無餘蘊矣雖然正心之功
密矣誠意之後非幾盡黜所未正者先事後事
之際耳正之云者豈有加於誠之之功哉操而
存之順天機自然之妙而不容以人力參焉未
應不先已應不後感而遂通可以言正亦可以
言脩矣噫此聖學也善學者思之
子曰吾十有五而志于學
punctuated:
心固事之綱維也，于未事之先而懋夫操存之力，誠其所必有事焉者矣；欲身之善其應物之則也，而心固物之權度也，于無物之始而致夫時保之功，誠其所不容緩焉者矣。存養夫至虛之體，俾將迎之私不得以擾之，是非專事于心也，不如是，吾懼心一馳焉，而身將無所管攝也，然則經文語脩身而必在正心也，非此之謂哉？省察夫至靈之用，俾情欲之感不得以累之，是非徒存其心也，不如是，吾恐心一放焉，而身將無所檢束也，然則經文以脩身而本之正心也，非此之謂哉？誠能正心以脩身，則齊治均平一以貫之，而《大學》之道無餘蘊矣。雖然，正心之功密矣。誠意之後，非幾盡黜，所未正者，先事後事之際耳。正之云者，豈有加於誠之之功哉？操而存之，順天機自然之妙，而不容以人力參焉。未應不先，已應不後，感而遂通，可以言正，亦可以言脩矣。噫！此聖學也，善學者思之。

子曰：「吾十有五而志于學。」
translation_en:
…the mind is indeed the guiding thread of affairs; before affairs arise, to exert effort in grasping and preserving it is truly something one must be engaged in. If one wishes the person to perfect its principles for responding to things, the mind is indeed the scale and measure of things; at the beginning when no things are present, to apply the effort of constant preservation is truly something that brooks no delay. To preserve and nurture its supremely tenuous substance so that the selfishness of anticipation and lingering cannot disturb it—this is not merely attending exclusively to the mind; without this, I fear that once the mind gallops away, the person will have nothing to govern and hold it together. This being so, when the Classic text speaks of cultivating the person and insists that it lies in rectifying the mind, is this not what it means? To examine and scruntinize its supremely numinous function so that the stirrings of passions and desires cannot encumber it—this is not merely preserving the mind in vain; without this, I fear that once the mind is let loose, the person will have nothing to restrain and bind it. This being so, when the Classic text takes cultivating the person and roots it in rectifying the mind, is this not what it means? If one can truly rectify the mind in order to cultivate the person, then regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world will all be threaded together as one, and the Way of the Great Learning (Daxue) will have no remaining secrets. Even so, the effort of rectifying the mind is subtle indeed. After making the intentions sincere, improper incipient tendencies are completely dismissed; what remains unrectified is only at the juncture before and after affairs. What is called rectifying it—how could it add anything beyond the effort of making the intentions sincere? Grasping and preserving it, one follows the natural subtlety of the heavenly mechanism without allowing human artifice to interfere therein. Before responding, one does not anticipate; after responding, one does not linger; when stirred, it immediately penetrates—this can be called rectified, and it can also be called cultivated. Alas! This is the learning of the sages; let those who are good at learning ponder it.

The Master said: "At fifteen I set my heart on learning."

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王建中
同考試官教諭陳批聖學成始成終不外此志
是作得之宜式
同考試官教諭黃批發志學在於及時尤得聖
人語意
考試官教諭林批親切有味
考試官教諭吳批平正
聖人自叙其始之所志作聖之功在是矣蓋學
以求至乎聖也始學而志于是焉謂非夫子聖
===
功之所在乎宜其自叙以勉人也若曰君子之
學有所似詣其極必有所似立其基我非生而
知之者也而其始之所從事何如哉蓋年至十
五成人之德雖未敢以自居聖脩之功則于是
乎託始意念之精專不眩於他岐必以大道爲
嚮往之歸精神之凝聚不安於小成務以至善
爲進脩之準方幸其時之旣至而又慮其或至
于易失也汲汲焉乗時以自勵而一心典學之
勤固有好古敏求而日與此學相爲周旋者矣
punctuated:
王建中
同考試官教諭陳批：聖學成始成終，不外此志。是作得之，宜式。
同考試官教諭黃批：發志學在於及時，尤得聖人語意。
考試官教諭林批：親切有味。
考試官教諭吳批：平正。
聖人自叙其始之所志，作聖之功在是矣。蓋學以求至乎聖也，始學而志于是焉，謂非夫子聖功之所在乎？宜其自叙以勉人也。若曰：君子之學有所似詣其極，必有所似立其基。我非生而知之者也，而其始之所從事何如哉？蓋年至十五，成人之德雖未敢以自居，聖脩之功則于是乎託始。意念之精專，不眩於他岐，必以大道爲嚮往之歸；精神之凝聚，不安於小成，務以至善爲進脩之準。方幸其時之旣至，而又慮其或至于易失也，汲汲焉乗時以自勵，而一心典學之勤，固有好古敏求而日與此學相爲周旋者矣。
translation_en:
Wang Jianzhong 王建中
Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: "From beginning to end, the learning of the sages is nothing other than this determination. This essay grasps it and ought to serve as a model."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Huang 黃 comments: "By bringing out that setting one's heart on learning lies in seizing the proper time, he especially captures the meaning of the Sage's words."
Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: "Intimate and full of flavor."
Examiner and Instructor Wu 吳 comments: "Balanced and proper."
When the Sage recounted what he set his heart upon at the beginning, the effort of becoming a sage lay right here. For learning is the quest to reach sagehood; at the very outset of learning to set one's heart upon it—how could one say this is not where the Master's effort toward sagehood lay? Fitting it is that he recounted his own experience in order to encourage others.
It is as if he said: For the learning of the noble man, if there is that whereby [?] he reaches its ultimate pinnacle, there must first be that whereby [?] he establishes its foundation. I am not one who was born possessing knowledge; what, then, was the pursuit to which I devoted myself at the beginning? When my years reached fifteen, although I did not yet dare claim for myself the virtue of a fully grown adult, the effort of sage cultivation nonetheless took its start right here. With single-minded focus of thought and intention, unbedazzled by divergent paths, I was resolved to take the Great Way as the destination of my aspiration; with concentrated vitality and spirit, refusing to rest content with minor accomplishments, I strove to take the highest good as the standard for my advancement and cultivation. Just as I rejoiced that the time had arrived, I was also anxious lest it prove all too easy to lose; earnestly seizing the moment to spur myself on, with the diligence of a mind wholly devoted to constant learning, I was indeed one who loved antiquity and earnestly sought it out, daily revolving in the company of this learning. …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
此志立而大人之學不有以心而會其精乎方
喜其年之可爲而尤懼其或至于不及爲也孜
孜焉及時以自勉而一念發憤之誠固有忘食
忘憂而時與此學相爲循環者矣此志定而大
學之道不有以心而體其全乎功難驟進而志
有所先道難徑造而趨則已定此固吾之在始
學者然也過此以往雖造漸以純不能有加于
此志而道漸以妙亦不能有加于此學信乎志
一辨而聖功無餘事也已抑聖人生知安行宜
===
若無所事志者然觀其自敘始學以至從心不
踰矩皆於志焉基之何哉蓋從容中道者夫子
天縱之聖而純亦不已者聖不自聖之心故堯
之兢舜之勑湯之盤武之銘皆是道也聖人之
心類如此
尊賢使能俊傑在位則天下之士皆悅而
願立於其朝矣市廛而不征法而不廛
則天下之商皆悅而願藏於其市矣關
譏而不征則天下之旅皆悅而願出於
punctuated:
此志立，而大人之學不有以心而會其精乎？方喜其年之可爲，而尤懼其或至于不及爲也。孜孜焉及時以自勉，而一念發憤之誠，固有忘食忘憂而時與此學相爲循環者矣。此志定，而大學之道不有以心而體其全乎？功難驟進而志有所先，道難徑造而趨則已定，此固吾之在始學者然也。過此以往，雖造漸以純，不能有加于此志；而道漸以妙，亦不能有加于此學。信乎志一辨而聖功無餘事也已。抑聖人生知安行，宜若無所事志者。然觀其自敘始學以至從心不踰矩，皆於志焉基之，何哉？蓋從容中道者，夫子天縱之聖；而純亦不已者，聖不自聖之心。故堯之兢、舜之勑、湯之盤、武之銘，皆是道也。聖人之心類如此。

尊賢使能，俊傑在位，則天下之士皆悅，而願立於其朝矣；市，廛而不征，法而不廛，則天下之商皆悅，而願藏於其市矣；關，譏而不征，則天下之旅皆悅，而願出於
translation_en:
When this resolve is established, does not the learning of the great man grasp its essence through the mind? Just as I rejoice that my years allow for action, I am even more fearful lest I fail to act in time. Diligently I seize the moment to spur myself on, and in the sincerity of a single thought of roused determination, I truly forget to eat and forget my worries, constantly revolving together with this learning. When this resolve is settled, does not the Way of the Great Learning embody its entirety through the mind? Effort cannot advance suddenly, yet resolve takes the lead; the Way cannot be reached all at once, yet the direction is already fixed—such indeed was my state when I first began to learn. Beyond this point, although my attainment gradually became pure, nothing could be added to this resolve; and although the Way gradually became subtle, nothing could be added to this learning. Truly, once one's resolve is clearly discerned, there is nothing left over in the work of sagehood! Yet a sage knows from birth and practices with ease, so it would seem he has no need to work at setting his resolve. When we observe his own account, however, from the beginning of his learning right up to following what his heart desired without overstepping the square, all of it was founded upon resolve—why is that? It is because hitting the mean effortlessly was the Master's Heaven-endowed sagehood, whereas unceasing purity was the mind of a sage who did not regard himself as a sage. Thus the caution of Yao, the admonition of Shun, the basin inscription of Tang, and the inscriptions of Wu all followed this same Way. The minds of the sages are all like this.

"If a ruler honors the worthy and employs the able so that men of outstanding talent are in office, then all the scholars of the world will be pleased and wish to stand in his court. In the marketplace, if he assigns stall spaces without taxing the goods, or enforces the regular regulations without taxing the stall spaces, then all the merchants of the world will be pleased and wish to store their goods in his marketplace. At the passes, if there is inspection without levying duties, then all the travelers of the world will be pleased and wish to travel on …"

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其路矣耕者助而不稅則天下之農皆
悅而願耕於其野矣廛無夫里之布則
天下之民皆悅而願爲之氓矣
楊道南

大賢詳舉王政之行盡天下而歸心焉夫人心
未易感也王者之政盡天下而仁之則咸歸之
也固宜孟子之意蓋謂王天下以得人心爲本
得人心以行王政爲先王政惟何蓋天下之人
其環向于一人之治至弗齊也王者之政其聯
屬于億兆之心至無外也誠知得人爲王政之
首務而賢者尊之能者使之則列之朝廷固已
慶一時之選而風之天下莫不起效用之思天
punctuated:
其路矣；耕者助而不稅，則天下之農皆悅，而願耕於其野矣；廛無夫里之布，則天下之民皆悅，而願爲之氓矣。

楊道南

… its roads; if tillers of the soil give mutual aid in farming the public land and are not otherwise taxed, then all the farmers in the world will be pleased and wish to till in its fields; if residential plots are exempt from the individual poll tax and the neighborhood cloth levy, then all the people in the world will be pleased and wish to become its subjects."

Yang Daonan 楊道南

The great worthy enumerates in detail the practice of kingly government, whereby all the world turns its hearts in allegiance to him. Now, human hearts are not easily moved; yet when the government of a true king extends benevolence to all the world, it is certainly fitting that all turn to him in allegiance. The meaning of Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) is roughly that ruling the world as a true king takes winning the hearts of the people as its foundation, and winning the hearts of the people takes practicing kingly government as its first priority. What, then, is kingly government? Indeed, as the people of the world turn from all sides toward the rule of the One Man, they are most diverse and unequal; yet as the government of a true king binds together the hearts of the millions, it leaves nothing outside its reach. If one truly knows that obtaining worthy men is the foremost task of kingly government, honoring the worthy and employing the capable, then placing them in the court will already cause men to rejoice over the finest selection of the age, and as their influence spreads across the world, none will fail to be stirred by the thought of rendering service.
