title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
下之士歸而天下之人心舉係於斯矣以言其
仁乎商雖市地之廛市官之法固未甞廢而貨
非其所征焉由是商有餘蓄有不願藏於市者
否矣以言其仁乎旅雖譏察之禁禦暴之令固
弗敢弛而稅非其所取焉由是旅有餘資有不
願出於塗者否矣至於國有常賦使民輸之制
也然特藉其力耳而私田之稅蠲之則天下之
農皆動耕野之思非悅其野也悅吾政之足以
厚其生也民有常業以廛賦之制也然特賦其
===
廛耳而夫里之罰緩之則天下之氓皆懷受廛
之願非悅其廛也悅吾政之足以恤其私也至
是仁心仁政之兼著萬邦士庶之共臣其感而
悅也皆至德之孚也其悅而歸也亦誠心之應
也蓋奉天之道而天下所當聽命焉者矣雖然
王政固足以孚天下而謂其有所要於天下非
也蓋王者自盡其道而天下自獻其誠如天道
運而萬物化生均之無心焉耳若有所爲而爲
之是則覇者之假仁而民亦將以僞應之矣又
punctuated: 下之士歸，而天下之人心舉係於斯矣。以言其仁乎商，雖市地之廛、市官之法固未甞廢，而貨非其所征焉。由是商有餘蓄，有不願藏於市者？否矣。以言其仁乎旅，雖譏察之禁、禦暴之令固弗敢弛，而稅非其所取焉。由是旅有餘資，有不願出於塗者？否矣。至於國有常賦，使民輸之，制也；然特藉其力耳，而私田之稅蠲之，則天下之農皆動耕野之思，非悅其野也，悅吾政之足以厚其生也。民有常業，以廛賦之，制也；然特賦其廛耳，而夫里之罰緩之，則天下之氓皆懷受廛之願，非悅其廛也，悅吾政之足以恤其私也。至是，仁心仁政之兼著，萬邦士庶之共臣，其感而悅也，皆至德之孚也；其悅而歸也，亦誠心之應也。蓋奉天之道，而天下所當聽命焉者矣。雖然，王政固足以孚天下，而謂其有所要於天下，非也。蓋王者自盡其道，而天下自獻其誠，如天道運而萬物化生，均之無心焉耳。若有所爲而爲之，是則覇者之假仁，而民亦將以僞應之矣，又
translation_en: … scholars of the world will give their allegiance, and the hearts of all the people in the world will be bound to this. As for extending benevolence to merchants: although the ground-tax on market stalls and the regulations of the market officials are certainly never abolished, no levy is imposed upon their goods. Consequently, merchants have surplus savings; would there be any who do not wish to store their goods in the ruler's markets? Surely not. As for extending benevolence to travelers: although the prohibitions of inspection at the passes and the ordinances for guarding against violence are certainly not relaxed, no customs duty is exacted from them. Consequently, travelers have surplus funds; would there be any who do not wish to travel upon the ruler's roads? Surely not. As for the state having regular revenues that require the people to contribute, that is the established system; yet if the ruler merely borrows their labor to cultivate the public fields and remits the tax on their private fields, then all the farmers of the world will be moved by the desire to plough in his countryside—not because they delight in the countryside itself, but because they delight that our governance suffices to enrich their livelihood. As for the people having regular occupations and being taxed according to their dwelling sites, that is the established system; yet if the ruler taxes only their dwelling sites and remits the punitive levies of thepoll-tax and silk-cloth tax on the idle, then all the common folk of the world will cherish the wish to receive a dwelling site from him—not because they delight in the dwelling site itself, but because they delight that our governance suffices to show compassion for their private needs. At this point, a benevolent heart and benevolent governance are both made manifest, and the scholars and commoners of all states together submit as subjects. That they are moved and delighted is wholly due to the trust inspired by supreme virtue; that they delight and give their allegiance is likewise the response of sincere hearts. Indeed, such a ruler upholds the Way of Heaven, and the whole world ought rightly to obey his command. Even so, while kingly governance certainly suffices to win the trust of the world, to say that the ruler does this in order to seek something from the world would be wrong. Rather, the true king simply fulfills his own Way to the utmost, and the world naturally offers up its sincerity—just as the Way of Heaven revolves and the myriad things are transformed and generated, both alike acting without ulterior motive. If one acts with an ulterior purpose in mind, that is the feigned benevolence of a hegemon, and the people for their part will respond with deceit; how then…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
何以心悅而誠服耶吁知王霸之辨可與行王
政矣
易
彖曰大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天雲行雨
施品物流形大明終始六位時成時乗
六龍以御天乾道變化各正性命保合
大和乃利貞首出庶物萬國咸寧象曰
天行健君子以自彊不息
孫如游
===
同考試官教諭田批天道聖人之四德皆健之
所爲也是作能發明之深於易者
同考試官教諭畢批天人合一之理言之詳明
而意更貫串可錄
考試官教諭林批深得題旨
考試官教諭吳批雅健
彖象交發乾義而天人合一之妙見矣盖天以
四德運于上而所以本之者健也然則聖人憲
天之化謂非同天之健以致之哉宜彖象交發
punctuated:
何以心悅而誠服耶？吁！知王霸之辨，可與行王政矣。

易

「彖曰：大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。雲行雨施，品物流形。大明終始，六位時成，時乗六龍以御天。乾道變化，各正性命，保合大和，乃利貞。首出庶物，萬國咸寧。象曰：天行健，君子以自彊不息。」

孫如游

同考試官教諭田批：天道、聖人之四德，皆健之所爲也。是作能發明之，深於《易》者。
同考試官教諭畢批：天人合一之理，言之詳明，而意更貫串，可錄。
考試官教諭林批：深得題旨。
考試官教諭吳批：雅健。

彖、象交發乾義，而天人合一之妙見矣。盖天以四德運于上，而所以本之者，健也。然則聖人憲天之化，謂非同天之健以致之哉？宜彖、象交發
translation_en:
…how could they rejoice in their hearts and sincerely submit? Alas! With those who understand the distinction between the True King and the Hegemon, one can carry out kingly governance.

Book of Changes (Yi)

"The Commentary on the Judgment (Tuan) says: Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! All things owe their beginning to it, and thus it governs Heaven. The clouds move and the rain is distributed, and the various things flow into their forms. Greatly understanding the end and the beginning, how the six positions are completed in their due time, in due time he mounts the six dragons to drive across Heaven. The Way of Qian changes and transforms, so that each thing obtains its correct nature and destiny; preserving and uniting the great harmony, thus it is advantageous and firm. Rising above the multitude of things, the myriad states all enjoy peace. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: Heaven's movement is vigorous; the noble man accordingly strengthens himself ceaselessly."

Sun Ruyou 孫如游

Associate Examiner Instructor Tian comments: The four virtues of the Way of Heaven and of the Sage are all brought about by vigor. This composition is able to elucidate this—one who is profound in the Book of Changes.
Associate Examiner Instructor Bi comments: The principle of the unity of Heaven and Man is stated in detail and with clarity, and the meaning is even more coherent throughout. Worthy of recording.
Examiner Instructor Lin comments: Deeply grasps the purport of the theme.
Examiner Instructor Wu comments: Elegant and vigorous.

The Commentary on the Judgment (Tuan) and the Commentary on the Images (Xiang) mutually bring forth the meaning of Qian, and the subtlety of the unity of Heaven and Man is thereby revealed. For Heaven revolves on high through the four virtues, and that upon which they are founded is vigor. This being so, when the Sage models himself on the transformations of Heaven, could it be said that he does not achieve this through a vigor identical to that of Heaven? Rightly do the Commentary on the Judgment and the Commentary on the Images mutually bring forth…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其義也且夫聖人者法天者也天有至敎聖人
有至德均於乾義盡之矣是故天道有元亨自
其開物之始著物之形者見之也聖人者以吾
之心契天之心則乾道終始之運旣大明于中
而六龍卷舒之妙自以時措之焉一天之元亨
而已矣天道有利貞自其足物之理凝物之氣
者見之也聖人者體天之化焉吾之化則首出
庶物之上雖不見其爲而萬國咸寧之治自垂
拱而致焉一天之利貞而已矣若是者豈無所
===
本哉蓋乾之象天也四德循環迭運不已非至
健乎君子觀乾之象法天之行而亦如其健焉
以吾精一之學養其天德之剛而毅然者常在
我蓋自一念之微以達於萬感之著而道心不
爲之少懈矣以吾有主之天勝其易動之欲而
浩然者常不屈蓋自無斁之保以極於不已之
純而己私不爲之少間矣至是則君子之彊卽
天之健存之于心是謂純天之德達之于治是
謂憲天之化而所以乘龍御天萬國咸寧者皆
punctuated: 其義也。且夫聖人者，法天者也。天有至敎，聖人有至德，均於乾義盡之矣。是故天道有元亨，自其開物之始、著物之形者見之也。聖人者，以吾之心契天之心，則乾道終始之運旣大明于中，而六龍卷舒之妙自以時措之焉，一天之元亨而已矣。天道有利貞，自其足物之理、凝物之氣者見之也。聖人者，體天之化焉吾之化，則首出庶物之上，雖不見其爲，而萬國咸寧之治自垂拱而致焉，一天之利貞而已矣。若是者，豈無所本哉？蓋乾之象，天也。四德循環，迭運不已，非至健乎？君子觀乾之象，法天之行，而亦如其健焉。以吾精一之學，養其天德之剛，而毅然者常在我，蓋自一念之微，以達於萬感之著，而道心不爲之少懈矣。以吾有主之天，勝其易動之欲，而浩然者常不屈，蓋自無斁之保，以極於不已之純，而己私不爲之少間矣。至是，則君子之彊，卽天之健。存之于心，是謂純天之德；達之于治，是謂憲天之化。而所以乘龍御天、萬國咸寧者，皆
translation_en: … its meaning. Moreover, the sage is one who models himself upon Heaven. Heaven possesses supreme instruction, and the sage possesses supreme virtue; both are fully exhausted within the meaning of Qian (the Creative). Therefore, the Way of Heaven has origination and flourishing (yuanheng), which is seen from its initiating the beginning of things and manifesting the forms of things. The sage aligns his own mind with the mind of Heaven; thus, once the cycle of the end and beginning of the Way of Qian is greatly illuminated within him, the wondrous subtlety of the six dragons furling and unfurling is naturally put into practice according to the time—this is simply one with Heaven's origination and flourishing. The Way of Heaven has advantage and firmness (lizhen), which is seen from its fulfilling the principles of things and condensing the vital energy of things. The sage embodies the transformation of Heaven as [?] his own transformation; thus, rising preeminent above the multitude of things, although his action is unseen, the governance that brings peace to all the myriad states is naturally achieved with robes hanging down and hands folded—this is simply one with Heaven's advantage and firmness. How could such an achievement be without a foundation? For the image of Qian is Heaven. The four virtues revolve in a cycle, operating in alternation without cease—is this not supreme vigor? The superior man observes the image of Qian, models himself on the movement of Heaven, and likewise matches its vigor. Through one's learning of refinement and unity, he nourishes the firmness of his heavenly virtue so that what is resolute always abides within him; from the subtlety of a single thought to the manifestation of ten thousand responses, the mind of the Way never slackens in the slightest because of them. Through one's innate nature that has a master within, he overcomes desires that are easily stirred, so that what is vast and flood-like never yields; from preservation without weariness to the ultimate of unceasing purity, selfish personal desires never interrupt it in the slightest. When it reaches this point, the strength of the superior man is none other than the vigor of Heaven. Preserved in the mind, this is called the purity of Heavenly virtue; extended to governance, this is called taking Heaven's transformation as one's model. And that whereby one mounts the dragons to drive across the heavens and brings peace to all the myriad states all…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
自此出也是故合彖與象觀之而乾之義寧有
餘蘊哉蓋嘗觀之堯之放勳舜之重華其治隆
矣然而無怠無荒之念欽若昊天之誠堯舜且
惓惓焉何也聖人自彊不息之心固如是也故
曰帝王之治本於道帝王之道本於心明乎乾
之義者可以識帝王之心矣
形而上者謂之道
屠隆
同考試官教諭田批卦爻陰陽無非至理聖人
===
所以立象盡意也是作能言之宜錄以式
同考試官教諭畢批發揮道妙於形之意簡明
可觀
考試官教諭林批理明詞整
考試官教諭吳批切實不浮
大傳卽易之超乎形者而著道之名焉夫道妙
於無形者也自易之形而上者觀之而道在是
矣孰謂意之不盡於象乎且夫聖人之作易也
意固盡於象之中而象實涵乎道之蘊何以言
punctuated:
自此出也。是故合《彖》與《象》觀之，而乾之義寧有餘蘊哉？蓋嘗觀之：堯之放勳，舜之重華，其治隆矣。然而無怠無荒之念，欽若昊天之誠，堯、舜且惓惓焉，何也？聖人自彊不息之心，固如是也。故曰：「帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於心。」明乎乾之義者，可以識帝王之心矣。

形而上者謂之道

屠隆

同考試官教諭田批：卦爻陰陽，無非至理，聖人所以立象盡意也。是作能言之，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭畢批：發揮道妙於形之意，簡明可觀。
考試官教諭林批：理明詞整。
考試官教諭吳批：切實不浮。

《大傳》卽《易》之超乎形者，而著道之名焉。夫道，妙於無形者也。自《易》之形而上者觀之，而道在是矣。孰謂意之不盡於象乎？且夫聖人之作《易》也，意固盡於象之中，而象實涵乎道之蘊。何以言
translation_en:
… issue forth from this. Therefore, when one examines the Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) together with the Commentary on the Images (Xiang), how could there be any remaining profundities in the meaning of the Qian hexagram left unexpressed? Indeed, if we consider how Yao’s merit was vast and far-reaching and Shun’s brilliance matched Yao’s, their governance was truly flourishing. Yet even Yao and Shun held earnestly and tirelessly to the thought of being neither remiss nor negligent, and to the sincerity of reverently following vast Heaven. Why was this? Because the sage’s mind of unceasing self-strengthening is inherently like this. Thus it is said: “The governance of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and the Way of emperors and kings is rooted in the mind.” One who understands the meaning of Qian can recognize the mind of emperors and kings.

"What is above form is called the Way." [Book of Changes, Great Treatise, I.12]

Tu Long 屠隆

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Tian: The hexagrams, lines, yin, and yang are nothing other than ultimate principle; this is how the sages established images to fully express their meaning. This essay is able to articulate this and should be recorded as a model.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Bi: It develops the idea that the subtlety of the Way transcends form; concise, clear, and worth reading.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Lin: The reasoning is clear and the phrasing well-ordered.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Wu:Substantial and not superficial.

The Great Treatise (Dazhuan) looks directly at that in the Changes (Yi) which transcends form, and thereby makes manifest the name of the Way. Now the Way is that which is wondrous in its formlessness. When viewed from that in the Changes which is above form, the Way is right there. Who then could say that meaning is not fully expressed in the images? Moreover, in the sages’ creation of the Changes, their meaning was assuredly exhausted within the images, while the images truly encompass the depths of the Way. How can we explain…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之卦爻陰陽皆形也若不足以為道也然陰之
形不徒陰也必有超乎陰之上者存焉陽之形
不徒陽也亦必有超乎陽之上者寓焉斂之無
端而主宰於二體之中不滯於剛柔之畫藏之
無朕而貫徹於六虛之內不泥於奇偶之文若
此者將不謂之道乎吾知陰而曰上陰不足盡
之也意象俱泯一於穆不已之眞陽而曰上陽
不足名之也方體俱無實太極本然之懿統觀
於卦而其不囿於卦者乃道之渾然者焉二體
===
之成列皆兩間之至理而所謂通神明之德者
通此而已踰法象而獨運孰非乾坤之精也哉
析觀於爻而其不囿於爻者乃道之燦然者焉
六位之時成皆三才之妙用而所謂順性命之
理者順此而已超形器而獨存孰非乾坤之祕
也哉要之爻象未立而理已具道固不倚於形
也爻象旣立而理斯顯道亦不離於形也自理
之可見者若為形自形之不可見者實為道矣
知道不外乎形此象之能盡乎意也歟雖然易
punctuated: 之？卦爻陰陽皆形也，若不足以為道也。然陰之形不徒陰也，必有超乎陰之上者存焉；陽之形不徒陽也，亦必有超乎陽之上者寓焉。斂之無端，而主宰於二體之中，不滯於剛柔之畫；藏之無朕，而貫徹於六虛之內，不泥於奇偶之文。若此者，將不謂之道乎？吾知陰而曰上，陰不足盡之也，意象俱泯，一於穆不已之眞；陽而曰上，陽不足名之也，方體俱無，實太極本然之懿。統觀於卦，而其不囿於卦者，乃道之渾然者焉。二體之成列，皆兩間之至理，而所謂「通神明之德」者，通此而已。踰法象而獨運，孰非乾坤之精也哉！析觀於爻，而其不囿於爻者，乃道之燦然者焉。六位之時成，皆三才之妙用，而所謂「順性命之理」者，順此而已。超形器而獨存，孰非乾坤之祕也哉！要之，爻象未立而理已具，道固不倚於形也；爻象旣立而理斯顯，道亦不離於形也。自理之可見者若為形，自形之不可見者實為道矣。知道不外乎形，此象之能盡乎意也歟！雖然，易
translation_en:
… it? The hexagrams, lines, yin, and yang are all forms, which might seem insufficient to constitute the Way. Yet the form of yin is not merely yin; there must be something existing above and beyond yin. The form of yang is not merely yang; there must likewise be something lodged above and beyond yang. Gathered in without beginning or end, it presides within the two constituent trigrams without being bogged down in the strokes of the firm and the yielding; hidden away without trace or sign, it penetrates throughout the six fluctuating line-positions without being mired in the patterns of the odd and the even. Could that which is like this not be called the Way?

I know that when one speaks of yin and says "above," yin is insufficient to exhaust it: thought and image are both obliterated, and it is wholly the true reality of that which is profoundly solemn and unceasing. When one speaks of yang and says "above," yang is insufficient to name it: spatial direction and physical body are both absent, and it is truly the original excellence of the Supreme Ultimate.

Viewed synthetically in the hexagrams, that which is not confined by the hexagrams is the Way in its undifferentiated wholeness. The arrayed formation of the two constituent trigrams is in every case the ultimate principle between heaven and earth, and what is called "comprehending the virtues of spiritual intelligence" is nothing more than comprehending this. Transcending models and images to operate alone, what part of it is not the essence of Qian and Kun! Viewed analytically in the lines, that which is not confined by the lines is the Way in its resplendent clarity. The timely completion of the six positions is in every case the wondrous function of the Three Powers, and what is called "according with the principles of nature and destiny" is nothing more than according with this. Rising above forms and vessels to exist alone, what part of it is not the mystery of Qian and Kun!

In sum, before the lines and images were established, the principle was already complete; the Way indeed does not depend upon form. Once the lines and images were established, the principle was thereby made manifest; the Way likewise does not separate from form. Viewed from what is visible of principle, it appears as form; viewed from what is invisible of form, it is in reality the Way. Knowing that the Way is not external to form—is this not how the images are able to exhaust the meaning! Even so, the Changes…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之理固不外於陰陽而實吾心之動靜也聖人
作易不過以心之精而形之易以濟民行耳學
易者靜虛動直存吾心以契聖人之心則由象
識意易之形而上者在我矣噫此聖人洗心之
訓昭如也學易者其知之
書
帝曰咨四岳有能典朕三禮僉曰伯夷帝
曰俞咨伯汝作秩宗夙夜惟寅直哉惟
清伯拜稽首讓于夔龍帝曰俞往欽哉
===
帝曰夔命汝典樂教胄子直而溫寬而
栗剛而無虐簡而無傲詩言志歌永言
聲依永律和聲八音克諧無相奪倫神
人以和
胡士奇
同考試官教諭陳批題以禮樂作對類難整齊
此作鋪叙得體而發明虞廷命官之旨殆盡可錄
考試官教諭林批整飭
考試官教諭吳批莊重
punctuated:
之理固不外於陰陽，而實吾心之動靜也。聖人作《易》，不過以心之精而形之《易》，以濟民行耳。學《易》者靜虛動直，存吾心以契聖人之心，則由象識意，《易》之形而上者在我矣。噫！此聖人洗心之訓昭如也，學《易》者其知之。

《書》：
「帝曰：『咨！四岳，有能典朕三禮？』僉曰：『伯夷。』帝曰：『俞。咨！伯，汝作秩宗。夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。』伯拜稽首，讓于夔、龍。帝曰：『俞，往欽哉！』帝曰：『夔！命汝典樂，教胄子：直而溫，寬而栗，剛而無虐，簡而無傲。詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲。八音克諧，無相奪倫，神人以和。』」

胡士奇。
同考試官教諭陳批：題以禮樂作對，類難整齊。此作鋪叙得體，而發明虞廷命官之旨殆盡，可錄。
考試官教諭林批：整飭。
考試官教諭吳批：莊重。
translation_en:
…the principle of the Book of Changes (Yi) certainly does not lie outside of yin and yang, yet in reality it is the movement and stillness of our own mind. In creating the Changes, the sages did nothing more than take the essence of the mind and give it form in the Changes so as to aid the conduct of the people. If those who study the Changes are empty in stillness and upright in movement, preserving our own mind so as to tally with the mind of the sages, then through the images they will recognize the meaning, and what is above form in the Changes will reside within us. Alas! How luminous is this teaching of the sages on cleansing the mind; may those who study the Changes know it.

Book of Documents (Shu):
"The Emperor said, 'Ah! Four Mountains, is there anyone who can direct my three ritual ceremonies?' All said, 'Boyi 伯夷.' The Emperor said, 'Yes. Ah! Bo, you shall act as Director of Sacrifices (Zhizong). Morning and night be reverent; be upright and pure.' Bo bowed and touched his head to the ground, yielding in favor of Kui 夔 and Long 龍. The Emperor said, 'Yes, go and be reverent!' The Emperor said, 'Kui! I appoint you to direct music and to teach the scions of state: to be upright yet mild, broad-minded yet firm, strong yet not tyrannical, simple yet not arrogant. Poetry expresses intent, song prolongs the words, notes depend on the prolongation, and pitch-pipes harmonize the notes. When the eight timbres can be brought into harmony without encroaching upon one another's order, spirits and men will thereby be brought into harmony.'"

Hu Shiqi 胡士奇.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (Jiaoyu) Chen 陳: Because this topic pairs ritual and music as parallels, it is generally difficult to make the composition neat and balanced. This essay unfolds its narrative with proper proportion and almost completely elucidates the purport of the Yu 虞 court's appointment of officials; it is worthy of selection.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Lin 林: Well-ordered and disciplined.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Wu 吳: Dignified and grave.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖君命官以典禮樂惟敬與和而已夫禮主於
敬而樂主於和也聖君命官以是禮樂其有興
乎且夫天子建中和之極人臣職明聽之司吾
於虞廷之命官而知其得人矣彼幽以事神存
乎禮而知禮者伯夷其選也故帝因四岳之舉
而命之曰秩宗之官所以交神明而命汝作之
則凡祀天地而享人鬼者固有在於禮矣而禮
豈外于心之敬乎必嚴諸夙夜之際而惕然其
常寅者克純夫直內之功斯反諸本原之天而
===
湛然其無欲者適得乎澄清之體一敬之所以
常存固三禮之所以無愧矣伯夷宜承命以莅
其職而顧有夔龍之讓帝能已于往欽之勅乎
是命一伯夷而典禮者有專責也已明以育材
存乎樂而知樂者夔其選也故帝因夷之讓而
命之曰典樂之官所以敎冑子而命汝爲之則
凡翼其偏而防其過者固有在于樂矣而樂豈外
于心之和乎始則詩以言志而歌聲因之既肇
夫聲氣之原旣則律以和聲而損益成之適得
punctuated: 聖君命官以典禮樂，惟敬與和而已。夫禮主於敬，而樂主於和也。聖君命官以是，禮樂其有興乎！且夫天子建中和之極，人臣職明聽之司，吾於虞廷之命官，而知其得人矣。彼幽以事神存乎禮，而知禮者伯夷其選也。故帝因四岳之舉而命之曰：「秩宗之官，所以交神明，而命汝作之，則凡祀天地而享人鬼者，固有在於禮矣。而禮豈外于心之敬乎？必嚴諸夙夜之際，而惕然其常寅者，克純夫直內之功；斯反諸本原之天，而湛然其無欲者，適得乎澄清之體。一敬之所以常存，固三禮之所以無愧矣。」伯夷宜承命以莅其職，而顧有夔、龍之讓，帝能已于「往欽」之勅乎？是命一伯夷，而典禮者有專責也已。明以育材存乎樂，而知樂者夔其選也。故帝因夷之讓而命之曰：「典樂之官，所以敎冑子，而命汝爲之，則凡翼其偏而防其過者，固有在于樂矣。而樂豈外于心之和乎？始則詩以言志，而歌聲因之，既肇夫聲氣之原；旣則律以和聲，而損益成之，適得
translation_en:
When the sage ruler appointed officials to take charge of ritual and music, it was solely a matter of reverence and harmony. For ritual is grounded in reverence, and music is grounded in harmony. When the sage ruler appointed officials on this basis, how could ritual and music fail to flourish! Moreover, as the Son of Heaven establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony, and his ministers fulfill the duties of clear-sightedness and acute hearing, in the appointment of officials at the court of Yu [Shun], I know that he found the right men.

In the unseen realm, serving the spirits depends upon ritual, and among those who understood ritual, Boyi was the choice. Therefore, on the recommendation of the Four Peaks, the Emperor commanded him, saying: "The office of Arranger of Ancestral Temple Rituals (Zhizong) is that by which one communicates with the bright spirits, and since I command you to fill it, all sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and offerings to human ghosts truly depend upon ritual. Yet how could ritual lie outside the reverence of the mind? Only when one maintains strictness day and night, remaining vigilantly and ever respectfully alert, can one perfect the work of straightening the inner self; and only then, returning to the original Heaven within, pellucid and free of selfish desires, does one attain the pure and clear substance. That by which single-minded reverence is constantly preserved is indeed that by which one may stand unashamed before the Three Rituals." Boyi ought to have accepted the command and assumed his post, yet he yielded instead in favor of Kui and Long; how could the Emperor refrain from the admonition, "Go, and be reverent!"? Thus, by appointing a single Boyi, the direction of ritual was given its dedicated responsibility.

In the visible realm, nurturing talent depends upon music, and among those who understood music, Kui was the choice. Therefore, following Boyi's yielding in his favor, the Emperor commanded him, saying: "The office of Director of Music (Dianyue) is that by which one instructs the eldest sons of state, and since I command you to undertake it, all efforts to rectify their one-sidedness and guard against their excesses truly depend upon music. Yet how could music lie outside the harmony of the mind? In the beginning, poetry expresses intent, and singing and vocal notes follow from it, thereby initiating the source of sound and vital breath; thereafter, the pitch-pipes harmonize the notes, and through subtraction and addition bring them to completion, thereby attaining…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夫節宣之妙八音克諧而不亂斯神人協和而
不違矣后夔能率是以盡其職而爲胄子之教
尚何感化之難乎是命一后夔而典樂者有攸
賴也已要之和敬一心禮樂一道而惟夷夔之
深於禮樂者當之此虞廷禮明樂備其盛矣乎
雖然帝舜不自有其盛也方且亮功之戒咨命
惟勤黜陟之法大明罔私而交儆之謨敕天之
歌相與都俞于一堂者秩秩乎渢渢乎揖讓希
音可觀而聆也故曰見禮知政聞樂知德吾于
===
帝舜有深感焉
君子所其無逸先知稼穡之艱難乃逸則
知小人之依
陳性學
同考試官教諭陳 批 講所其與知稼穡處皆有
分曉且清逸俊雅迥異他作
考試官教諭林 批 涵蓄有味深得周公忠愛
之意
考試官教諭吳 批 調格古雅
punctuated:
夫節宣之妙。八音克諧而不亂，斯神人協和而不違矣。后夔能率是以盡其職，而爲胄子之教，尚何感化之難乎？是命一后夔，而典樂者有攸賴也已。要之，和敬一心，禮樂一道，而惟夷、夔之深於禮樂者當之，此虞廷禮明樂備，其盛矣乎！雖然，帝舜不自有其盛也，方且亮功之戒，咨命惟勤；黜陟之法，大明罔私。而交儆之謨，敕天之歌，相與都俞于一堂者，秩秩乎！渢渢乎！揖讓希音，可觀而聆也。故曰：「見禮知政，聞樂知德。」吾于帝舜有深感焉。

君子所其無逸，先知稼穡之艱難，乃逸，則知小人之依。
陳性學
同考試官教諭陳批：講「所其」與「知稼穡」處皆有分曉，且清逸俊雅，迥異他作。
考試官教諭林批：涵蓄有味，深得周公忠愛之意。
考試官教諭吳批：調格古雅。
translation_en:
… the subtlety of regulation and expression. When the eight timbres are brought into harmony and do not fall into disorder, then spirits and men are brought into accord without conflict. If Lord Kui (后夔) can follow this to fulfill his duties and instruct the noble youths, what difficulty could there still be in moving and transforming them? Thus, by appointing a single Lord Kui, there was someone reliable to take charge of music. In sum, harmony and reverence stem from a single mind, and rites and music share a single Way; only those as profound in rites and music as Boyi (夷) and Kui were fit to undertake these charges. How flourishing indeed was the court of Yu, where rites were illustrious and music was complete! Even so, Emperor Shun (帝舜) did not regard this flourishing as his own achievement. Just then, in his admonitions to assist in achievements, he was diligent in his consultations and commands; in his laws of demotion and promotion, he was grandly discerning and without partiality. Moreover, the counsels of mutual admonition and the songs of reverence for Heaven, through which sovereign and ministers expressed their agreement in a single hall—how orderly! how resonant! The rare tones of their deferential court may still be beheld and heard. Therefore it is said: "By viewing a ruler's rites, one knows his governance; by hearing his music, one knows his virtue." Regarding Emperor Shun, I am deeply moved.

"The noble man makes having no leisure his dwelling-place; he first knows the hardships of sowing and reaping, and then takes his ease, and so he knows that on which the common people depend." [Book of Documents, "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi 無逸)]
By Chen Xingxue 陳性學.
Associate Examiner, Instructor (教諭) Chen, comments: The explanations of "makes ... his dwelling-place" (suo qi 所其) and "knowing the sowing and reaping" are both clear and distinct; moreover, the style is pure, unconstrained, refined, and elegant, vastly different from other compositions.
Examiner, Instructor Lin, comments: Reserved and rich in flavor, it deeply grasps the Duke of Zhou's (周公) intent of loyalty and affection.
Examiner, Instructor Wu, comments: Its tone and structure are ancient and elegant.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大臣述君子之居勤而因原其所由勤焉蓋君
之逸者凡以其忽民事也君子先知其艱而克
勤也固其所哉周公戒成王若曰王業始于憂
勤而君道戒乎逸豫吾王纘艱難之業而居小
民之上也亦知君子之無逸乎蓋其仰觀天命
靈長之機而兢兢焉怠荒之是戒俯察民心怨
樂之故而業業乎勤勵之是圖內無逸志而所
以致謹于淵默之中者無一念不居于勤也外
無逸樂而所以矜持于臨御之際者無一事不
===
任其勞也君子之無逸如此果何由而然哉蓋
君之位至逸也民之稼穡至艱也惟不知其艱
而遽享其逸此逸心所由起也君子方其未居
位之先而慮周天下已洞徹其艱難之狀乃其
既居位之後而心存畎畝自莫巳其憂勤之思
知民之有稼民之所依以爲命也吾欲立民之
命則凡可以開其麗者雖勤力圖之而猶恐其
不給矣况敢乘以逸哉知民之有穡民之所依
以爲生也吾欲全民之生則凡可以導其利者
punctuated: 大臣述君子之居勤，而因原其所由勤焉。蓋君之逸者，凡以其忽民事也。君子先知其艱而克勤也，固其所哉！周公戒成王若曰：王業始于憂勤，而君道戒乎逸豫。吾王纘艱難之業，而居小民之上也，亦知君子之無逸乎？蓋其仰觀天命靈長之機，而兢兢焉怠荒之是戒；俯察民心怨樂之故，而業業乎勤勵之是圖。內無逸志，而所以致謹于淵默之中者，無一念不居于勤也；外無逸樂，而所以矜持于臨御之際者，無一事不任其勞也。君子之無逸如此，果何由而然哉？蓋君之位至逸也，民之稼穡至艱也，惟不知其艱而遽享其逸，此逸心所由起也。君子方其未居位之先，而慮周天下，已洞徹其艱難之狀；乃其既居位之後，而心存畎畝，自莫巳其憂勤之思。知民之有稼，民之所依以爲命也。吾欲立民之命，則凡可以開其麗者，雖勤力圖之，而猶恐其不給矣，况敢乘以逸哉？知民之有穡，民之所依以爲生也。吾欲全民之生，則凡可以導其利者，
translation_en:
The great minister recounts how the noble ruler abides in diligence, and thereupon traces the origin of why he is diligent. For whenever a ruler indulges in ease, it is entirely because he neglects the affairs of the people. That the noble ruler first understands their hardships and is thereby able to be diligent—is this not indeed his proper place!

The Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) admonished King Cheng (Chengwang 成王) as if to say: Royal enterprise begins in anxious diligence, and the way of the ruler warns against ease and pleasure. Now that Our King has inherited a hard-won enterprise and sits above the common people, does he also understand how the noble ruler takes "against luxurious ease" as his dwelling place? Looking up, he contemplates the subtle mechanisms by which the Mandate of Heaven endures, and cautiously guards against negligence and waste; looking down, he examines the reasons behind the resentment and joy of the people's hearts, and assiduously plans for diligence and exertion. Within, he harbors no thoughts of ease, so that in exercising vigilance amidst deep silence, there is not a single thought that does not abide in diligence; without, he indulges in no pleasures of ease, so that in maintaining self-restraint when presiding over his subjects, there is not a single affair in which he does not shoulder the toil himself.

That the noble ruler is thus free from ease—from what indeed does this arise? Now, the position of the ruler is one of utmost ease, whereas the sowing and reaping of the people are of the utmost hardship. Only when one does not understand their hardship and abruptly enjoys one's ease does a mind of ease arise. Before the noble ruler has even assumed the throne, his thoughts encompass the whole world, and he already thoroughly perceives the conditions of their hardship; then, after he has assumed the throne, his heart remains among the furrowed fields, and he naturally cannot cease his thoughts of anxious diligence. He knows that the people's sowing is what they depend upon for their very lives. "If I wish to establish the lives of the people, then in all things that can open up their resources [? 麗], even though I plan for them with diligent effort, I still fear they may not suffice—how much less would I dare to take advantage of my position for ease?" He knows that the people's reaping is what they depend upon for their livelihood. "If I wish to preserve the livelihood of the people, then in all things that can channel their benefits,…"

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
雖勵精謀之而猶恐其弗迨矣况敢淫于逸哉
是可見惟知依而後能足民依惟無逸而後能
享其逸古君子之存心於民蓋如此王其知所
法矣抑周以后稷開基稼穡尤其所首務者成
王幼冲席已成之業而未見祖宗之勞周公所
爲懼也至於豳風之歌視無逸尤加咏嘆深長
思焉成王之所以享盛治而延卜歷也是故稱
周公之德不衰
詩
===
百辟卿士媚于天子不解于位民之攸墍
邵倬
同考試官教諭黃批 發揮不解民墍得詩人忠
愛之旨宜錄以傳
同考試官教諭徐批 規戒之意溢於言表也佳
士佳士
考試官教諭林批 旨遠詞文
考試官教諭吳批 醇正
羣臣愛君惟切保治之願焉蓋安民所以致治
punctuated:
雖勵精謀之，而猶恐其弗迨矣，况敢淫于逸哉？是可見惟知依，而後能足民依；惟無逸，而後能享其逸。古君子之存心於民蓋如此，王其知所法矣。抑周以后稷開基，稼穡尤其所首務者。成王幼冲，席已成之業，而未見祖宗之勞，周公所爲懼也。至於《豳風》之歌，視《無逸》尤加咏嘆深長思焉。成王之所以享盛治而延卜歷也，是故稱周公之德不衰。
詩
百辟卿士，媚于天子，不解于位，民之攸墍。
邵倬
同考試官教諭黃批：發揮「不解」、「民墍」，得詩人忠愛之旨，宜錄以傳。
同考試官教諭徐批：規戒之意溢於言表也，佳士，佳士。
考試官教諭林批：旨遠詞文。
考試官教諭吳批：醇正。
羣臣愛君，惟切保治之願焉。蓋安民所以致治，
translation_en:
…even if one strives with full vigor to plan for it, one still fears falling short—how much less would one dare to indulge in ease! From this it can be seen that only by knowing what the people depend upon can one suffice the people's dependence; only by not indulging in ease can one enjoy ease. Such was the way the noble men of antiquity kept their minds upon the people; may the King know to take them as his model! Furthermore, the Zhou founded its dynastic enterprise through Hou Ji 后稷, so sowing and reaping were especially its foremost task. King Cheng 成王 was young and tender, inheriting an already accomplished enterprise without having witnessed the toils of his ancestors; this was what the Duke of Zhou 周公 feared. As for the songs of the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng 豳風), compared to "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi 無逸), they add even more chanting, sighing, and deep, lasting reflection. This is how King Cheng enjoyed a flourishing rule and prolonged the divined duration of the dynasty; therefore, the praise of the Duke of Zhou's virtue has never waned.

Classic of Poetry (Shi 詩)

"All the feudal lords and grandees / Love the Son of Heaven; / Unremitting in his position, / In him the people find their rest."

Shao Zhuo 邵倬

Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu 教諭) Huang 黃 comments: He elaborates on "unremitting" and "the people find rest," grasping the loyal and affectionate purport of the poet. It ought to be recorded and transmitted.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu 徐 comments: The admonition and caution overflow beyond the words. A fine scholar, a fine scholar!
Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: Far-reaching in purport and refined in diction.
Examiner and Instructor Wu 吳 comments: Pure and upright.

When all the ministers love their ruler, they are earnestly devoted solely to the wish of preserving good governance. For bringing peace to the people is the means to achieve good governance…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而不解者乂安長治之道也羣臣以此願君忠
愛寧有既乎想其願嗣王之意以爲明君不以
世治而忽遠圖善保治者也良臣不以主聖而
忘進規善用愛者也嗣王之綱之紀固貽臣下
以莫大之安矣爲諸臣者將何以自效哉彼外
而百辟佐天子以分治者也其心同則其媚同
油然忠愛之無已者蓋不以今日之綏和爲可
樂而欲引之爲道久化成之休内而卿士輔天
子以出治者也同此心則同此媚翕然仰戴之
===
惟殷者蓋不以目前之寧謐爲可喜而欲衍之
爲悠乆無疆之慶運精神于五位而綱焉常張
效法於無斁焉則民之安者益以安而咸和之
化歷萬年如一日也凡在燕及之下者不以是
而輸忠藎耶厪念慮於萬幾而紀焉常理媲美
於執競焉則民之寧者益以寧而永清之治歷
萬禩如一時也凡興媚玆之懷者不以是而申
報稱耶夫臣之媚君不忘乎防微杜漸之思君
能諒臣不替其持盈保泰之慮君臣相與以有
punctuated: 而不解者，乂安長治之道也。羣臣以此願君，忠愛寧有既乎？想其願嗣王之意，以爲明君不以世治而忽遠圖，善保治者也；良臣不以主聖而忘進規，善用愛者也。嗣王之綱之紀，固貽臣下以莫大之安矣，爲諸臣者將何以自效哉？彼外而百辟，佐天子以分治者也；其心同則其媚同，油然忠愛之無已者，蓋不以今日之綏和爲可樂，而欲引之爲道久化成之休。内而卿士，輔天子以出治者也；同此心則同此媚，翕然仰戴之惟殷者，蓋不以目前之寧謐爲可喜，而欲衍之爲悠乆無疆之慶。運精神于五位，而綱焉常張，效法於無斁焉，則民之安者益以安，而咸和之化歷萬年如一日也。凡在燕及之下者，不以是而輸忠藎耶？厪念慮於萬幾，而紀焉常理，媲美於執競焉，則民之寧者益以寧，而永清之治歷萬禩如一時也。凡興媚玆之懷者，不以是而申報稱耶？夫臣之媚君，不忘乎防微杜漸之思；君能諒臣，不替其持盈保泰之慮。君臣相與以有
translation_en:
…while never slacking off is the way to achieve lasting peace and enduring order. When all the ministers wish this for their ruler, how could their loyalty and affection ever have an end?

Imagining the intent of their wishes for the succeeding king, they considered that an enlightened ruler does not neglect long-range plans just because the world is well-governed—he is one who excels at preserving good order; and good ministers do not forget to offer admonition just because their sovereign is sage—they are ones who excel at practicing affection. By giving overarching guidelines and detailed regulations, the succeeding king has surely bequeathed the greatest peace to his subjects below; how then shall all the ministers exert themselves in return?

Out in the provinces, the hundred lords assist the Son of Heaven by sharing in governance. Since their hearts are the same, their loving devotion is the same; that their welling loyalty and affection never cease is because they do not regard today's tranquility and harmony as mere cause for pleasure, but wish to extend it into the blessing of an enduring Way and completed transformation. Inside the court, the ministers and noblemen aid the Son of Heaven in issuing governance. Sharing this heart, they share this loving devotion; that their united reverence and support are so earnest is because they do not regard the present calm and quiet as mere cause for joy, but wish to prolong it into a felicity lasting and boundless.

If he exercises his vital spirit on the sovereign throne so that the overarching guidelines are constantly taut, modeling himself on untiring diligence, then the people who are at peace will become even more peaceful, and the transformation of universal harmony will pass through ten thousand years as if a single day. Among all who enjoy the extension of his comforting grace, who would not thereby offer up their loyal devotion? If he applies his anxious thoughts to the myriad affairs of state so that the detailed regulations are constantly in order, rivaling the excellence of steadfast vigor, then the people who are tranquil will become even more tranquil, and the governance of eternal clarity will pass through ten thousand generations as if a single moment. Among all who cherish the sentiment of loving devotion to this sovereign, who would not thereby express their recompense?

Now, in the ministers' loving devotion to their ruler, they do not forget the thought of guarding against minute beginnings and checking gradual tendencies; and when the ruler is able to understand his ministers, he does not abandon his concern for holding on to fullness and preserving great prosperity. Ruler and ministers working together to achieve…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
成王嗣之福孰有大於是哉噫此虞庭賡歌意
也舜之時稱極治矣而禹益諸臣惟惓惓以時
幾之勅逸樂之防告其君豈過計哉蓋有初鮮
終者人之恒情而憂盛危明藎臣之用心固如
此嘉樂詩人得之矣昔人謂太和之氣常在虞
周宇宙間有以夫
帝命式于九圍
查允元
同考試官教諭黃批帝命二字少能發揮惟此
作運意敷詞精雅宜錄以式
同考試官教諭徐批文以成命世德並起以建
中執中入講末用順治威嚴合着下意此何等心思
考試官教諭林批文思雋永
考試官教諭吳批精確
聖君受命而為法於天下一敬之所感也甚矣
天之所親惟敬也然則命湯以式天下也固其
所哉此商人祫祭而歌之也若曰天有成命商
有世德而所以靈承之有常光紹之弗替者匪
punctuated:
成，王嗣之福，孰有大於是哉！噫！此虞庭賡歌意也。舜之時稱極治矣，而禹、益諸臣惟惓惓以時幾之勅、逸樂之防告其君，豈過計哉？蓋有初鮮終者，人之恒情；而憂盛危明，藎臣之用心固如此。《嘉樂》詩人得之矣。昔人謂太和之氣常在虞、周宇宙間，有以夫！

「帝命式于九圍。」
查允元
同考試官教諭黃批：「帝命」二字少能發揮，惟此作運意敷詞精雅，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭徐批：文以成命、世德並起，以建中、執中入講，末用順治、威嚴合着下意，此何等心思！
考試官教諭林批：文思雋永。
考試官教諭吳批：精確。

聖君受命而為法於天下，一敬之所感也。甚矣，天之所親惟敬也！然則命湯以式天下也，固其所哉！此商人祫祭而歌之也，若曰：天有成命，商有世德，而所以靈承之有常、光紹之弗替者，匪
translation_en:
… achievement; as for the blessing of the royal succession, what could be greater than this! Alas, this is the spirit of the antiphonal songs in the court of Yu [Shun]! The era of Shun was praised as the pinnacle of good governance, yet Yu, Yi, and the other ministers earnestly admonished their sovereign only to be cautious at every moment and the slightest sign, and to guard against idleness and pleasure—was this excessive calculation? Indeed, having a good beginning but rarely a good end is the constant nature of men; whereas worrying in times of prosperity and sensing danger in times of enlightenment is truly how loyal ministers apply their minds. The poet of the ode "Jia le" (Admirable and Amiable) grasped this. When people of the past said that the vital breath of Supreme Harmony abided ever in the universe of Yu and Zhou, there was good reason for it!

"God on High charged him to be a model to the nine regions." [Classic of Poetry, "Chang fa"]
Zha Yunyuan

Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Huang: Few candidates were able to fully develop the two words "God's charge" (Di ming); only this essay marshals its ideas and deploys its diction with refined elegance. It ought to be recorded as a model.
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Xu: The essay opens by pairing the settled mandate and hereditary virtue, enters the exposition through "establishing the Mean" and "holding fast to the Mean," and at the end brings together compliant governance and majestic severity to connect with the meaning of the following lines—what extraordinary thought!
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Lin: The literary thought is rich and enduring.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Wu: Precise and exact.

That the sage ruler received the Mandate and became a model for all under Heaven was moved by his single-minded reverence alone. Profound indeed is it that Heaven holds dear only reverence! Such being the case, that it charged Tang to be a model to all under Heaven was truly fitting! This is what the people of Shang sang at the collective ancestral sacrifice (xia), as if to say: Heaven has its settled Mandate, and Shang has its hereditary virtue; yet that whereby one responsively receives it with constancy and gloriously continues it without fail is not…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
敬弗克也我湯純敬以祗帝德斯其至矣而天
之命之也何如哉彼監觀求莫帝之心也惟日
躋則一敬之精純有以孚其簡在之實降衷綏
猷帝之命也惟昭假則一敬之專一足以承其
申錫之休故九圍異制無所於統紀則弗率乃
作之君若曰凡厥弗率爾其正域之而天與之
意昭然於行事之示也九圍異俗無所於節約
則罔中乃作之師若曰凡厥罔中爾其表正之
而帝眷之隆顯然於咨命之間也中天地而為
===
綱常之主紀綱法度於此乎受成焉建中之矩
其治統之所歸乎纘有夏而膺曆數之傳禮樂
敎化於此乎立極焉執中之要其道統之所傳
乎至是則命之始受於玄王而今會其成列辟
侯服於順治而輯瑞者盡天下也旣發之丕基
此其維新矣孰非一德之所致哉命之益大於
相土而今統其盛庶邦震疊於威嚴而貢琛者
盡天下也有截之弘烈此其重光矣又孰非一
敬之所感哉吁此湯之所以大造我商也嗣天
punctuated: 敬弗克也。我湯純敬以祗帝，德斯其至矣，而天之命之也何如哉？彼監觀求莫，帝之心也；惟日躋，則一敬之精純有以孚其簡在之實。降衷綏猷，帝之命也；惟昭假，則一敬之專一足以承其申錫之休。故九圍異制，無所於統紀則弗率，乃作之君，若曰：凡厥弗率，爾其正域之。而天與之意，昭然於行事之示也。九圍異俗，無所於節約則罔中，乃作之師，若曰：凡厥罔中，爾其表正之。而帝眷之隆，顯然於咨命之間也。中天地而為綱常之主，紀綱法度於此乎受成焉。建中之矩，其治統之所歸乎？纘有夏而膺曆數之傳，禮樂敎化於此乎立極焉。執中之要，其道統之所傳乎？至是則命之始受於玄王，而今會其成，列辟侯服於順治，而輯瑞者盡天下也。旣發之丕基，此其維新矣，孰非一德之所致哉！命之益大於相土，而今統其盛，庶邦震疊於威嚴，而貢琛者盡天下也。有截之弘烈，此其重光矣，又孰非一敬之所感哉！吁！此湯之所以大造我商也，嗣天
translation_en:
… reverence, it could not be achieved. Our Tang, with pure reverence in honoring the Lord on High, reached the utmost of virtue; and how then did Heaven confer its mandate upon him? Watching from above and seeking tranquility for the people—such is the mind of the Lord on High. Only because his reverence ascended daily did its refined purity answer to the reality of His selection. Bestowing a moral nature and giving peace through the Way—such is the mandate of the Lord on High. Only because his bright devotion reached on high was the single-mindedness of his reverence sufficient to receive the blessing of His renewed gift.

Therefore, when the nine regions had different institutions, without an overarching order they would not follow; thus Heaven made him their ruler, as if to say: "All who are unruly, do you bring their realms into order!" And Heaven's intention in granting him the realm was clearly manifested in the demonstration of his deeds. When the nine regions had different customs, without restraint they would miss the mean; thus Heaven made him their teacher, as if to say: "All who miss the mean, do you set the standard to rectify them!" And the abundance of the Lord's favor was evident in the words of His charge. Standing at the center of Heaven and Earth as master of the cardinal principles and constant virtues, the laws and institutions took their completion from him. Was not the standard of establishing the mean that to which the succession of governance returned? Succeeding the house of Xia and receiving the transmission of the heavenly destiny, rites, music, and moral teaching had their supreme standard set by him. Was not the essence of holding fast to the mean that by which the succession of the Way was transmitted?

At this point, the Mandate that was first received by the Dark King (Xuanwang) now met its fulfillment; the various lords and feudatories submitted to his benign rule, and those who gathered to present their jade tallies encompassed the whole world. The great foundation already laid was hereby renewed—what part of this was not brought about by his pure virtue? The Mandate that grew ever greater under Xiangtu now reached its full flourishing in his unification; the numerous states trembled before his majesty, and those who offered precious tribute encompassed the whole world. The vast enterprise of bringing all territories into order hereby shone with redoubled brilliance—and what part of this, again, was not inspired by his single-minded reverence? Alas! This is how Tang so greatly established our Shang dynasty. Those who succeed to the…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
下者顧不當永念之乎抑斯敬也即堯舜禹相
傳之心法也心之敬即道之中也湯以此得統
亦以此造商而後賢又能世守其德故享年六
百最爲有道之長也然則敬之一言其萬世帝
王祈天永命之本乎吁君天下者可以惕然思
矣
春秋
夏六月公會齊侯宋公陳侯鄭伯同盟于
幽〔莊公二十有七年〕齊人救邢〔閔公元〕
===
〔年〕遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕秋七月公會齊侯
宋公陳世子款鄭世子華盟于寗母〔僖公七年〕
沈雲楫
同考試官教諭梁批此篇發齊桓始霸以見魯
怨當釋且不脫易世意乃長於經者
考試官教諭林批發魯當從義意明盡
考試官教諭吳批詞簡意明
觀嗣世者迭爲霸圖見怨之所當釋矣蓋魯怨
punctuated:
下者，顧不當永念之乎？抑斯敬也，即堯、舜、禹相傳之心法也。心之敬，即道之中也。湯以此得統，亦以此造商，而後賢又能世守其德，故享年六百，最爲有道之長也。然則敬之一言，其萬世帝王祈天永命之本乎！吁！君天下者，可以惕然思矣。

春秋
夏六月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、鄭伯同盟于幽〔莊公二十有七年〕；齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕；遂伐楚〔僖公四年〕；秋七月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳世子款、鄭世子華盟于寗母〔僖公七年〕。
沈雲楫
同考試官教諭梁批：此篇發齊桓始霸，以見魯怨當釋，且不脫易世意，乃長於經者。
考試官教諭林批：發魯當從義，意明盡。
考試官教諭吳批：詞簡意明。

觀嗣世者迭爲霸圖，見怨之所當釋矣。蓋魯怨
translation_en:
… the realm—ought he not keep this forever in mind? Moreover, this reverence is none other than the method of the mind transmitted down from Yao, Shun, and Yu. Reverence of the mind is the centrality of the Way. Tang gained the legitimate succession by means of this, and also founded the Shang dynasty by means of this; and because the worthy rulers who came after him were able to preserve his virtue from generation to generation, the dynasty enjoyed six hundred years of rule—the longest-enduring of those that possessed the Way. This being so, is not this single word, "reverence," the foundation upon which emperors and kings for ten thousand generations pray to Heaven for a perpetual mandate! Alas! Those who rule over the realm may well reflect upon this with vigilant awe.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In summer, in the sixth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, and together they made a covenant at You" [twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhuang]; "Men of Qi rescued Xing" [first year of Duke Min]; "They thereupon invaded Chu" [fourth year of Duke Xi]; "In autumn, in the seventh month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, Kuan, Heir Apparent of Chen, and Hua, Heir Apparent of Zheng, and made a covenant at Ningmu" [seventh year of Duke Xi].

Shen Yunji 沈雲楫

Associate Examiner, Instructor Liang comments: This essay brings out how Duke Huan of Qi initiated the hegemony in order to show that Lu's grievance ought to be laid aside, and furthermore it does not lose sight of the meaning of the change of generations; it is the work of one well-versed in the Classic.
Examiner, Instructor Lin comments: It brings out how Lu ought to follow righteousness; the meaning is clear and thorough.
Examiner, Instructor Wu comments: The diction is concise and the meaning clear.

Observing how the ruler of a succeeding generation repeatedly pursued hegemonic designs, one sees that the grievance ought to be laid aside. For the grievance of Lu…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之所當報者非桓也而况肇於圖霸乎春秋所
以不貶于柯之盟也且桓何人也非襄之子乎
爲襄之子者是爲魯也仇乃莊之釋怨而與盟
安得遽從無貶耶蓋君子不責於易世之怨孝
子必圖夫宗社之安襄魯仇也而今則非其人
矣况桓之創霸又義之所當從焉今觀其于幽
一盟懷鄭貳也則衆志孚而諸侯合矣又慮諸
夏不可棄也畏簡書以恤患而于邢安焉于楚
一伐聲外暴也則大義著而夷狄攘矣又慮周
===
室所當尊也定方物以作貢而甯母盟焉卽今
日之成匡合之功雖未著而所以樹厥功者從
玆始也從之卽所以從霸而魯安矣若之何其
以一盟而不惠徼於魯之社稷也卽今日之舉
尊攘之績雖未成而所以建厥績者由玆肇也
悖之卽所以悖霸而魯危矣若之何愛於一盟
而不以綏夫魯之宗社耶故春秋不貶于柯之
盟蓋與其脩怨怒鄰之爲孝不若順義安邦之
爲孝亦度其怨之可釋而非與之也明乎此者
punctuated: 之所當報者，非桓也，而况肇於圖霸乎？《春秋》所以不貶于柯之盟也。且桓何人也？非襄之子乎？爲襄之子者，是爲魯也仇；乃莊之釋怨而與盟，安得遽從無貶耶？蓋君子不責於易世之怨，孝子必圖夫宗社之安。襄，魯仇也，而今則非其人矣；况桓之創霸，又義之所當從焉。今觀其于幽一盟，懷鄭貳也，則衆志孚而諸侯合矣；又慮諸夏不可棄也，畏簡書以恤患，而于邢安焉。于楚一伐，聲外暴也，則大義著而夷狄攘矣；又慮周室所當尊也，定方物以作貢，而甯母盟焉。卽今日之成，匡合之功雖未著，而所以樹厥功者從玆始也。從之卽所以從霸，而魯安矣；若之何其以一盟而不惠徼於魯之社稷也？卽今日之舉，尊攘之績雖未成，而所以建厥績者由玆肇也。悖之卽所以悖霸，而魯危矣；若之何愛於一盟而不以綏夫魯之宗社耶？故《春秋》不貶于柯之盟，蓋與其脩怨怒鄰之爲孝，不若順義安邦之爲孝；亦度其怨之可釋，而非與之也。明乎此者，
translation_en: …that which ought to be avenged was not Duke Huan; how much more so when he was just beginning his pursuit of hegemony? This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) did not censure the covenant at Ke. Moreover, what sort of man was Duke Huan? Was he not a son of Duke Xiang [or successor in his line]? To be the son of Duke Xiang would be to stand as Lu's enemy; when Duke Zhuang let go of his resentment and entered into a covenant with him, how could the Annals so readily refrain from censure? It is because a gentleman does not press for vengeance across a change of generations, and a filial son must plan for the security of his ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain. Duke Xiang was Lu's enemy, yet now the ruler was no longer that man; how much more so since Duke Huan's founding of the hegemony was a righteous cause that ought to be followed! Look now at his single covenant at You, which won over wavering Zheng: the minds of the multitude were inspired with trust, and the feudal lords were united. Fearing further that the central states must not be abandoned, he revered the bamboo dispatches to succor those in distress, and thus at Xing peace was secured. Look at his single campaign against Chu, which denounced external aggression: great righteousness was made manifest, and the barbarians were repelled. Fearing further that the royal house of Zhou must be honored, he fixed the regional tribute goods to be offered, and thus the covenant at Ningmu was concluded. In light of today's settlement [at Ke], although his merit of rectifying the realm and uniting the lords was not yet manifest, the foundation for establishing that merit began right here. To follow him was to follow the hegemon, and thereby Lu was made secure; how could one, on account of a single covenant, refuse to seek blessings for the altars of Lu? In light of today's undertaking, although his achievement of honoring the king and repelling the barbarians was not yet complete, the basis for erecting that achievement originated right here. To oppose him was to oppose the hegemon, and thereby Lu would be imperiled; how could one begrudge a single covenant and fail to bring peace to the ancestral temple and altars of Lu? Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not censure the covenant at Ke, for rather than counting it filial to nurse a grudge and provoke a neighbor's wrath, it is better to count it filial to comply with righteousness and give peace to the state; it also judged that the resentment could properly be laid aside, rather than simply granting unconditional approval to the act. Those who understand this…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
可以知權可以擇義而霸業其有興矣抑是盟
也莊公謂生不如死曹子欲請當其臣似憤然
有激於衷者而竟以汶陽之田請則彭生之刃
魯且忘之矣而能以許地之信孚於諸侯而霸
業成焉故桓之伯仲敎之也
晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕
蔣承勛
同考試官敎諭梁批〔此篇作者多褒荀吳語予獨發免於貶意最得經旨〕
考試官敎諭林批〔鎔鑄傳語而題旨自明〕
考試官敎諭吳批〔得春秋用兵禦狄之旨〕
===
春秋於霸兵之近正而特平詞以紀之焉蓋兵
以却叛爲正荀吳之伐鮮虞近於是矣春秋所
以平其詞乎且鮮虞之伐以略遠也而荀吳實
董是役焉殆於潞甲之滅昔陽之入等耳何以
獨稱名氏與其稱人稱國者殊耶蓋兵一耳而
期於殄滅者失之暴行以狄道者失之詐均之
非用兵之正也乃若荀吳則異於是方圍鼓而
punctuated:
可以知權，可以擇義，而霸業其有興矣。抑是盟也，莊公謂生不如死，曹子欲請當其臣，似憤然有激於衷者，而竟以汶陽之田請，則彭生之刃，魯且忘之矣；而能以許地之信孚於諸侯，而霸業成焉，故桓之伯，仲敎之也。

晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕
蔣承勛
同考試官敎諭梁批〔此篇作者多褒荀吳語，予獨發免於貶意，最得經旨。〕
考試官敎諭林批〔鎔鑄傳語，而題旨自明。〕
考試官敎諭吳批〔得《春秋》用兵禦狄之旨。〕

《春秋》於霸兵之近正，而特平詞以紀之焉。蓋兵以却叛爲正，荀吳之伐鮮虞近於是矣，《春秋》所以平其詞乎！且鮮虞之伐，以略遠也，而荀吳實董是役焉，殆於潞甲之滅、昔陽之入等耳，何以獨稱名氏，與其稱人、稱國者殊耶？蓋兵一耳，而期於殄滅者失之暴，行以狄道者失之詐，均之非用兵之正也。乃若荀吳則異於是：方圍鼓而
translation_en:
… will know how to weigh contingencies and choose what is right, and the hegemonic enterprise will surely flourish. Yet in this covenant, when Duke Zhuang declared that life was worse than death and Master Cao (Cao沫) asked permission to confront the ministers of Qi, they seemed filled with righteous indignation stirred from within. In the end, however, they merely requested the return of the fields of Wenyang—meaning that Lu had already forgotten the blade of Pengsheng! Meanwhile, Duke Huan of Qi was able to win the trust of the feudal lords through his good faith in promising to return the land, and thus his hegemony was achieved. Therefore, Duke Huan’s attainment of hegemony was taught to him by Guan Zhong.

“Xun Wu of Jin Led an Army to Attack Xianyu” [Fifteenth Year of Duke Zhao]
By Jiang Chengxun

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Liang: [Other writers on this topic mostly use language praising Xun Wu; this author alone brings out the idea that he was merely spared from censure, which best grasps the meaning of the Classic.]
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Lin: [By smelting and casting the words of the commentaries, the meaning of the theme becomes self-evident.]
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wu: [Captures the *Spring and Autumn Annals*’ essential meaning regarding the use of military force to resist the Di barbarians.]

Toward the military expeditions of a hegemon that approximated rectitude, the *Spring and Autumn Annals* specially recorded them in neutral terms. Indeed, in warfare, rejecting defectors is the standard of rectitude, and Xun Wu’s campaign against Xianyu came close to this; is this not why the *Spring and Autumn Annals* used neutral wording for it? Moreover, the campaign against Xianyu was undertaken to seize distant territory, and Xun Wu was in fact the commander directing this expedition. It was nearly on a par with the annihilation of the L氏 and Jiashi (Lujia) or the entry into Xiyang—why then is he alone recorded by his clan and personal name, differing from those passages that refer merely to “men” or to the “state”? For while military action is one and the same, those who aim at total extermination err through brutality, and those who act after the manner of the Di barbarians err through deceit; both alike depart from the proper use of military force. As for Xun Wu, however, he differed from these: just when he was besieging Gu and…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
請以城叛力屈而請以城降也在彼已無效死
之心然請叛而俾之繕守力屈而俾之修城也
在我則堅却叛之信非故獲城而不取也以好
惡不愆而後民知所適惡吾叛而受其叛何以
示民信耶是故雖可以得城而弗受也非故勤
民而頓兵也以率義不爽而後民知事君邑可
獲而賈民怠其何以事君耶是故雖可以獲邑
而弗爲也以是用兵則不欲城而邇姦是謂守
正而行其得城且不戮也暴云乎哉不失信以
===
===
庇民是謂師貞之吉其力盡而後取也詐云乎
哉經故於荀吳而獨舉名氏非褒之也纔免於
貶耳而窮兵略遠者可知矣春秋此義不可以
見用兵禦狄之略哉抑鮮虞之伐却叛正也嗣
是陸渾之滅以靖王室君子以爲義而猶有所
不滿者蓋晉昭之世荆楚暴横不是之慮而攘
却無聞焉獨於鮮虞陸渾是亟自是吳楚爭衡
而晉霸之業衰荀吳諸臣不得不任其咎
禮記
punctuated:
請以城叛，力屈而請以城降也，在彼已無效死之心；然請叛而俾之繕守，力屈而俾之修城也，在我則堅却叛之信。非故獲城而不取也，以好惡不愆，而後民知所適；惡吾叛而受其叛，何以示民信耶？是故雖可以得城而弗受也。非故勤民而頓兵也，以率義不爽，而後民知事君；邑可獲而賈民怠，其何以事君耶？是故雖可以獲邑而弗爲也。以是用兵，則不欲城而邇姦，是謂守正而行，其得城且不戮也，暴云乎哉？不失信以庇民，是謂師貞之吉，其力盡而後取也，詐云乎哉？經故於荀吳而獨舉名氏，非褒之也，纔免於貶耳，而窮兵略遠者可知矣。《春秋》此義，不可以見用兵禦狄之略哉？抑鮮虞之伐，却叛，正也。嗣是陸渾之滅，以靖王室，君子以爲義，而猶有所不滿者。蓋晉昭之世，荆楚暴横，不是之慮，而攘却無聞焉，獨於鮮虞、陸渾是亟。自是吳、楚爭衡，而晉霸之業衰，荀吳諸臣不得不任其咎。

《禮記》
translation_en:
… asked to defect with their city, and when their strength was exhausted they asked to surrender with their city, on their part they already had no heart to fight to the death. Yet when they asked to defect he had them mend their defenses, and when their strength was exhausted he had them repair their walls; on our part this was to stand firm in the good faith of rejecting defectors. It was not that he deliberately declined to take a city within his grasp: only when likes and dislikes are free from error do the people know what course to follow. If we hate defection among our own people yet accept defection from theirs, how can we display good faith to the people? Therefore, even though he could have obtained the city, he would not accept it. Nor was it that he deliberately wore out the people and blunted his troops: only when the lead in righteousness is unfailing do the people know how to serve their ruler. If a town can be gained at the price of buying laxity among the people, how then will they serve their ruler? Therefore, even though he could have gained the town, he would not do so. To employ troops in this manner—not coveting a city at the cost of drawing near to treachery—is what is meant by acting in adherence to rectitude. When he took the city and moreover slew no one, could that be called brutal? Not breaking faith in order to shelter the people is what is meant by the auspiciousness of a righteous army (shi zhen zhi ji). When he took it only after their strength was spent, could that be called deceitful? Thus the Classic (Spring and Autumn Annals) uniquely records Xun Wu 荀吳 by his personal name and clan name—not to praise him, but merely because he barely escaped censure; and from this one may know how those who exhausted their weaponry to seize distant lands are to be judged. In this principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), can one not see the grand strategy for employing troops to ward off the Di barbarians? Yet in the campaign against Xianyu 鮮虞, rejecting defection was upright. Thereafter, in the destruction of the Luhun 陸渾戎 to pacify the Royal House, the gentleman considered it righteous and yet still found something unsatisfactory in it. For in the reign of Duke Zhao of Jin 晉昭公, Chu 荆楚 was violent and overbearing; instead of taking thought for this—so that nothing was heard of repelling them—Jin was urgent only against Xianyu and Luhun. From this time onward Wu 吳 and Chu contended for supremacy while the hegemonic enterprise of Jin declined, and Xun Wu and the other ministers cannot escape bearing the blame for it.

Record of Rites (Liji)

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
是故昔先王尚有德尊有道任有能舉賢
而置之聚眾而誓之是故因天事天因
地事地因名山升中于天因吉土以饗
帝于郊升中于天而鳳皇降龜龍假饗
帝于郊而風雨節寒暑時是故聖人南
面而立而天下大治
王豫
考試官敎諭林批先王祭則受福而至治成
得人故耳子能詳言之且簡潔可誦取之
===
考試官敎諭吳批詞約而意已盡
觀聖王用賢舉祀之效而其享至治也有由矣
夫治至無爲治之極也先王得賢以舉大祭而
瑞應臻焉此所以享無爲之治歟記禮器者蓋
謂人君一身敬天勤民之責萃焉所以迓神休
而登治理者要在於用賢也已吾觀先王以天
地肇乎大祭而助祭貴於得人也于是尚德尊
道而使能之不遺焉舉賢誓眾而莅事之有恪
焉其慎擇乎左右者無弗豫已由是因天因地
punctuated:
「是故昔先王尚有德，尊有道，任有能，舉賢而置之，聚眾而誓之。是故因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中于天，因吉土以饗帝于郊。升中于天而鳳皇降，龜龍假；饗帝于郊而風雨節，寒暑時。是故聖人南面而立，而天下大治。」
王豫
考試官敎諭林批：先王祭則受福而至治成，得人故耳。子能詳言之，且簡潔可誦，取之。
考試官敎諭吳批：詞約而意已盡。
觀聖王用賢舉祀之效，而其享至治也有由矣。夫治至無爲，治之極也。先王得賢以舉大祭，而瑞應臻焉，此所以享無爲之治歟！記《禮器》者，蓋謂人君一身，敬天勤民之責萃焉，所以迓神休而登治理者，要在於用賢也已。吾觀先王以天地肇乎大祭，而助祭貴於得人也。于是尚德尊道，而使能之不遺焉；舉賢誓眾，而莅事之有恪焉。其慎擇乎左右者，無弗豫已。由是因天因地
translation_en:
"Therefore, the former kings of old exalted those who possessed virtue, honored those who possessed the Way, and employed those who possessed ability. They elevated the worthy and placed them in office, gathered the multitude and bound them with solemn oaths. Therefore, in accordance with Heaven they served Heaven; in accordance with Earth they served Earth; making use of famous mountains, they offered up notice of great peace and completion to Heaven; making use of auspicious ground, they feasted the Supreme Ancestor in the suburban sacrifice. When they offered up notice of completion to Heaven, phoenixes descended and tortoises and dragons arrived; when they feasted the Supreme Ancestor in the suburban sacrifice, wind and rain were regulated, and cold and heat came in their proper seasons. Therefore, the sage stood facing south, and All-under-Heaven was in a state of great order."

Wang Yu 王豫

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Lin: When the former kings sacrificed, they received blessings and achieved supreme order, simply because they obtained the right men. You are able to expound upon this in detail, and the prose is concise and worthy of recitation. Selected.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wu: The words are economical, yet the meaning is fully expressed.

When we observe the efficacy of the sage kings employing the worthy to perform the sacrifices, we see there is a reason why they enjoyed supreme order. Now, when governance reaches non-action (wuwei), that is the pinnacle of governance. When the former kings obtained worthy men to perform the great sacrifices, auspicious responses arrived—was this not how they enjoyed the governance of non-action? The author who recorded the "Vessels of Rites" (Liqi 禮器) chapter meant to say that upon the person of the ruler alone are gathered the responsibilities of revering Heaven and laboring for the people; thus, the means to welcome divine blessings and ascend to orderly governance lies essentially in employing the worthy. I observe that the former kings initiated the great sacrifices on the basis of Heaven and Earth, and in assisting at the sacrifices, the most vital thing was obtaining the right men. Thereupon, they exalted virtue and honored the Way, not overlooking the employment of ability; they elevated the worthy and bound the multitude with oaths, approaching the ceremony with reverence. In carefully selecting their attendants and aides, there was nothing not prepared in advance. From this, by conforming to Heaven and conforming to Earth…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而天地之禮制焉升中享帝而內外之祭行焉
其秩舉乎祀典者無弗周已惟其禮行於天則
天心鑒之而鳳皇龜龍之咸臻所以昭其貺于
神物也惟其禮行於郊則天神享之而寒暑風
雨之以時所以效其靈于歲功也夫衆職樂于
官備而神道速於感通如此聖王於此又何爲
哉但見其撫運於穆清惟克端其嚮明之度而
弘化于熈皡自聿臻夫極治之休王心無爲而
有道之化以成百姓則太和也萬物則咸若也
===
各順治於無方矣帝位允陟而無虞之盛以隆
中國則乂安焉外夷則輯服焉咸蕩平於無外
矣向非先王擇人於未祭之先舉祭於得人之
後胡爲而有是休徵瑞物也又胡爲而能致天
下之盛治也圖治者信必有道矣抑考虞書夷
典禮夔典樂而禋望肆類之禮無不徧舉以故
七政順於上鳳皇儀於庭非天下大治之驗歟
所以然者以聖人之心與天爲一而感格之本
端是以天不愛道地不愛寳而至治成耳若本
punctuated: 而天地之禮制焉，升中享帝而內外之祭行焉，其秩舉乎祀典者無弗周已。惟其禮行於天，則天心鑒之，而鳳皇、龜、龍之咸臻，所以昭其貺于神物也；惟其禮行於郊，則天神享之，而寒、暑、風、雨之以時，所以效其靈于歲功也。夫衆職樂于官備，而神道速於感通如此，聖王於此又何爲哉？但見其撫運於穆清，惟克端其嚮明之度，而弘化于熈皡，自聿臻夫極治之休。王心無爲，而有道之化以成：百姓則太和也，萬物則咸若也，各順治於無方矣；帝位允陟，而無虞之盛以隆：中國則乂安焉，外夷則輯服焉，咸蕩平於無外矣。向非先王擇人於未祭之先，舉祭於得人之後，胡爲而有是休徵瑞物也？又胡爲而能致天下之盛治也？圖治者，信必有道矣。抑考《虞書》，夷典禮、夔典樂，而禋、望、肆、類之禮無不徧舉，以故七政順於上、鳳皇儀於庭，非天下大治之驗歟？所以然者，以聖人之心與天爲一，而感格之本端，是以天不愛道、地不愛寳，而至治成耳。若本
translation_en: …and the rites of Heaven and Earth are established; ascending the sacred peak to present offerings to the Supreme Ruler, both the inner and outer sacrifices are performed—in celebrating the sacrificial canons in due order, nothing is left incomplete. Because these rites are performed before Heaven, the mind of Heaven beholds them, and the phoenix, tortoise, and dragon all arrive, thereby manifesting its blessing through numinous creatures. Because these rites are performed at the suburban altar, the spirits of Heaven enjoy the offerings, and cold, heat, wind, and rain come in their proper seasons, thereby displaying their efficacy in the year's harvest. Now, when the many offices rejoice in having their posts fully staffed and the way of the spirits is so swift to respond and communicate, what further need the sage-king do in this regard? One sees him merely presiding over the cycle of rule in solemn purity, able simply to rectify his bearing as he faces the light of day, while his expansive transformation unfolds in serene contentment, naturally attaining the blessings of utmost order. The king's mind acts through non-action, and the transformation of the Way is thereby accomplished: the hundred surnames enjoy supreme harmony, the myriad things all flourish according to their natures, and each is brought into orderly accord without spatial limit. The imperial throne is truly ascended, and the flourishing age free of anxiety reaches its height: the Central States enjoy peace and stability, the outer barbarians are brought into harmonious submission, and all alike are leveled and pacified with nothing left outside. Had the former kings not selected the right men before the sacrifices were held, and performed the sacrifices only after obtaining the right men, how could there have been these auspicious signs and felicitous creatures? And how could they have brought about the flourishing governance of All under Heaven? Those who plan for governance must truly possess the proper Way. Moreover, if we examine the Book of Yu (Yushu), Boyi was in charge of rites and Kui was in charge of music, and the rites of the pure sacrifice (yin), the distant sacrifice to mountains and rivers (wang), the offering of whole victims (si), and the special sacrifice to Heaven (lei) were all comprehensively performed; consequently, the Seven Regulators moved in harmony above, and the phoenixes came in stately array to the court below—was this not proof of the great ordering of All under Heaven? The reason this was so is that the mind of the sage was one with Heaven, and the foundation for moving and reaching the spirits was upright; therefore, Heaven did not begrudge its Way, Earth did not begrudge its treasures, and utmost governance was achieved. If the foundation…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之不端而徒欲徼福於神明可乎故曰惟聖人
爲能饗帝信夫
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣
吳一貫
考試官教諭林批說武王偃武修文而天下
知臣禮明鬯可觀
考試官教諭吳批得諸侯知所以臣意
聖王制禮而天下喻于忠焉夫以臣尊君忠道
也武王制朝覲之禮而諸侯知尊君焉其文教
===
之隆何如哉夫子舉之以告賓牟賈也蓋謂上
之所以率下與下之所以奉上者惟禮以爲之
防也觀我周文教之修而知臣禮之明矣蓋周
自受命以來武王已爲天下君而天下既幸其
有君亦欲知其所以臣也但禮未制耳武王於
是撫萬邦之廣以昭一統之尊因典禮之常以
示服從之化時其春也而制爲之朝以聯其情
藹乎喜起之休也時乎秋也而制爲之覲以明
其分秩乎等威之辨也斯禮也所以明君臣之
punctuated:
之不端，而徒欲徼福於神明，可乎？故曰：「惟聖人爲能饗帝。」信夫！

朝覲，然後諸侯知所以臣。
吳一貫
考試官教諭林批：說武王偃武修文而天下知臣禮，明鬯可觀。
考試官教諭吳批：得「諸侯知所以臣」意。

聖王制禮，而天下喻于忠焉。夫以臣尊君，忠道也。武王制朝覲之禮，而諸侯知尊君焉，其文教之隆何如哉！夫子舉之以告賓牟賈也，蓋謂上之所以率下，與下之所以奉上者，惟禮以爲之防也。觀我周文教之修，而知臣禮之明矣。蓋周自受命以來，武王已爲天下君，而天下既幸其有君，亦欲知其所以臣也，但禮未制耳。武王於是撫萬邦之廣，以昭一統之尊；因典禮之常，以示服從之化。時其春也，而制爲之朝，以聯其情，藹乎喜起之休也；時乎秋也，而制爲之覲，以明其分，秩乎等威之辨也。斯禮也，所以明君臣之
translation_en:
…is not upright, yet one merely wishes to seek blessings from the gods and spirits, how could that be acceptable? Therefore it is said: "Only the sage is able to make offerings to the Lord on High." Truly so!

"Through spring and autumn court audiences, the feudal lords thereupon knew how to act as subjects."
Wu Yiguan 吳一貫
Examiner and County Director of Studies Lin comments: Its explanation of how King Wu desisted from military affairs and cultivated civil culture so that all under Heaven understood the rites of a subject is clear, fluent, and worth reading.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Wu comments: It grasps the meaning of "the feudal lords knew how to act as subjects."

When the sage-king instituted the rites, all under Heaven came to understand loyalty. Now, for a subject to honor his ruler is the way of loyalty. When King Wu instituted the rites of spring and autumn court audiences, the feudal lords knew how to honor their ruler—how grand was the flourishing of his civil teachings! When the Master cited this to instruct Bin Moujia 賓牟賈, he meant that whereby superiors lead inferiors and inferiors serve superiors has only ritual to serve as its dyke. By observing the cultivation of civil teachings in our Zhou dynasty, one knows that the rites of a subject were made clear. For ever since the Zhou received the Mandate, King Wu had already become ruler of all under Heaven, and while all under Heaven rejoiced in having a ruler, they also wished to know how to act as subjects; it was only that the rites had not yet been instituted. Thereupon, King Wu pacified the vastness of the myriad states to manifest the dignity of unified rule, and relied on the constancy of canonical rites to display the transforming influence of obedience. When the season was spring, he instituted the spring court audience (chao 朝) to bind their affections, harmonious in the felicity of joyful exhilaration; when the season was autumn, he instituted the autumn audience (jin 覲) to clarify their stations, orderly in the distinction of hierarchical majesty.
