title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
九重達孝之恩錫類於四海則夫因
郊祀而益推本之以會
祖宗之作述於一原因
視學而益講求之以垂
尊親之典禮於萬世豈非
帝王之盛遇而臣民之頌法也哉請得而敬陳
之粤自帝舜有肆類之文而言天祀者昉
之逮成周大宗伯掌天神地祇而燔燎之
典明堂之位其禮於是乎大備有虞氏有
===
上庠之名而言太學者祖之逮成周大司
徒掌敎國子弟而成均之法辟雍之創其
文於是乎益彰考之詩書所載則圜丘方
澤布其位也陶匏繭栗明其牲也蒼璧黃
琮昭其獻也此郊祀之制之大略也而明
堂之祀則所以因文王而隆大報也其品
式之具蓋莫有盛焉者矣若夫分祀也者
陰陽以類而求之謂也合祀也者父母共
牢而食之謂也祭天于泰壇而以祖有功
punctuated:
九重，達孝之恩錫類於四海。則夫因郊祀而益推本之，以會祖宗之作述於一原；因視學而益講求之，以垂尊親之典禮於萬世。豈非帝王之盛遇，而臣民之頌法也哉？請得而敬陳之。

粤自帝舜有「肆類」之文，而言天祀者昉之；逮成周，大宗伯掌天神地祇，而燔燎之典、明堂之位，其禮於是乎大備。有虞氏有「上庠」之名，而言太學者祖之；逮成周，大司徒掌敎國子弟，而成均之法、辟雍之創，其文於是乎益彰。

考之《詩》《書》所載，則圜丘、方澤，布其位也；陶匏、繭栗，明其牲也；蒼璧、黃琮，昭其獻也：此郊祀之制之大略也。而明堂之祀，則所以因文王而隆大報也。其品式之具，蓋莫有盛焉者矣。若夫分祀也者，陰陽以類而求之謂也；合祀也者，父母共牢而食之謂也；祭天于泰壇，而以「祖有功…
translation_en:
… the ninefold palace, and the grace of His far-reaching filial piety extends to his kind across the four seas. Thus, building upon the suburban sacrifices to trace their roots ever deeper, so as to unite the creations and transmissions of the Imperial Ancestors into a single source; and building upon the imperial inspection of the Directorate of Education to investigate them ever more thoroughly, so as to hand down the canonical rites for honoring parents to ten thousand generations—is this not a magnificent occasion for sovereigns, and something for subjects and commoners to praise and emulate? Allow me to reverently set this forth.

Ever since Emperor Shun had the text on "performing the Sacrifice to Heaven (lei)," those who speak of sacrifices to Heaven have traced their beginnings to it; coming down to the flourishing Zhou dynasty, the Grand Minister of Rites (da zongbo) took charge of the celestial spirits and terrestrial deities, and with the statutes of burning offerings on a pyre and the positions in the Hall of Light (mingtang), the rites reached full completion. The Lord of Yu (Shun) had the name "Upper School (shangxiang)," and those who speak of the Grand Academy (taixue) take it as their ancestor; coming down to the flourishing Zhou dynasty, the Grand Minister of Education (da situ) took charge of instructing the sons and younger brothers of the state, and with the methods of the Equalizing Academy (chengjun) and the establishment of the Jade-Ring Moat (biyong), their cultural forms became ever more manifest.

Examining what is recorded in the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu): the Round Mound (huanqiu) and the Square Pool (fangze) laid out their sites; earthenware, gourds, and calves with cocoon- or chestnut-sized horns defined their sacrificial vessels and victims; the azure bi-disc and yellow cong-tube displayed their offerings—such is the general outline of the system of suburban sacrifices. As for the sacrifice in the Hall of Light, it was the means by which, through King Wen, the great recompense was exalted. In the completeness of their grades and forms, nothing could have been more flourishing. As for separate sacrifices, this refers to seeking yin and yang according to their respective categories; as for joint sacrifices, this refers to father and mother sharing the same sacrificial animals and eating together; sacrificing to Heaven at the Grand Altar (taitan), and matching it with "the Ancestor who has merit…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者配尊之之謂也祀帝于明堂而以宗有
德者配親之之謂也其義寧不各有所指
哉彼三歲之中僅制一郊則漢武之失於
疏也乃昊天上帝太乙五帝之祠愈益見
其謬爾是惡足以語郊祀之精乎水環合
璧文以象也天子諸侯名以別也貍首騶
虞射以義也此視學之制之大略也而辟
雍之歌則所以美多士而慶思服也其禮
樂之盛蓋莫有詳焉者矣若夫先聖先師
===
則釋奠之所由名也國老庶老則養老之
所由名也以之合舞以之合聲而又有所
謂頒樂舞之名也移之郊遂移之遠方而
又有所謂簡不率教之名也其事寧不各
有所屬哉彼太學之外復視四學非周制
之過於繁也乃尚親尚賢尚齒尚貴之義
愈益見其勤爾又豈不足以備視學之末
乎洪惟我
太祖高皇帝奄有中夏肇脩人紀謂
punctuated: 者配，尊之之謂也；祀帝于明堂而以宗有德者配，親之之謂也。其義寧不各有所指哉？彼三歲之中僅制一郊，則漢武之失於疏也；乃昊天上帝、太乙、五帝之祠，愈益見其謬爾。是惡足以語郊祀之精乎？水環合璧，文以象也；天子諸侯，名以別也；《貍首》、《騶虞》，射以義也。此視學之制之大略也；而《辟雍》之歌，則所以美多士而慶思服也。其禮樂之盛，蓋莫有詳焉者矣。若夫先聖、先師，則釋奠之所由名也；國老、庶老，則養老之所由名也。以之合舞，以之合聲，而又有所謂頒樂舞之名也；移之郊，遂移之遠方，而又有所謂簡不率教之名也。其事寧不各有所屬哉？彼太學之外復視四學，非周制之過於繁也；乃尚親、尚賢、尚齒、尚貴之義，愈益見其勤爾。又豈不足以備視學之末乎？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，奄有中夏，肇脩人紀。謂
translation_en:
… of merit as coadjutor—this is what is meant by honoring him; sacrificing to the Lord on High in the Bright Hall (Mingtang) and associating an exemplar (zong) of virtue as coadjutor—this is what is meant by treating him with familial affection. Does not the meaning of each have its own specific point of reference? As for performing the suburban sacrifice only once every three years, that was Emperor Wu of Han's error of excessive infrequency; and his shrines to Sovereign Heaven the Lord on High (Haotian Shangdi), the Supreme Unity (Taiyi), and the Five Emperors (Wudi) all the more reveal his absurdity. How could this suffice to speak of the essence of the suburban sacrifices?

Water encircling like a jade disk (bi) gives form through symbolic imagery; the Son of Heaven and the feudal lords are distinguished by name; the tunes "Wildcat's Head" (Lishou) and "Zouyu" imbue the archery ritual with moral meaning. This is the general outline of the system of imperial inspection of the academy; and the songs of the Circular Moat Academy (Piyong) were composed to praise the multitude of scholars and celebrate their heartfelt submission. In the flourishing of rites and music, nothing was more detailed than this. As for the Former Sages and Former Teachers, it is from them that the libation and offering ritual (shidian) derives its name; as for the elders of state and the elders of the common people, it is from them that the ritual of nourishing the aged (yanglao) derives its name. Using the academy to harmonize the dances and harmonize the music gave rise to the designation of "promulgating music and dance"; transferring the recalcitrant to the suburbs and then to distant regions gave rise to the designation of "winnowing out those who do not follow instruction." Does not each of these affairs have its own proper sphere? That outside the Grand Academy (Taixue) the ruler also inspected the Four Academies was not because the Zhou system was overly elaborate; rather, the principles of esteeming kinship, esteeming worth, esteeming age, and esteeming nobility all the more reveal its diligence. How could this fail to suffice even for the lesser details of inspecting the academy?

Vast indeed was our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi), who, taking possession of the central lands, first rectified the human moral order! Holding that …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天地乃報本反始之大也建
圜丘於鍾山之陽而以冬至
祀天建
方丘於鍾山之陰而以夏至
祀地此因周禮之文者也行之數年風雨變異
乃斷
宸衷而合祀之典永為定制其禮則舉於
南郊大祀之殿其吉則卜以首春上辛之日
列聖以來遵之百有餘年
===
天心享孚奕奕乎稱盛矣謂太學乃崇文重道
之首也
大位甫正而亟隆釋奠之行及太學告成而再
舉
臨幸之禮此極垂統之善者也嗣是以後規制
大備凡
卽位改元而郊祀之後必先
臨幸登孔聖之廟則躬釋奠之拜
御彝倫之堂則賜坐講之榮
punctuated: 天地乃報本反始之大也。建圜丘於鍾山之陽，而以冬至祀天；建方丘於鍾山之陰，而以夏至祀地，此因《周禮》之文者也。行之數年，風雨變異，乃斷宸衷，而合祀之典，永為定制。其禮則舉於南郊大祀之殿，其吉則卜以首春上辛之日。列聖以來，遵之百有餘年，天心享孚，奕奕乎稱盛矣。謂太學乃崇文重道之首也。大位甫正，而亟隆釋奠之行；及太學告成，而再舉臨幸之禮，此極垂統之善者也。嗣是以後，規制大備，凡卽位改元，而郊祀之後，必先臨幸。登孔聖之廟，則躬釋奠之拜；御彝倫之堂，則賜坐講之榮。
translation_en:
… Heaven and Earth are the greatest matters of repaying one's origin and returning to the beginning. He erected the Round Altar (Huanqiu) on the southern slope of Bell Mountain (Zhongshan) and sacrificed to Heaven at the winter solstice; he erected the Square Altar (Fangqiu) on the northern slope of Bell Mountain and sacrificed to Earth at the summer solstice. This followed the text of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). After practicing this for several years, anomalies of wind and rain occurred; he then made a resolute decision from his imperial heart, and the rite of joint sacrifice permanently became the established institution. The ritual was performed in the Hall of the Great Sacrifice (Dasi dian) in the Southern Suburb (Nanjiao), and the auspicious day was divined as the first xin day of the first month of spring. Since the succession of sacred emperors, this was observed for over a hundred years; the mind of Heaven accepted the offerings in mutual trust, and how gloriously flourishing it was!

He considered that the National University (Taixue) is the foremost institution for honoring literature and esteeming the Way. As soon as he ascended the great throne, he promptly exalted the performance of the libation sacrifice to Confucius (shidian); and when the completion of the National University was announced, he once again held the ceremony of an imperial visit. This was the ultimate excellence in handing down a tradition to posterity. Thereafter, the regulations and institutions became fully complete: whenever an emperor ascended the throne and changed the reign era, following the suburban sacrifice he would invariably first make an imperial visit to the National University. Ascending the temple of the Sage Confucius, he personally performed the obeisance of the libation sacrifice; taking his seat in the Hall of Moral Constant (Yilun tang), he bestowed the honor of sitting and lecturing on the classics. …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
列聖以來遵之代不闕儀
聖化風行奕奕乎稱盛矣迨我
世宗肅皇帝
神聖逺度於哲王
仁孝媲休於
太祖議
南北郊壇之分而奏燔圜丘感
欽天記頌之製正
先師孔子之號而
===
重幸太學行弁服四拜之禮豈非
大聖人之作爲夐有出於作述典禮之外者哉
然精誠屢格於
玄穹而合祀之典未復孝享亟隆於追配而養
老之制未講則明問所謂尊
天教孝之實謂不有待於
今日
聖天子之議禮乎恭惟
皇上欽崇
punctuated: 列聖以來遵之，代不闕儀，聖化風行，奕奕乎稱盛矣！迨我世宗肅皇帝，神聖逺度於哲王，仁孝媲休於太祖，議南北郊壇之分，而奏燔圜丘，感《欽天記頌》之製；正先師孔子之號，而重幸太學，行弁服四拜之禮。豈非大聖人之作爲，夐有出於作述典禮之外者哉！然精誠屢格於玄穹，而合祀之典未復；孝享亟隆於追配，而養老之制未講。則明問所謂「尊天教孝之實」，謂不有待於今日聖天子之議禮乎？恭惟皇上欽崇
translation_en: Since the successive Sacred Emperors, this has been observed without missing a single ceremony in any generation. The sacred transformation has spread like the wind—how magnificently flourishing it is called! Coming down to our Emperor Shizong Su [the Jiajing Emperor], his divine sagacity far surpassed that of the wise kings of old, and his benevolence and filial piety matched the glory of Taizu. He deliberated on the separation of the northern and southern suburban altars, and when presenting the burnt offering at the Circular Mound, he was moved to compose the Record and Ode on Revering Heaven (Qintian jisong); he rectified the title of the Former Teacher Confucius, and visited the National University a second time, performing the rite of four prostrations in ceremonial cap and robes. Are these not the deeds of a Great Sage, rising far beyond the mere creation and transmission of canonical rites? Yet although his utmost sincerity repeatedly reached the Dark Vault of Heaven, the canon of joint sacrifice had not yet been restored; and although his filial offerings were urgently exalted in associating ancestors with Heaven, the institution of nourishing the aged had not yet been discussed. Then as for what the brilliant question calls "the reality of honoring Heaven and teaching filial piety," can it be said that this does not await the ritual deliberations of today's Sacred Son of Heaven? I reverently reflect that Your Majesty reveres and exalts…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天道嘉惠人文恭行
郊祀則納輔臣之言而積誠致潔凡戒具省視
壇飾宫齋視昔益加虔焉百辟之望
皇宇而駿奔者莫不欣欣曰
聖天子冲睿其至敬足以對越
上帝也如此
駕幸太學則循禮官之請而崇祀臨觀凡秩坐
命講宣諭宴錫視昔益加渥焉四方之圜橋門
而觀聽者莫不欣欣曰
===
聖天子冲睿其至敎足以風動士類也如此於
戲休哉夫郊祭古矣而分祀之義則於經
為鮮据虞書言類于上帝而未及祭地之
文周詩言上帝居歆而未列后土之祀戴
禮記郊特牲而未秩大社之具是故合祀
也者
聖祖所以破漢儒之習舍周禮之文而直復有
虞之典豈非卓卓然達天地之精者乎厥
後分祀起
punctuated:
天道，嘉惠人文。恭行郊祀，則納輔臣之言，而積誠致潔，凡戒具省視、壇飾宫齋，視昔益加虔焉。百辟之望皇宇而駿奔者，莫不欣欣曰：「聖天子冲睿，其至敬足以對越上帝也如此！」駕幸太學，則循禮官之請，而崇祀臨觀，凡秩坐命講、宣諭宴錫，視昔益加渥焉。四方之圜橋門而觀聽者，莫不欣欣曰：「聖天子冲睿，其至敎足以風動士類也如此！」於戲休哉！

夫郊祭古矣，而分祀之義則於經為鮮据。《虞書》言「類于上帝」，而未及祭地之文；《周詩》言「上帝居歆」，而未列后土之祀；《戴禮》記《郊特牲》，而未秩大社之具。是故合祀也者，聖祖所以破漢儒之習，舍《周禮》之文，而直復有虞之典，豈非卓卓然達天地之精者乎？厥後分祀，起
translation_en:
… the Way of Heaven and graciously favors human culture. In reverently performing the Suburban Sacrifices, He accepted the counsel of His Grand Secretaries, accumulating sincerity and achieving purity; in all matters of preparing the sacrificial implements, inspecting the victims, adorning the altars, and fasting in the palace, He was even more devout than in the past. Among the hundred officials who gazed upon the imperial precincts and hastened forward in service, there were none who did not rejoice and say: "The Sacred Son of Heaven, though young, is wise; such is His utmost reverence that suffices to respond to the Lord on High!" When the Imperial Carriage visited the National University, He followed the request of the ritual officials, exalting the sacrifice and personally observing the rites; in all matters of arranging the seating, commanding the lectures, proclaiming edicts, and bestowing banquets and gifts, His grace was even more generous than in the past. Among the people from the four quarters who surrounded the gates of the university to watch and listen, there were none who did not rejoice and say: "The Sacred Son of Heaven, though young, is wise; such is His utmost teaching that suffices to inspire and move the literati!" Oh, how magnificent!

Now, the Suburban Sacrifice is ancient indeed, yet the principle of separate sacrifices finds scant basis in the Classics. The Book of Yu (Yushu) speaks of "performing the lei sacrifice to the Lord on High," without any text mentioning a sacrifice to Earth; the Odes of Zhou (Zhoushi) say "the Lord on High tranquilly enjoys the offering," without listing a sacrifice to the Sovereign Earth; the Record of Rites by Dai (Dai Li) records the "Single Victim at the Border Sacrifices" (Jiao tesheng), without ordering the implements for the Great Altar of the Soil. Therefore, this joint sacrifice was whereby the Sacred Ancestor broke with the habits of the Han Confucians, set aside the text of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), and directly restored the canons of the Lord of Yu—was this not a towering comprehension of the essence of Heaven and Earth? Thereafter, the separate sacrifices arose from…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
世宗維新講禮之會有取周禮郊祀而順陰陽
因高下以祈來享之說也而
穆考因之奕世未復蓋惟曰秉
仁敬之德足以宣
饗帝之誠而無擇於分合之地且於議爲聚訟
於孝爲無改耳然禮有神而明之者寧可
憚其難而弗之易歟自今觀之壇分南北
是矣然
天地旣父母對待之稱則
===
王者事
天如事親也而南與北馳得非隔室而處乎祭
因二至是矣然
國朝旣用夏建寅之月則周歲自夏而徂冬
也而地先天祭得非越次而食乎至於寒
暑凝極則
聖躬無乃勞而百官亦有跛倚從事者乎一歲
再出則
聖駕無乃煩而六御亦有侍衞乞休者乎然則
punctuated: 世宗維新講禮之會，有取《周禮》郊祀，而順陰陽、因高下，以祈來享之說也。而穆考因之，奕世未復，蓋惟曰：秉仁敬之德，足以宣饗帝之誠，而無擇於分合之地；且於議爲聚訟，於孝爲無改耳。然禮有神而明之者，寧可憚其難而弗之易歟？自今觀之，壇分南北，是矣；然天地旣父母對待之稱，則王者事天如事親也，而南與北馳，得非隔室而處乎？祭因二至，是矣；然國朝旣用夏建寅之月，則周歲自夏而徂冬也，而地先天祭，得非越次而食乎？至於寒暑凝極，則聖躬無乃勞，而百官亦有跛倚從事者乎？一歲再出，則聖駕無乃煩，而六御亦有侍衞乞休者乎？然則
translation_en: … at the juncture when Emperor Shizong carried out his renewal and deliberated on the rites, adopting the Suburban Sacrifices of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) and the doctrine of conforming to yin and yang and following height and lowness in order to pray that the spirits come and accept the offerings. Our late Imperial Father, Emperor Muzong, continued this, and across generations the joint sacrifice has not been restored. This was surely only because it was said that holding fast to the virtues of benevolence and reverence is sufficient to manifest the sincerity of feasting the Lord on High, without needing to choose between separate or joint places of worship; and moreover, that debating it would only lead to endless contention, whereas making no change was the way of filial piety. Yet in ritual there is that which iscomprehended through spiritual insight and brought to clarity—how could one shrink from its difficulty and refrain from changing it? Viewed from the present: dividing the altars between south and north is all very well; yet since Heaven and Earth are the paired designations of father and mother, the true king serves Heaven as he serves his parents—so when one gallops between south and north, is this not like making them dwell in separate chambers? Scheduling the sacrifices according to the two solstices is all very well; yet since our dynasty uses the Xia calendar beginning with the yin month, the course of the year proceeds from summer toward winter—so when Earth is sacrificed to before Heaven, is this not like serving a meal out of proper order? As for the times when cold and heat reach their severest extremes, does this not fatigue the Sacred Person, while among the hundred officials there are also those who perform their duties leaning and slouching? And with going out twice in a single year, does this not trouble the Imperial Carriage, while among the Six Teams of the imperial retinue there are also guards who beg for respite? If so, then…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
復合祀之禮者甚有關於昭事之原而於
我
皇上郊祀之大典不爲已精而愈精也耶夫視
學古矣而養老之義則於經爲尤著禮言
適學而有設饌省醴之具詩歌行葦而有
酌斗介耇之儀明帝中主而亦有臨雍拜
饗之詔是故養老也者聖王所以正父子
之敘明長幼之節而永敦齒讓之德豈非
彬彬然敦孝弟之實者乎竊惟
===
今日值
至聖尊親孝養之朝固宜法周王視學而養國
老養庶老以大推恩之化也而翹跂俟之
閱歲未聞蓋惟曰屈萬乘之尊乃以事耄
耋之叟而無益於齒爵之等且於文爲繁
飾於今爲無據耳然禮有會而通之者寧
可詘其迂而弗之言歟自今觀之冕而總
干袒而割牲誠過矣然適東序而一奠於
先老遂設三老五更之席位而明象焉將
punctuated:
復合祀之禮者，甚有關於昭事之原，而於我皇上郊祀之大典，不爲已精而愈精也耶？
夫視學古矣，而養老之義，則於經爲尤著。《禮》言適學而有設饌省醴之具，《詩》歌《行葦》而有酌斗介耇之儀，明帝中主，而亦有臨雍拜饗之詔。是故養老也者，聖王所以正父子之敘，明長幼之節，而永敦齒讓之德，豈非彬彬然敦孝弟之實者乎？竊惟今日值至聖尊親孝養之朝，固宜法周王視學而養國老、養庶老，以大推恩之化也。而翹跂俟之，閱歲未聞，蓋惟曰屈萬乘之尊，乃以事耄耋之叟，而無益於齒爵之等，且於文爲繁飾，於今爲無據耳。然禮有會而通之者，寧可詘其迂而弗之言歟？自今觀之，冕而總干，袒而割牲，誠過矣；然適東序而一奠於先老，遂設三老五更之席位而明象焉，將
translation_en:
… restoring the rite of joint sacrifice is deeply connected to the fundamental principles of reverently serving Heaven, and with respect to our Sovereign's grand ceremonial of the suburban sacrifices, would it not make what is already refined even more refined?

Now, inspecting the Imperial Academy is an ancient practice, and the meaning of nourishing the aged is especially prominent in the Classics. The Book of Rites speaks of going to the school and making preparations for setting out food and inspecting the sweet wine; the Book of Odes sings in "Wayside Reeds" (Xingwei) of the ceremony of pouring from a large dipper to assist the aged; and Emperor Ming of the Han, though a ruler of middling caliber, also issued an edict on visiting the Imperial Academy (Biyong) to bow and offer a banquet. Therefore, nourishing the aged is the means by which sage kings rectify the order between father and son, clarify the distinctions between elder and younger, and perpetually cultivate the virtue of yielding to seniority. Is this not a resplendent way of cultivating the substance of filial piety and fraternal submission?

I humbly reflect that today we encounter a court where the Most Sage Sovereign honors his parents with filial nourishment; it is certainly fitting to model ourselves on the Zhou kings in inspecting the schools to nourish the elders of the state and the elders of the common people, thereby greatly expanding the transforming influence of extending grace. Yet people have stood on tiptoe waiting for this, and as the years pass nothing has been heard of it. This is surely only because some say that bending the dignity of the Lord of Ten Thousand Chariots to serve octogenarian and nonagenarian old men is of no benefit to the gradations of age and rank, and furthermore is overly ornate in form and lacks any basis in present practice. Yet in ritual there are principles that can be synthesized and adapted—how could one dismiss this as impractical and refuse to speak of it? Viewed from the standpoint of the present day, wearing the ceremonial cap while holding the shield, and baring the arm to carve the sacrificial victim, would indeed be excessive. However, if the Emperor were to proceed to the Eastern Hall (Dongxu), offer a single libation to the Former Elders, and thereupon set out the mats and seats for the Three Elders (Sanlao) and Five Experienced Men (Wugeng) to clearly display their symbolic model, would there…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
無有師傅之可尊者乎執醬而饋執爵而
酳誠泰矣然陳管象而一告以樂闋遂命
公侯伯子男以反養而終仁焉將無耆幼
之可序者乎且夫
兩宮承顏
聖孝誠備物也而由此以推太學虞庠之養俾
羣老皆得蒙肉帛焉可乎
兩宮徽號
聖孝誠備文也而由此以推太學高年之爵俾
===
子弟皆知有父母焉可乎然則行養老之
禮者甚有關於錫極之要而於我
皇上視學之大典不爲已盛而愈盛也耶於戲
此之謂
格天之至仁此之謂
法聖之達孝而愚生鋪張揚摧以爲
聖天子贊議無出於此者也雖然
仁與
孝一理也
punctuated: 無有師傅之可尊者乎？執醬而饋、執爵而酳，誠泰矣；然陳《管》《象》而一告以樂闋，遂命公、侯、伯、子、男以反養而終仁焉，將無耆幼之可序者乎？且夫兩宮承顏，聖孝誠備物也，而由此以推太學虞庠之養，俾羣老皆得蒙肉帛焉，可乎？兩宮徽號，聖孝誠備文也，而由此以推太學高年之爵，俾子弟皆知有父母焉，可乎？然則行養老之禮者，甚有關於錫極之要，而於我皇上視學之大典，不爲已盛而愈盛也耶？於戲！此之謂格天之至仁，此之謂法聖之達孝，而愚生鋪張揚摧，以爲聖天子贊議，無出於此者也。雖然，仁與孝一理也，
translation_en: …there not be Preceptors and Tutors worthy of being honored? For the ruler personally to hold the sauce and offer food, or hold the goblet for rinsing the mouth after the meal, is indeed excessive; yet if we set forth the flute music of the "Elephant" dance and once announce the conclusion of the music, and thereupon command the dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons to return to their domains to practice the nourishing of the aged and thereby bring benevolence to completion, would there not be an ordering of elders and youths? Moreover, in attending with pleased countenance upon the Two Palaces [the Empresses Dowager], His Sacred Filiality has truly provided all material offerings in full; and to extend this to the nourishing of the aged in the Imperial University and the local schools on the model of the Yu dynasty, so that all the elders may receive meat and silk—would this not be fitting? In conferring honorific titles upon the Two Palaces, His Sacred Filiality has truly perfected the ceremonial forms; and to extend this to the bestowal of honorary ranks upon those of advanced years in the Imperial University, so that all younger men may know how to honor their own fathers and mothers—would this not be fitting? If so, then performing the rite of nourishing the aged is deeply connected to the essential principle of bestowing the Supreme Standard upon the people; and as for the grand ceremony of Our August Emperor's inspection of the Imperial University, would it not make what is already flourishing flourish all the more? Alas! This is what is called the ultimate benevolence that reaches Heaven; this is what is called the universal filial piety that models itself on the Sages. What this foolish student has elaborated and set forth to offer in support of the Sacred Son of Heaven's deliberations goes no further than this. Even so, benevolence and filial piety are one and the same principle,…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天與
親一氣也事天與事親一道也未有孝德備而
仁有弗至亦未有親心悅豫而天心弗爲
之克享者也我
皇上純孝天植
至仁性成而又敬
天法
祖講學親賢
德日茂而
===
化日隆將見合祀於郊必有若鳳皇降龜龍假
風雨節寒暑時凡休祥之應出焉養老於
學必有若鄉里有齒老窮不遺强不犯弱
衆不暴寡凡泰和之象徵焉愚何幸躬逢
其盛
第二問
朱用光
同考試官教諭田批吏治之不古誠急於精
核之爲要此作經畫明確可行誠知務之言也
punctuated:
天與親一氣也，事天與事親一道也。未有孝德備而仁有弗至，亦未有親心悅豫而天心弗爲之克享者也。我皇上純孝天植，至仁性成，而又敬天法祖，講學親賢，德日茂而化日隆。將見合祀於郊，必有若鳳皇降、龜龍假，風雨節、寒暑時，凡休祥之應出焉；養老於學，必有若鄉里有齒、老窮不遺，强不犯弱、衆不暴寡，凡泰和之象徵焉。愚何幸躬逢其盛！

第二問
朱用光
同考試官教諭田批：吏治之不古，誠急於精核之爲要。此作經畫明確可行，誠知務之言也，
translation_en:
…Heaven and parents share a single vital force (qi), and serving Heaven and serving one's parents follow a single Way. Never has filial virtue been complete while benevolence failed to reach perfection, nor have the hearts of one's parents ever been joyful and content without the mind of Heaven being able to accept one's offerings in turn. Our August Emperor's pure filial piety is implanted by Heaven, and his supreme benevolence is formed by nature. Moreover, he reveres Heaven and models himself on the Ancestors, expounds upon learning and draws close to the worthy, so that his virtue grows more flourishing by the day and his transformative influence becomes ever more grand. We shall soon see that when joint sacrifices are offered in the suburban altar, there will surely be auspicious responses of every kind appearing—such as phoenixes descending, divine tortoises and dragons arriving, winds and rains keeping due measure, and cold and heat coming in their proper seasons; and when the aged are nourished in the Imperial University, there will surely be signs of supreme harmony of every kind manifested—such as seniority being respected in the villages, the aged and destitute not being neglected, the strong not infringing upon the weak, and the many not bullying the few. How fortunate am I, ignorant student that I am, to witness such flourishing magnificence in person!

Second Question
Zhu Yongguang 朱用光
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Tian comments: When official governance falls short of antiquity, what is most urgent is indeed to make precise verification the essential priority. The plans laid out in this essay are clear, definite, and practicable—truly the words of one who understands practical affairs; …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宜錄
考試官敎諭林批明通治體
考試官敎諭吳批議論詳核
論治體者貴率袒而莫大乎正紀綱稽治
功者貴飭吏而莫大乎振風化夫天下患
無治人不患無治法不患人之不奉法患
張法之無據而風動之無機是故隆替之
運因乎漸勤倦之氣乗乎習播而脩之體
斯立鼓而舞之功斯揚畫而壹之志斯寧
===
變而裁之化斯順此其興滯起敝之略類
非優游玩愒者之所能辦而亦豈能外
祖宗之成法以别求致理之方舍人臣之常憲
而過爲督責之令也哉要在正紀綱以整
齊於上振風化以維持於下夫然故出之
也瓴建加之也草偃人臣有奉法脩職之
忠而
國家收考成覈實之效寧不煕煕然
太平盛事耶愚請述前王之芳轍誦
punctuated:
宜錄。
考試官敎諭林批：明通治體。
考試官敎諭吳批：議論詳核。
論治體者，貴率袒而莫大乎正紀綱；稽治功者，貴飭吏而莫大乎振風化。夫天下患無治人，不患無治法；不患人之不奉法，患張法之無據，而風動之無機。是故隆替之運因乎漸，勤倦之氣乗乎習。播而脩之，體斯立；鼓而舞之，功斯揚；畫而壹之，志斯寧；變而裁之，化斯順。此其興滯起敝之略，類非優游玩愒者之所能辦，而亦豈能外祖宗之成法以别求致理之方，舍人臣之常憲而過爲督責之令也哉？要在正紀綱以整齊於上，振風化以維持於下。夫然，故出之也瓴建，加之也草偃；人臣有奉法脩職之忠，而國家收考成覈實之效，寧不煕煕然太平盛事耶？愚請述前王之芳轍，誦
translation_en:
… It is worthy of inclusion in the record.

Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: Clear and conversant with the principles of governance.

Examiner and Instructor Wu comments: The arguments are detailed and well-verified.

Those who discuss the structure of governance value following the imperial ancestors [? 袒 for 祖], yet nothing is greater than rectifying the fundamental laws and discipline; those who examine the achievements of governance value disciplining officials, yet nothing is greater than revitalizing moral customs and transformation. Now, the Empire suffers from a lack of men who can govern, not from a lack of laws for governance; it does not suffer from men failing to observe the laws, but from the lack of a firm basis in extending the laws and the lack of a vital mechanism for inspiring transformation like the wind. Therefore, the cycle of flourishing and decline comes about gradually, and the spirit of diligence or laxity rides upon habit. Broadcast and cultivate them, and the structure of governance is thereby established; rouse and inspire them, and achievements are thereby exalted; make them uniform and unified, and minds are thereby settled; adapt and regulate them, and moral transformation thereby flows smoothly. Such strategies for reviving what is stagnant and rectifying what is decayed are generally not what those who indulge in leisurely neglect and waste time can manage. Yet how could one go outside the established laws of the Imperial Ancestors to seek elsewhere a method for bringing about order, or abandon the constant statutes for subjects and excessively issue orders of harsh supervision and责 (reproof)? The key lies in rectifying the fundamental laws and discipline to bring order from above, and revitalizing moral customs to sustain things from below. When this is so, issuing commands is like pouring water from a rooftop jar, and applying them to the people is like the wind bending the grass. Subjects will possess the loyalty of observing the laws and fulfilling their duties, while the State will reap the results of evaluating performance and verifying realities—would this not be a harmonious and magnificent affair of Great Peace? Humbly I beg to recount the fragrant tracks of former kings, recite …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
昭代之徽猷以及近日之弊竇而借前箸規
救時之長筭可乎夫虞廷欽亮禹臯賛屢
省之謨成周董訓旦奭儼正色之師維其
時庶政和而萬國寧旣醉歌而鳧鷖應郁
郁乎盛也迺其百工之熙必率作而後興
事惇大之裕必明作而後有功則勵精之
效虞周以來記之矣漢宣帝以綜核名實
之權行信賞必罰之令海內肅清姦宄屏
息黠虜消甘泉之警强藩泯吳濞之驕吏
===
皆廉明强幹之材民享安田樂里之慶視
賈生之所流涕太息者無一有焉崔寔稱
其筭計見效優於孝文誠哉非憤世之論
也若文帝雖云躬脩玄默其實精通黃老
觀其甫卽代邸而夜拜宋昌蠲除肉刑而
笞率致死殺使之罪當誅則法不貸於元
舅窺器之僇難逭則恩不假於季昆若賈
生之所謂髖髀斧斤者亦未始不嘗試焉
崔寔稱其以嚴致平非以寬致平卓哉其
punctuated: 昭代之徽猷，以及近日之弊竇，而借前箸規救時之長筭，可乎？夫虞廷欽亮，禹、臯賛屢省之謨；成周董訓，旦、奭儼正色之師。維其時，庶政和而萬國寧，《旣醉》歌而《鳧鷖》應，郁郁乎盛也！迺其百工之熙，必率作而後興事；惇大之裕，必明作而後有功。則勵精之效，虞、周以來記之矣。漢宣帝以綜核名實之權，行信賞必罰之令，海內肅清，姦宄屏息，黠虜消甘泉之警，强藩泯吳濞之驕，吏皆廉明强幹之材，民享安田樂里之慶，視賈生之所流涕太息者，無一有焉。崔寔稱其筭計見效優於孝文，誠哉非憤世之論也！若文帝雖云躬脩玄默，其實精通黃老。觀其甫卽代邸而夜拜宋昌，蠲除肉刑而笞率致死；殺使之罪當誅，則法不貸於元舅；窺器之僇難逭，則恩不假於季昆。若賈生之所謂「髖髀斧斤」者，亦未始不嘗試焉。崔寔稱其「以嚴致平，非以寬致平」，卓哉其…
translation_en: …the splendid counsels of our Illustrious Dynasty, as well as the abuses of recent days, and borrow the chopsticks in front of us to plan long-term strategies for rescuing the times—may I? Now, in the court of Yu [Shun], where reverence and brightness prevailed, Yu and Gao Yao assisted with counsels of frequent inspection; in the era of Accomplished Zhou, which supervised and instructed, Dan [the Duke of Zhou] and Shi [the Duke of Shao] stood in awe-inspiring rectitude as preceptors. At those times, the numerous affairs of government were harmonious and the myriad states were at peace; the ode "Already Drunk" (Jizui) was sung and "Wild Ducks" (Fuyi) responded—how magnificently flourishing! Yet for the hundred officials to thrive, their leaders had to take the initiative before enterprises could rise; for generous magnanimity to be abundant, they had to act with clear discernment before merit could be achieved. Thus the efficacy of vigorous diligence has been recorded ever since Yu and Zhou. Emperor Xuan of Han, wielding the authority of comprehensively verifying names and realities, enforced commands of trustworthy rewards and certain punishments. Within the seas all was purged and clear, wicked traitors held their breath, the crafty caitiffs ceased their alarms at Ganquan, and powerful feudatories extinguished the arrogance of a Wu Pi. Officials were all men of incorruptible, perceptive, strong, and capable talent, while the people enjoyed the blessing of peaceful fields and happy villages. Compared to the things over which Master Jia [Jia Yi] had shed tears and heaved deep sighs, not a single one remained. Cui Shi praised his calculations and visible results as superior to those of the Filial Emperor Wen—truly, this was no mere cynical discourse! As for Emperor Wen, although he was said to personally cultivate mysterious silence, in reality he was thoroughly versed in the teachings of Huang-Lao. Observe how, having just arrived at the Dai residence, he appointed Song Chang by night; and when he abolished corporal mutilation, thebastinado routinely resulted in death. When the crime of killing an envoy warranted execution, the law did not spare his chief maternal uncle [Bo Zhao]; when the punishment for coveting the imperial regalia could hardly be escaped, grace was not extended to his younger brother [Liu Chang, King of Huainan]. What Master Jia called "applying the hatchet and axe to hipbones and femurs" was something he had by no means failed to try out. When Cui Shi praised him as "achieving peace through strictness, not achieving peace through leniency," how eminent was his…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
知文帝之深也唐太宗加意刺史而書其
姓名於御座貞觀之治赫然爲創業之宗
玄宗留心縣令而試理人策於內殿開元
之治煥乎爲中興之烈於戲歷稽往籍英
辟碩輔何嘗有廢精核之能而程功實之
課者哉洪惟我
太祖稽古建官樹師保置六卿體統相維而一
制命於
天子
===
成祖纂服肯構建
兩京控列省內外相率而一受法於
朝廷
列聖嗣興靡不飭弘規而脩紀法凡以稽實政
而勵臣工其載在
會典者則銓注有式舉刺有式考察有式所
以懸之象魏而示趨事赴功之準者明且
備矣臣子之所目屬而心誌之矣而又部
院有記科臣有記
punctuated: 知文帝之深也。唐太宗加意刺史，而書其姓名於御座，貞觀之治，赫然爲創業之宗；玄宗留心縣令，而試理人策於內殿，開元之治，煥乎爲中興之烈。於戲！歷稽往籍，英辟碩輔，何嘗有廢精核之能，而程功實之課者哉！洪惟我太祖稽古建官，樹師保，置六卿，體統相維，而一制命於天子；成祖纂服肯構，建兩京，控列省，內外相率，而一受法於朝廷。列聖嗣興，靡不飭弘規而脩紀法，凡以稽實政而勵臣工。其載在《會典》者，則銓注有式，舉刺有式，考察有式，所以懸之象魏，而示趨事赴功之準者，明且備矣，臣子之所目屬而心誌之矣。而又部院有記，科臣有記，
translation_en:
… deeply indeed did he understand Emperor Wen! Emperor Taizong of the Tang paid special heed to the Regional Inspectors (cishi) and inscribed their names upon his imperial screen; thus the governance of the Zhenguan era shone forth as the model for founding a dynasty. Emperor Xuanzong devoted close attention to the District Magistrates (xianling) and tested them with policy questions on governing the people in the inner palace; thus the governance of the Kaiyuan era blazed brightly as the glory of a dynastic restoration. Alas! Looking throughout past records, among heroic rulers and great ministers, when did they ever dispense with the capacity for meticulous verification or the assessment of actual achievements?

Reflecting deeply upon our Grand Progenitor (Taizu), he examined antiquity to establish offices, setting up the Grand Preceptors and Grand Guardians and instituting the Six Ministers; the hierarchical system held together in mutual support, while all commands were determined solely by the Son of Heaven. Our Accomplished Progenitor (Chengzu) succeeded to the realm and carried forward the foundational work, establishing the Two Capitals and controlling the various provinces; the inner and outer administrations led one another forward, while all received their laws solely from the imperial court. The successive sacred emperors rose in turn, none failing to consolidate the grand regulations and maintain discipline and law—all in order to verify actual governance and encourage the officials. As for what is recorded in the Collected Statutes (Huidian), there are fixed forms for selection and appointment, fixed forms for recommendation and impeachment, and fixed forms for personnel evaluation. The means by which these are hung from the palace gates to display the standards for hastening to service and achieving merit are clear and complete; they are what officials fix their eyes upon and engrave in their hearts. Moreover, the Ministries and the Censorate keep records, the Supervising Secretaries keep records, …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
內閣有記所以具之方策而示率作屢省之
要者亦明且備矣亦臣子之所目屬而心
誌之矣
奕世以來吏侁侁奉職而治亦班班可紀說
者謂
國初之法井而嚴其吏恪其治察其民渾以
堅宣成之法順而齊其吏脩其治淳其民
安以樸弘治之法謹而敘其吏舒其治昌
其民泰以樂嘉靖之法綜而核其吏辨其
===
治肅其民循分而慕義於戲休哉盖二百
年來海內乂安
昭代之盛庶幾乎虞周媲隆矣恬熈日久吏
治少弛功緒鮮稽我
穆考煥然有作新之詔而惜乎未見德化之成
肆我
皇上英睿紹圖勵精求治屢降
璽書申明令甲者非別有更絃易轍之舉也皆
先朝已著之成憲取其因循廢閣者而振勵之
punctuated:
內閣有記，所以具之方策而示率作屢省之要者，亦明且備矣，亦臣子之所目屬而心誌之矣。
奕世以來，吏侁侁奉職而治，亦班班可紀。說者謂國初之法井而嚴，其吏恪，其治察，其民渾以堅；宣、成之法順而齊，其吏脩，其治淳，其民安以樸；弘治之法謹而敘，其吏舒，其治昌，其民泰以樂；嘉靖之法綜而核，其吏辨，其治肅，其民循分而慕義。於戲休哉！盖二百年來，海內乂安，昭代之盛，庶幾乎虞、周媲隆矣。恬熈日久，吏治少弛，功緒鮮稽。我穆考煥然有作新之詔，而惜乎未見德化之成。肆我皇上英睿紹圖，勵精求治。屢降璽書，申明令甲者，非別有更絃易轍之舉也，皆先朝已著之成憲，取其因循廢閣者而振勵之
translation_en:
…and the Grand Secretariat has its records. The means by which these are set forth on bamboo and wood tablets to demonstrate the essentials of leading in initiative and making frequent inspections are likewise clear and complete, and are likewise what officials and subjects fix their eyes upon and engrave in their hearts.

For generations running, officials in great numbers have faithfully discharged their duties in governance, and their achievements can be clearly chronicled one by one. Commentators say that the laws at the founding of the dynasty were orderly and strict: its officials were reverent, its governance was discerning, and its people were simple and steadfast. The laws of the Xuande (1426–1435) and Chenghua (1465–1487) eras were harmonious and uniform: their officials were cultivated, their governance was pure, and their people were peaceful and unadorned. The laws of the Hongzhi era (1488–1505) were prudent and well-ordered: its officials were unhurried, its governance was flourishing, and its people were tranquil and joyful. The laws of the Jiajing era (1522–1566) were comprehensive and exacting: its officials were discriminating, its governance was solemn, and its people abided by their lot and admired righteousness. Oh, how magnificent! Indeed, for two hundred years all within the seas has been peaceful and secure, and the flourishing of our illustrious dynasty nearly rivals the glory of Yu [Shun] and the Zhou.

Yet as peace and tranquility lasted long, administrative governance slackened somewhat, and actual accomplishments were rarely verified. Our Deceased Imperial Father Muzong (the Longqing Emperor, r. 1567–1572) brilliantly issued edicts of renewal, yet regrettably did not live to see the completion of his moral transformation. Now His Majesty the Emperor, with heroic wisdom, has succeeded to the imperial enterprise and exerts his spirit to seek good governance. That he has repeatedly sent down imperial letters under the玺 seal to reiterate the primary statutes is not a move to restring the instrument or change the tracks; rather, these are all established constitutions already set forth by previous reigns, taking what had been neglected and shelved through routine complacency and rousing them into vigor…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也昔魏相條奏漢家之故事數獻晁賈之
遺言其意不猶是歟屢奉
明旨申勅有司者非別有舉毛束溼之病也皆
昔臣已試之成規取其怠緩悅從者而提
撕之也昔漢宣責吏之不奉詔書責計簿
之徒具空文其意不猶是歟於戲是則所
謂率
祖也已是則所謂飭吏也已宜乎治體日恢治
功日茂而稍慰
===
主上宵旰閔元元至意也夷考其實迺有大謬
不然者司農閱籍司會奏籌歲多逋負觀
之壤賦尚有未盡盈也暵溢時作千里枵
罄環貸迭飼觀之戶口尚有未盡殷也民
性漸漓而寡廉鮮恥者日議於辟兵戎文
具而建牙飲博者日耗於廩武斷睚眦於
井閭窮盜剽禦於大都矯虔蓋有未遜矣
編民不滿於尺籍窮邨莽望於空煙流移
蓋有未復矣夫上之人責望如彼其殷而
punctuated: 也。昔魏相條奏漢家之故事，數獻晁、賈之遺言，其意不猶是歟？屢奉明旨申勅有司者，非別有舉毛束溼之病也，皆昔臣已試之成規，取其怠緩悅從者而提撕之也。昔漢宣責吏之不奉詔書，責計簿之徒具空文，其意不猶是歟？於戲！是則所謂率祖也已，是則所謂飭吏也已。宜乎治體日恢，治功日茂，而稍慰主上宵旰閔元元至意也。夷考其實，迺有大謬不然者：司農閱籍，司會奏籌，歲多逋負，觀之壤賦，尚有未盡盈也；暵溢時作，千里枵罄，環貸迭飼，觀之戶口，尚有未盡殷也；民性漸漓，而寡廉鮮恥者日議於辟；兵戎文具，而建牙飲博者日耗於廩；武斷睚眦於井閭，窮盜剽禦於大都，矯虔蓋有未遜矣；編民不滿於尺籍，窮邨莽望於空煙，流移蓋有未復矣。夫上之人責望如彼其殷，而
translation_en:
… In antiquity, Wei Xiang 魏相 submitted itemized memorials on the precedents of the Han house and repeatedly presented the surviving words of Chao Cuo 晁錯 and Jia Yi 賈誼; was his intent not just like this? That we have repeatedly received explicit imperial decrees sternly instructing the authorities is not because there is some other fault of petty hair-splitting or harsh urgency; rather, these are all established regulations already tested by former ministers, taking those in which officials have grown lax, dilatory, or merely compliant, and rousing them to attention. In antiquity, Emperor Xuan of Han 漢宣帝 rebuked officials for failing to carry out imperial edicts and criticized accounting registers for being mere empty words; was his intent not just like this? Alas! This is truly what is meant by following the ancestors; this is truly what is meant by disciplining the officials. It ought to follow that the substance of governance expands daily and the achievements of rule flourish daily, bringing some comfort to the Sovereign's earnest intention of laboring from dawn till dusk in compassion for the common people.

Yet when we calmly examine the reality, we find it to be gravely contrary to this: when the Minister of Revenue inspects the registers and the Chief Accountant presents the tallies, every year there are many arrears in taxes—judging by the land revenues, they are not yet completely full. Droughts and floods occur from time to time, leaving a thousand li barren and depleted, with people borrowing in circles and feeding one another in turn—judging by the registered households and population, they are not yet completely prosperous. The people's nature gradually grows thin and澆 [degenerate], and those lacking integrity and a sense of shame are daily adjudicated under the penal laws; military preparations are mere formalities on paper, while commanders who set up banners indulge in drinking and gambling, daily depleting the state granaries. Tyrannical bullies glare in hostility in the neighborhoods and villages, while desperate bandits plunder and rob in the great cities—the defiant and rapacious have not yet yielded in submission. The registered commoners do not fill out the census rosters, and impoverished villages stretch out in overgrown weeds with empty chimneys—the displaced and wandering have not yet returned. Now, when those above demand and expect so earnestly like that, while…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
下之人報效如此其略凡爲臣子者名繫
仕籍身膺爵祿而又耳熟
德音手握尺符豈不慨然以豪傑忠良自許而
忍貽
主上之憂敢干瘝曠之僇哉毋亦所以張治法
而風治人者尚有所可念也愚故欲以正
紀綱振風化之說進焉夫
朝著四方之所承風者也而監司又百僚之
所具瞻而奉
===
寵靈者也綱之不攝而欲紀之有條也不亦難
乎愚謂紀綱之正其說有二夫議論滋多
成功愈尠處華堂而譚操舟者揚帆之狀
捩柁之神聽之駸駸然臨淵而挐之舲則
長年三老目攝咲之矣今之建言何以異
此同一事也而條陳互異則頒四方者必
牴牾而難行同一法也而操縱殊科則持
三尺者必掣肘而難運繼自今請無以昌
論扇繁文而凡有興革必熟計長便始下
punctuated: 下之人報效如此其略。凡爲臣子者，名繫仕籍，身膺爵祿，而又耳熟德音，手握尺符，豈不慨然以豪傑忠良自許，而忍貽主上之憂，敢干瘝曠之僇哉？毋亦所以張治法而風治人者，尚有所可念也。愚故欲以正紀綱、振風化之說進焉。夫朝著，四方之所承風者也；而監司，又百僚之所具瞻而奉寵靈者也。綱之不攝，而欲紀之有條也，不亦難乎？愚謂紀綱之正，其說有二：夫議論滋多，成功愈尠。處華堂而譚操舟者，揚帆之狀、捩柁之神，聽之駸駸然；臨淵而挐之舲，則長年三老目攝咲之矣。今之建言，何以異此？同一事也，而條陳互異，則頒四方者必牴牾而難行；同一法也，而操縱殊科，則持三尺者必掣肘而難運。繼自今，請無以昌論扇繁文，而凡有興革，必熟計長便，始下
translation_en:
… those below render service in return so perfunctorily. Among all who serve as ministers and subjects, their names are inscribed on the roster of officials and their persons enjoy noble rank and emolument; moreover, their ears are familiar with the Sovereign's virtuous words, and their hands hold the foot-long tallies of authority. How could they not earnestly regard themselves as heroic and loyal men, or bear to bequeath anxiety to the Sovereign Above and dare to incur the punishment for negligence and dereliction of duty? Is it not rather that there is still something worthy of consideration in the means by which the laws of governance are extended and the men who govern are inspired? I therefore wish to advance a proposal for rectifying the overarching principles and subsidiary regulations of government and revitalizing moral transformation through custom.

Now, the court is that from which the four quarters take their cue; and the Surveillance Commissioners and provincial intendants are in turn those toward whom the hundred officials all look up and through whom they receive the imperial favor and majesty. If the headrope of a net is not drawn taut, yet one wishes its smaller meshes to be in order, is that not difficult indeed?

In my humble view, rectifying the overarching principles and subsidiary regulations involves two points. First, the more deliberations and arguments proliferate, the rarer actual achievements become. When someone sitting in a splendid hall talks of handling a boat—describing the manner of hoisting the sail and the miraculous skill of turning the rudder—to listen to him, it sounds brisk and convincing; yet when he approaches the deep water and takes hold of the skiff, the veteran helmsmen and boatswains will exchange glances and laugh at him. How are the proposals submitted today any different from this? Concerning one and the same matter, the itemized memorials differ from one another, so that what is promulgated to the four quarters is bound to be contradictory and difficult to carry out; concerning one and the same law, its application and relaxation follow different standards, so that those who uphold the three-foot statutory code are bound to be hampered at every turn and find it hard to operate. From now on, I beg that we cease stirring up elaborate paperwork with grandiloquent discussions, and that whenever there is a measure to be instituted or abolished, its long-term convenience must be thoroughly weighed before it is sent down to …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
郡國庶觀聽一而措置宜此簡議論之綱
一也指臂相運氣之通安在乎形之齊而
方圓局命則枘鑿必不入矣今或取一邑
之良法而欲槩行於列郡則因民襲土者
其勢格徒煩規畫爾或責一令之集事而
先定之以條格則相宜權機者其智沮姑
應期會爾繼自今請無問其體式奚若約
束奚若而惟其足以惠吾民應吾實而不
違吾程否則吾不貸吾法庶謀力展而積
===
累便此壹法令之綱二也於戲紀綱旣正
則神氣自張乃闒茸叨憤拘文鮮奮之徒
咸不足以廑執事之憂而唐之八計聽吏
漢之居部九歲者其法實與
今日相會通矣夫功名之會人情所願趨也
伐盤錯而挽江河又勇智者之所不得輒
施也風之不易而欲化之速成也不亦難
乎愚謂風化之振其說亦有二夫玉卮華
而不酻雕龍飾而不雨然而晶光飛飾之
punctuated:
郡國，庶觀聽一而措置宜，此簡議論之綱一也。指臂相運，氣之通安在乎形之齊？而方圓局命，則枘鑿必不入矣。今或取一邑之良法而欲槩行於列郡，則因民襲土者其勢格，徒煩規畫爾；或責一令之集事而先定之以條格，則相宜權機者其智沮，姑應期會爾。繼自今，請無問其體式奚若、約束奚若，而惟其足以惠吾民、應吾實而不違吾程，否則吾不貸吾法，庶謀力展而積累便，此壹法令之綱二也。於戲！紀綱旣正，則神氣自張，乃闒茸叨憤、拘文鮮奮之徒，咸不足以廑執事之憂，而唐之八計聽吏、漢之居部九歲者，其法實與今日相會通矣。

夫功名之會，人情所願趨也；伐盤錯而挽江河，又勇智者之所不得輒施也。風之不易而欲化之速成也，不亦難乎？愚謂風化之振，其說亦有二：夫玉卮華而不酻，雕龍飾而不雨，然而晶光飛飾之
translation_en:
…the commanderies and principalities, so that public perception will be unified and administrative measures fitting. This—simplifying policy discussions—is the first fundamental principle.

When fingers and arms move in coordination, how does the flow of vital energy depend on uniformity of physical shape? Yet if square and round are rigidly prescribed, then tenon and mortise will surely fail to fit together. Nowadays, if one takes a sound measure from a single district and wishes to apply it uniformly across all prefectures, then those who adapt to the people and follow local conditions find their circumstances obstructed, and it merely adds to the trouble of planning. Or if one demands that a single magistrate accomplish a task while predetermining it with fixed regulations, then those who adjust to circumstances and weigh opportunities find their resourcefulness thwarted, and they merely go through the motions to meet deadlines and quotas. From now on, I beg that we do not ask what the formal format is or what the restrictive rules are, looking only to whether they suffice to benefit our people, correspond to our practical realities, and not violate our standards—and if they fail in this, we will not pardon them under our laws. Thus strategic efforts can be unfolded and cumulative achievements facilitated. This—unifying laws and ordinances—is the second fundamental principle.

Alas! Once discipline and fundamental order are rectified, the vital spirit will naturally expand. Then the base, greedy, and muddled [?], or those bound by the letter of the law who rarely rouse themselves to action, will all cease to warrant Your Excellency's concern; and the Tang system of assessing officials by the Eight Criteria, as well as the Han practice of keeping officials in their posts for nine years, will in their principles truly converge and harmonize with our present day.

Now, the opportunity for merit and fame is what human nature eagerly pursues; yet cutting through knotted roots and turning back great rivers are feats that even the brave and wise cannot readily perform. If the prevailing ethos is not changed, yet one wishes for transformation to be swiftly achieved, is that not difficult indeed? In my humble view, for reinvigorating the ethos and moral transformation, there are likewise two explanations. A jade goblet is resplendent yet cannot hold liquid without leaking [?]; a carved dragon is ornate yet cannot bring rain. Nevertheless, wherever their radiant gleam and flying ornaments…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所過其有不回波斯之價而動滕公之悅
者幾希今之士躐崇膴何以異此據所建
白則品式章幾微著而公私之蠹實積於
絲棼籍所計簿則訟牘清賦斂給而黔蒸
之瘵實蒙於蔀屋彼且聲騰於月旦薦列
於公車超然鴻舉於華要之津而民亦罔
然莫測斯人之父母於我何居也迺悃愊
撫摩之政反不若詡智鼓飾者之速化循
良安得不解體哉誠一反之斯功皐無所
===
逃狀而人自淬礪矣此敦名實之風一也
國有豪俠而後姦宄憑之以恣睢山有豺
豹而後狐貉依之以固穴今之逋賦山積
豈盡窮編之氓乎大率皆連阡陌而侵帑
藏者之囊橐案牘雲擁豈盡入井之孺乎
大半皆騁虓滑而主逋逃者之淵藪吏胥
相倚爲城社而莫暴其姦衣冠相齒爲耳
目而莫詰其狀一令之出一禁之申彼且
昂昂敢以其身爲嘗試之衝撼之稍不動
punctuated:
所過，其有不回波斯之價、而動滕公之悅者幾希！今之士躐崇膴，何以異此？據所建白，則品式章、幾微著，而公私之蠹實積於絲棼；籍所計簿，則訟牘清、賦斂給，而黔蒸之瘵實蒙於蔀屋。彼且聲騰於月旦，薦列於公車，超然鴻舉於華要之津，而民亦罔然莫測斯人之父母於我何居也。迺悃愊撫摩之政，反不若詡智鼓飾者之速化，循良安得不解體哉？誠一反之，斯功皐無所逃狀，而人自淬礪矣。此敦名實之風一也。
國有豪俠，而後姦宄憑之以恣睢；山有豺豹，而後狐貉依之以固穴。今之逋賦山積，豈盡窮編之氓乎？大率皆連阡陌而侵帑藏者之囊橐；案牘雲擁，豈盡入井之孺乎？大半皆騁虓滑而主逋逃者之淵藪。吏胥相倚爲城社，而莫暴其姦；衣冠相齒爲耳目，而莫詰其狀。一令之出，一禁之申，彼且昂昂敢以其身爲嘗試之衝；撼之稍不動，
translation_en:
…passes by, rare indeed are those who would not reverse a Persian merchant's appraisal or stir the delight of Duke Teng! When the scholars of today leap into lofty and lucrative posts, how are they any different from this? Looking at the proposals they submit, the regulations are resplendent and the subtlest details are made manifest, yet in reality the pests of public and private life accumulate in a tangled skein; consulting the account books they compile, the litigation dockets are cleared and tax revenues are fully supplied, yet in reality the suffering of the common folk is shrouded beneath their thatched roofs. Meanwhile, their reputations soar in monthly appraisals, their recommendations line the official carriages, and they rise aloft like wild geese to the fords of illustrious and vital offices—while the people remain utterly bewildered, unable to fathom in what way such a man has acted as a father and mother to them. When sincere, unpretentious, and nurturing governance proves less conducive to rapid advancement than boasting of cleverness and drumming up superficial display, how can upright and virtuous officials not lose heart? If we truly reverse this trend, then merits and offenses will have no way to escape exposure, and men will naturally temper and sharpen themselves. This is the first way to cultivate the custom of matching name with reality.

Only when a state harbors powerful magnates do villains and traitors rely on them to act with unbridled arrogance; only when a mountain holds jackals and leopards do foxes and badgers depend on them to secure their dens. Today, tax arrears pile up like mountains—are they all owed by destitute registered commoners? For the most part, they fill the moneybags of those who join fields across paths and ridges and encroach upon the state treasury. Legal case files gather like clouds—do they all concern innocent children about to fall into a well? More than half are the havens of those who indulge in fierce cunning and harbor fugitives. Subaltern clerks and runners lean on them as city walls and altars of the soil, so that no one exposes their villainy; capped and gowned gentry rank themselves alongside them as ears and eyes, so that no one interrogates their conduct. Whenever a single order is issued or a single prohibition is proclaimed, they brazenly dare to throw themselves forward as the vanguard to test the authorities; if shaken and they barely budge,…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而觀望者螽然騖矣又能煽簧鼓之技而
聚瑜璧之蠅俾在位者凜垂堂之誡而包
荒於傳舍之謀夫荆棘不剪芝蘭賊也鏌
耶不割鉛刀同也誠於若輩壹繩剷之何
患足國安民之政有不沛然而風行也耶
此除姦豪之風二也於戲風化既振則治
運聿新乃競名襲奇采名凅璧之徒何足
以廑執事之慮而漢以六條察二千石唐
以五術省民風者其法實與
===
今日相發明矣詩曰不愆不忘率由舊章又
曰勉勉我王綱紀四方周書曰戒爾卿士
功崇惟志業廣惟勤而漢儒亦曰移風易
俗使天下回心而嚮化此誠
今日率
祖而飭吏者所當前席進之也惟
聖君賢相留意亟圖焉而又課之以章奏厲之
以賞罰堅之如金石信之如四時百辟萬
方有不輻輳並進而媚于
punctuated:
而觀望者螽然騖矣。又能煽簧鼓之技，而聚瑜璧之蠅，俾在位者凜垂堂之誡，而包荒於傳舍之謀。夫荆棘不剪，芝蘭賊也；鏌耶不割，鉛刀同也。誠於若輩壹繩剷之，何患足國安民之政，有不沛然而風行也耶？此除姦豪之風，二也。

於戲！風化既振，則治運聿新，乃競名襲奇、采名凅璧之徒，何足以廑執事之慮？而漢以六條察二千石，唐以五術省民風者，其法實與今日相發明矣。《詩》曰：「不愆不忘，率由舊章。」又曰：「勉勉我王，綱紀四方。」《周書》曰：「戒爾卿士，功崇惟志，業廣惟勤。」而漢儒亦曰：「移風易俗，使天下回心而嚮化。」此誠今日率祖而飭吏者，所當前席進之也。惟聖君賢相留意亟圖焉，而又課之以章奏，厲之以賞罰，堅之如金石，信之如四時，百辟萬方，有不輻輳並進而媚于
translation_en:
…then the onlookers will swarm and run wild like locusts. Moreover, they are able to fan the flames of glib-tongued manipulation and gather like flies tarnishing flawless jade, causing those in office to tremble at the warning against sitting under the eaves of a hall, and to tolerate corruption out of a mindset of treating their offices as mere waystations. Now, if brambles and thorns are not pruned, they are the ruin of fragrant irises and orchids; if the Mo Ye sword does not cut, it is no different from a lead knife. If we truly apply the law uniformly to eradicate such people, what worry would there be that policies for enriching the state and pacifying the people would not sweep across the land like a torrent and the wind? This is the second point: eliminating the trend of treacherous magnates.

Alas! Once moral transformation is revitalized, the era of good governance will be renewed. How then could those who vie for fame, copy eccentricities, and fish for reputation with empty pretensions [?] be worth troubling the minds of you, the examiners? As for the Han dynasty inspecting Two-thousand-bushel Officials according to the Six Articles, and the Tang dynasty examining popular customs by means of the Five Methods, those institutions truly illuminate the needs of the present day! The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: "Neither erring nor forgetting, following the old statutes." It also says: "Ever diligent is our king, giving law and order to the four quarters." The Book of Zhou (Zhoushu) says: "Warn your ministers and gentlemen: high merit depends on aspiration, broad achievement depends on diligence." And a Han Confucian also said: "Transform customs and change habits, making all under Heaven turn their hearts toward moral transformation." This is truly what today's rulers and officials, in following the ancestors and rectifying the bureaucracy, ought to lean forward on their mats to advance. May the sacred sovereign and worthy chief councilors pay close attention and urgently plan for this, evaluating them through memorials, encouraging them with rewards and punishments, making commands as firm as metal and stone and as trustworthy as the four seasons—then among the hundred lords and ten thousand regions, could there be any who do not converge like spokes to a hub, advance together, and devote themselves in love to…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天子者否也若曰此狂辯爾則非愚之所敢聞
第三問
楊道南
同考試官敎諭黃批心正則學正探本論也且
辨析幾微示以趨向足破羣疑而挽世敎矣
同考試官敎諭徐批是作深切時弊錄之
考試官敎諭林批議論明悉有裨正學
考試官敎諭吳批是於心學有得者
甞謂異端之害道也易闢而吾儒之害道
===
也難攻害之見於學術者易知而害之隱
於心術者難測故欲明道者莫若正學而
欲正學者莫若正心夫弗戾經傳則聖賢
此學夫人亦此學他岐雜之而學始僞矣
然亦豈必離經畔道而後爲學之疵凡投
一時之好而厚貌深情炫奇飾異者皆僞
也弗漓天真則聖賢此心夫人亦此心已
私鑿之而心斯邪矣然亦豈必出檻紆籌
而後爲心之累凡有一念之動而不可以
punctuated:
天子者否也？若曰此狂辯爾，則非愚之所敢聞。

第三問
楊道南
同考試官敎諭黃批：心正則學正，探本論也。且辨析幾微，示以趨向，足破羣疑而挽世敎矣。
同考試官敎諭徐批：是作深切時弊，錄之。
考試官敎諭林批：議論明悉，有裨正學。
考試官敎諭吳批：是於心學有得者。

甞謂異端之害道也易闢，而吾儒之害道也難攻；害之見於學術者易知，而害之隱於心術者難測。故欲明道者莫若正學，而欲正學者莫若正心。夫弗戾經傳，則聖賢此學，夫人亦此學；他岐雜之，而學始僞矣。然亦豈必離經畔道，而後爲學之疵？凡投一時之好，而厚貌深情，炫奇飾異者，皆僞也。弗漓天真，則聖賢此心，夫人亦此心；已私鑿之，而心斯邪矣。然亦豈必出檻紆籌，而後爲心之累？凡有一念之動，而不可以
translation_en:
… the Son of Heaven? If one were to say that this is mere wild rhetoric, that is something I would not dare to accept.

Third Question
Yang Daonan 楊道南
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Huang 黃: "When the mind is rectified, learning is rectified—this is an argument that reaches the fundamental root. Moreover, it analyzes subtle intricacies and points out the proper direction, sufficient to dispel the doubts of the multitude and restore the teachings of the age."
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Xu 徐: "This piece cuts deeply into the ills of the time; record it."
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Lin 林: "The discussion is clear and thorough, beneficial to orthodox learning."
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Wu 吳: "This is someone who has attained insight into the learning of the mind (xinxue)."

I have held that the harm done to the Way by heterodox teachings is easy to refute, whereas the harm done to the Way by us Confucians is difficult to attack; the harm that manifests in scholarly methods is easy to recognize, whereas the harm that hides within the intentions of the mind is difficult to fathom. Therefore, for one who wishes to illuminate the Way, nothing is better than rectifying learning, and for one who wishes to rectify learning, nothing is better than rectifying the mind. Now, if one does not violate the Classics and commentaries, then the sages and worthies share this learning, and all people likewise share this learning; only when other diverging paths adulterate it does learning become false. Yet must one depart from the Classics and rebel against the Way before it counts as a flaw in learning? All who cater to the fashions of the moment, assuming a solemn countenance while harboring deep ulterior motives, showing off novelties and adorning themselves with eccentricities—all of this is falsehood. If one does not dilute one's heavenly genuineness, then the sages and worthies share this mind, and all people likewise share this mind; only when selfish desiresbore into it does the mind become depraved. Yet must one step across the threshold of transgression and contrive crooked schemes [?] before it counts as an encumbrance to the mind? Whenever a single thought stirs that cannot…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
盟天地質鬼神者悉邪也邪心萌故正學
裂正學裂故道統蝕隱微疑似之際識者
有深憂焉不此之咎而徒異端之尤惑也
甚矣執事策士而惓惓於崇正學以明道
統蓋扶世教淑人心之大機括也愚生繪
天測海何足以復明問雖然學術之誠偽
則甞聞之孔子矣古曰為己今曰為人是
也心術之邪正則甞聞之孟子矣為善為
舜為利為蹠是也一念之幾微而係終身
===
之造詣若之何其弗求道於學而求學於
心也夫道統始於堯舜後自周公傳之孔
子又自孔子傳之孟子匪耳提之匪面命
之以心授之也則孔孟所以演道真開來
學者蓋亦以心受之矣故古今語道統之
正者莫若孔孟語學術之正者亦莫若孔
孟而其語害道者則曰老佛曰楊墨夫老
佛楊墨其道何道其學何學而其為吾道
與學之害者其心何心為老氏之說者曰
punctuated:
盟天地、質鬼神者，悉邪也。邪心萌故正學裂，正學裂故道統蝕。隱微疑似之際，識者有深憂焉。不此之咎，而徒異端之尤，惑也甚矣！執事策士，而惓惓於崇正學以明道統，蓋扶世教、淑人心之大機括也。愚生繪天測海，何足以復明問？雖然，學術之誠偽，則甞聞之孔子矣：古曰為己、今曰為人是也。心術之邪正，則甞聞之孟子矣：為善為舜、為利為蹠是也。一念之幾微，而係終身之造詣，若之何其弗求道於學，而求學於心也？
夫道統始於堯、舜，後自周公傳之孔子，又自孔子傳之孟子，匪耳提之、匪面命之，以心授之也；則孔、孟所以演道真、開來學者，蓋亦以心受之矣。故古今語道統之正者，莫若孔、孟；語學術之正者，亦莫若孔、孟。而其語害道者，則曰老、佛，曰楊、墨。夫老、佛、楊、墨，其道何道？其學何學？而其為吾道與學之害者，其心何心？為老氏之說者曰：
translation_en:
…be sworn before Heaven and Earth or vouched for before ghosts and spirits is entirely depraved. Because a depraved mind sprouts, orthodox learning is rent asunder; because orthodox learning is rent asunder, the transmission of the Way (daotong) is eroded. At the juncture of what is hidden, subtle, and specious, men of discernment harbor deep忧虑 (concern). To not blame this, and instead merely fault heterodox teachings, is a grave delusion indeed! Your Excellency, in putting policy questions to the scholars, is earnestly devoted to exalting orthodox learning in order to clarify the transmission of the Way; this is truly the great pivot for upholding the teachings of the age and purifying human minds. For a foolish student like myself, it is like painting the heavens or fathoming the sea—how could I be equal to replying to your enlightened inquiry? Even so, regarding the sincerity or falsity of scholarly learning, I have heard of it from Confucius: in antiquity one learned for oneself, whereas today one learns for the sake of others—that is what it means. Regarding the depravity or rectitude of the mind's intentions, I have heard of it from Mencius: to act for goodness is to be a Shun, whereas to act for profit is to be a Robber Zhi—that is what it means. The subtle incipient stirrings of a single thought determine the attainments of an entire lifetime; how, then, could one not seek the Way in learning, and seek learning in the mind?

Now, the transmission of the Way began with Yao and Shun; afterward it was transmitted from the Duke of Zhou to Confucius, and again from Confucius to Mencius. It was not by holding them by the ear, nor by instructing them face to face, but by transmitting it through the mind; thus, the means by which Confucius and Mencius expounded the truth of the Way and opened the path for future scholars was likewise by receiving it through the mind. Therefore, past and present, when speaking of the orthodoxy of the transmission of the Way, none compare to Confucius and Mencius; when speaking of the orthodoxy of scholarly learning, likewise none compare to Confucius and Mencius. Yet when speaking of those who harm the Way, people say Laozi and the Buddha, and they say Yang Zhu and Mo Di. Now as for Laozi, the Buddha, Yang Zhu, and Mo Di—what sort of Way is their Way? What sort of learning is their learning? And in being a harm to our Way and our learning, what sort of mind is their mind? Those who espouse the doctrines of Laozi say: …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
去仁義絕禮樂而後天下安爲佛氏之說
者曰棄父絕子不爲夫婦放雞豚食菜茹
而後萬物遂迺楊氏則以老爲宗而墨之
與佛前後亦若互相印證彼其與吾孔孟
之道蓋判若黑白然矣然遡其源則非特
孔孟之心欲以治天下雖老佛楊墨亦何
心於害天下極其流則非特老佛楊墨之
徒亂天下而學孔孟之學者亦或至於亂
天下有繇也當孔子時佛氏未入中國時
===
與接轂者惟一老氏孔子弗之闢也且就
之而問禮稱之爲猶龍而特不以其術授
諸其徒則以吾道方明而彼弗能爲吾徒
惑也彼弗爲吾徒惑則亦何暇嘵嘵然與
之爭角雄長然嘗謂丘遊方之內者也彼
遊方之外者也內外之辨其隱然不闢之
闢歟故曰攻乎異端斯害也已孔子之心
可知矣孔子沒而微言絕楊朱墨翟之言
盈天下孟子出稍晚與其徒爲敵辭而闢
punctuated: 「去仁義，絕禮樂，而後天下安。」爲佛氏之說者曰：「棄父絕子，不爲夫婦，放雞豚，食菜茹，而後萬物遂。」迺楊氏則以老爲宗，而墨之與佛前後亦若互相印證，彼其與吾孔、孟之道，蓋判若黑白然矣。然遡其源，則非特孔、孟之心欲以治天下，雖老、佛、楊、墨亦何心於害天下？極其流，則非特老、佛、楊、墨之徒亂天下，而學孔、孟之學者亦或至於亂天下，有繇也。當孔子時，佛氏未入中國，時與接轂者惟一老氏，孔子弗之闢也。且就之而問禮，稱之爲「猶龍」，而特不以其術授諸其徒，則以吾道方明，而彼弗能爲吾徒惑也。彼弗爲吾徒惑，則亦何暇嘵嘵然與之爭角雄長？然嘗謂：「丘遊方之內者也，彼遊方之外者也。」內外之辨，其隱然不闢之闢歟！故曰：「攻乎異端，斯害也已。」孔子之心可知矣。孔子沒而微言絕，楊朱、墨翟之言盈天下。孟子出稍晚，與其徒爲敵，辭而闢
translation_en: … "Discard benevolence and righteousness, abandon rites and music, and only then will the world be at peace." Those who espouse the doctrines of the Buddha say: "Abandon fathers and sever ties with sons, do not marry, release chickens and pigs, eat vegetables and herbs, and only then will the myriad things flourish." Now, Master Yang took Laozi as his ancestor, while Mozi and the Buddha, coming before and after one another, also seem to mutually corroborate each other. Their relation to the Way of our Confucius and Mencius is indeed as distinct as black and white. Yet if we trace their origins, not only did the minds of Confucius and Mencius desire to bring order to the world, what intention did Laozi, the Buddha, Yang, and Mo ever have of harming the world? And if we follow their currents to their extremes, not only do the followers of Laozi, the Buddha, Yang, and Mo throw the world into disorder, even those who study the learning of Confucius and Mencius may sometimes end up throwing the world into disorder—and there is a reason for this. In the time of Confucius, Buddhism had not yet entered China, and the only one with whom he crossed paths at the time was Laozi alone; Confucius did not refute him. Moreover, he approached him to ask about the rites and praised him as being "like a dragon," merely refraining from transmitting Laozi's arts to his own disciples. This was because our Way was then bright, and the other was unable to delude our followers. Since the other did not delude our followers, what need was there to clamorously contend with him for supremacy? Yet he once said, "I, Qiu, roam within the bounds of society; they roam beyond the bounds." Is not the distinction between within and beyond an implicit refutation without refuting? Therefore he said, "To apply oneself to heterodox doctrines is harmful indeed." The mind of Confucius can thus be known. After Confucius died, subtle words ceased, and the doctrines of Yang Zhu and Mo Di filled the world. Mencius appeared somewhat later, stood as an adversary to their followers, and with words refuted…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之指爲無父無君比之夷狄禽獸迸逐之
將使無所逃臯則以吾道方否而彼將爲
天下禍也彼爲天下禍而吾既不得位以
制其方張之焰乃又默默焉視其日熾而
莫爲之所則承三聖以正人心誰復任其
責者是以闢之惟恐其不嚴也故曰予豈
好辩哉予不得已也孟子之心可知矣自
是仁義說昌楊墨迹息無庸復辩及宋興
而程朱輩出則又有斥二家似是之非而
===
謂其彌近理大亂真者既謂其似又指其
非既謂其近又虞其亂此何以說也今夫
食者弗甘稻粱而慕餐霞吸露之奇衣者
弗華布帛而羨霓裳羽衣之巧學者弗樂
庸言庸行而好聞高世絕塵之論厭常喜
新理有固然而況二氏之指歸亦多依俙
吾道之影響堯舜曰精一孔子曰一貫而
彼老氏亦曰抱一孔子曰正心孟子曰存
心而彼佛氏亦曰明心又安知人情之弗
punctuated: 之，指爲無父無君，比之夷狄禽獸，迸逐之將使無所逃臯。則以吾道方否，而彼將爲天下禍也。彼爲天下禍，而吾既不得位以制其方張之焰，乃又默默焉視其日熾而莫爲之所，則承三聖以正人心，誰復任其責者？是以闢之惟恐其不嚴也。故曰：「予豈好辩哉？予不得已也。」孟子之心可知矣。自是仁義說昌，楊、墨迹息，無庸復辩。及宋興而程、朱輩出，則又有斥二家似是之非，而謂其「彌近理，大亂真」者。既謂其似，又指其非；既謂其近，又虞其亂，此何以說也？今夫食者弗甘稻粱，而慕餐霞吸露之奇；衣者弗華布帛，而羨霓裳羽衣之巧；學者弗樂庸言庸行，而好聞高世絕塵之論。厭常喜新，理有固然，而況二氏之指歸，亦多依俙吾道之影響。堯、舜曰「精一」，孔子曰「一貫」，而彼老氏亦曰「抱一」；孔子曰「正心」，孟子曰「存心」，而彼佛氏亦曰「明心」。又安知人情之弗
translation_en:
…them, denouncing them as acknowledging neither father nor ruler, likening them to barbarians and beasts, and driving them out so that they would have nowhere to escape their guilt. This was because our Way was then in decline, and they were about to become a calamity for the world. Since they were becoming a calamity for the world, and we did not hold a position of authority from which to check their rising flames, if we had furthermore looked on in silence as they grew more rampant by the day without doing anything about them, then who else would have shouldered the responsibility of succeeding the Three Sages in rectifying human minds? Therefore, in refuting them, his only fear was that he would not be severe enough. Thus he said, "Am I fond of disputing? I have no alternative." The mind of Mencius can thus be known.

From then on, the doctrines of benevolence and righteousness flourished, the traces of Yang Zhu and Mo Di vanished, and there was no need for further disputation. When the Song dynasty arose and thinkers such as the Cheng brothers [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] and Zhu Xi 朱熹 appeared one after another, there were once again those who denounced the specious falsehoods of the two schools [Daoism and Buddhism], saying that they "come ever closer to principle and greatly confound the truth." Since they called them "specious," why did they also point out their "falsehood"? Since they called them "close," why did they also worry about their "confounding"? How is this to be explained?

Now, when it comes to food, people do not relish rice and millet, but yearn for the marvel of dining on rosy clouds and sipping dew; when it comes to clothing, people do not consider linen and silk splendid, but admire the ingenuity of rainbow skirts and feathered robes; when it comes to learning, scholars do not take pleasure in ordinary words and ordinary deeds, but love to hear lofty discourses that transcend the world and leave the dust behind. To tire of the commonplace and delight in the novel is a natural tendency of things; how much more so when the ultimate aims of the two sects [Laozi and the Buddha] also frequently bear a vague resemblance to the echoes and shadows of our Way! Yao and Shun spoke of "refinement and singleness," and Confucius spoke of "one thread binding all," while that Laozi also spoke of "embracing the One"; Confucius spoke of "rectifying the mind," and Mencius spoke of "preserving the mind," while that Buddha also spoke of "illuminating the mind." How, then, can one be sure that human sentiment will not…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
疑而且信也是故似者雖終不可以爲是
而易以惑吾之是玉表石中賈者目眩彪
文麕質獵夫神驚正惟其似也近者雖終
不可以爲眞而易以亂吾之眞素絲以染
而化剛金以煉而柔正惟其近也是以知
道者斥之也雖然大明中天則爝火無所
容其光聖道昭著則異端無所置其喙我
明興斥去異端尊崇孔孟旣取其書而表章
之復拜其人而俎豆之至我
===
皇上嗜學好問
萬幾之暇時進館閣之臣與之講明古先哲王
之道海內皆家詩書戶禮樂佩仁而服義
寧復有所謂無父無君者出爲吾道障而
正道之蝕正學之裂復厪執事憂則議者
以老佛之敎尚蔓延而未殄也宋儒有言
昔之害人也乘其愚昧今之害人也乘其
高明迺今緇黃之流曳籍玄梵者不過以
禍福輪迴營惑黔首實莫究厥宗旨而清
punctuated: 疑而且信也。是故似者雖終不可以爲是，而易以惑吾之是；玉表石中，賈者目眩，彪文麕質，獵夫神驚，正惟其似也。近者雖終不可以爲眞，而易以亂吾之眞；素絲以染而化，剛金以煉而柔，正惟其近也。是以知道者斥之也。雖然，大明中天，則爝火無所容其光；聖道昭著，則異端無所置其喙。我明興，斥去異端，尊崇孔、孟，旣取其書而表章之，復拜其人而俎豆之。至我皇上嗜學好問，萬幾之暇，時進館閣之臣，與之講明古先哲王之道，海內皆家詩書、戶禮樂，佩仁而服義，寧復有所謂無父無君者出爲吾道障？而正道之蝕、正學之裂，復厪執事憂，則議者以老、佛之敎尚蔓延而未殄也。宋儒有言：「昔之害人也，乘其愚昧；今之害人也，乘其高明。」迺今緇黃之流、曳籍玄梵者，不過以禍福輪迴營惑黔首，實莫究厥宗旨；而清
translation_en: …doubt and come to believe in them? Therefore, although that which merely resembles can never truly be right, it easily confuses what we hold to be right. When a stone inside has the exterior of jade, the merchant's eyes are dazzled; when the substance of a hornless deer wears the stripes of a tiger, the hunter's spirit is startled—precisely because of the resemblance. Although that which is merely near the truth can never be the genuine truth, it easily confounds what we hold to be genuine. White silk is transformed by dyeing, and hard metal is softened by smelting—precisely because of their proximity. That is why those who know the Way reject them. Even so, when the great sun and moon are at the zenith of heaven, torch-fires have no place to show their light; when the Way of the Sages shines forth clearly, heterodoxies have no room to interject a word. Since the rise of our Ming dynasty, heterodoxies have been cast out and Confucius and Mencius revered; not only have their books been selected and honored, but their persons have been bowed to and offered sacrificial vessels. Down to our reigning Emperor, who loves learning and delights in inquiry, in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state he frequently summons the ministers of the Hanlin Academy and the Grand Secretariat to expound and clarify with them the Way of the ancient sage-kings. Within the seas, every family has the Odes and Documents, every household has rites and music, wearing benevolence at their girdle and clothing themselves in righteousness—how could there still be those so-called deniers of father and ruler emerging to obstruct our Way? Yet the erosion of the orthodox Way and the fracturing of orthodox learning still cause Your Excellency anxiety. Critics say this is because the teachings of Laozi and the Buddha still spread and have not been eradicated. The Song Confucians had a saying: "In the past, they harmed people by taking advantage of their ignorance; today, they harm people by taking advantage of their lofty intelligence." Yet nowadays, the black-robed Buddhist monks and yellow-capped Daoist priests who trail their robes and register themselves in Daoist and Buddhist orders do no more than delude the common folk with talk of fortune, misfortune, and karmic reincarnation, without truly fathoming their own fundamental doctrines; while as for pure…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
淨空虛谷神遣累雖吾儒之賢者亦罕窺
之則所謂乗其高明者又與宋異夫復何
憂焉誠憂之藉令人其人火其書廬其居
悉教以先王之道矣今之道果明而學果
正焉否歟噫此則愚生所謂不在異端而
在吾儒不在學術而在心術者也彼羹牆
唐虞者豈盡精一之真傳乎步趨孔孟者
豈盡誠明之奧旨乎陳仁義而談性命者
豈盡含英而咀華者乎世有淵識邃養之
===
士登聖賢之堂閾發經傳之精微誠亦足
以為世教助而彼好名之徒印其中尚不
能窺異端之藩籬也乃亦肆為游談蠱我
正道何哉彼其包藏於中者則既詐且譎
矣而懼夫人之摘其隱也於是乎朋援集
矣標幟立矣門竇開矣齋居而默坐曰吾
以凝真靜也谿藏而壑伏曰吾以崇恬退
也布衣而蔬食曰吾以黜浮靡也絕交而
却餽曰吾以養廉潔也似信似忠無舉無
punctuated: 淨空虛、谷神遣累，雖吾儒之賢者亦罕窺之，則所謂乗其高明者又與宋異，夫復何憂焉？誠憂之，藉令人其人，火其書，廬其居，悉教以先王之道矣，今之道果明而學果正焉否歟？噫！此則愚生所謂不在異端而在吾儒，不在學術而在心術者也。彼羹牆唐虞者，豈盡精一之真傳乎？步趨孔孟者，豈盡誠明之奧旨乎？陳仁義而談性命者，豈盡含英而咀華者乎？世有淵識邃養之士，登聖賢之堂閾，發經傳之精微，誠亦足以為世教助。而彼好名之徒，印其中尚不能窺異端之藩籬也，乃亦肆為游談，蠱我正道，何哉？彼其包藏於中者，則既詐且譎矣，而懼夫人之摘其隱也，於是乎朋援集矣，標幟立矣，門竇開矣。齋居而默坐，曰：「吾以凝真靜也。」谿藏而壑伏，曰：「吾以崇恬退也。」布衣而蔬食，曰：「吾以黜浮靡也。」絕交而却餽，曰：「吾以養廉潔也。」似信似忠，無舉無
translation_en: … purity, emptiness, the valley spirit, and casting off worldly entanglements, even the worthy among us Confucians rarely peer into them. Thus, what was called "taking advantage of their lofty intelligence" is again different from the Song dynasty; what more is there to worry about? If we truly worry about them, even supposing we returned their followers to lay life, burned their books, turned their monasteries into ordinary dwellings, and taught them all the Way of the former kings—would the Way today truly be illuminated and learning truly be orthodox, or not? Alas! This is what I, a foolish student, mean by saying that the problem lies not in heterodoxy, but in us Confucians; not in scholarly methods, but in the disposition of the mind. Those who see Tang Yao and Yu Shun in their soup and on their walls—do they all possess the true transmission of subtlety and unity? Those who walk in the footsteps of Confucius and Mencius—do they all grasp the profound meaning of sincerity and enlightenment? Those who set forth benevolence and righteousness and discourse on human nature and destiny—are they all people who savor the finest essence and chew the blossoms of truth? In the world there are scholars of deep insight and profound cultivation who ascend the halls and thresholds of the sages and worthies and bring forth the subtle essentials of the Classics and commentaries; they are indeed sufficient to serve as an aid to moral teaching in the world. Yet those seekers of fame—when you examine what is inside them, they cannot even peer over the outer fence of heterodoxy—nevertheless recklessly indulge in floating talk to bewitch our orthodox Way; why is this? What they harbor within is already deceitful and duplicitous, and because they fear that others will expose their hidden motives, they gather cliques of mutual support, set up banners, and open up factional gateways. Dwelling in fasts and sitting in silence, they say: "By this I concentrate true tranquility." Hiding in ravines and crouching in gullies, they say: "By this I esteem calm retirement." Wearing coarse cloth and eating vegetables, they say: "By this I reject superficial extravagance." Cutting off social intercourse and refusing gifts, they say: "By this I nourish integrity and purity." Seeming trustworthy and seeming loyal, offering nothing to be cited for praise and nothing to be…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
剌而或者其口則然而行則戾之旦則然
而暮則違之昭昭則然而冥冥且墮之矣
又其甚者懼吾說之不足簧皷天下也且
將借浮游猖狂之說以投好怪樂誕之心
俾傾聽者皓首窮年深求力索而莫識端
倪弊將至於廢天下之職業而弗之顧嗟
夫彼爲老佛之徒者曰吾師之說是也爲
楊墨之徒者亦曰吾師之說是也吾黨陽
習孔孟之敎而顧陰用異端之長且以違
===
道干譽之心而謬躋於淵識邃養之列使
聞且見者莫辨玉石其舛不較甚而其禍
不尤烈哉嗚呼吾道之不能無異端猶中
國之不能無夷狄也中國而夷狄也匡中
國者將治夷狄耶治中國之夷狄耶吾道
而異端也衞吾道者將攻異端耶攻吾道
之異端耶吾聞春秋之疾夷狄非疾純夷
狄者也疾夫以中國而入夷狄者也然則
孟子有作其所息而距之者端有所歸矣
punctuated: 剌。而或者其口則然，而行則戾之；旦則然，而暮則違之；昭昭則然，而冥冥且墮之矣。又其甚者，懼吾說之不足簧皷天下也，且將借浮游猖狂之說，以投好怪樂誕之心，俾傾聽者皓首窮年，深求力索，而莫識端倪，弊將至於廢天下之職業而弗之顧。嗟夫！彼爲老、佛之徒者，曰：「吾師之說是也。」爲楊、墨之徒者，亦曰：「吾師之說是也。」吾黨陽習孔、孟之敎，而顧陰用異端之長，且以違道干譽之心，而謬躋於淵識邃養之列，使聞且見者莫辨玉石，其舛不較甚，而其禍不尤烈哉？嗚呼！吾道之不能無異端，猶中國之不能無夷狄也。中國而夷狄也，匡中國者將治夷狄耶？治中國之夷狄耶？吾道而異端也，衞吾道者將攻異端耶？攻吾道之異端耶？吾聞《春秋》之疾夷狄，非疾純夷狄者也，疾夫以中國而入夷狄者也。然則孟子有作，其所息而距之者，端有所歸矣。
translation_en:
…to criticize. Yet perhaps what they say with their mouths, they contradict in their actions; what they affirm in the morning, they violate by evening; what they uphold in the bright light of day, they abandon in the dark. Even worse, fearing that their own doctrines are insufficient to gull and stir up the world, they go so far as to borrow floating, unbridled, and wild theories to cater to minds that fancy the strange and delight in the absurd. They cause those who listen intently to grow white-haired through the years, searching deeply and striving mightily without ever grasping the slightest clue—an abuse that will end in causing people to abandon the practical duties of the world without a second thought.

Alas! Those who are followers of Laozi and the Buddha say, "Our master's doctrine is right." Those who are followers of Yang Zhu and Mo Di likewise say, "Our master's doctrine is right." Yet those of our own Confucian party outwardly practice the teachings of Confucius and Mencius while secretly employing the strong points of heterodoxies; moreover, with minds set on violating the Way to seek fame, they falsely elevate themselves into the ranks of those of profound insight and deep cultivation. Making it impossible for those who hear and see them to distinguish jade from stone—is this perversity not far worse, and its calamity not even more fierce?

Alas! That our Way cannot be without heterodoxy is just as the Central States cannot be without the Yi and Di barbarians. When the Central States act like barbarians, should those who would rectify the Central States bring order to the barbarians, or bring order to the barbarians within the Central States? When our Way becomes heterodox, should those who defend our Way attack heterodoxy, or attack the heterodoxy within our Way? I have heard that when the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) detests the barbarians, it does not detest those who are purely barbarian; it detests those of the Central States who lapse into barbarism. If so, were Mencius to arise again, that which he would put an end to andward off would surely have a definite target!

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
吁此可謂務講學而不務正心者戒也而
柰何世之弗察也其僞之弗能辨而倂以
疑眞其邪之不能識而槩以詆正歌哭一
言而洛蜀之黨遽成誠正一疏而僞學之
禁遂起吁亦悖甚矣夫噎者病食食終不
可廢盜者挾弓矢弓矢卒不可禁也儒者
之害道亦儒名而異學者害之耳而學可
以終弗講歟大學之道自格致誠正而達
之脩齊治平如日月之麗天而不容隱也
===
如江河之行地而不容息也苟能辨之精
而毫釐弗爽守之定而須臾弗離則天下
之邪者僞者竊似而亂眞者皆潜消而默
奪之矣有世道之責者可不加之意哉
第四問
姚鳳翔
同考試官教諭田 批 習俗通弊子能扼腕劇陳
刋落繁蕪全歸悃幅是亦文字之還淳者
考試官教諭林 批 條答時務鑿鑿可行有用
punctuated:
吁！此可謂務講學而不務正心者戒也。而柰何世之弗察也！其僞之弗能辨，而倂以疑眞；其邪之不能識，而槩以詆正。歌哭一言，而洛蜀之黨遽成；誠正一疏，而僞學之禁遂起。吁！亦悖甚矣。夫噎者病食，食終不可廢；盜者挾弓矢，弓矢卒不可禁也。儒者之害道，亦儒名而異學者害之耳，而學可以終弗講歟？《大學》之道，自格致誠正而達之脩齊治平，如日月之麗天而不容隱也，如江河之行地而不容息也。苟能辨之精而毫釐弗爽，守之定而須臾弗離，則天下之邪者、僞者、竊似而亂眞者，皆潜消而默奪之矣。有世道之責者，可不加之意哉！

第四問
姚鳳翔
同考試官教諭田批：習俗通弊，子能扼腕劇陳。刋落繁蕪，全歸悃幅，是亦文字之還淳者。
考試官教諭林批：條答時務，鑿鑿可行，有用
translation_en:
Alas! This may serve as a warning to those who devote themselves to lecturing on learning without devoting themselves to rectifying their minds. Yet how is it that the world fails to examine this! Unable to distinguish the false, people go so far as to doubt the true as well; unable to recognize the heterodox, they sweepingly slander the orthodox. Over a single remark about singing and weeping, the Luo and Shu factions suddenly formed; over a single memorial on making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind, the prohibition of "false learning" consequently arose. Alas, this is utterly perverse! Now, one who chokes suffers from food, yet food cannot ultimately be abandoned; robbers carry bows and arrows, yet bows and arrows cannot in the end be prohibited. When Confucians harm the Way, it is merely those who bear the name of Confucian while practicing heterodox learning who harm it—so how could learning ultimately not be discoursed upon? The Way of the Great Learning (Daxue), extending from the investigation of things, extension of knowledge, making the intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind to the cultivation of the person, regulation of the family, ordering of the state, and pacification of the world, is like the sun and moon shining in the heavens, which cannot be concealed, and like the Yangtze and Yellow rivers coursing across the earth, which cannot be halted. If one can discern it with precision so as not to err by the slightest hair, and hold to it withsteadfastness so as not to depart from it for a single moment, then all in the world that is heterodox, false, or usurping the semblance of truth to confound the genuine will be quietly dispelled and silently stripped away. How could those who bear responsibility for the Way of the world not give heed to this!

Fourth Question
Yao Fengxiang 姚鳳翔

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之文宜錄以式
考試官教諭吳批洞悉弊源
嘗謂轉移習尚之機在上而不在下維持
風教之本以實而不以文蓋上者下之基
基奠而藩固矣反是而中心不正是撤藩
也實者文之輻輻端而輈隨矣反是而輪
轅徒飾是虛車也此司世道者宵旦怔營
圖回反正之不暇可泄泄然以固址完輪
視今日哉記有之廣谷大川異制民生其
===
間異俗剛柔輕重遲速異齊五味異和器
械異制衣服異宜此習尚之殊自古記之
矣然風俗之美莫踰於成周當時姬旦篤
棐弼翼仔肩德教薰蒸遍徹九埏行葦既
醉之休風繼唐虞而再見然及其季也鄭
衛淫僻齊陳荒穢魏國儉嗇褊急惟有唐
存憂深思遠之風檜曹切困窮望治之想
故孔子刪詩以豳風終焉謂變而克正危
而克扶始終不失其本唯周公能之也微
punctuated:
之文，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭吳批：洞悉弊源。
嘗謂轉移習尚之機，在上而不在下；維持風教之本，以實而不以文。蓋上者下之基，基奠而藩固矣；反是而中心不正，是撤藩也。實者文之輻，輻端而輈隨矣；反是而輪轅徒飾，是虛車也。此司世道者宵旦怔營、圖回反正之不暇，可泄泄然以固址完輪視今日哉！《記》有之：「廣谷大川異制，民生其間異俗，剛柔、輕重、遲速異齊，五味異和，器械異制，衣服異宜。」此習尚之殊，自古記之矣。然風俗之美，莫踰於成周。當時姬旦篤棐弼翼，仔肩德教，薰蒸遍徹九埏，《行葦》、《既醉》之休風，繼唐、虞而再見。然及其季也，鄭、衛淫僻，齊、陳荒穢，魏國儉嗇褊急，惟有唐存憂深思遠之風，檜、曹切困窮望治之想。故孔子刪《詩》，以《豳風》終焉，謂變而克正、危而克扶，始終不失其本，唯周公能之也。微
translation_en:
… prose; it should be recorded as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Wu comments: Thoroughly understands the roots of the abuses.
I have held that the pivot for transforming customs and habits lies with those above and not with those below, and the foundation for upholding moral teachings lies in substance and not in ornament. For those above are the foundation of those below; when the foundation is laid, the defensive hedge is secure. To do the opposite, with the center itself uprightly unaligned, is to tear down the hedge. Substance is the spokes for ornament; when the spokes are straight, the carriage pole follows. To do the opposite, merely adorning the wheels and shafts, is to have an empty carriage. Thus those in charge of the moral order of the world work anxiously day and night, scarcely having enough time to plan a return to rectitude—how could they leisurely view the present day as having a firm foundation and intact wheels! The Record of Rites (Liji) states: "Broad valleys and great rivers differ in their formations, and the people born among them differ in their customs. Their temperaments—yielding or unyielding, light or grave, slow or swift—are differently balanced; the five flavors are differently blended; implements and tools are differently fashioned; and garments are differently suited." Such differences in customs and habits have been recorded since antiquity. Yet in the beauty of its customs, no era surpassed the flourishing Zhou. At that time, Ji Dan [the Duke of Zhou] faithfully assisted and supported the royal house, shouldering the burden of moral instruction until its pervasive influence reached throughout the nine regions; the virtuous customs celebrated in the odes "Wayside Reeds" (Xingwei) and "Drunk with Wine" (Jizui) appeared once again in succession to the eras of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun]. Yet when the dynasty reached its decline, Zheng and Wei grew licentious and perverse, Qi and Chen became dissolute and foul, and the state of Wei became stingy and narrow-minded; only Tang preserved an ethos of deep concern and far-reaching thought, while Kuai and Cao felt the urgent longing of the distressed for good governance. Therefore, when Confucius edited the Book of Odes (Shijing), he concluded the Airs of the States with the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng), meaning that in the midst of change to be able to restore rectitude, and in the midst of peril to be able to give support, never losing sight of the root from beginning to end, was something only the Duke of Zhou could achieve.
