title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
公而風之潰也不可返巳他日猶諄切于
野史之辨不遜寧固之譏而寤寐憲章則
惟先進是從焉孔子非不知頹波之橫流
而力爲之障其情則誠亟也嗟乎知孔子
維周之意則今日誠不容以不汲汲矣洪
惟我
太祖定鼎開基首崇風敎以浙服爲文獻峩冕
靈秀鬱鍾金華一莅啓萬年文治之精華
于時懸禮樂而置軌範家稷契而人皐陶
卽山陬海澨咸翕然相逐淳謹官府斂董
治之威闤闠聞頌聲之作鄉之老成猶能
談浙之舊事乃今之浙固昔之浙而今之
習則殊非昔之習矣故杭承先朝繁華又
舟車所輳湖山所環其四方之游士賈客
肩摩踵躡風會趨靡遂日流於妤蕩而無
節其西郡澤沮田疇殖餉攸資民俗多饒
而繁文競侈不免喜事之嫌又其甚則私
艇出沒群猾所淵藪也其東郡聲名文物
punctuated: 公，而風之潰也不可返巳。他日猶諄切于野史之辨、不遜寧固之譏，而寤寐憲章，則惟先進是從焉。孔子非不知頹波之橫流，而力爲之障，其情則誠亟也。嗟乎！知孔子維周之意，則今日誠不容以不汲汲矣。洪惟我太祖定鼎開基，首崇風敎。以浙服爲文獻峩冕、靈秀鬱鍾，金華一莅，啓萬年文治之精華。于時懸禮樂而置軌範，家稷契而人皐陶，卽山陬海澨，咸翕然相逐淳謹。官府斂董治之威，闤闠聞頌聲之作，鄉之老成猶能談浙之舊事。乃今之浙固昔之浙，而今之習則殊非昔之習矣。故杭承先朝繁華，又舟車所輳、湖山所環，其四方之游士賈客肩摩踵躡，風會趨靡，遂日流於妤蕩而無節。其西郡澤沮田疇，殖餉攸資，民俗多饒，而繁文競侈，不免喜事之嫌；又其甚則私艇出沒，群猾所淵藪也。其東郡聲名文物，
translation_en:
… the Duke [of Zhou], the collapse of customs could never have been reversed. On other occasions, he was still earnestly concerned with distinguishing between the rustic and the courtly, and with the criticism that it is better to be obstinate than presumptuous; and in his waking and sleeping thoughts of the constitutional models, it was solely the men of former times whom he followed. It was not that Confucius did not know that the decadent tide was overflowing everywhere, yet he strove with all his might to dam it, for his concern was truly urgent. Alas! If one understands Confucius's intention in upholding the Zhou, then today we truly cannot afford not to be urgently concerned!

We humbly reflect upon how our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) established the dynastic Tripods and founded the imperial enterprise, placing the highest priority on moral instruction and customs. Regarding the Zhejiang region as a place of cultural heritage and lofty caps of office where numinous talent was richly concentrated, his single visit to Jinhua inaugurated the finest essence of ten thousand years of civil governance. At that time, rites and music were displayed and standards and models were set up; every family was a Ji or a Xie, and every person a Gao Yao. Even in mountain corners and on the shores of the sea, all harmoniously pursued pure and cautious ways together. Government offices restrained the severity of their supervision and punishment, while in the marketplaces the sounds of praise were heard; the elders of the villages are still able to speak of the old affairs of Zhejiang.

Yet the Zhejiang of today is certainly the Zhejiang of the past, whereas the customs of today are utterly different from the customs of the past! Thus Hangzhou has inherited the splendour and luxury of the previous dynasty, and is furthermore a hub where boats and carriages converge and which lakes and hills encircle. Wandering scholars and traveling merchants from all four directions rub shoulders and follow on one another's heels there; the prevailing trends incline toward extravagance, and so day by day they flow into wantonness [?] and licentiousness without restraint. In the western prefectures, marshes and lowlands and cultivated fields provide the resources for production and grain supply. The people's customs are largely affluent, yet they indulge in elaborate formalities and compete in luxury, not escaping the suspicion of being fond of stirring up affairs; and at its worst, private boats appear and disappear, making it a haven for gangs of cunning villains. In the eastern prefectures, renowned for fame and cultural artifacts, …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詩書比屋民俗多慧而嗇業尚虚稍沿江
左之習又其甚則齒繁射利游食所四出
也上游諸郡睦之俗簡訟而奉公較爲寡
尤然業貧而惰事亦緣以積困至婺衢之
墟衣冠淳龐猶有先民之遺然訐而好鬭
勇而尚氣乃家藏戈矛視殺人僅若草菅
則其居使之然矣甌栝之俗奢儉異習亦
有近古之稱然負山阻海均爲遠屬乃法
令多玩積逋賦且至千萬則其流之弊乆
===
矣習俗之異若此是豈振古如兹而竟莫
可挽耶愚聞之上化下謂之風下從上謂
之俗言應也又曰上行下效謂之風衆心
安定謂之俗言機也故風之所在不兵革
而威不燎揚而焰不迅雷而厲不戴星而
馳有移風之責者亦慎其所以風之而已
矣夫三家之市十金之貲乃中人所恃以
卒歲而不至展轉流離於中路者也然能
儉約以居之則用享延年使奢靡以繼之
punctuated:
詩書比屋，民俗多慧而嗇業尚虚，稍沿江左之習；又其甚，則齒繁射利，游食所四出也。上游諸郡，睦之俗簡訟而奉公，較爲寡尤，然業貧而惰事，亦緣以積困；至婺、衢之墟，衣冠淳龐，猶有先民之遺，然訐而好鬭，勇而尚氣，乃家藏戈矛，視殺人僅若草菅，則其居使之然矣。甌、栝之俗，奢儉異習，亦有近古之稱，然負山阻海，均爲遠屬，乃法令多玩，積逋賦且至千萬，則其流之弊乆矣。習俗之異若此，是豈振古如兹，而竟莫可挽耶？
愚聞之：上化下謂之風，下從上謂之俗，言應也；又曰：上行下效謂之風，衆心安定謂之俗，言機也。故風之所在，不兵革而威，不燎揚而焰，不迅雷而厲，不戴星而馳。有移風之責者，亦慎其所以風之而已矣。
夫三家之市，十金之貲，乃中人所恃以卒歲，而不至展轉流離於中路者也。然能儉約以居之，則用享延年；使奢靡以繼之，
translation_en:
…the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents are found in every house side by side; the local customs are mostly clever, yet people are stinting in productive labor and esteem empty pretension, somewhat following the habits of Jiangzuo [the lower Yangtze region]. And at their worst, the population is dense and pursues profit, whence idlers go forth in all directions to make a living. Among the prefectures of the upper reaches, the customs of Mu [Yanzhou] are sparing of litigation and obedient to public duty, making it comparatively free of faults; yet their livelihoods are poor and they are lax in their affairs, and because of this they accumulate distress. As for the territories of Wu [Jinhua] and Qu [Quzhou], the gentry are simple and honest, still retaining the legacy of the ancients; yet the people are contentious and fond of fighting, fierce and prizing bravado, to the point that households hide halberds and spears, and regard killing a man as no more than cutting grass—their environment makes them so. In the customs of Ou [Wenzhou] and Gua [Chuzhou], extravagance and frugality differ in practice, and they also have a reputation for approaching antiquity; yet backed by mountains and blocked by the sea, both are distant dependencies, so laws and ordinances are often treated with contempt, and accumulated tax arrears reach into the tens of millions—thus the abuses that have flowed down are of long standing. That the differences in customs are like this—could it really be so from remotest antiquity, and ultimately impossible to reverse?

I, in my simplicity, have heard: "When superiors transform inferiors, it is called moral influence (feng); when inferiors follow superiors, it is called custom (su)"—this speaks of resonance. And it is also said: "When superiors act and inferiors imitate, it is called moral influence; when the hearts of the multitude are settled and secure, it is called custom"—this speaks of the pivot of action. Therefore, where moral influence resides, without weapons and armor it is awe-inspiring, without blazing fire it flames up, without swift thunder it is severe, and without traveling under the stars it speeds forth. Those who bear the responsibility of transforming customs need only be careful about that by which they exercise moral influence over them, and nothing more.

Now a hamlet of three households and a property of ten pieces of gold are what people of middling means rely upon to get through the year without coming to toss about and wander destitute along the road. Yet if they can dwell in it with frugality and restraint, their resources will suffice to sustain them through the years; whereas if they continue it with extravagance and waste…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則立見傾覆此其明效大驗者況進三家
十金而上之者乎今環浙之境有獻酬而
動費數金竭其身力以奉者有作嬪而傾
貲無量不足則稱貸以益者奔走之僕紈
綺相炫輿臺之輩絢縟爭侈不知在上之
章德何物也專業樗蒲延招朋類轉瞬一
擲蓋藏靡遺不知注孤而盜起相繼也披
緇髡髮寔繁有徒寶觀崇菴侈隆鼎建是
不可以不急汰也振履連翩競標姱麗結
===
驩絡繹馳騖冶容是不可以不急逐也里
閈富強偃仰瞪盻浚貧民之錐刀以冒道
家之忌所謂陸梁其性也是不可以不重
懲也少年遊俠黨附逍遙飛終日之崇觴
以起遊觀之艷所謂蜉蝣其習也是不可
以不亟屏也見隸戎籍用之本省所謂練
土著者誠以是矣而各省徵募復且歲至
安可不蚤杜以塞其流乎歲輸課額殷剥
艱阻所繇免漕輓者誠以是矣而本郡餉
punctuated: 則立見傾覆，此其明效大驗者，況進三家十金而上之者乎？今環浙之境，有獻酬而動費數金，竭其身力以奉者；有作嬪而傾貲無量，不足則稱貸以益者。奔走之僕，紈綺相炫；輿臺之輩，絢縟爭侈，不知在上之章德何物也。專業樗蒲，延招朋類，轉瞬一擲，蓋藏靡遺，不知注孤而盜起相繼也。披緇髡髮，寔繁有徒，寶觀崇菴，侈隆鼎建，是不可以不急汰也。振履連翩，競標姱麗，結驩絡繹，馳騖冶容，是不可以不急逐也。里閈富強，偃仰瞪盻，浚貧民之錐刀，以冒道家之忌，所謂陸梁其性也，是不可以不重懲也。少年遊俠，黨附逍遙，飛終日之崇觴，以起遊觀之艷，所謂蜉蝣其習也，是不可以不亟屏也。見隸戎籍，用之本省，所謂練土著者誠以是矣，而各省徵募復且歲至，安可不蚤杜以塞其流乎？歲輸課額，殷剥艱阻，所繇免漕輓者誠以是矣，而本郡餉…
translation_en: …then it will immediately fall into ruin. This is a clear and great proof—how much more so for what goes beyond a market of three households or property of ten pieces of gold? Today, throughout the territory of Zhejiang, there are those who, in hosting banquets and exchanging toasts, readily spend several pieces of gold, exhausting their own strength to provide for them; and there are those who, in marrying off daughters, pour out their wealth without limit, and when it is insufficient, take out loans to add to it. Errand-running servants show off fine white silks and damasks to one another; menial underlings compete in the extravagance of their colorful, ornate attire, not knowing what the emblems of virtue for those above even are. Those who make a profession of gambling invite and gather their cohorts, and in the blink of an eye, with a single throw, their stored savings are completely gone—not realizing that when their stakes are desperate, banditry arises in succession. Those who don black robes and shave their heads are truly numerous in their followers; precious Daoist temples and lofty Buddhist nunneries are extravagantly and grandly erected—these must be urgently culled. Trailing their shoes in a continuous stream, courtesans compete to display their alluring beauty, forming liaisons in an unbroken succession and chasing after seductive appearances—these must be urgently expelled. The rich and powerful of the neighborhoods carry themselves arrogantly and glare about, extracting the tiniest profits from the poor and thereby defying what Daoists taboo; this is what is called having an unruly and domineering nature—these must be severely punished. Young wandering gallants form cliques and roam at leisure, passing high goblets around all day long to stir up envy at their sightseeing excursions; this is what is called having the habits of mayflies—these must be swiftly banished. Those currently registered on the military rolls are employed within this province; what is called training local natives is truly on account of this. Yet recruitment and conscription from various other provinces still arrive year after year—how can we not block this early to stop the flow? The annual tax quotas delivered involve painful exploitation and difficult obstacles; the reason the grain tribute transport was exempted was truly on account of this. Yet the military provisioning [quota] of this prefecture…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
額復且歲逋安可不嚴覈以懲其玩乎凡
若是者均於習俗爲累非細故也顧風會
之趨今之各郡俱互有之靡靡風塵悠悠
歲月其所由來有漸矣玆欲捄之其道何
繇董子曰質樸之謂性性非敎化不成人
欲之謂情情非制度不節今之敝也無它
敎化不章而制度未壹也夫蓬之蔓生匪
麻弗直水之就下匪堤弗止誠使崇奬恬
澹抑黜澆漓遵漢詔之孝弟力田禁吳客
===
之短纓曼胡寧用萬石之恂恂謹厚勿取
嗇夫之喋喋利口而又彷夫里之罰酌農
桑之條申車服宮室之等約冠昏喪祭之
儀諸凡名器攸存者雖繁纓無所假借講
飲射讀法之禮聯比閭族黨之衆俾父老
相慰於農晦少年相戒於出疆而游食有
禁俠邪有禁作奇技淫巧者有禁操戈矛
而相目從軍者有禁如是而時察其化訓
之民表宅里而樹之風聲簡其弗率之民
punctuated: 額復且歲逋，安可不嚴覈以懲其玩乎？凡若是者，均於習俗爲累，非細故也。顧風會之趨，今之各郡俱互有之。靡靡風塵，悠悠歲月，其所由來有漸矣。玆欲捄之，其道何繇？董子曰：「質樸之謂性，性非敎化不成；人欲之謂情，情非制度不節。」今之敝也無它，敎化不章而制度未壹也。夫蓬之蔓生，匪麻弗直；水之就下，匪堤弗止。誠使崇奬恬澹，抑黜澆漓，遵漢詔之孝弟力田，禁吳客之短纓曼胡，寧用萬石之恂恂謹厚，勿取嗇夫之喋喋利口；而又彷夫里之罰，酌農桑之條，申車服宮室之等，約冠昏喪祭之儀，諸凡名器攸存者，雖繁纓無所假借。講飲射讀法之禮，聯比閭族黨之衆，俾父老相慰於農晦，少年相戒於出疆。而游食有禁，俠邪有禁，作奇技淫巧者有禁，操戈矛而相目從軍者有禁。如是，而時察其化訓之民，表宅里而樹之風聲；簡其弗率之民，
translation_en: … quotas are moreover in arrears year after year—how can we not strictly audit them so as to punish such negligence? All matters such as these alike burden our customs and habits; they are no trivial affairs. Yet as for the trends of the prevailing ethos, the various prefectures today all share them with one another to some degree. Amidst decadent worldly currents and the long passage of years and months, their origins have developed gradually. If we now wish to remedy them, by what way should we proceed? Master Dong [Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒] said: "What is simple and unadorned is called human nature, and human nature cannot be perfected without moral instruction and transformation; what stems from human desires is called emotion, and emotion cannot be regulated without institutional systems." The abuses of the present day have no other cause than that moral instruction is not made manifest and institutional systems are not unified. Indeed, when fleabane grows wild and sprawling, without hemp to support it, it will not stand straight; when water flows downward, without dikes to contain it, it will not stop. If we truly honor and encourage quiet contentment and suppress and dismiss perfidy and frivolity; if we follow the Han imperial edicts promoting filial piety, fraternal respect, and diligent farming, and prohibit the short cap-strings and coarse, unrefined robes of the swordsmen of Wu; if we would rather employ the sincere and cautious honesty of Lord Wanshi [Shi Fen 石奮] and refuse to select the glib, chattering eloquence of the Petty Official [of Shanglin]; and if furthermore we model policies on the fines of the "furi" [taxes on idlers from the Rites of Zhou], deliberate on regulations for agriculture and sericulture, reiterate the gradations of carriages, clothing, and dwellings, and restrain the ceremonies of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice—so that in all matters where ritual titles and insignia are at stake, even for something like a horse's ornamental girth-straps, no irregular concession is ever granted; if we practice the rites of the district symposium, archery contests, and reading of the laws, and bind together the multitudes of the local neighborhoods, villages, clans, and districts, causing the elders to comfort one another in the farmed fields [reading 晦 as 畝] and the youths to warn one another against crossing outside their local borders; and if there are prohibitions against idle parasitism, prohibitions against errant vigilantism and depravity, prohibitions against crafting bizarre techniques and licentious contrivances, and prohibitions against grasping halberds and spears and eyeing one another to join the military—if we do thus, and at regular times inspect the people who respond to transformative instruction, marking out their homes and villages to establish their reputation as a moral exemplar, while selecting out those people who are disobedient…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
殊井疆而俾之畏慕庶幾乎制度以壹然
後敎化以章敎化章然後人心以古人心
古然後風俗以淳起敝維風之道意者不
出乎此也然此特論其政令當先禁革當
急而其本猶不在是申公曰爲治不在多
言顧力行何如耳故有一朱子而男女不
敢入僧廬有一楊綰而宴座音樂減十之
七今之司世敎者其果端諸意嚮運諸精
神由躬行而表帥之又鄕之宦達相與羽
===
翼而倡導於邑里民之俊秀相與講明而
率先於黌校刊爲定則著爲章程鄕約以
此而示旌別保甲以此而犁苗莠無上下
賢愚無遠近大小咸使變聽改觀回心而
嚮道間猶有言不顧行實不中聲是薄惡
之尤孔子相魯所以首正于兩觀而不可
使一日梗化于明盛者也夫表帥旣端則
鄕黨知慕禁令旣肅則黎庶懷刑省會先
舉則僻壤嚮風持之以有恒積之以歲月
punctuated: 殊井疆而俾之畏慕。庶幾乎制度以壹，然後敎化以章；敎化章，然後人心以古；人心古，然後風俗以淳。起敝維風之道，意者不出乎此也。然此特論其政令當先、禁革當急，而其本猶不在是。申公曰：「爲治不在多言，顧力行何如耳。」故有一朱子，而男女不敢入僧廬；有一楊綰，而宴座音樂減十之七。今之司世敎者，其果端諸意嚮，運諸精神，由躬行而表帥之；又鄕之宦達相與羽翼而倡導於邑里，民之俊秀相與講明而率先於黌校，刊爲定則，著爲章程。鄕約以此而示旌別，保甲以此而犁苗莠，無上下賢愚，無遠近大小，咸使變聽改觀，回心而嚮道。間猶有言不顧行、實不中聲，是薄惡之尤，孔子相魯所以首正于兩觀，而不可使一日梗化于明盛者也。夫表帥旣端，則鄕黨知慕；禁令旣肅，則黎庶懷刑；省會先舉，則僻壤嚮風。持之以有恒，積之以歲月，
translation_en: …segregating their neighborhoods and boundaries so as to make them feel both awe and admiration. In this way, perhaps institutions will be unified, and only then will moral instruction become manifest; when moral instruction is manifest, then human hearts will return to antiquity; and when human hearts return to antiquity, then customs will become pure. The way to remedy decadence and uphold good customs presumably does not go beyond this. Yet this merely discusses what administrative orders should take precedence and what prohibitions and reforms are urgent, while the root of the matter still does not lie here. Master Shen (Shen Gong) said: "Governance does not lie in many words; it depends only on how earnestly one puts it into practice." Thus, when there was a single Master Zhu (Zhu Xi), men and women did not dare enter Buddhist monasteries; when there was a single Yang Wan, the music at banquets was reduced by seven-tenths. If those in charge of the moral instruction of the world today truly rectify their intentions, exert their spiritual energy, and set an example through personal practice; and if, furthermore, the eminent retired officials of the locality assist and take the lead in the towns and villages, while the talented scholars among the people expound upon these principles and set the pace in the schools—engraving them as fixed rules and publishing them as regulations—then the community compacts (xiangyue) will use these to display distinctions between good and bad, and the mutual-security groups (baojia) will use these to weed out the tares from the sprouts. Regardless of high or low, worthy or foolish, far or near, great or small, all will be made to change what they hear and alter what they see, turning their hearts toward the Way. If among them there are still those whose words do not match their deeds and whose reality does not correspond to their reputation, these are the worst of the shallow and wicked—the very sort whom Confucius, when serving as minister of Lu, first executed beneath the twin watchtowers, and who must not be allowed for a single day to obstruct moral transformation in an enlightened and flourishing age. Now, when the leaders are upright, the local communities know what to admire; when prohibitions and orders are strict, the common people remain mindful of punishments; and when the provincial capital initiates the practice first, the remote hinterlands will turn toward its influence. Holding to this with constancy and accumulating results over the months and years…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
將見侈者可使約薄者可使敦輕生者變
賈勇之習逐末者返力本之圖而謂全浙
之民有不迪德承休遵行古道者否也由
是上追成周忠厚太平之盛仰符
國初樸素醇謹之遺而孔子從先進之意其
在玆乎語不云乎日中必彗操刀必割又
曰日中則昃月盈則食隨其盈虛與時消
息識其弊而亟反之誠今日所當轉移而
斡旋者若行一事曰煩苛也布一令曰操
===
切也相安上下和同之爲功而不知挽回
風俗之爲急是失明彗剸割之方昧盈虛
消息之道俗之衰奚有已也而况四方之
偷靡尤有逾倍於浙者其杞人之憂又當
何如也睹時感事烏得而不凜凜惟執事
重圖之
第五問
秦應鵬
同考試官敎諭畢批此策以移風易俗爲弭盜
punctuated:
將見侈者可使約，薄者可使敦，輕生者變賈勇之習，逐末者返力本之圖，而謂全浙之民有不迪德承休、遵行古道者？否也。由是上追成周忠厚太平之盛，仰符國初樸素醇謹之遺，而孔子從先進之意，其在玆乎！語不云乎：「日中必彗，操刀必割。」又曰：「日中則昃，月盈則食。」隨其盈虛，與時消息，識其弊而亟反之，誠今日所當轉移而斡旋者。若行一事曰「煩苛也」，布一令曰「操切也」，相安上下和同之爲功，而不知挽回風俗之爲急，是失明彗剸割之方，昧盈虛消息之道，俗之衰奚有已也？而况四方之偷靡尤有逾倍於浙者，其杞人之憂，又當何如也！睹時感事，烏得而不凜凜？惟執事重圖之。

第五問
秦應鵬
同考試官敎諭畢批：此策以移風易俗爲弭盜
translation_en:
…then we shall see that the extravagant can be made frugal, the superficial can be made sincere, those who hold life cheaply will change their habit of flaunting bravado, and those who pursue secondary occupations will return to plans of exerting themselves in fundamental agriculture. Could it then be said that the people of all Zhejiang would fail to walk in virtue, receive blessings, and follow the ancient Way? Certainly not. Thus we may reach back to the flourishing loyalty, generosity, and grand peace of the Accomplished Zhou, and look up to match the legacy of simplicity, purity, and prudence from the founding of our dynasty; is not Confucius's intention in following the earlier generations of ritual and music to be found right here? Does the saying not go: "When the sun is at midday, one must dry things in it; when holding a knife, one must cut with it"? And it is also said in the Classic of Changes: "When the sun reaches midday, it declines; when the moon is full, it wanes." Following fullness and emptiness, waxing and waning with the times, recognizing the abuses and urgently reversing them—this is truly what ought to be transformed and turned around today. If, whenever a single measure is carried out, people call it "petty and harsh," and whenever a single order is promulgated, people call it "overly drastic," resting content in taking superficial harmony between superiors and inferiors as a merit while not knowing that reversing the decline of customs is an urgent priority—this is to lose the method of drying in the bright sun and decisively cutting, and to be blind to the Way of fullness and emptiness, waxing and waning. How then could the decline of customs ever cease? Moreover, when the frivolity and extravagance of the four quarters are even many times worse than in Zhejiang, how much greater should be the anxiety of the man of Qi! Observing the times and being moved by current affairs, how can one not tremble with awe? May Your Excellency give this weighty consideration.

Question 5
Qin Yingpeng 秦應鵬
Associate Examiner and Instructor Bi's 畢 comment: This policy essay takes transforming customs and changing habits as the means to quell banditry…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之原誠非謾語
考試官教諭林批策末尤究極於為政得人
足徵經濟之略
考試官教諭吳批學博才優
聖王疆畫天下犁若土田然民譬則穀也
官司者所以耘耡非種而佐之植者也寒
暑失節雨暘愆期如是而病天可也若其
嘉種而化為稂莠上田而化為瘠丘是天
之所以為鹵莽滅裂報也田者責也而奚
===
責焉故樹穀者務索草樹民者務索盜束
以法禁程以政教先民而使民有不敢為
盜之意日訢訢鋤其莠心而不自知是道
民之上務而弭盜之首策已自昔之論盜
者曰衣食不足也守令無良也政賦不均
也三者之外無他異故也然有不盡爾者
往者鯨鯢失路海波播颺而我民之無良
者出入島嶼之間以為之鄉而熾其兇於
是乎有瀕海之盜師旅繁興征發繹騷壘
punctuated:
之原，誠非謾語。
考試官教諭林批：策末尤究極於為政得人，足徵經濟之略。
考試官教諭吳批：學博才優。
聖王疆畫天下，犁若土田然。民，譬則穀也；官司者，所以耘耡非種而佐之植者也。寒暑失節，雨暘愆期，如是而病天，可也；若其嘉種而化為稂莠，上田而化為瘠丘，是天之所以為鹵莽滅裂報也，田者責也，而奚責焉？故樹穀者務索草，樹民者務索盜。束以法禁，程以政教，先民而使民有不敢為盜之意，日訢訢鋤其莠心而不自知，是道民之上務，而弭盜之首策已。自昔之論盜者曰：「衣食不足也，守令無良也，政賦不均也。」三者之外，無他異故也。然有不盡爾者。往者鯨鯢失路，海波播颺，而我民之無良者，出入島嶼之間，以為之鄉，而熾其兇，於是乎有瀕海之盜；師旅繁興，征發繹騷，壘…
translation_en:
…the fundamental source of [eliminating banditry]; these are truly not empty words.

Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: At the end of the policy essay, he especially probes thoroughly into how governance depends on obtaining the right men, which is sufficient to demonstrate his talent for statecraft.

Examiner and Instructor Wu comments: Broad in learning and superior in talent.

The sage kings demarcated the realm, plowing it as though it were farmland. The common people may be compared to grain; the officials are those who weed out the alien species and assist the grain in growing. When cold and heat lose their seasonal regularity, and rain and sunshine miss their proper times, to blame Heaven in such cases is permissible. Yet if fine seed turns into wild grass and weeds, and superior fields turn into barren mounds, this is Heaven’s retribution for careless and slapdash farming—it is the fault of the farmer, so whom else could one blame? Therefore, he who cultivates grain strives to root out weeds, and he who cultivates the people strives to root out bandits. Restraining them with legal prohibitions, guiding them with governance and education, leading the people beforehand so that they harbor an unwillingness to dare become bandits, and day by day joyfully weeding out their own wayward minds without even realizing it—this is the highest task in guiding the people and the foremost strategy for eliminating banditry.

Those who have discussed banditry since antiquity have said: "Food and clothing are insufficient; prefects and magistrates are unscrupulous; governance and taxation are unequal." Beyond these three, there are no other unusual causes. Yet this does not entirely account for it. In the past, when great sea-monsters lost their way and the ocean waves were tossed about, unscrupulous elements among our people went in and out among the islands, serving as their guides and fanning their ferocity; thereupon there were bandits along the coast. As military campaigns frequently arose and requisitions and conscriptions caused continuous disruption, camp [?]…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
吏乗機而剝膚庶頑樂亂而弄兵於是乎
有內地之盜探丸借客避仇亡命之徒以
武犯禁於是乎有郷里之盜今則異是
天子憂勞萬民曠然與天下更始而氛霾清明
暴豪善良有司斤斤守法五穀時登海淮
之間帖席而宴起焉不可謂非樂時寧歲
也然而洪波曲沚之間尚有馳舠鼓楫隱
約於暮夜而椎剽以為利者卽如兩浙都
會名區豈乏譏關詰慝之素廼羣飮之徒
===
邂逅將輸之命吏乗其弗戒倏起而奪之
金至廑
嚴㫖督責長吏雖其時縶之不旋踵而黨與以
次就縛然豈盛世事哉夫不有饑寒困苦
之迫與怨家墨吏之敺而甘棄其身於盜
賊非人之所宜有也而今有之愚故曰導
民之無策而教化之不先也蓋後世所以
考鏡于先王者莫備于周禮周禮太宰以
九職任萬民大司徒辨十有二土之名物
punctuated: 吏乗機而剝膚，庶頑樂亂而弄兵，於是乎有內地之盜；探丸借客、避仇亡命之徒，以武犯禁，於是乎有郷里之盜。今則異是。天子憂勞萬民，曠然與天下更始，而氛霾清明，暴豪善良，有司斤斤守法，五穀時登，海淮之間，帖席而宴起焉，不可謂非樂時寧歲也。然而洪波曲沚之間，尚有馳舠鼓楫，隱約於暮夜，而椎剽以為利者。卽如兩浙都會名區，豈乏譏關詰慝之素？廼羣飮之徒，邂逅將輸之命吏，乗其弗戒，倏起而奪之金，至廑嚴㫖督責長吏。雖其時縶之不旋踵，而黨與以次就縛，然豈盛世事哉？夫不有饑寒困苦之迫，與怨家墨吏之敺，而甘棄其身於盜賊，非人之所宜有也，而今有之。愚故曰：導民之無策，而教化之不先也。蓋後世所以考鏡于先王者，莫備于《周禮》。《周禮》：太宰以九職任萬民，大司徒辨十有二土之名物，
translation_en:
…subordinate officials seized the opportunity to flay the people to the skin, and the refractory commoners delighted in disorder and played with weapons—and thus there were bandits of the interior. Those who drew lots to kill magistrates, hired assassins, fled vendettas, and lived as fugitives violated prohibitions through martial force—and thus there were bandits of the rural communities.

Today, however, things are different from this. The Son of Heaven is anxious and toils for the myriad people, making a grand fresh start with the empire. Noxious mists have cleared into brightness, the violent and overbearing have become good and virtuous, the authorities scrupulously abide by the law, and the five grains ripen in season. Between the sea and the Huai River, people sleep peacefully on their mats and rise late in comfort; it cannot be said that these are not happy times and peaceful years. And yet, amid the surging waves and winding shoals, there are still those who race skiffs and ply oars, lurking in the dusk and night to murder and rob for profit. Even in so famous a metropolitan region as Two Zhe [Zhejiang], how could there be any lack of routine inspections at passes and questioning of evildoers? Yet a gang of carousers chanced upon an appointed official transporting tax silver, took advantage of his lack of vigilance, and suddenly rose up to seize the silver from him—to the point of troubling His Majesty to issue a stern decree reprimanding the senior officials. Although at the time they were captured before one could turn on one's heel, and their accomplices were bound one after another, how could this be a matter befitting a flourishing age?

Now, without the pressure of hunger, cold, and hardship, or the driving force of personal enemies and corrupt officials, for people to willingly cast themselves into banditry is something that ought not to exist in human nature—and yet today it exists. Therefore I foolishly say: there is no policy for guiding the people, and moral transformation through instruction has not been put first. Indeed, among the means by which later ages examine and mirror the former kings, none is more complete than the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). In the Rites of Zhou, the Grand Councilor (Taizai) employs the myriad people by means of the nine occupations, the Grand Minister of Education (Da situ) distinguishes the names and products of the twelve types of land…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而施十有二敎鄉大夫考德行察道藝州
長讀法黨正掌敎治族師掌政事司諫糾
民德司救誅邪惡日夜整齊其民而納之
於善惟恐不及然而有不勝也於是乎大
司馬以九伐正邦國士師掌八成聯什伍
比追胥司厲辨盜物野廬櫏賓客達道路
司寤詔夜禁脩閭禁徑踰所以捍禦不虞
而遏民狂謀者如此故雖有奇心袤行無
以爲也夫先王非恃其有圉姦之法而恃
===
其有擯姦之法非恃其民之必相戒不扞
吾網而恃其民無恣睢之心蓋禁於未發
則逸而有成禁於已發則勞而罔功此先
王深憂天下而豫爲之隄防者也愚獨悲
夫後世不講于先王防微之意而詳于先
王救敗之法故建議畫制日易月更聯之
以官司布之以邏諜專之以信地課之以
賞罰自謂是足以弭盜而不知和恒輯寧
之方未講於上徒恃法度禁令之繁遏止
punctuated: 而施十有二敎，鄉大夫考德行、察道藝，州長讀法，黨正掌敎治，族師掌政事，司諫糾民德，司救誅邪惡。日夜整齊其民而納之於善，惟恐不及。然而有不勝也，於是乎大司馬以九伐正邦國，士師掌八成，聯什伍，比追胥，司厲辨盜物，野廬櫏賓客、達道路，司寤詔夜禁，脩閭禁徑踰。所以捍禦不虞而遏民狂謀者如此，故雖有奇心袤行，無以爲也。夫先王非恃其有圉姦之法，而恃其有擯姦之法；非恃其民之必相戒不扞吾網，而恃其民無恣睢之心。蓋禁於未發，則逸而有成；禁於已發，則勞而罔功。此先王深憂天下而豫爲之隄防者也。愚獨悲夫後世不講于先王防微之意，而詳于先王救敗之法。故建議畫制，日易月更，聯之以官司，布之以邏諜，專之以信地，課之以賞罰，自謂是足以弭盜，而不知和恒輯寧之方未講於上，徒恃法度禁令之繁遏止
translation_en: …and implemented the twelve teachings. The Grand Master of the District (Xiang dafu) examined moral conduct and observed competence in the Way and the arts; the Subprefectural Head (Zhouzhang) read out the laws; the Community Head (Dangzheng) took charge of moral instruction and governance; the Clan Preceptor (Zushi) managed administrative affairs; the Director of Remonstrance (Sijian) corrected the people's virtue; and the Director of Relief (Sijiu) punished wickedness and evil. Day and night they ordered and regulated their people and led them toward goodness, only fearing they might fall short. Yet when there were still those who could not be overcome, the Minister of War (Da sima) rectified the states with the nine punitive expeditions; the Master of Uprightness (Shishi) took charge of the eight judicial precedents, linked the people in groups of five and ten, and organized the pursuit and capture of criminals; the Director of Confiscations (Sili) identified stolen goods; the Lodge Master of the Open Country (Yelu) kept night watch with wooden clappers for guests and kept the roads passable; the Director of Night Watches (Siwu) proclaimed the night curfews; and the Maintainer of Community Gates (Xiulü) forbade taking shortcuts or climbing over walls. Such were the means by which they guarded against the unexpected and curbed the reckless plots of the people; therefore, even if someone harbored deviant intentions or perverse conduct, there was no way to act upon them. Now, the former kings did not rely on having laws to imprison the wicked, but relied on having methods to banish wickedness before it arose; they did not rely on their people necessarily warning one another not to violate the net of the law, but relied on their people having no unbridled and defiant minds. Indeed, to prohibit evil before it breaks out is effortless and effective; to prohibit it after it has broken out is laborious and fruitless. This is how the former kings, deeply concerned for the empire, built dikes and defenses in advance. I am only saddened that later ages do not study the former kings' intention of preventing evil in itsincipience, while elaborating instead upon the former kings' methods for rescuing situations after they have failed. Thus they propose plans and draw up regulations, changing them daily and altering them monthly: linking them through official agencies, spreading out patrols and informants, assigning specific jurisdictions of responsibility, and evaluating performance with rewards and punishments. They tell themselves that this suffices to suppress banditry, not realizing that when the methods for harmonizing, stabilizing, and pacifying the people are not cultivated above, and one merely relies on the proliferation of laws and prohibitions to restrain them…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於下末矣故趙廣漢之治京兆也以鈎鉅
王溫舒之治關中也以投缿張敞之治長
安也以致羣偷尹翁歸之治扶風也以知
主名龔遂之治渤海也以解亂繩虞詡之
治朝歌也以設三科張綱之治廣陵也以
驟單車非不足以博稜名于一時而快雄
心于小割然而車不旋軫坐不敝席而鳴
鏑已交於境內矣則何也恃其勝之之術
以爲已之之術故也善乎秦觀之言曰盜
===
賊者平之非難絕之爲難今欲絕盜其惟
抑遊惰定經制乎夫今之四民非古之四
民也古之爲士者羣萃而州處閒燕則服
仁義稱先王父與父言慈子與子言孝今
士作無用之文以媒祿利鶩寵而炫華矣
古之爲工者無斲削之技磨礱之功相材
審時成構而已今工刻畫五色金罍玉尊
雕文彤漆銀口黃耳箕子之譏始在主上
今在匹夫矣古之商者察其四時而監貨
punctuated: 於下，末矣。故趙廣漢之治京兆也，以鈎鉅；王溫舒之治關中也，以投缿；張敞之治長安也，以致羣偷；尹翁歸之治扶風也，以知主名；龔遂之治渤海也，以解亂繩；虞詡之治朝歌也，以設三科；張綱之治廣陵也，以驟單車。非不足以博稜名于一時，而快雄心于小割；然而車不旋軫，坐不敝席，而鳴鏑已交於境內矣。則何也？恃其勝之之術，以爲已之之術故也。善乎秦觀之言曰：「盜賊者，平之非難，絕之爲難。」今欲絕盜，其惟抑遊惰、定經制乎！夫今之四民，非古之四民也。古之爲士者，羣萃而州處，閒燕則服仁義、稱先王，父與父言慈，子與子言孝；今士作無用之文，以媒祿利，鶩寵而炫華矣。古之爲工者，無斲削之技、磨礱之功，相材審時，成構而已；今工刻畫五色，金罍玉尊，雕文彤漆，銀口黃耳，箕子之譏，始在主上，今在匹夫矣。古之商者，察其四時而監貨，
translation_en: …them from below—this is attending merely to the branches. Thus, Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢 governed Jingzhao 京兆 through clever entrapment (gouju); Wang Wenshu 王溫舒 governed Guanzhong 關中 through secret denunciation boxes (touxiang); Zhang Chang 張敞 governed Chang'an 長安 by co-opting the chief thieves; Yin Wenggui 尹翁歸 governed Fufeng 扶風 by knowing the names of the ringleaders; Gong Sui 龔遂 governed Bohai 渤海 as one untangles a knotted cord; Yu Xu 虞詡 governed Zhaoge 朝歌 by establishing three categories of recruits; and Zhang Gang 張綱 governed Guangling 廣陵 by riding alone in a single carriage. It is not that these measures were insufficient to win a reputation for stern vigor in their own time, or to gratify an ambitious spirit with minor surgical strikes. Yet before their carriages had even turned around or their sitting mats had worn thin, whistling arrows were already flying across the borders again. Why was this? Because they relied on techniques for defeating bandits as though those were techniques for putting an end to them. Well spoken were the words of Qin Guan 秦觀: "With bandits and thieves, pacifying them is not difficult; eradicating them is what is difficult." If today we wish to eradicate banditry, must it not be by curbing idleness and establishing enduring regulations? Now, the four categories of people today are not the four categories of people of antiquity. In antiquity, those who were scholars (shi) gathered together and dwelt in communities; in times of leisure, they practiced benevolence and righteousness and praised the former kings, fathers speaking with fathers of parental kindness, and sons speaking with sons of filial piety. Today, scholars compose useless writings as a means to court emoluments and profit, chasing after favor and showing off华麗 [flashy ornamentation]. In antiquity, those who were artisans (gong) did not indulge in fancy carving or elaborate polishing; they simply examined the materials, observed the seasons, and completed the fabrication. Today, artisans carve and paint in the five colors, making gold wine-jars and jade goblets, with engraved patterns, vermilion lacquer, silver rims, and gilt handles—what Jizi 箕子 once criticized began with the ruler above, but now is found among commoners! In antiquity, those who were merchants (shang) observed the four seasons and inspected their goods,…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
知賈服牛輅馬以遊四方今商粥難得之
貨剷山沒淵以市異物矣古者常民衣服
溫煖而不靡器質牢樸而致用車足以自
載馬足以代步酒取合懽而不湛樂取理
心而不淫行即負擔止即鋤耘養生適而
不奢送死哀而不華今民間有層梁雕檻
飛榱步欄被服纖麗翫好玄黃塗屏錯跗
文杯畫案燔胾之食靡曼之聲葬死殫家
遣女滿車富者欲過貧者欲及富者空藏
===
貧者稱息矣古者君子孳孳思其德小人
孜孜思其力故其心安焉不見異物而遷
焉今豪家惡少商販庸兒黏竿掩罝逐狗
呼雞擁脂曲房探赤通衢宵宴朝歌博塞
投壺不富家而富身不耻盜而耻貧矣易
曰負且乘致寇至夫是數者則謂之盜夸
何也彼其所以靡麗衍溢者皆足以生民
心而荒淫佚樂之後又未有不胥而為盜
者故今之為盜者率是類也欲令盜賊不
punctuated: 知賈，服牛輅馬，以遊四方；今商粥難得之貨，剷山沒淵，以市異物矣。古者常民，衣服溫煖而不靡，器質牢樸而致用，車足以自載，馬足以代步，酒取合懽而不湛，樂取理心而不淫，行即負擔，止即鋤耘，養生適而不奢，送死哀而不華；今民間有層梁、雕檻、飛榱、步欄，被服纖麗，翫好玄黃，塗屏、錯跗、文杯、畫案，燔胾之食，靡曼之聲，葬死殫家，遣女滿車，富者欲過，貧者欲及，富者空藏，貧者稱息矣。古者君子孳孳思其德，小人孜孜思其力，故其心安焉，不見異物而遷焉；今豪家惡少、商販庸兒，黏竿掩罝，逐狗呼雞，擁脂曲房，探赤通衢，宵宴朝歌，博塞投壺，不富家而富身，不耻盜而耻貧矣。《易》曰：「負且乘，致寇至。」夫是數者，則謂之盜夸。何也？彼其所以靡麗衍溢者，皆足以生民心，而荒淫佚樂之後，又未有不胥而為盜者，故今之為盜者，率是類也。欲令盜賊不
translation_en: …and knew their prices, yoking oxen and harnessing horses to travel in all directions; today, merchants peddle hard-to-get goods, scraping the mountains and diving into the depths to trade in exotic things. In antiquity, among ordinary folk, clothing was warm and comfortable without being extravagant; vessels were sturdy and simple, made for practical use; carts sufficed to carry oneself, and horses sufficed to spare one's steps; wine was taken to share joy without sinking into drunkenness, and music was taken to order the mind without becoming licentious; when traveling they carried loads on their shoulders, and when staying home they hoed and weeded; in nourishing the living they sought comfort without luxury, and in sending off the dead they showed grief without ostentation. Today, among the people there are tiered beams, carved balustrades, flying rafters, and veranda railings; garments of fine, delicate fabrics and playthings of dark and yellow silks; painted screens, inlaid stands, patterned cups, and painted tables; meals of roasted and sliced meats and seductively alluring music. Burying the dead exhausts a family's estate, and marrying off a daughter fills whole carriages with dowry. The rich seek to outdo others, while the poor strive to keep up; thus the rich empty their treasuries, and the poor borrow at interest. In antiquity, the gentleman tirelessly pondered his virtue, and the lesser man diligently attended to his labor; therefore their minds were at peace, and they did not change their ways upon seeing novel things. Today, unruly youths of powerful families and base lads among peddlers use limed poles and spread nets, chase dogs and call cocks, embrace painted beauties in secluded chambers, and draw murderous blades [?] in the thoroughfares, feasting by night and singing by dawn, playing board games and pitch-pot; they enrich their own persons rather than their households, and are ashamed not of banditry, but of poverty. The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Bearing a burden on one's back while riding in a carriage invites bandits to come." Now, these several types may be called theflaunting that invites banditry. Why is this? Because all their extravagant and overflowing displays are enough to stir up covetousness in the hearts of the people, and once they have indulged in dissipation and idle pleasure, they never fail to end up turning into bandits together. Therefore, those who become bandits today are generally of this sort. If one wishes to keep bandits and thieves from…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
興莫若脩其本如以爲周人之敎有難卒
幾者非也曷不引已事觀之
高皇帝體國經野設法明禁制度昭於日星典
則貽于
子孫與周官之意皆相表裏至詳密也及夫
理道陵夷網亦疏闊民如蜚鳥曾無寧心
故遊食多於丁夫漏口什於見戶一人務
奢而弗禁衆皆馳騖以爲奢曰此所以爲
廣大也彼戔戔胡爲者也一人務佚而不
===
禁衆皆遊遨以爲佚曰此所以爲通適也
彼踽踽胡爲者也笑勤恪爲俗吏詆約嗇
爲守虜俗尚既成恬不爲怪夫天之所覆
者雖難窮而地之所容者則有限以氣數
之不齊而重以人事之多變於是乎生民
有盛衰生物有多寡以益盛之生民而用
益寡之生物然且不操夫撙節之政而猥
恣其無已之心此立盡之術也愚請取天
下之民不緣南畝者一切繩之以法非已
punctuated: 興，莫若脩其本。如以爲周人之敎有難卒幾者，非也。曷不引已事觀之？高皇帝體國經野，設法明禁，制度昭於日星，典則貽于子孫，與《周官》之意皆相表裏，至詳密也。及夫理道陵夷，網亦疏闊，民如蜚鳥，曾無寧心。故遊食多於丁夫，漏口什於見戶。一人務奢而弗禁，衆皆馳騖以爲奢，曰：「此所以爲廣大也，彼戔戔胡爲者也？」一人務佚而不禁，衆皆遊遨以爲佚，曰：「此所以爲通適也，彼踽踽胡爲者也？」笑勤恪爲俗吏，詆約嗇爲守虜。俗尚既成，恬不爲怪。夫天之所覆者雖難窮，而地之所容者則有限。以氣數之不齊，而重以人事之多變，於是乎生民有盛衰，生物有多寡。以益盛之生民，而用益寡之生物，然且不操夫撙節之政，而猥恣其無已之心，此立盡之術也。愚請取天下之民不緣南畝者，一切繩之以法：非已
translation_en: … arise, nothing is better than cultivating the fundamental root. If one thinks that the teachings of the people of Zhou are difficult to suddenly attain, that is wrong. Why not examine past events from our own dynasty? When the High Augustus Emperor [Hongwu] organized the state and laid out the countryside, establishing laws and clarifying prohibitions, his institutions were as bright as the sun and stars, and his canons and rules were bequeathed to his descendants; they all complemented the intent of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) as outer and inner aspects, being detailed and thorough in the extreme. Yet when the way of governance declined, the net of the law also grew loose and wide, and the people, like flying birds, never had a settled mind. Thus, idle consumers outnumber able-bodied laborers, and unregistered persons are ten times the registered households. When one person pursues extravagance and is not prohibited, the multitude all rush after it to be extravagant, saying, "This is what it means to be grand and magnanimous! Why be like those petty, stingy ones?" When one person pursues idleness and is not prohibited, the multitude all roam about in idleness, saying, "This is what it means to be free and at ease! Why be like those solitary, plodding ones?" They laugh at the diligent and respectful as vulgar clerks, and disparage the frugal and thrifty as mere money-guarding slaves. Once such customs and fashions are formed, people take them for granted and do not consider them strange. Now, although what Heaven covers is hard to exhaust, what Earth can hold is finite. Because of the unevenness of natural cycles, compounded by the many vicissitudes of human affairs, the population has its flourishing and decline, and natural products have their abundance and scarcity. To take an ever-growing population and consume ever-scarcer products, and yet fail to exercise a policy of restraint and moderation while instead rashly indulging their endless desires—this is a recipe for immediate exhaustion. I humbly request that all people in the empire who do not work the southern acres be strictly bound by the law: unless one has already …

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嘗仕者不得服華美非戍卒不得帶劒非
大享燕不得舉樂非飲射讀法不得羣留
於城市宮室器用輿馬之物婚娶喪葬之
儀一稟裁於
國典不得有所踰越有司時察其奇袤者而
法之必無赦若是則雖未逮夫先王化民
成俗之意而猶庶幾乎禁姦銷慝之心此
所謂朝令而夕至上不勞而下易從之術
又何憚而不爲此也賈子有言天下有瑰
===
政於此予民而民愈貧衣民而民愈寒使
民樂而民愈苦使民智而民愈罹於懸網
有瑋術於此奪民而民益富不衣民而民
益煖苦民而民益樂使民愈愚而益不罹
於懸網夫雕文刻鏤之物繁多而纖微苦
窳之器日變民棄完堅而競巧脆宜一日
而作者今十日不能成可用一歲者今半
歲而敝不耕而食農人之食是天下之所
以困貧而不足也故以末予民民大貧以
punctuated: 嘗仕者，不得服華美；非戍卒，不得帶劒；非大享燕，不得舉樂；非飲射讀法，不得羣留於城市。宮室、器用、輿馬之物，婚娶、喪葬之儀，一稟裁於國典，不得有所踰越。有司時察其奇袤者而法之，必無赦。若是，則雖未逮夫先王化民成俗之意，而猶庶幾乎禁姦銷慝之心。此所謂朝令而夕至，上不勞而下易從之術，又何憚而不爲此也？賈子有言：「天下有瑰政於此，予民而民愈貧，衣民而民愈寒，使民樂而民愈苦，使民智而民愈罹於懸網。有瑋術於此，奪民而民益富，不衣民而民益煖，苦民而民益樂，使民愈愚而益不罹於懸網。」夫雕文刻鏤之物繁多，而纖微苦窳之器日變，民棄完堅而競巧脆。宜一日而作者，今十日不能成；可用一歲者，今半歲而敝。不耕而食農人之食，是天下之所以困貧而不足也。故以末予民，民大貧；以
translation_en: …who have previously held official office, none may wear sumptuous attire; unless one is a garrison soldier, none may carry a sword; unless it is a grand ritual banquet, none may perform music; and unless it is for the community drinking ceremony, archery ritual, or reading of the laws, none may gather and linger in the cities and markets. Matters of residences, utensils, and carriages and horses, as well as the rites of marriage and funerals, shall all be regulated strictly according to the statutes of the state, with no transgression permitted. The authorities should periodically investigate those who are deviant and perverse and subject them to the law, without pardon. If this is done, then even though it may not yet attain the former kings' ideal of transforming the people and perfecting customs, it will still come close to the intention of prohibiting wickedness and eradicating evil. This is what is meant by a method whereby an order issued in the morning takes effect by evening, where superiors are not wearied and inferiors easily comply—why then shrink from doing this? Master Jia [Jia Yi 賈誼] had a saying: "There is a seemingly splendid policy in the world: you give to the people, yet the people grow poorer; you clothe the people, yet the people grow colder; you seek to make the people happy, yet the people suffer more; you make the people clever, yet the people increasingly fall into the suspended nets of the law. Conversely, there is an extraordinary art: you take from the people, yet the people grow richer; you do not clothe the people, yet the people grow warmer; you impose hardship on the people, yet the people grow happier; you make the people more simple-minded, yet they increasingly avoid falling into the suspended nets of the law." Now, when carved and engraved objects proliferate, and fine, delicate, yet shoddy and defective wares change by the day, the people abandon what is whole and sturdy to compete over what is ingenious and fragile. What ought to be made in a single day cannot now be completed in ten; what could be used for a whole year now wears out in half a year. Those who do not plow yet eat the food of farmers—this is why the world is distressed, impoverished, and lacking in sufficiency. Therefore, if you grant the people secondary pursuits, the people become…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
本予民民大富其數不可不知也故語曰
豐世無盜者足也治世無盜者均也化世
無盜者順也然而陶唐之世比屋可封舜
總百揆咎繇作士而寇賊姦宄之命諄諄
不忘聖人豈以平世忘戒備哉天下之患
不在於有形而在於無形於不足畏之中
而藏深可畏之端常人以其無畏成其可
畏聖人以其有畏成其無畏彼其椎牛掘
冢鑄山煑海行氣勢於鄉里而使一方爲
===
之下者皆畏人也雖堯舜之世何嘗無之
而堯舜能使其帖然以終其身故晋用隨
會而盜奔秦子太叔用子產之言而萑苻
之澤不久驚夫盜何足憂哉君子憂其大
者而已矣
punctuated: 本予民，民大富，其數不可不知也。故語曰：「豐世無盜者，足也；治世無盜者，均也；化世無盜者，順也。」然而陶唐之世，比屋可封，舜總百揆，咎繇作士，而寇賊姦宄之命，諄諄不忘，聖人豈以平世忘戒備哉？天下之患，不在於有形，而在於無形；於不足畏之中，而藏深可畏之端。常人以其無畏成其可畏，聖人以其有畏成其無畏。彼其椎牛掘冢，鑄山煑海，行氣勢於鄉里，而使一方爲之下者，皆畏人也。雖堯、舜之世，何嘗無之？而堯、舜能使其帖然以終其身。故晋用隨會而盜奔秦，子太叔用子產之言而萑苻之澤不久驚。夫盜何足憂哉？君子憂其大者而已矣。
translation_en: … the fundamental [agriculture], the people become greatly wealthy. This principle must not go unknown. Therefore, the saying goes: "That an age of abundance has no bandits is because there is sufficiency; that an age of order has no bandits is because there is equity; that an age of moral transformation has no bandits is because there is compliance." And yet, in the age of Tao Tang [Yao], when every household was worthy of enfeoffment, Shun supervised all the offices and Gao Yao served as Chief Justice, and still the charge regarding robbers, bandits, villains, and traitors was reiterated tirelessly and never forgotten. How could the sages forget vigilance and preparedness just because the world was at peace? The calamities of the world lie not in the visible, but in the invisible; within what seems unworthy of fear, there lurks the deeply fearsome beginning. Ordinary men, through their lack of fear, bring about what is to be feared; sages, through their possession of fear, achieve a state where there is nothing to fear. Those who slaughter cattle and rob graves, who smelt metal from mountains and boil salt from the sea, who lord their power over the villages and make a whole region submit to them—all these are formidable men. Even in the age of Yao and Shun, how could there never have been such men? Yet Yao and Shun were able to keep them submissive to the end of their lives. Thus, when Jin employed Sui Hui, the bandits fled to Qin; when Zitaishu followed the advice of Zichan, the Marsh of Huanfu was not long disturbed. What need is there to worry about bandits? The gentleman worries only about what is great.

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
萬曆丙子浙江遵例舉士於
鄉錄旣告成守萬乃颺言曰
昔在先王之世衆建萬國以
親諸侯諸侯各收其士而用
之所求者狹所用者小然猶
鏗鉤炳燿以樹勳于當時光
===
載史冊後世讓弗及焉今天
下一家
皇化汪濊士風蔚起有司盡羅而
貢之南宮以爲
一人用故學官之士百而一鄉書
之士千而一南宮之士萬而
一至於協化翊世爛焉不朽
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

萬曆丙子，浙江遵例舉士於鄉。錄旣告成，守萬乃颺言曰：「昔在先王之世，衆建萬國以親諸侯。諸侯各收其士而用之，所求者狹，所用者小，然猶鏗鉤炳燿，以樹勳于當時，光載史冊，後世讓弗及焉。今天下一家，皇化汪濊，士風蔚起，有司盡羅而貢之南宮，以爲一人用。故學官之士百而一，鄉書之士千而一，南宮之士萬而一；至於協化翊世，爛焉不朽
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the bingzi year of the Wanli era [1576], Zhejiang followed precedent in recommending scholars through the Provincial Examination. Once the record of the examination was completed, I, Shouwan, spoke forth to say:

"In antiquity, during the age of the Former Kings, myriad states were widely established in order to maintain close ties with the feudal lords. Each feudal lord gathered his own scholars and employed them. What they sought was narrow in scope, and how they employed them was on a small scale; yet even so, those men rang out like resounding metal and shone with brilliant splendor, establishing meritorious deeds in their own time and having their glory recorded in the historical annals, such that later generations yield to them as unattainable.

"Today, all under Heaven is a single family; the August transformation is vast and deep, and the ethos of the literati flourishes luxuriantly. The authorities cast their nets to gather them all and present them as tribute to the Southern Palace [the Ministry of Rites, for the Metropolitan Examination], to be employed by the One Man [the Emperor]. Thus, among the scholars in the state schools, one in a hundred is chosen; among the scholars registered on the provincial rolls, one in a thousand; and among the scholars at the Southern Palace, one in ten thousand. As for those who assist in the transformative governance and support the age, shining brilliantly in imperishable…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者不過億兆而一故古者諸
侯求士得國士焉用之足矣
今有司爲
天子求士非得天下士不足以塞
厚望稱隆寄也乃諸士之貢
直發軔耳無爲豪於鄉必也
銘太常勒彝鼎睥睨百世上
===
下而爲豪諸士往矣且
明興二百餘年以來史氏大書
之事凡幾見其賛
元命迪
靈符斡軸
乾坤濯磨
日月至于今望其人如龍如虎不
punctuated: 者，不過億兆而一。故古者諸侯求士，得國士焉，用之足矣；今有司爲天子求士，非得天下士，不足以塞厚望、稱隆寄也。乃諸士之貢，直發軔耳，無爲豪於鄉；必也銘太常、勒彝鼎，睥睨百世上下而爲豪。諸士往矣！且明興二百餘年以來，史氏大書之事凡幾見，其賛元命、迪靈符、斡軸乾坤、濯磨日月，至于今望其人如龍如虎，不
translation_en: … are no more than one in a hundred million or a trillion. Therefore, in antiquity, when the feudal lords sought scholars, if they obtained a scholar of peerless worth within their state, employing him was sufficient. Today, when the authorities seek scholars on behalf of the Son of Heaven, unless they obtain scholars of peerless worth throughout the realm, it is insufficient to fulfill the profound expectations and match the exalted trust placed in them. Thus, the tribute-recommendation of you scholars is merely the unblocking of the carriage wheels at the start of the journey. Do not merely act as heroes in your home districts; rather, you must have your merits inscribed on the banners of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials and engraved upon sacrificial bronze vessels and tripods, looking proudly across a hundred generations past and future as true heroes. Go forth, scholars! Moreover, in the more than two hundred years since the rise of the Ming, how many times have great deeds been prominently recorded by the historians? And among those who assisted the Primal Mandate, guided the Numinous Tally, turned the axis of Heaven and Earth, and cleansed and polished the sun and moon—men whom people to this day look upon like dragons and tigers, not…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
可狎視者凡幾人守萬不暇
更僕請論其大者
高皇帝草芟羣雄雲從衆傑其時
居中持議論尊禮不名則青
田金華與閎夭散宜生爭烈
矣名世嗣興若肅愍
社稷之勛屹然底定不啻虞淵
夾日也新建奮烏合之旅經
營江右甫旬日而氛曀廓清
分瑞析圭傳世罔極繇斯以
談凡我
國家殊尤之績多浙人士功也
故海內之望而浙若神龍之
重淵黝然深矣寶劔出匣萬
punctuated: 可狎視者，凡幾人？守萬不暇更僕，請論其大者。高皇帝草芟羣雄，雲從衆傑，其時居中持議論，尊禮不名，則青田、金華與閎夭、散宜生爭烈矣。名世嗣興，若肅愍社稷之勛，屹然底定，不啻虞淵夾日也。新建奮烏合之旅，經營江右，甫旬日而氛曀廓清，分瑞析圭，傳世罔極。繇斯以談，凡我國家殊尤之績，多浙人士功也。故海內之望而浙，若神龍之重淵，黝然深矣；寶劔出匣，萬
translation_en: … to be trifled with—how many such men have there been? I, Shouwan, have no time to count them all out one after another, so allow me to speak of the greatest among them. When Emperor Gao (the Hongwu Emperor, Zhu Yuanzhang 朱元璋) weeded out the rival warlords and a multitude of heroes followed him like clouds, those who at the time remained at the center holding forth in council, honored with ritual and not addressed by their personal names, were the men of Qingtian (Liu Ji 劉基) and Jinhua (Song Lian 宋濂), who vied in glory with Hong Yao 閎夭 and San Yisheng 散宜生 of antiquity. Famous men of their generation subsequently arose: take, for instance, the merit of Suming (Yu Qian 于謙, posthumously titled忠肅/肅愍) on behalf of the altars of state and grain, standing like a towering peak to bring stability—it was nothing less than holding up the sun over the Abyss of Yu! And the Earl of Xinjian (Wang Shouren 王守仁, Wang Yangming) roused a hastily gathered band of troops to campaign in Jiangxi (Jiangyou); in barely ten days the miasmic gloom was swept clear, and he was granted a tally and ajade tablet of investiture to be handed down to his descendants without end. Speaking from these examples, all the most extraordinary achievements of our Dynasty have largely been the work of gentlemen from Zhejiang. Thus the way the realm within the seas looks up to your Zhejiang is like gazing into thelayered abyss of a divine dragon, dark and unfathomably deep; or like a treasured sword drawn from its scabbard, before which ten thousand…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夫搖精諸士之往天下目隨
焉其何以無媿於先達而名
天下士哉始守萬應聘未至
常患以爲空言質人若空券
質貝故曰雖有健筆不如缺
斧或謂不然金錫不和不成
噐事詞不會不成文文何容
===
易彼四君子之始遭猶之乎
諸士也彼主司之得四君子
猶之乎今也士脩之於家而
慷慨論事則任者多効官擔
爵持之太重則讓者多夫人
而讓豪傑不幾見矣守萬固
願諸生之毋讓務趨前茅斯
punctuated: 夫搖精。諸士之往，天下目隨焉，其何以無媿於先達，而名天下士哉？始守萬應聘未至，常患以爲空言質人，若空券質貝。故曰：「雖有健筆，不如缺斧。」或謂不然，金錫不和不成噐，事詞不會不成文，文何容易？彼四君子之始遭，猶之乎諸士也；彼主司之得四君子，猶之乎今也。士脩之於家，而慷慨論事，則任者多；効官擔爵，持之太重，則讓者多。夫人而讓，豪傑不幾見矣。守萬固願諸生之毋讓，務趨前茅，斯
translation_en: … men are dazzled in spirit. As you gentlemen go forth, the eyes of the empire follow you; how then will you avoid bringing shame upon your predecessors and rightly be called scholars of the empire? At first, before I, Shouwan, had arrived in response to the invitation to serve, I often worried that judging men by empty words was like pawning cowries with an empty promissory note. Thus it is said: "Even a vigorous brush is not as good as a chipped axe." Yet some say this is not so: if bronze and tin are not blended in harmony, they cannot form a vessel; if practical affairs and literary expression do not meet, they cannot form true writing—how could writing be taken lightly? When those four noble men first met with their opportunity, they were just like you gentlemen; when those examiners obtained those four noble men, it was just like today. When scholars cultivate themselves at home and impassionedly discuss affairs, many are ready to take up the burden; yet when they enter office and bear noble rank, holding too heavily to caution and self-interest, many yield and shrink back. If everyone yields, outstanding heroes will scarcely be seen! I, Shouwan, earnestly hope that you students will not yield, but strive to press forward to the vanguard, so that…

title: 萬曆四年浙江鄉試錄
text:
主司之質不爽矣如以爲四
君子猶其小者也則主司謝
不敏大喜過望其懋勉行哉
河南開封府鄭州榮澤縣儒
學教諭林守萬謹序
punctuated:
主司之質不爽矣。如以爲四君子猶其小者也，則主司謝不敏，大喜過望，其懋勉行哉！
河南開封府鄭州榮澤縣儒學教諭林守萬謹序。
translation_en:
… the pledge of the examiners will not fail to be fulfilled. And if you should deem even those four worthy gentlemen to be of small account, then we examiners will apologize for our own inadequacy and rejoice beyond all expectation. Strive earnestly and go forth!

Respectfully prefaced by Lin Shouwan 林守萬, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xingze 榮澤 County in Zheng 鄭 Subprefecture, Kaifeng 開封 Prefecture, Henan 河南.
